_comment: GENERATED by scripts/gen-tool-index.mjs. Do not edit. Searched locally by the plugin so the full tool surface stays discoverable without advertising ~1,500 tool definitions per session. timeoutMs is the server's own declared budget for the tool (mapping.timeoutMs), read by lib/upstream.mjs so the bridge does not abort a call the server is still working on; null means the declaration carries none, which is UNKNOWN and not a budget of zero.
generatedFrom: live MCP tools/list (authoritative — includes runtime-registered tools)

tools.name: account_audit_health
tools.description: Single-call account health snapshot for drift / neglect detection. Returns counts and last-activity timestamps for memory, Mission Control, PM tasks, sites, MCP keys, and CRM contacts — plus a derived `drift_flags[]` array (no_memory_entries, mcp_inactive_14d, mission_control_stale_3d_with_pending_decisions, etc.) and a `drift_score` so you can sort 312 accounts by 'most neglected first.' crm.contact_count counts LIVE contacts only (soft-deleted excluded), the same basis as crm_account_summary.contacts and crm_list_contacts, so the numbers reconcile. Per-tenant: the account_id in the URL must match the key's home account. There is no cross-tenant variant; sweep a portfolio by calling this once per account, each with that account's own key.

tools.name: account_context_get
tools.description: ALWAYS CALL THIS FIRST on a new conversation before generating any copy, plans, analysis, or strategy. Returns the account context the Hiveku dashboard agents get hydrated with internally. The DEFAULT load is identity, brand voice, domain memory and rules plus SUMMARIZED customer avatars and journey maps; skills (the department workflows), content_examples (recent published content), grids (active before/after grids) and social (the social department setup: scheduling timezone, content pillars, connected accounts, schedule slots) are OPT-IN via include=. The response says which sections it loaded (sections_included) and which exist but were not loaded (has.*), so read that before assuming a section is empty. Without this, your output is generic AI slop with the wrong tone, wrong audience, and wrong facts — even when the user asks for "a blog post about X", the post will not match the account's brand and may contradict its content rules. Pass `domain` to scope the load to a specific department: • content — blog, articles, landing pages, social copy • marketing — strategy, campaign plans, positioning • seo — keyword research, audits, on-page recommendations • sales — outreach, sequences, deal motions • helpdesk — ticket replies, KB articles, macros • branding, ppc, social, customer_avatar, customer_journey, etc. The response includes a top-level `instructions` field — re-read it before every generative tool call. Cache the result in your scratchpad for the conversation; re-call if the user switches domains. Size: the default set fits ~40KB and the response reports size.approx_chars + sections_included; pass include=memory,rules (or whichever sections you need) for a small load, verbose=true only when you need full avatar/journey rows. Before doing work a skill covers, pass include=skills (they are not in the default). For social planning pass include=social (and include=grids for transformation / proof posts); for social work call with domain=social and include=identity,brand,memory,rules,avatars,social.

tools.name: account_entitlements
tools.description: Return the account's plan + the per-page access map (plan ∩ release-tier) so a UI can mirror ONLY the sections/features the account's plan entitles. Response.data: { plan, access_tier, account:{id,name}, page_access:{<key>:bool}, entitled_features:[keys where true], lock_reason:{<key>:"plan"|"tier"|null} }. page_access keys are the dashboard sections, e.g. crm, marketing, marketing_ppc, marketing_seo, commerce, accounting, accounting_ap, accounting_ar, accounting_payroll, communications, helpdesk, workflows, pm_projects, hiveboards, discussions. A hosting-only account has e.g. marketing_ppc=false. Use this to hide unentitled sections.

tools.name: account_seed_initialize
tools.description: Bulk-onboard an account: create a brand_guide + many avatars + many journeys + many grids + many media assets in ONE call. Designed for the 300-account migration where each account previously needed 15-20+ MCP calls. Each section is independent — passing only `avatars` is fine. Items in each section accept the same flat-or-`*_data`-wrapper shape that the dedicated `*_create` tools accept; the `5xx` field-naming applies the same way (errors come back with section + index + field). Cross-references: a grid may set `target_avatar_name` to point at an avatar created in the SAME payload — the server substitutes the freshly-created avatar's id automatically. Returns: {brand_guide_id, avatar_ids[], journey_ids[], grid_ids[], media_asset_ids[], summary, errors}. Errors are per-row so one bad item doesn't fail the rest of the seed.

tools.name: accounting_ap_aging
tools.description: Accounts payable aging — what you owe vendors, bucketed current / 1-30 / 31-60 / 61-90 / 90+ days by due date.

tools.name: accounting_ar_aging
tools.description: Accounts receivable aging — what customers owe you (open invoices), bucketed by due date.

tools.name: accounting_bank_import
tools.description: Import a bank/credit-card statement CSV into the reconciliation ledger. CSV ONLY — OFX/QFX is not supported yet; export CSV from the bank instead. column_mapping maps fields to the file's header names: { posted_at, description, amount } for a single signed amount column, OR { posted_at, description, debit, credit } for two-column statements; optional txn_id (the bank's own reference column — strongly recommended: without it ids are derived from row content and duplicate detection across overlapping files is weaker) and currency. Re-importing the same or an overlapping statement is SAFE: already-imported rows are skipped, keyed on (source_name, transaction id). Malformed rows NEVER abort the file — they come back per-row in errors. Amounts are signed cents (negative = money out). Writes nothing to bills, invoices, or payment rows.

tools.name: accounting_bank_match
tools.description: Link one bank line to the payment row it cleared: matched_kind bill_payment or crm_payment with matched_id, matched_kind 'ignored' for fees/interest/transfers (matched_id null), or matched_kind null to UNMATCH. Annotates the bank line ONLY — it never mutates the payment row. Direction must agree with the line's sign; a payment already claimed by another bank line returns 409 (unmatch that line first). Amount mismatches are allowed (fees) and echoed back as amount_delta_cents.

tools.name: accounting_bank_suggestions
tools.description: For each unmatched bank line, propose candidate matches from the payment ledgers — bill payments for money-out lines, customer payments for money-in — by EXACT amount within ±window_days, ranked by date proximity. SUGGESTIONS ONLY: nothing is written and no payment row is touched; confirm each with accounting_bank_match. A line with no suggestion may differ by a fee, be unrecorded (candidate for a reversal/entry on the payment ledger), or be ignorable (fees/interest → matched_kind ignored). Payments already matched to another bank line are excluded.

tools.name: accounting_bank_transactions_list
tools.description: List imported bank-statement lines. Amounts are signed cents (negative = money out). matched filters: unmatched (never reconciled), matched (linked to a payment on either ledger), ignored (written off — fees/interest/transfers), bill_payment, crm_payment, or all. from/to are inclusive calendar days on the posted date. pagination.total is the whole-filter count, not the page size.

tools.name: accounting_bill_approve
tools.description: Approve a bill (→ open, ready to pay) or reject it (approve=false → back to draft).

tools.name: accounting_bill_attachment_create
tools.description: Attach a receipt or source document to a vendor bill: pass file_name + content (base64, max 15MB; a data-URI prefix is stripped). Only PDF and image receipts are accepted (application/pdf, image/jpeg, image/png, image/webp, image/heic) — file_type is inferred from the file_name extension when omitted, and anything else is a 400. The file goes to S3 under accounting/bills/<bill_id>/ with a timestamp+uuid uniquifier, so uploading the same file twice stores TWO attachments rather than overwriting (the idempotency layer only dedupes retries of the same call). Works on any non-deleted bill regardless of status — a paid bill can still receive its receipt. uploaded_by_user_id is null in this service-key context. Returns the created attachment row with its cdn_url.

tools.name: accounting_bill_attachment_delete
tools.description: Remove ONE attachment from a bill, by explicit attachment id from accounting_bill_attachment_list — there is no bulk or pattern form. The DB row is deleted first, then the S3 object best-effort, so the worst failure mode is an orphaned file in storage, never a dangling row in the books. Destructive and irreversible (no undelete route exists); confirm with the human before calling, especially if the books-close discipline treats the receipt as the approval evidence. An id that does not belong to this bill and account is a 404.

tools.name: accounting_bill_attachment_list
tools.description: List receipt/document attachments on one vendor bill (newest first). Returns id, bill_id, file_name, file_type, file_size (bytes), cdn_url (the download link), uploaded_by_user_id (null for agent uploads) and created_at — use the id with accounting_bill_attachment_delete. attachment_count on accounting_bill_list/accounting_bill_get tells you whether a bill has any without this extra call. An unknown or deleted bill id is a 404.

tools.name: accounting_bill_create
tools.description: Create a draft vendor bill. vendor_id is required. line_items is an array of { description, quantity, unit_cents, discount_cents?, tax_bps?, category_id?, sort_order? }. tax_bps is document tax in basis points (875 = 8.75%). bill_number is auto-generated.

tools.name: accounting_bill_delete
tools.description: SOFT-delete one vendor bill and return { ok: true }. Refused with 409 the moment amount_paid_cents is above 0 (void it with accounting_bill_void instead), so this only ever removes bills no money has moved against. There is NO status guard: a draft, an approved bill and an already-voided bill all delete the same way. Destructive and effectively irreversible: the route reads no request body, so there is no confirm or force field to soften it, and no Olympus route anywhere sets deleted_at back to null. After the call the bill disappears from accounting_bill_list, 404s from accounting_bill_get, and stops counting toward accounting_ap_aging if its status was open, partially_paid, submitted or approved (a draft was never in the aging to begin with). Nothing cascades: the row is stamped, not removed, so its line items, any attachment rows and the consumed bill_number all stay in the database, and the per-account bill-number counter only moves forward, so the number is never reused. The P&L is unaffected because it is cash basis over recorded payments and a deletable bill has none. Confirm with the human before calling.

tools.name: accounting_bill_get
tools.description: Get one bill by UUID, including line items, recorded payments, and attachment_count (receipt/source-document attachments — list them with accounting_bill_attachment_list).

tools.name: accounting_bill_list
tools.description: List vendor bills. Filter by status (draft/submitted/approved/open/partially_paid/paid/void/all), vendor_id, free-text q (bill number/vendor ref/notes/vendor name). Each row includes vendor + category and attachment_count (receipt/source-document attachments — see accounting_bill_attachment_list).

tools.name: accounting_bill_record_payment
tools.description: Record a payment (money OUT) against a bill. amount_cents in cents; method one of check|ach|wire|card|cash|credit|other. Updates the bill balance + status. This records the payment in the books — it does NOT actually transfer funds.

tools.name: accounting_bill_schedule_create
tools.description: Create a recurring vendor-bill schedule; returns 201 with { schedule }. line_items is REQUIRED (at least one line, each carrying description, quantity and unit_cents) and is stored as template_json, the template every generated bill is built from. THE FIRST BILL CAN LAND ON THE NEXT TICK: next_run_at is taken straight from start_date, an omitted or unparseable start_date falls back to now, and a past start_date is kept as-is, so for anything except a FUTURE start_date next_run_at is already at or before now and the compile-bills cron (daily 05:00 UTC) issues a real bill. Those bills are created status open with approval_status not_required, so they never pass submit or approve: a schedule is a standing authorization to pay. is_active is NOT in the create schema, so is_active: false is silently stripped and the schedule goes live anyway; pause it afterwards with accounting_bill_schedule_update. Every other unknown key is stripped the same way by the Zod parse, pause_reason and next_run_at and template_json included. interval_count is ignored for the first run and applies only to later ones. anchor_day must be 1-28 (anything else is a 400) and is applied only when interval_unit is month, where it rewrites the day-of-month of the first run and can therefore move it into the past. vendor_id and every category_id (schedule level and per line) are ownership-checked and rejected with 400 rather than attaching a foreign row. The MCP proxy sends an Idempotency-Key derived from the body, so an identical retry replays the cached 201 for an hour instead of creating a second schedule, and a rejected payload replays the same 400 for an hour until the body changes. Money is CENTS; tax_bps is basis points (875 = 8.75%).

tools.name: accounting_bill_schedule_delete
tools.description: Permanently delete a recurring bill schedule; returns { ok: true }. DESTRUCTIVE AND UNCONDITIONAL: a hard row delete, with no soft-delete column on the model, no confirm field anywhere on the route and no restore path, so confirm with a human first. Bills the schedule already generated are NOT deleted, but they are silently orphaned: accounting_bills.schedule_id is ON DELETE SET NULL, so every past bill loses its link to the schedule and can no longer be traced back to it, including bills still sitting unpaid in the pay queue. To stop future billing while keeping the row, its counters and the provenance of past bills, send is_active false through accounting_bill_schedule_update; that is reversible, this is not. A missing id or one owned by another account returns 404.

tools.name: accounting_bill_schedule_get
tools.description: One recurring bill schedule by UUID as { schedule }, with vendor and category resolved to { id, name } and the full runtime state: next_run_at, last_run_at, iteration_count against max_iterations, is_active, paused_at, pause_reason and the line template. THE READ AND WRITE SHAPES DIFFER: the template comes back as template_json, but writing it back requires the key line_items, and a template_json key sent to accounting_bill_schedule_update is silently dropped, returning 200 with nothing changed. The compile-bills cron matches is_active true AND next_run_at at or before now, so a schedule showing is_active true with next_run_at null is exhausted or stopped and will never fire again however active it looks; read both fields before concluding anything about it. A schedule owned by another account 404s exactly like a missing id. Money is CENTS; tax_bps is basis points.

tools.name: accounting_bill_schedule_update
tools.description: Update a recurring bill schedule; returns { schedule }. EDITING THE CADENCE IS A BILLING EVENT: sending interval_unit, interval_count, anchor_day or start_date, or sending is_active true while the schedule is paused or its next_run_at is null, recomputes next_run_at, and only a FUTURE start_date defers it. Anything else recomputes to now (for interval_unit month with an anchor_day, to that day of the CURRENT month, which is already past once the day has gone by), so the compile-bills cron issues a bill at the next 05:00 UTC tick. Reactivating a schedule that already reached max_iterations also resets iteration_count to 0, granting the whole allowance again. This route is NOT idempotency-protected, so repeating a cadence edit re-arms next_run_at every time and can produce a second bill. line_items REPLACES the entire template instead of merging, so a one-line payload deletes every other line. is_active false stamps paused_at and stops generation; is_active true clears paused_at. vendor_id: null detaches the vendor, and bills generated afterwards carry no vendor. Only schema keys are read: pause_reason, next_run_at, last_run_at, iteration_count and template_json are stripped by the Zod parse, so a call carrying only those returns 200 having changed nothing, and pause_reason has no writer anywhere in the product. Omitted keys keep their stored value; schema defaults do NOT re-apply on a PATCH. Money is CENTS; tax_bps is basis points.

tools.name: accounting_bill_schedules_list
tools.description: Recurring bill schedules — the definitions that generate bills on a cadence. Read before creating one so you do not duplicate an existing cadence.

tools.name: accounting_bill_submit
tools.description: Submit a draft bill for approval (draft → submitted).

tools.name: accounting_bill_update
tools.description: Edit an unpaid vendor bill and return the updated bill with its line items and vendor (payments are NOT included in this response; use accounting_bill_get for those). Editable ONLY while status is draft, submitted, approved or open AND amount_paid_cents is 0; anything else is a 409 telling you to duplicate the bill instead, so reach for accounting_bill_void on a paid or voided one. line_items REPLACES the whole set inside one transaction: every existing line is deleted and only the array you send is recreated, so a call carrying one line silently destroys the rest, and each surviving line gets a NEW row id because a line-level id you pass is dropped on the way in. An empty line_items array is a 400, so a bill cannot be emptied this way. sort_order defaults to 0 on any line that omits it, so omitting it on a full replace collapses the ordering the reads sort by; send it on every line. subtotal_cents, tax_cents, discount_cents and total_cents are recomputed ONLY when line_items, tax_bps or discount_cents is present, so a notes-only edit leaves the stored totals exactly as they were. discount_cents is clamped to the subtotal, so an oversized discount is stored smaller than you sent. tax_bps is document tax in basis points (875 = 8.75%) and applies only to lines whose own tax_bps is null; a line-level tax_bps overrides it. Pass null to clear vendor_invoice_number, po_number, notes, terms, category_id, bill_date or due_date; omit a key to leave it alone. Dates are parsed leniently and NOT validated: an unparseable bill_date or due_date string is stored as NULL rather than rejected, so a malformed date silently clears the field. Unknown keys are stripped by the Zod parse and currency is parsed but never written, so a call carrying only currency, or only status, returns 200 having changed nothing: status moves through accounting_bill_submit, accounting_bill_approve and accounting_bill_void, and bill_number, currency and owner_id cannot be changed here at all. A vendor_id or category_id belonging to another account is a 400, and an unknown bill id is a 404.

tools.name: accounting_bill_void
tools.description: Void a bill so it no longer counts toward expenses or A/P. Not allowed once it has payments.

tools.name: accounting_expense_category_archive
tools.description: Archive one expense category. This is a SOFT delete: it flips is_archived to true and returns only { ok: true }, never the row, so capture the id BEFORE calling. It is destructive and unconditional: the route reads no body, has no confirm field, does not check whether bills are still coded to the category, and returns ok even on an already-archived row. Nothing cascades: bills, bill line items and bill schedules keep their category_id, so historical coding survives; an ACTIVE recurring bill schedule pointed at this category also keeps generating new bills coded to it, because archiving does not touch schedules. Recovery is narrow: the archived row disappears from accounting_expense_category_list (that route filters `is_archived: false`), so the only way back is accounting_expense_category_update with `is_archived: false` on the exact id you archived. The name also stays claimed by the per-account unique index, so creating a replacement under the same name returns 409 until the original is restored or renamed. An id from another account returns 404.

tools.name: accounting_expense_category_create
tools.description: Create one expense category in the chart of accounts that bills code to. Returns 201 with { data: <row> } (id, name, code, sort_order, is_archived), so the new id can go straight into accounting_bill_create. Only `name`, `code` and `sort_order` are read: the Zod parse drops every other key, so an `is_archived` sent here does nothing and the row is always created active. Omitting `code` persists null; omitting `sort_order` writes 0, and the list is ordered sort_order asc then name asc, so a category left at 0 sorts alphabetically in among the auto-seeded presets instead of landing at the end. `name` is UNIQUE per account and that constraint ignores is_archived, so reusing the name of an ARCHIVED category returns 409 'A category with that name already exists' and creates nothing; the way through is accounting_expense_category_update with `is_archived: false` on that archived id. The MCP proxy sends an Idempotency-Key on every write, so a retried create replays the first response instead of writing a duplicate row.

tools.name: accounting_expense_category_list
tools.description: List expense categories (the chart of accounts bills code to). Auto-seeds niche defaults from the account industry on first call. Use these category ids when creating bills so the P&L groups expenses correctly.

tools.name: accounting_expense_category_update
tools.description: Rename, recode, reorder, archive or RESTORE one expense category by id. Returns { data: <updated row> }. Only `name`, `code`, `sort_order` and `is_archived` reach the route; anything else is dropped before the write, so it cannot be persisted here. All four are optional, so a call that passes `category_id` and no field at all reaches Prisma as an EMPTY update: HTTP 200 with the row echoed back and nothing changed, and because the model has no @updatedAt even updated_at stays put. `is_archived: false` is the ONLY way to restore an archived category, and it works only if you already hold the id: accounting_expense_category_list filters `is_archived: false`, so an archived category cannot be rediscovered through any Olympus tool. `code: null` clears the GL code. Renaming onto a name already used in this account, archived rows included, returns 409 and changes nothing. An id belonging to another account returns 404, not 403.

tools.name: accounting_invoice_create
tools.description: Create a DRAFT customer invoice (AR). Creating does NOT send: the draft is invisible to the client until it is sent - use accounting_invoice_send (preview without confirm:true first, send on an explicit yes) or the dashboard. Never tell a user the invoice went out on the strength of this call alone. Exactly one of contact_id or company_id is REQUIRED (400 with neither; both is allowed), and every linked contact/company/deal must belong to this account or the call 400s. line_items needs at least one of { description (1-500 chars), quantity, unit_cents, discount_cents?, tax_bps?, product_id?, sort_order?, metadata? }; money is in CENTS. invoice_number is minted by the per-account atomic counter (INV-YYYY-000042 style) - there is no way to supply one, and a gap in the sequence after a failed create is normal. tax_bps is deliberately THREE-STATE: omit it (or send null) and the rate resolves from the customer's jurisdiction and the account default; send a number - including an explicit 0 - and that is stamped forever (a later tax-rule edit never re-rates an issued document). A line-level tax_bps overrides the document rate for that line. Document discount_cents is clamped to the subtotal, and tax applies to the post-discount base. issue_date defaults to today; issue_date/due_date parse leniently and an unparseable string stores as the default/NULL rather than rejecting. Optional: currency (ISO 4217, default USD), po_number, title (client-facing headline), notes, terms, allow_partial_payment (default false), send_payment_receipts (default true), delivery ({ attach_pdf?, mode: 'default'|'custom', to?, bcc?, subject?, body? } - prefills the dashboard send dialog), invoice_template_id (validated against the account; silently falls back to the account default template when foreign or omitted). Unknown keys are stripped by the Zod parse. Returns { data } with the created invoice and its line items; owner_id/created_by stay null under a service key. Idempotent: an identical retried call within 1 hour replays the first result instead of minting a second draft - including a cached error, so to genuinely retry after a failure, vary the body.

tools.name: accounting_invoice_get
tools.description: Read one customer invoice (AR) by UUID: the full crm_invoices row plus line_items sorted by sort_order, payment_applications (each carrying amount_applied_cents, applied_at and a display-safe payment: amount_cents, refunded_cents, method, gateway, gateway_transaction_id, status, card brand/last4, captured/settled/refunded timestamps, and the metadata holding any reference/note from accounting_invoice_record_payment - never the raw gateway payload), plus the linked contact (name/email/phone), company and deal. This is the ONLY Olympus read of an invoice's line items; accounting_invoice_list returns summary rows without them. Balance fields come back exactly as stored - total_cents, amount_paid_cents, balance_due_cents - because the record-payment transaction is their single writer; do not recompute them from the applications. REVERSED payment applications are excluded (same surface the dashboard shows), and the stored balance already reflects any reversal, so the visible applications may sum to less than amount_paid_cents implies historically. A refunded payment shows refunded_cents on the ORIGINAL payment row, never as a separate negative application. Money is in cents. Unknown id, another tenant's id, or a soft-deleted invoice is a 404.

tools.name: accounting_invoice_list
tools.description: List customer invoices (accounts receivable). status: draft|sent|viewed|partially_paid|paid|void|all. Each row includes the linked contact + company.

tools.name: accounting_invoice_record_payment
tools.description: Record a customer payment received against an invoice (AR). amount_cents in cents; method check|wire|cash|credit_note|manual|ach. Books cash already received — does NOT move money.

tools.name: accounting_invoice_send
tools.description: Email/text a customer invoice (AR) with its secure tokenized pay link. CONFIRM CONTRACT: without confirm:true this call SENDS NOTHING — it returns a preview of exactly what would go out (resolved recipient with its source: explicit override, then the invoice's saved delivery prefs, then the invoice contact; from name/address including the invoices@notifications.hiveku.com platform fallback; subject; attach_pdf; channel legs), minting no token and burning no rate-limit budget. Show that preview to the human, get a yes, then repeat the SAME call with confirm:true to send. Refusals: 409 on a void or fully paid invoice, 400 when the invoice has zero line items or no reachable recipient for the requested channel, 404 on an unknown or foreign id. channel email (default) | sms | both — 'both' sends email THEN texts the pay link, and an SMS failure never unsends the email (per-channel results in the response). SMS goes through the shared rail with STOP opt-out suppression; email is rate-limited per account (429 with Retry-After). A successful send flips a draft to sent, stamps sent_at, logs an invoice.sent billing event, and writes a crm_activities note so it shows on the contact's CRM timeline. Idempotent within the ~1h replay window automatically (the proxy injects an Idempotency-Key derived from account+path+body — do NOT invent per-retry keys, and note two SEPARATE identical-body sends within the hour replay the first result instead of sending twice; change the body, e.g. the message, to force a genuinely new send). Money fields in the preview are CENTS.

tools.name: accounting_member_create
tools.description: Add a payroll member. pay_rate is in DOLLARS (per hour when pay_rate_type=hourly, per period when fixed). pay_period: weekly|bi_weekly|semi_monthly|monthly. target_currency is the Wise payout currency.

tools.name: accounting_member_delete
tools.description: Soft-delete a payroll member: stamps deleted_at, sets is_archived true and status inactive, then returns { ok: true }. Destructive and unconditional; the route accepts no confirm field and writes on the first call. NOTHING CASCADES, because this is an update and not a row delete: the time entries, payroll items, PTO balances and PTO requests all survive. Those time entries keep appearing in accounting_time_entries_list, still carrying the member name through the join, while the member row itself is unreachable from accounting_member_get and accounting_member_list. Two consequences to know before calling: accounting_time_entry_create then refuses that member with a 400 Unknown member, because it resolves members on deleted_at: null, and future payroll runs skip the member entirely. Irreversible through Olympus: every member read filters deleted_at: null, so once stamped the row cannot be found or restored by any Olympus tool. Prefer accounting_member_update with status: inactive to stop paying someone while keeping their timesheet writable; is_archived: true only hides them from the roster and does not stop payroll. Both of those are reversible while you hold the id.

tools.name: accounting_member_get
tools.description: Read one payroll member by UUID. Returns { member }: the whole row, including pay_rate_cents, bill_rate_cents, status, is_archived and the Wise payout fields (source_currency, target_currency, payment_type, payment_reference). Money is in CENTS on this read even though accounting_member_update takes dollars. This is the only Olympus read that can see an ARCHIVED member: accounting_member_list filters is_archived: false as well as deleted_at: null, so an archived roster row is invisible there while this route still returns it. Soft-deleted members are filtered out here too, so a 404 means unknown id, wrong account, or already deleted; it never means merely archived.

tools.name: accounting_member_list
tools.description: List payroll members (the team roster you pay): pay rate, type, period, payout currency.

tools.name: accounting_member_update
tools.description: Update a payroll member. Returns { member }, the updated row. Only name, email, status, pay_rate_type, pay_rate, bill_rate, pay_period, source_currency, target_currency, payment_type, payment_reference, weekly_limit_minutes, daily_limit_minutes, time_tracking_enabled, project_count, notes and is_archived are read; every other key is silently dropped by the Zod parse, so a call sending pay_rate_cents, bill_rate_cents or avatar_url returns 200 with nothing changed. user_id is the worst case: it survives the parse but the update data block never references it, so linking a member to a Hiveku user through this tool always returns 200 and writes nothing. pay_rate and bill_rate are DOLLARS here and are multiplied by 100 at the route edge; every read surface reports them back as pay_rate_cents and bill_rate_cents. is_archived: true only hides the row from accounting_member_list: payroll run creation selects members on deleted_at: null plus status active and never reads is_archived, so an ARCHIVED MEMBER IS STILL PAID in every new run. Set status: inactive to take someone off payroll. weekly_limit_minutes, daily_limit_minutes, time_tracking_enabled, project_count and bill_rate are display-only on the members dashboard and nothing enforces them, so time entries still log past a limit and with time tracking disabled. Bad enums 400 the whole call: status active|inactive, pay_rate_type hourly|fixed, pay_period weekly|bi_weekly|semi_monthly|monthly, currencies exactly 3 characters. 404 once accounting_member_delete has stamped deleted_at.

tools.name: accounting_payment_reverse
tools.description: Reverse a recorded vendor bill payment (AP). Writes an OFFSETTING negative payment row pointing at the original via reversal_of_payment_id (the crm_payments refund marker-row model) — the original payment row is NEVER edited or deleted and stays visible in the ledger; the two rows net to zero in every SUM. Restores the bill balance and status in the same transaction, and when the paid total returns to zero the bill becomes voidable again. A payment can be reversed exactly once — a second attempt is a 409. reason is required and is kept on the reversal row.

tools.name: accounting_payments_list
tools.description: Unified payments JOURNAL for CPA/QuickBooks handoff: every payment that actually moved money in a date window, both directions, in one list. Money is integer CENTS at this layer. direction=out rows are vendor bill payments (accounts payable: paid_at, amount_cents, method, reference, vendor_id/vendor_name, bill_id/bill_number, category_id, note, currency from the bill); direction=in rows are customer payments (accounts receivable: dated by CAPTURE, amount_cents, refunded_cents, method, gateway, gateway_transaction_id, contact_id, company_id, deal_id, invoice_ids from non-reversed payment applications). from/to are REQUIRED (YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive, max 366 days per call). REFUND SEMANTICS: zero-money refund marker rows are excluded by design; a refund appears as refunded_cents ON the original captured row, dated by capture - a January payment refunded in June shows its refund in the January export, and refunded_cents is lifetime-to-date at export time, so do not treat this as a June cash movement. DELIBERATE EXCLUSIONS: payroll (its own Wise CSV export rail) and platform billing (Hiveku charging this account) - neither belongs in the tenant's books here. vendor_id filters AP only and REQUIRES direction=out (400 otherwise - AR rows have no vendor). format=json (default) returns data plus pagination { out_total, in_total, total } so a completeness check (e.g. the 1099 play) can prove it saw every row; format=csv returns the raw text/csv import artifact with a fixed 21-column order (invoice_ids joined with ';') - CSV mode carries totals only in HTTP headers this tool cannot read, so run format=json first for the counts, then csv for the file. limit caps at 1000 (default 500); page with offset against the JSON totals. Strictly read-only: no money moves, nothing is sent, no payment row is touched.

tools.name: accounting_payroll_run_create
tools.description: Generate a payroll run for a period (period_start/period_end as YYYY-MM-DD). Computes each member amount from tracked time × rate (hourly) or the flat rate (fixed). Returns the run with per-member items. Download the Wise CSV at /api/accounting/payroll/<run_id>/export.

tools.name: accounting_payroll_run_get
tools.description: One payroll run plus every per-member item (name, email, minutes, pay_rate_type, pay_rate_cents, amount_cents, target_currency, payment_type, payment_reference), items sorted by name, wrapped as { data: run }. accounting_payroll_run_list returns each run header with an item COUNT only, so for any run you did not just create this is the only Olympus surface carrying per-member amounts. READ-ONLY, and there is no Olympus mutation path at all: this route exports GET alone, so finalizing a run, marking it paid, deleting it and editing a single item exist only on the dashboard route, and the Wise payout CSV is only at /api/accounting/payroll/:id/export. Runs are born status draft and nothing on the Olympus surface can move them out of draft. minutes and amount_cents are a SNAPSHOT computed when the run was created; nothing recomputes them, so time entries logged for the period afterwards never appear here and the only fix is generating a new run, since the stale one cannot be deleted from Olympus. A run id owned by another account returns the same bare 404 as a nonexistent id, so a 404 is not proof the run does not exist. Money is CENTS.

tools.name: accounting_payroll_run_list
tools.description: List recent payroll runs (period, status, total, member count).

tools.name: accounting_pnl_summary
tools.description: Profit & Loss (cash basis): revenue (customer payments received) − expenses (vendor bills paid). Optional period_start/period_end (YYYY-MM-DD); omit for all-time. Returns revenue_cents, expenses_cents, profit_cents, margin_bps.

tools.name: accounting_pto_balance_set
tools.description: Sets a member's granted PTO under one policy and returns the stored balance row. This is an absolute SET, not an accrual top-up: the previous grant is overwritten and no history row is kept, so a retry is harmless but a second call with a smaller number silently erases the first. granted_hours is in HOURS and is persisted as Math.round(hours * 60) minutes, so a fraction under a minute vanishes. The returned row carries granted_minutes and no used or remaining figure: `accounting_pto_balances_list` recomputes those at read time by summing every approved request, so a wrong used figure can only be corrected by re-reviewing requests, never here. Both ids are re-checked against this account, and a member that is unknown, soft-deleted or another tenant's returns 400 'Unknown member' while an unknown or foreign policy returns 400 'Unknown policy'. Granting under a DEACTIVATED policy succeeds, but the balances list resolves names for active policies only, so that row comes back as policy_name 'Policy'. This route is NOT idempotency-wrapped; it is safe to retry only because the write is an absolute set.

tools.name: accounting_pto_balances_list
tools.description: PTO balances per team member — granted, used and remaining. Read this before approving a request so the decision is against a real balance.

tools.name: accounting_pto_policies_list
tools.description: PTO policies configured for the account (accrual rules, carry-over, entitlement).

tools.name: accounting_pto_policy_create
tools.description: Creates a PTO policy and returns it with 201. accrual_hours_per_year is in HOURS and is stored as accrual_minutes_per_year (hours * 60, rounded); 0 means unlimited or manually granted, not zero entitlement. Only name, paid and accrual_hours_per_year are persisted: `is_active` is accepted by the Zod parse and then never passed to the create, so a policy created with is_active false comes back ACTIVE anyway and must be switched off afterwards with `accounting_pto_policy_deactivate`. Every other key is silently dropped. `paid` is metadata that the PTO reads echo back; payroll runs never read PTO at all, so flagging a policy paid adds nothing to any pay run. The handler is wrapped in withIdempotency, so the proxy's auto-injected Idempotency-Key makes a timed-out retry replay the first response for one hour instead of creating a duplicate policy.

tools.name: accounting_pto_policy_deactivate
tools.description: Soft deactivate for one PTO policy, addressed by id. Despite the DELETE verb NOTHING is deleted: the route sets is_active false and returns { ok: true }. The policy row, every accounting_pto_balances grant and every accounting_pto_requests row under it survive untouched, because the onDelete: Cascade on policy_id in both child tables would only fire on a real row delete, which this route never does. Fully reversible with `accounting_pto_policy_update` is_active true. Two traps: filing a PTO request checks policy OWNERSHIP but not is_active, so a deactivated policy still accepts brand-new requests and their minutes still count once approved; and `accounting_pto_balances_list` resolves names for ACTIVE policies only, so every existing balance row under it silently starts reporting policy_name 'Policy'. An unknown or foreign id returns 404 and writes nothing.

tools.name: accounting_pto_policy_update
tools.description: Patches one PTO policy in place and returns the updated row. Every field is optional and unknown keys are dropped by the Zod parse, so a call carrying only `accrual_minutes_per_year` (the stored column name) or any other unrecognised key returns 200 with the policy completely unchanged: the input unit is accrual_hours_per_year, in HOURS, converted with Math.round(hours * 60). Omitted fields are left alone, they are not nulled. `is_active: true` is the ONLY way to bring back a policy that `accounting_pto_policy_deactivate` switched off, and it is always available because `accounting_pto_policies_list` returns inactive policies too, sorted active first. An unknown id or another tenant's id returns 404 and writes nothing. Not idempotency-wrapped, but every field is an absolute set, so a retry converges.

tools.name: accounting_pto_request_create
tools.description: Files a PTO request and returns it with 201. status is hardcoded 'pending' and is never read from the body, so a pre-approved request cannot be created here; review it afterwards with `accounting_pto_request_review`. hours is in HOURS, capped at 2000 by the parse and stored as Math.round(hours * 60) minutes. start_date and end_date are parsed with a bare new Date() and land in DATE columns, so send plain YYYY-MM-DD; an unparseable string returns 400 'Invalid dates', while a full ISO timestamp is accepted and its time component is discarded. Nothing validates the remaining balance, overlapping dates, or whether the policy is still active, so this happily books time the member does not have and approving it later drives remaining_minutes negative: read `accounting_pto_balances_list` first. A member that is unknown, soft-deleted or another tenant's returns 400 'Unknown member'; an unknown or foreign policy returns 400 'Unknown policy'. Wrapped in withIdempotency, so the proxy's Idempotency-Key makes a timed-out retry replay for one hour rather than filing a second request.

tools.name: accounting_pto_request_review
tools.description: Approve, deny or cancel ONE PTO request by id and return the updated row. action maps to status approved, denied or cancelled and stamps reviewed_at; a missing or unrecognised action returns 400 and every other body key is dropped. There is NO status guard: an already approved, denied or cancelled request can be flipped to any other state repeatedly, and nothing checks the member's remaining balance first, so read `accounting_pto_balances_list` before approving. 'approved' is the only status that counts anywhere: used_minutes is a live SUM over approved requests with no date window, so approving a request from any period moves the current remaining figure immediately, and flipping it back to denied restores it. reviewed_by_user_id is forced to NULL on this service-key route, leaving no record of who approved it. Nothing else downstream reads the status: no email or notification is sent, and payroll runs never read PTO, so approving PAID time off adds zero to any pay run. An unknown or foreign id returns 404.

tools.name: accounting_pto_requests_list
tools.description: PTO requests, filterable by member and status (pending/approved/denied). The queue an approver works from.

tools.name: accounting_settings_get
tools.description: Accounting settings: bill_prefix, default_currency, default_payment_terms. There is no dashboard page for these — this is the only surface that reads them.

tools.name: accounting_settings_update
tools.description: Update bill_prefix, default_currency or default_payment_terms. No dashboard route mirrors this, so it is the only way to change them outside the database.

tools.name: accounting_time_entries_list
tools.description: Logged time entries, optionally scoped to one member and a date range. The read half of timesheets — pair with accounting_time_entry_create to log.

tools.name: accounting_time_entry_create
tools.description: Log a time entry. Body mirrors the accounting dashboard's timesheet form.

tools.name: accounting_time_entry_delete
tools.description: Permanently delete one time entry. Returns { ok: true }. This is a HARD row delete and it is unconditional: the route accepts no confirm field, and accounting_time_entries carries no deleted_at column, so the logged hours are gone and the only recovery is re-logging them with accounting_time_entry_create. Nothing else is removed. An already-generated payroll run keeps the minutes and total_cents it snapshotted when it was created, so deleting an entry after that run exists does NOT reduce what the run pays, and accounting_payroll_run_create would add a second run for the period rather than correct the first. 404 if the id does not exist or does not belong to the calling account.

tools.name: accounting_time_entry_update
tools.description: Update one logged time entry. Returns { entry }, the updated row. Only work_date, minutes, hours, project, billable and note are read; every other key is dropped by the Zod parse, so a call carrying only unknown fields returns 200 with nothing changed. member_id is NOT patchable: an entry logged against the wrong person must be removed with accounting_time_entry_delete and re-logged with accounting_time_entry_create. minutes wins when both minutes and hours are sent, hours is rounded to whole minutes, and minutes must be an integer 0 to 1440 (anything outside 400s the whole call). Unlike accounting_time_entry_create, this route ACCEPTS minutes: 0 and zeroes the entry instead of rejecting it; sending neither key leaves the logged time untouched. work_date runs through parseDateOrNull and an unparseable string collapses to undefined rather than erroring, so a malformed date returns 200 with the OLD date still in place: send YYYY-MM-DD. Nothing recomputes downstream: a payroll run snapshots minutes, pay_rate_cents and amount_cents onto its items and stores total_cents at create time, so editing an entry inside a period that already has a run leaves that run untouched, and accounting_payroll_run_create adds an ADDITIONAL run for the period rather than correcting the existing one.

tools.name: accounting_vendor_create
tools.description: Create a vendor. target_currency is the payout currency for the Wise export (e.g. USD, PHP). is_1099 flags year-end 1099 reporting.

tools.name: accounting_vendor_delete
tools.description: Soft-delete a vendor: stamps deleted_at, forces is_archived true, and returns only { ok: true } with no copy of the row. DESTRUCTIVE AND UNCONDITIONAL: the route accepts no confirm field and refuses nothing, so a vendor carrying open unpaid bills is retired without a word. Read open_bill_count and open_balance_cents from accounting_vendor_get and get a human yes before calling. Nothing cascades, because this is an UPDATE and not a row delete: the onDelete SetNull relations never fire, so every bill, bill payment and recurring bill schedule keeps its vendor_id, accounting_bill_list and accounting_bill_get still hydrate the deleted vendor's name onto those bills, and accounting_ap_aging does not move (it buckets the surviving bills by due date and never looks at the vendor). Two live consequences instead: accounting_bill_create now rejects this vendor with 400 'Unknown vendor', while any active recurring bill schedule pointed at it KEEPS generating bills on its cron, since the compiler copies vendor_id forward without checking deleted_at. It is one-way through Olympus: every vendor route filters deleted_at null, so afterwards the id 404s on accounting_vendor_get and accounting_vendor_update, it is absent from accounting_vendor_list, and no tool can undelete it. When the goal is only to get the vendor out of pickers, call accounting_vendor_update with is_archived true instead; that one is reversible.

tools.name: accounting_vendor_get
tools.description: Read one vendor by UUID: returns `data` (the full vendor row) plus a `stats` rollup of open_balance_cents, open_bill_count and lifetime_paid_cents. open_balance_cents sums balance_due_cents across bills whose status is submitted, approved, open or partially_paid ONLY, and open_bill_count counts that same set, so draft and void bills are invisible here and a vendor whose bills are all still drafts reads as 0 owed. lifetime_paid_cents sums every payment row denormalized to this vendor with no date window and no check on the bill's deleted_at, so payments against since-deleted bills still count; it is a lifetime figure, never a period one. This is the only Olympus read that resolves an ARCHIVED vendor, since accounting_vendor_list filters is_archived false, so it is how you confirm an id you archived, but only while you still hold that id. A vendor retired by accounting_vendor_delete 404s here.

tools.name: accounting_vendor_list
tools.description: List vendors/suppliers you pay bills to (accounts payable). Optional free-text q (name/email). Distinct from CRM companies — these are who you OWE money to.

tools.name: accounting_vendor_update
tools.description: Update one vendor in place; returns the saved row as `data`. Only name, email, phone, website, address_line1, address_line2, city, region, postal_code, country, tax_id, is_1099, default_expense_category_id, default_payment_terms, notes and is_archived survive the Zod parse; every other key is stripped in silence, so a call carrying only unknown fields returns 200 with nothing changed (target_currency is exactly that case: accounting_vendor_create advertises it, but no vendor column exists and both routes drop it). An empty object is a legal no-op 200; sending no body at all makes the route 500 inside the JSON parse, so always send an object. `is_archived: true` hides the vendor from accounting_vendor_list, which filters is_archived false, and `is_archived: false` is the only way back: it works solely if you already hold the id, since an archived vendor cannot be rediscovered through list (accounting_vendor_get still resolves it). Archiving blocks nothing else; accounting_bill_create still accepts an archived vendor, because it checks deleted_at only. default_expense_category_id must be an expense category owned by this same account or the entire call 400s with 'Unknown default expense category'; pass null to clear it. Nothing recomputes downstream: default_expense_category_id is read only by the dashboard bill form, so bills written by accounting_bill_create never inherit it, and default_payment_terms, tax_id and is_1099 are stored labels rendered in the vendors table with no bill-creation or year-end 1099 consumer. Bills already recorded keep their own terms, category and totals. A vendor retired by accounting_vendor_delete 404s here, so this cannot undo a delete.

tools.name: add_task_comment
tools.description: Add a comment to a task

tools.name: agent_approval_approve
tools.description: Approve a staged coder-agent action — approving EXECUTES IT FOR REAL: action='deploy_project' DEPLOYS CODE TO THE CLIENT'S LIVE PRODUCTION SITE; 'github_commit' pushes to their repository. This is the execution half of the implement rail and of any coder-chat staged action. TWO-STEP CONFIRM: the first call (without confirm) executes NOTHING — it returns { requires_confirm: true, preview } with the staged action name, its summary, the target project id, and expiry. Show it to the user, then repeat the IDENTICAL call with confirm: true (strict boolean) to execute. A token is single-use: already-handled tokens 409, expired tokens 410. Execution resumes a full agent turn, so billing gates apply (402 when blocked). Optional environment overrides the staged deploy environment (the agent server validates it and falls back to the staged value). Execution can take a couple of minutes — do not retry on timeout; re-check with agent_approval_get / seo_task_implement_status first (the token may already be consumed and the deploy shipping).

tools.name: agent_approval_get
tools.description: Inspect one staged coder-agent action by token, non-destructively — returns the action, summary, staged request payload, and consumed/expired/approvable flags so you can tell "already handled" apart from "still approvable" before approving or rejecting. Works regardless of state. Read-only.

tools.name: agent_approval_list
tools.description: List staged coder-agent actions awaiting approval (coder_agent_pending_actions) — the approval rail behind the coder chat AND the SEO implement rail (its staged production deploy appears here with action='deploy_project'; match it via session_id from seo_task_implement). Each row: token, action, human-readable summary, session_id, the staged request (kwargs include the target project_id), created/expires timestamps. Default shows only approvable rows (unconsumed + unexpired); status='all' includes handled/expired history. Read-only — approve via agent_approval_approve (EXECUTES the action), discard via agent_approval_reject.

tools.name: agent_approval_reject
tools.description: Reject a staged coder-agent action WITHOUT executing it — marks the token consumed so it disappears from the pending list and can never be approved. Nothing is dispatched and nothing deploys; the coder session simply never gets its confirmation. Idempotent-ish: an already-handled or unknown token returns 404. No confirm gate (rejecting only discards).

tools.name: agent_identity_domains_list
tools.description: List all _identity:* domains configured on this account, so agents stop guessing-and-getting-404s when calling agent_identity_get(domain=...). Returns each domain's bare name (after the '_identity:' prefix) plus its last update time so callers can stale-detect.

tools.name: agent_identity_get
tools.description: Pull the FULL agent identity bundle for one of the account's internal departments — the same context the live department agent gets hydrated with when it runs. Use this INSTEAD OF talk_to_department when you want to act AS the department directly (no upstream call, no streaming wait). Returns the department's identity persona, brand guide, account memory, all skills/rules/commands/sub-agents tagged for that domain, customer avatars + journeys, knowledge base index, recent published content, AND cross-domain memory (so a content agent can see what marketing/seo know). Also returns a `claude_md` field — a fully-assembled CLAUDE.md-style markdown block. Drop that into your workspace as `CLAUDE.md` and your Claude Code session will pick up the persona, voice, rules, and skills automatically. Domains: • content — blog, articles, landing pages, social copy • marketing — strategy, campaign plans, positioning • seo — keyword research, audits, on-page recommendations • sales — outreach, sequences, deal motions • helpdesk — ticket replies, KB articles, macros • branding, ppc, social, customer_avatar, customer_journey, before_after_grid, website_design, knowledge_base, workflow, outbound Use `format: "markdown"` for a slim JSON response containing just the synthesized CLAUDE.md under `data.content` (handy for writing straight to a file: read `data.content` and dump it as CLAUDE.md). Default `format: "json"` returns the full structured payload including the same markdown under `data.claude_md`.

tools.name: agent_inbox_get
tools.description: Get one agent-ops inbox item in full — title, markdown body, metadata (machine-readable context for the underlying problem, e.g. connection ids/thresholds), action_type/action_payload, and lifecycle timestamps. Works on items in ANY state (including expired/closed), unlike the list default. Read-only.

tools.name: agent_inbox_list
tools.description: List agent-ops inbox items — the platform's staged alert/suggestion queue (guardrail sweep findings, Shopify webhook-health / scope-drift / compliance alerts, briefing suggestions, voice/billing/deploy-health warnings). Filter by category (free-form dotted vocabulary, e.g. 'shopify.scope_drift'), severity (info | suggestion | urgent), and lifecycle status (comma list; default 'new,seen' = the open queue; also: snoozed, actioned, dismissed, expired). Rows past their expiry are hidden unless 'expired' is requested. Read-only; close items with agent_inbox_resolve.

tools.name: agent_inbox_resolve
tools.description: Close an agent-ops inbox item. resolution: 'resolved' (default — you handled the underlying problem; status becomes 'actioned') or 'dismissed' (deliberately not acting; a negative signal for producer tuning). This ONLY closes the queue row — it never executes the item's action handler, so no confirm is needed. Only open items (new/seen/snoozed) can be closed; already-closed or expired items 409. Fix the underlying problem FIRST, then resolve — resolving does not make the alert's cause go away, and deduped producers will re-file it.

tools.name: ai_optimization_keyword_data_locations_and_languages
tools.description: Utility tool for ai_keyword_data_search_volume to get list of availible locations and languages

tools.name: ai_optimization_keyword_data_search_volume
tools.description: This endpoint provides search volume data for your target keywords, reflecting their estimated usage in AI LLMs

tools.name: analytics_channel_scorecard
tools.description: THE answer to 'why isn't Google Ads / Meta / Microsoft recording conversions?'. Loads the customer's live converting pages in a real browser TWICE (once as a first-time visitor, once as one who already accepted cookies), records what each ad channel actually sends, and compares it against what the platform says it received. Returns one verdict per channel — tracking | partially_tracking | not_tracking | unknown — each with `headline` (one sentence, safe to relay verbatim), `hiveku_recorded` vs `platform_recorded` conversion counts, `how_we_know`, `how_to_fix`, and `agent_task`. Relay the headline verbatim: it carries the number that makes the problem undeniable (e.g. "24 leads arrived from Google Ads clicks and Google Ads recorded 0"). A tag being installed is NOT the same as a tag firing, and this is the only tool that can tell them apart. Slow (loads real pages) — call it once, not in a loop.

tools.name: analytics_diagnose_tracking
tools.description: Per-project conversion-tracking diagnosis: scans the project source AND loads the deployed pages in a browser, then returns findings with `what_is_wrong` / `how_we_know` / `how_to_fix` / `agent_task`, plus a `coding_agent_brief` written to be handed straight to the coding agent. Catches a conversion gated on a value no route passes, a mistyped conversion label, a tag in the code that never reached the deployed bundle, a conversion that fires while consent is denied, and duplicate firing paths. Use when the scorecard says a channel is not tracking and you need the cause in the code.

tools.name: analytics_events_list
tools.description: Raw analytics events for an account or project, filterable by event_name, event_category, page_path, session_id and date range. Use when analytics_overview/analytics_pages summaries are not specific enough and you need the individual events behind a number.

tools.name: analytics_overview
tools.description: Get website analytics overview — traffic metrics, top devices, countries, and landing pages for a date range

tools.name: analytics_pages
tools.description: List top pages by traffic with metrics for a date range

tools.name: analytics_probe_page
tools.description: Load ONE page of a site this account owns in a real browser and report every tracking request it made, under two consent conditions. Use to answer "does the cookie banner have to be accepted for this conversion to count?" with a measurement instead of an opinion, or to confirm a fix actually reached visitors. Returns `as_first_time_visitor` and `as_visitor_who_accepted`; compare their `observed` arrays. Refuses URLs on domains this account does not own.

tools.name: analytics_sessions
tools.description: List website visitor sessions with device and country filters

tools.name: analytics_traffic_sources
tools.description: Get traffic source breakdown (organic, direct, referral, paid, social, email)

tools.name: analytics_visitors
tools.description: Visitor intelligence — visitor profiles with identification (email/identified_data) and ICP matching (matched_icp_id, icp_match_confidence/criteria/source), event counts and first/last seen. THE SDR/BDR chase list: has_icp_match=true + sort_by=icp_confidence surfaces warm, high-fit visitors to pursue; marketing uses it to judge traffic relevance. Account-scoped (all sites).

tools.name: assets_delete
tools.description: Delete a WEBSITE PROJECT asset row by UUID AND its S3 object (website project files on S3 — NOT the marketing Media Library; marketing_media_* tools cover that surface). project_id is REQUIRED in the call (the route scopes by project to prevent cross-tenant deletes — passing only asset_id without project_id returns 400). The response carries `s3_object_deleted`. If it is false the row is gone but the object is STILL SERVED — clear it with project_assets_orphan_sweep. This tool previously deleted only the row, citing a repair job that does not exist, which is how projects accumulated permanently-served orphans that also kept regenerating CloudFront asset behaviors over their page routes.

tools.name: assets_info
tools.description: Look up one BINARY asset (image / video / font / etc.) in a WEBSITE PROJECT's asset store by UUID or file_path. Website project files on S3 — NOT the marketing Media Library; for social/design media use marketing_media_get. ⚠️ Binary-assets table only. Returns 404 for paths that exist as TEXT files in builder_code_versions (e.g. `public/icon.svg` if it was saved via project_file_save). Binary assets live in builder_project_assets (S3-backed); source/text files live in builder_code_versions. If assets_info 404s on a path that exists as a project file, use project_file_get instead.

tools.name: assets_list
tools.description: List binary assets (images, videos, fonts) for a WEBSITE PROJECT — project files on S3, NOT the marketing Media Library; for social/design media use marketing_media_list. Optional filters: path_prefix (e.g. 'public/images/'), mime_type (e.g. 'image/'), and search (contains match on path/name). Paginated. Search this library BEFORE generating images - prefer the user's uploaded photos. PAGINATED (default limit 100): ALWAYS check pagination.total vs rows returned before concluding an asset does not exist — absence from page 1 is NOT absence (this produced two wrong conclusions and a false bug report on 2026-08-07). Filter server-side with path_prefix/search instead of grepping one page. ★ Each row carries 17 columns. Pass _fields:["id","file_path","file_size_bytes"] when you only need to find a file or spot a heavy image - the pagination envelope survives regardless.

tools.name: assets_migrate_to_public
tools.description: Move a WEBSITE PROJECT's legacy root-level images/ and videos/ paths into public/images/ and public/videos/. Updates DB + copies S3 objects. Idempotent. (Website project files only — the marketing Media Library has no path concept.)

tools.name: assets_upload
tools.description: Upload a binary asset (image, video, font, etc.) into a WEBSITE PROJECT's S3-backed asset store — the same path /api/builder/visual-editor/upload-image writes to from the dashboard. These are website project files on S3 — NOT the marketing Media Library (media_assets); for social-post/design media use the marketing_media_* tools instead. Use this instead of project_file_save({encoding:"base64"}) when you have an actual asset (e.g. an image to ship to production). project_file_save puts bytes in builder_code_versions (works for the live Fly preview but bloats checkpoints and doesn't flow through the production assets pipeline). assets_upload writes to S3 + builder_project_assets, so the file shows up in assets_list, survives properly through deploys, and is served via the CDN. Allowed MIME types: image/*, video/*, audio/*, font/*, application/octet-stream. Reject application/* (code) — use project_file_save for source code. SVG EXCEPTION: do NOT upload SVGs here if they are imported by components (`import Logo from "./logo.svg"`) — the S3 asset lane breaks that import. Save those with project_file_save (encoding utf-8), which keeps them in the code lane. Uploading an SVG here is fine ONLY for a plain public/ file referenced by URL. Either way, script/handler content in an SVG is stripped for safety. Path convention: pass file_path like "public/images/hero.jpg" (relative to the project root). Paths that do NOT start with "public/" are also mirrored at "public/<file_path>" in S3 so SSR containers can serve them from /app/public/. Hard cap: 25MB after base64 decode. For larger assets, use the dashboard or split into smaller pieces. Companion path: stock_photos_download already handles the full upload flow for stock-library URLs; use this tool when you have raw bytes (decoded image, screenshot, etc.).

tools.name: audit_query
tools.description: Query this account's MCP audit log. Every MCP tool call writes a row here with the api_key_preview (last 10 chars), tool name, sanitized args summary, status (success/error/rate_limited), duration, IP, and user agent. Use this to investigate destructive actions, debug agent behavior, or audit which key did what. Filters compose with AND. Examples: `{tool_name: "project_file_delete"}` — every delete on this account. `{tool_contains: "delete", since: "2026-05-14T00:00:00Z"}` — every destructive tool since a date. `{args_contains: "Footer", status: "success"}` — who successfully touched anything matching "Footer" in args.

tools.name: avatar_create
tools.description: DEPRECATED thin alias for customer_avatar_create - PREFER THAT ONE. Same route, but this tool declares only a handful of fields, so an avatar created here is sparse and needs a second call to fill in. It used to declare `demographics`, `psychographics` and `goals`: there is no demographics and no psychographics column in the schema at all, and the goals column is `primary_goals`, so all three were accepted, forwarded, ignored by the route, and returned 201 - a create that reported success while silently discarding most of what it was given. They are gone; use customer_avatar_create for the full 30-field ICP shape, including the canonical buying_behavior and online_behavior objects the dashboard renders.

tools.name: before_after_grid_create
tools.description: Create a before/after grid (transformation showcase). Accepts fields flat OR inside `grid_data`. Fields: name (required), description, grid_items (array of {before, after} objects), transformation_story, key_benefits (string[]), measurable_results (string[]), target_avatar_id (link to customer_avatars row), audience_context, transformation_story_before_image_url, transformation_story_after_image_url, metadata, is_active. **Canonical grid_items shape** (the dashboard UI renders these keys; common synonyms are normalized server-side): { before: { title: string, // 'Before' card heading description: string, pain_points: string[], // bullet list under Before images?: [{id, url, prompt}] }, after: { title: string, // 'After' card heading description: string, benefits: string[], // bullet list under After images?: [{id, url, prompt}] }, transformation_details: string // free-text block below the pair } Server-side synonym handling: - top-level `label: "X"` → fills both `before.title` and `after.title` - flat `before: "text"` / `after: "text"` → wraps as `{description: "text"}` - top-level `transformation` / `transformation_story` → `transformation_details` Unknown keys are preserved but not rendered.

tools.name: before_after_grid_delete
tools.description: Delete a before/after grid. Accepts `id` or `grid_id`.

tools.name: before_after_grid_get
tools.description: Fetch one before/after grid. Accepts `id` or `grid_id`.

tools.name: before_after_grid_link_to_avatar
tools.description: Link a before/after grid to a customer_avatar by setting target_avatar_id. Convenience wrapper around before_after_grid_update — uses the grid's target_avatar_id column, the canonical relationship for 'this transformation story is for THIS persona.' Pass null to unlink. The avatar must belong to the same account; bad UUIDs return 400.

tools.name: before_after_grid_list
tools.description: List before/after grids (transformation showcases). Filter with `search` (name), `is_active`, or `target_avatar_id` to get just the grids built for one persona. Rows carry the full grid_items blob including every image URL and image prompt, so a page of 20 is heavy - shape the call with _fields, or take ids here and read one with before_after_grid_get.

tools.name: before_after_grid_populate
tools.description: LLM-enrich a sparse before_after_grid with GROUNDED context. Same contract as entity_populate with entity_type='grid' hardcoded. Enriches: transformation_story, key_benefits[], measurable_results[], audience_context, grid_items[] with each item {before:{title, description, pain_points[]}, after:{title, description, benefits[]}, transformation_details}. Flips populate_status to 'populated' on success.

tools.name: before_after_grid_update
tools.description: Update a before/after grid. Accepts `id` or `grid_id`. Fields flat or inside `grid_data`; flat takes precedence. Only the fields you send change. WRITING `grid_items` REPLACES THE WHOLE BLOB — re-send each item’s existing `before.images[]` and `after.images[]` or the generated imagery is lost. Read the grid first and send the full array back with your one change.

tools.name: before_after_grid_version_create
tools.description: Snapshot a before/after grid's CURRENT PERSISTED row into version history. Returns 201 {data: version} with the allocated version_number (previous max + 1) and the captured grid_data. The snapshot is read from the database, never from this call's body: change_message is the ONLY field the handler reads, so name, grid_items, grid_data or anything else sent here is accepted at 201 and silently dropped, and unsaved edits are NOT captured. Save with before_after_grid_update first, then snapshot. Usually you do not need this tool at all: before_after_grid_update already writes an 'Auto-snapshot before update' version of the pre-edit row whenever a substantive field changes, so calling this first just adds a duplicate history entry; use it for a deliberately labelled checkpoint. The stored version `name` is copied off the grid row, so renaming the grid renames what later snapshots record. Concurrent snapshots contend on the [grid_id, version_number] unique; the handler retries 5 times and then returns 503 'Failed to allocate version_number after retries', which is retryable rather than a bad request.

tools.name: before_after_grid_version_get
tools.description: Fetch one grid snapshot in full, including the grid_data blob that makes paging the list view expensive. Returns {data: {id, grid_id, version_number, name, grid_data, change_message, created_by, created_at}}. version_id is the snapshot ROW UUID from before_after_grid_version_list, NOT the integer version_number: passing 3 does not 404, it fails the uuid cast on the id column and comes back as a 500 'Failed to get grid version'. A real UUID belonging to a different grid does 404 'Version not found', because the lookup is scoped by grid_id. grid_data is the whole grid row as it stood, including the id, account_id, created_at and updated_at of that moment plus operational columns like populate_status and lock_version; a restore strips exactly those first four and writes every other key back, so read this first to see precisely what before_after_grid_version_restore would overwrite.

tools.name: before_after_grid_version_list
tools.description: List saved snapshots of one before/after grid, newest version_number first. Returns {data: [{id, grid_id, version_number, name, grid_data, change_message, created_by, created_at}], pagination: {page, limit, total, total_pages}}. Every row carries the FULL grid_data blob (no column selection), so a page of 20 is a heavy payload: take ids here and pull detail with before_after_grid_version_get. Traps: limit defaults to 20 and is silently clamped to 50, so asking for 200 returns 50 with no error, and page is floored to 1. The row's `id` (a UUID) is what version_get and version_restore take, NOT version_number. created_by is nullable and no route on this surface ever writes it, so it is always null: a snapshot cannot tell you who took it. Most rows here are automatic; before_after_grid_update snapshots the pre-edit row by itself on any substantive change unless it was called with snapshot false. A grid_id from another account returns 404 'Before/after grid not found', not 403; a grid_id that is not a UUID at all fails the uuid cast and comes back 500.

tools.name: before_after_grid_version_restore
tools.description: OVERWRITES the live before/after grid with a snapshot. Every key stored in that version's grid_data except id, account_id, created_at and updated_at is written straight back onto the row, so grid_items, transformation_story, key_benefits, target_avatar_id and any edit made since that snapshot are replaced, and operational columns captured in the blob (is_active, metadata, populate_status, populate_error, populated_at, lock_version) are rewound with them. There is NO confirm parameter and no body is parsed: the first call performs the restore. It is normally recoverable because the handler auto-snapshots the current state first and returns {data: restored grid, restored_from_version, auto_snapshot_version}, and restoring auto_snapshot_version undoes it. THE TRAP: if that auto-snapshot loses the version_number race 5 times it is abandoned and the restore proceeds ANYWAY, while auto_snapshot_version still reports the number it was trying to use; a returned number is not evidence the backup row exists, so confirm it with before_after_grid_version_list before treating it as your undo. Columns added to the grid after the snapshot was taken have no key in grid_data and keep their current values rather than being cleared. version_id is the snapshot ROW UUID; a version_number passed here fails the uuid cast and returns 500, not 404.

tools.name: brand_guide_create
tools.description: Create a new brand guide. REQUIRED: name + color_primary. Accepts ~100 fields flat OR inside `brand_guide_data` wrapper. Color fields are validated as `#rgb`/`#rrggbb`/`#rrggbbaa` — bad formats return a 400 naming the field instead of an opaque 500. 5xx responses now surface the underlying Prisma error code + column. populate_status is server-managed — currently always 'pending' (placeholder for future async enrichment).

tools.name: brand_guide_delete
tools.description: Soft-delete a brand guide (flips is_active=false). The row stays in the DB so it can be restored via brand_guide_update with is_active=true, or hard-deleted via brand_guide_purge once you confirm it should be gone for good. Accepts `id` or `guide_id`.

tools.name: brand_guide_font_create
tools.description: Register a self-hosted custom font on a brand guide. font_family and display_name are required and are trimmed; either one blank gives 400 'font_family and display_name are required'. Returns 201 {data: font}. THE SILENT FAILURE: only css_font_face is ever rendered. The generated brand stylesheet copies css_font_face verbatim and ignores file_woff2_url / file_woff_url / file_ttf_url / file_otf_url completely, so a row created from file URLs alone registers a font that no page can load, and the route still stamps upload_status='ready' whether or not any file URL was supplied (upload_status is hardcoded server-side and cannot be set here). weight goes through Number(), so a non-numeric string such as "bold" becomes NaN and the create 500s; omit it to take the 400 default. is_variable goes through Boolean(), so the string "false" stores true. A duplicate (font_family, weight, style) on the same guide returns 409, including against a soft-deleted tombstone. Columns not listed here (stretch, unicode_range, file_eot_url, font_feature_settings, font_variation_settings, file_size_bytes, file_checksum, is_active, upload_error) cannot be set on this route and are dropped without comment.

tools.name: brand_guide_font_delete
tools.description: SOFT-delete a custom font: flips is_active=false and returns {success: true}. The row survives, which has two consequences worth knowing BEFORE calling. First, it is one-way from here: no route on this surface accepts is_active, so brand_guide_font_update cannot bring the font back, and the brand UI's own font update only touches display_name, unicode_range and font_feature_settings. Second, the tombstone keeps the (brand_id, font_family, weight, style) unique slot forever, so re-registering that identical font answers 409 'Font with this family/weight/style already exists' while brand_guide_font_list shows nothing; the only way back is to register the family under a different weight or style. Effect on output: the font drops out of the guide's font list and out of the generated brand CSS (both read custom_fonts with is_active=true), but any stylesheet already deployed with that @font-face inlined keeps serving. Deleting a font a live page references is how that page silently falls back to the default sans. Account- and guide-scoped: a mismatch is 404 'Font not found'. The route supports no confirm field, so confirm with the human first.

tools.name: brand_guide_font_get
tools.description: Fetch one registered custom font by id. Returns {data: font} with the whole brand_custom_fonts row (font_family, display_name, weight, style, the four file URLs, css_font_face, is_variable, variable_axes, original_filename, upload_status, is_active, timestamps). Unlike brand_guide_font_list this does NOT filter is_active, so it is the only read on this surface that can see a soft-deleted font: use it to explain why brand_guide_font_create keeps answering 409 for a family/weight/style the list claims does not exist. The font must sit on the given guide AND the calling account; a mismatch on either is a flat 404 'Font not found' with no hint which id was wrong.

tools.name: brand_guide_font_list
tools.description: List the self-hosted custom fonts registered on one brand guide. Returns {data: brand_custom_fonts[], total}, ordered by font_family then weight, each row carrying the whole record (the four file_* URLs, css_font_face, upload_status, variable_axes, original_filename, timestamps). THE TRAP: this list silently filters is_active=true. A font soft-deleted by brand_guide_font_delete vanishes from here but keeps its (brand_id, font_family, weight, style) unique slot, so re-registering that exact family/weight/style still answers 409 while this list shows an empty shelf; brand_guide_font_get by id is the only way to see the tombstone.
