Takes no search, filter or pagination params: the handler reads no query string at all. A guideId belonging to another account returns 404 'Brand guide not found', not an empty list.

tools.name: brand_guide_font_update
tools.description: Update a registered custom font. Returns {data: font} with the saved row. Only keys actually present in the body are touched, and passing null clears a URL slot. THE SILENT DROP: the handler whitelists display_name, the four file URLs, css_font_face, is_variable, variable_axes and upload_status, and nothing else. font_family, weight and style are NOT accepted, so a rename or a weight change returns 200 having changed only updated_at; the identity can only be changed by a fresh brand_guide_font_create, and the old row goes on holding the (brand_id, font_family, weight, style) unique slot. is_active is not accepted either, so this cannot revive a font that brand_guide_font_delete soft-deleted. A body of purely non-whitelisted keys is a 200 that did nothing. upload_status is written as a free string with no enum check, so a typo persists, and the column is VarChar(20): anything longer 500s. Setting css_font_face is what actually makes the font load; changing file URLs alone leaves the generated brand CSS byte-for-byte as it was.

tools.name: brand_guide_get
tools.description: Get a single brand guide with its full configuration and fonts. Accepts `id` or `guide_id`.

tools.name: brand_guide_list
tools.description: List brand guides with search and active/default filters

tools.name: brand_guide_purge
tools.description: Hard-delete a brand guide that's ALREADY been soft-deleted (is_active=false). Cleanup tool for agent churn — `brand_guide_delete` only flips is_active, so soft-deleted rows accumulate and show up as inflated counts on the marketing dashboard. Use brand_guide_list with is_active="false" to find tombstones, then call this on each. Safety: refuses with 409 + code='still_active' if the guide is still active — must soft-delete first. Refuses with 409 + code='fk_constraint' if other rows reference the guide (typically custom_fonts) — caller must clear dependents first. Account-scoped; cross-account guides return 404.

tools.name: brand_guide_set_logo
tools.description: Set or update the logo URLs on a brand guide. Convenience wrapper around brand_guide_update that names the fields explicitly so the agent doesn't have to know the column names. Updates only the fields supplied — pass `null` (not omitted) to clear a slot. The URLs must be http(s) and should point to assets already in the media library (register via media_library_register_external_url first if you've got an external URL). Supported slots: logo_primary_url (the main logo), logo_secondary_url (alternate/horizontal), logo_wordmark_url (text-only), logo_icon_url (favicon/icon-only), logo_dark_url (for use on light backgrounds), logo_light_url (for use on dark backgrounds).

tools.name: brand_guide_update
tools.description: Update a brand guide. Accepts `id` or `guide_id`. Fields flat or inside `brand_guide_data`/`brand_data`. Color fields (color_primary, color_secondary, etc.) are validated as `#rgb`/`#rrggbb`/`#rrggbbaa` — bad formats now return a 400 naming the field instead of an opaque 500. Notable shapes: - `mood_board_images`: array of `{url, prompt?, style?}` objects. Plain url strings (`['https://…/x.png']`) are auto-wrapped, and `image_url` / `file_url` / `src` are accepted as `url` synonyms. The dashboard editor reads `img.url` per item — passing a flat string[] without normalization makes the editor render zero items even though the rows persist. - `cta_primary` / `cta_secondary`: editable VarChar(100) strings. Defaults are "Get Started" / "Learn More". Send the literal CTA text to override. - String[] columns (`brand_personality`, `copy_dos`, `copy_donts`, `ai_brand_adjectives`, `ai_forbidden_phrases`, `ai_preferred_phrases`, `brand_is`, `brand_is_not`): a bare string is auto-wrapped into a one-element array.

tools.name: brand_guide_voiceovers_get
tools.description: Read the account's APPROVED NARRATION VOICES before setting storyboard.voice.voice_id. Returns {brand_id, brand_name, approved_voices: [{key, provider, voice_id, label, usage_notes, approved_at, approved_by}], default_voice, guidance}: read usage_notes ('warm, use for testimonials') and send the matching voice_id rather than guessing a friendly name, which is the guess that produced a provider 400 retried every 32 seconds for an hour at 5%. Read-only by design: there is no Olympus write route, because approving a narrator is a human brand decision made in the brand UI, so an agent may choose from this set but can never widen it. TRAPS: the parser never throws and DROPS any stored entry whose provider is unknown or whose voice_id is not a syntactically valid id for that provider (Cartesia ids are UUIDs, so a friendly name saved by hand is simply absent here rather than reported), and it caps the list at 12, so this can be shorter than what a human sees in the UI. default_voice falls back to the FIRST approved voice whenever default_voice_key is missing or dangling, so a non-null default_voice is not evidence that anyone chose one. An empty approved_voices means nobody is approved: OMIT voice_id entirely and let the platform default apply, never invent one. With no brand_id the route picks the account's active guide (is_default first, then most recently updated); with brand_id it does NOT check is_active, so a soft-deleted guide still answers. No guide at all returns 404 with code 'no_brand_guide'.

tools.name: business_data_business_listings_search
tools.description: Business Listings Search API provides results containing information about business entities listed on Google Maps in the specified categories. You will receive the address, contacts, rating, working hours, and other relevant data

tools.name: calendar_create_event
tools.description: Create a Google Calendar event. Set conference=true to auto-generate a Google Meet link. send_updates="all" emails attendees on create.

tools.name: calendar_free_slots
tools.description: Suggest open booking slots within a window. Walks the window in duration_minutes increments, dropping any candidate that overlaps a busy interval, falls outside business hours, or lands on a weekend (when weekdays_only=true).

tools.name: calendar_get_event
tools.description: Fetch a single Google Calendar event by ID.

tools.name: calendar_list_events
tools.description: List Google Calendar events in a window with optional free-text search.

tools.name: checkpoint_create
tools.description: Snapshot the project NOW — captures every current file, every asset, and (when configured) a database backup. Returns a checkpoint_hash you can pass to checkpoint_restore later. ★ An explicit call is a MANUAL checkpoint: your description and tags are always stored (it no longer silently deduped into an earlier automatic checkpoint and discarded your label). Use BEFORE risky bulk edits, refactors, or template extractions so you have a one-call rollback. Requires builder_project_settings (i.e., a fully initialized builder project).

tools.name: checkpoint_delete
tools.description: Permanently delete a checkpoint. Irreversible. The project itself and current files are NOT touched.

tools.name: checkpoint_get
tools.description: Read a single checkpoint's full metadata (files manifest, asset manifest, db backup info, sizes, timestamps). Use this to inspect a checkpoint BEFORE restoring it.

tools.name: checkpoint_list
tools.description: List checkpoints for a project, newest first. Each entry: {checkpoint_hash, description, trigger (manual|deployment|scheduled|ai), files_count, assets_count, total_size, created_at}. Filter by trigger to e.g. see only AI-created snapshots.

tools.name: checkpoint_restore
tools.description: Restore the project to a checkpoint. Files in the snapshot revert to their snapshot content and assets are re-attached. ADDITIVE: files created AFTER the checkpoint are KEPT, not deleted — the project becomes a union of the two states, not an exact copy of the checkpoint. The database is NOT restored by this tool. Uncommitted changes to any file that IS in the snapshot are overwritten, so call checkpoint_create FIRST to make the operation reversible.

tools.name: cms_activity
tools.description: Project-wide CMS audit log. Returns newest-first events across every collection + the manifest, with attribution: `author` (signed-in user, or the agent's label for agent writes) and `actor` { kind: user|dashboard_agent|mcp_key|system, id, label } on every attributed write. collectionId is the MANIFEST collection id (plus collectionPath, slug, isDraft, locale). Use for "who changed this page?" / "what did the agent touch last week?" questions. Filter by action=create|update|delete — applied in the query before the limit, so old deletes are found; default returns all.

tools.name: cms_add_field
tools.description: Add a single field to an existing collection atomically (under the manifest write-lock). The body is the full CmsField object — { name, type, required?, label?, validation?, ... }. Call cms_field_types to see the required extras for each type (e.g. select needs `options`, array needs `items`).

tools.name: cms_ai_rewrite
tools.description: One-shot markdown rewrite helper. Sends prompt + current content to the builder's OpenRouter key and returns rewritten markdown. Non-streaming, single round-trip. Best for thin orchestrator agents without their own LLM access; agents that already have a model should call that directly to keep usage on their own billing.

tools.name: cms_asset_references
tools.description: Find every CMS entry that references a given asset (image / font / pdf / etc.). Accepts either a relative site path (/images/foo.jpg) or an absolute S3 URL — both match. Use as a preflight before renaming or deleting an asset so the agent can repoint or warn first.

tools.name: cms_attach_image
tools.description: One-shot: upload an image AND bind it to an image-typed field on a CMS entry. Saves a round trip vs (assets_upload → cms_write_entry). Two modes: • Upload + bind: pass `content` (base64) and optional `mime_type` + `file_path`. file_path defaults to "public/images/<slug>-<field>.<ext>". • Bind existing asset: pass `asset_path` instead of content. Validates that the target field exists on the collection AND has type=image or type=file before doing any work. Draft-aware bind: if a draft shadow exists the image lands on the DRAFT (all other fields preserved); else the live entry updates in place; else a fresh draft is created with just the image field set (useful when authoring fresh entries).

tools.name: cms_back_references
tools.description: List every entry across the manifest whose reference / multi-reference fields point at the given entry. Use as a PREFLIGHT before cms_delete_entry so the agent can offer to repoint or warn the user — deleting a referenced entry leaves dangling slugs that downstream renderers will hide. Returns { references: [{ collection_id, slug, field }] }.

tools.name: cms_bulk_delete
tools.description: Delete many entries from a collection in ONE call — the ONLY correct way to purge entries at scale (e.g. after cms_delete_collection). NEVER loop or parallelize cms_delete_entry for a wipe: a parallel per-entry fanout starves the builder's DB pool and expires its write locks (2026-08-20 incident). Deletes each slug's live file AND its draft shadow sequentially server-side, cancels pending schedules, and fires delete webhooks for live entries. Per-slug outcomes in the response: 'deleted' (with draftAlsoDeleted + orphaned_referrers[]) / 'not_found' (already gone — treat as success; retries are idempotent) / 'blocked' (other entries reference it through a REQUIRED field — referrers[] names them; referrers inside this same batch do not count) / 'error'. Pass force=true to delete blocked slugs anyway. Up to 500 slugs per call.

tools.name: cms_bulk_import
tools.description: Batch-create entries in a collection. Each entry: { slug?, fields }. Slugs are derived from the collection's slug_from if omitted. Each entry validates + saves through the normal pipeline (Prisma + Fly sync + GitHub auto-commit); per-entry failures don't block the rest — the response carries an outcome array. on_conflict controls slug-collision behavior: 'skip' (default) leaves existing entries alone, 'overwrite' creates a new version on top. Tops out at 60s for huge imports — split if needed. The parameter is `entries` (not items). PUBLISH STATE: an entry with no status signal lands as DRAFT and is hidden by the site's isLive filter and by cms_list_entries({status:'published'}); pass top-level status:'published' (applied to every entry that carries none of its own) or set fields.status per entry. Every entry passes the same live-write gate as cms_write_entry (defaults, select membership, reference existence — slugs in the same batch count as existing).

tools.name: cms_cascade_duplicate
tools.description: Clone a source entry into N siblings of any ancestor level. Canonical use case: "create one service page per city" — sourceCollectionId=services, sourceSlug=hvac-repair, axisCollectionId=cities, targetAxisSlugs=[austin,dallas,houston]. Pair with cms_list_collections first to discover collection ids. Pass dry_run=true to preview the create plan before writing. PRECONDITION: the axis must be an ANCESTOR of the source — a reference field on the source pointing at the axis collection (exactly one such field is inferred as the parent; otherwise declare it with cms_update_collection({ hierarchy: { parentField } })). When it is not, the call returns 422 { code: axis_not_ancestor | ambiguous_parent_field | axis_collection_missing, chain, fix } naming the exact manifest change — it no longer returns an empty plan.

tools.name: cms_cascade_reparent
tools.description: Move N entries under a new parent (single-level reparent). Each entry's hierarchy.parentField reference is rewritten to point at the new parent slug. If the collection has a routePattern reading the parent chain, projected URLs change — the response carries the old→new pairs for review. Pass dry_run=true first to inspect the plan before committing. URL redirects (301/302) are a hosting concern and NOT written here. A collection with no resolvable parent field comes back as 'no-hierarchy' skips — declare one with cms_update_collection({ hierarchy: { parentField } }).

tools.name: cms_create_collection
tools.description: Create a new CMS collection atomically. Safer than cms_update_manifest (which replaces the whole manifest and has race conditions on concurrent edits). Body is the full CmsCollection — { id, name, path, format, slugFrom: "filename", fields: [...] }. Call cms_field_types first to see what field shapes are valid.

tools.name: cms_delete_collection
tools.description: Remove a collection from the manifest atomically. Entry content files are LEFT IN PLACE (no destructive content delete) — use cms_bulk_delete (ONE call with all slugs) if you also want to purge them. NEVER loop cms_delete_entry per slug for a purge: parallel per-entry deletes starve the builder DB pool and expire its write locks.

tools.name: cms_delete_entry
tools.description: Delete a CMS entry by slug. Removes the live file AND its draft shadow (reports draftAlsoDeleted). REFUSES with 409 when other entries reference this one through a REQUIRED field — the response lists them (referrers[] with collection, slug, field, required); repoint them first (cms_back_references / cms_write_entry / cms_bulk_patch) or pass force=true to delete anyway and leave them dangling. Optional referrers never block but are returned as orphaned_referrers[] with a warning, so nothing is orphaned silently. For many slugs use cms_bulk_delete.

tools.name: cms_field_types
tools.description: Static catalog of every CMS field type the manifest validator accepts (string, markdown, html, number, boolean, date, image, file, url, color, select, array, object, reference — 14 types; html carries raw markup such as JSON-LD scripts verbatim) plus the validation keys and extras each type understands. Read this BEFORE authoring collection schemas via cms_create_collection / cms_add_field so the manifest validates on the first write.

tools.name: cms_list_collections
tools.description: Lightweight list of a project's CMS collections — id, name, format (mdx|json), path, slug_from, field_count, route_pattern, default_sort, group, hierarchy ({ parentField } when a parent link is declared, else null). No full field arrays; call cms_read_manifest for those.

tools.name: cms_list_entries
tools.description: List entries in a CMS collection (paginated server-side). Each entry carries derivedStatus and, when the collection has a routePattern, resolvedPath — the entry's projected URL with {slug} / {field:x} / {ref:a.b} placeholders filled (Express-style ':slug' patterns are normalised too). Entries with no status signal derive as draft.

tools.name: cms_list_entry_versions
tools.description: Return the full version history for a single CMS entry. Each PUT creates a new builder_code_versions row; this lists them as { versions: [{ id, versionNumber, createdAt, commitMessage, fileSize, isCurrent, isDelete, author: { kind, id, name, email }, actor: { kind, id, label } | null }] } (author is null only on rows written before attribution existed). File content is intentionally omitted — pick a version id and call cms_restore_entry_version to materialise it as the new live content.

tools.name: cms_preview_write
tools.description: Push a CMS file to the Fly preview WITHOUT writing to the database or queuing a GitHub commit. Use for "show the user what this would look like" patterns — the preview iframe updates but no version row is created. The real save still goes through cms_write_entry. How it stays out of the database: the container's file watcher reverse-syncs on-disk changes, and this route records a preview-only marker so the echo of exactly these bytes is dropped — no version row, live entry unchanged (before 2026-08-30 the echo came back as a 'Container reverse sync' version and the entry showed as published). A DIFFERENT edit made inside the container still persists. The pushed content lasts until the next real write of that path or a preview restart.

tools.name: cms_promote_draft
tools.description: Publish an entry's draft. Copies the draft shadow file over the live entry, deletes the draft, fires save webhooks. Use after a draft has been written (cms_write_entry with draft:true) + reviewed. Re-validates the draft against the CURRENT schema and scans for dangling references — refuses with 422 if either fails (drafts can sit while the schema evolves). 409 if a concurrent live edit landed since the draft was last saved; pass force=true to overwrite. 404 if no draft exists. For localized collections, set locale to promote a specific variant's draft.

tools.name: cms_read_entry
tools.description: Read one CMS entry by slug. Pass draft:"1" to read the entry's draft shadow (the working copy cms_write_entry creates with draft:true) instead of the live entry.

tools.name: cms_read_manifest
tools.description: Read the project's hiveku.cms.json manifest (collection definitions + field schemas).

tools.name: cms_reader_generate
tools.description: (Re)generate the project's typed CMS reader at lib/cms-server.ts from the CURRENT hiveku.cms.json. Use it when a project HAS a CMS but nothing reads it: cms_scaffold refuses with 409 once a manifest exists, which is exactly when you need the reader. Dependency-free and SERVER-ONLY. Per collection: get<Collection>Entries / Entry / Slugs / Url, plus getEntries, getEntry, resolveReference, getEntryUrl, isLive, getManifest. ★ DO NOT HAND-WRITE A FRONTMATTER PARSER AND DO NOT ADD gray-matter. One already ships inside this generated file, round-trip tested against the writer, including the two-space ` - <json>` block sequence used for array<object> fields. It also skips .draft. shadows and locale variants, applies the isLive filter and resolves references. Idempotent, and rarely needed: the reader is regenerated automatically on every manifest save. Reach for this when lib/cms-server.ts is missing or was deleted. A reader without the generated header is never overwritten (outcome skipped_hand_written) unless you pass overwrite_hand_written:true. Response shape: { path, outcome, dry_run, collections[{id,name}], source_bytes, source?, hint?, note }. outcome is written | unchanged | skipped_hand_written | would_write | would_skip_hand_written. 404 no_cms_manifest when there is no hiveku.cms.json. include_source:true returns the ~15KB of TypeScript; dry_run:true returns it and writes nothing.

tools.name: cms_remove_field
tools.description: Remove a field from a collection atomically. Existing entry files retain the value of the removed field (no destructive content rewriting). Field name is immutable — to rename, remove + add.

tools.name: cms_restore_entry_version
tools.description: Restore a historical entry version by writing its content as a NEW version on top of the current one — the restore is itself visible in history, never a destructive rewind. Triggers the standard Fly sync + GitHub auto-commit. Pair with cms_list_entry_versions to find a version_id.

tools.name: cms_scaffold
tools.description: Seed a project that has NO CMS yet: writes hiveku.cms.json with a starter blog collection, content/blog/hello-world.mdx, and a GENERATED typed reader at lib/cms-server.ts (get<Collection>Entries / get<Collection>Entry / get<Collection>Slugs / get<Collection>Url, resolveReference, isLive filtering, draft-shadow skipping — dependency-free, server-only). Takes ONLY project_id: the starter collection is always a blog, so there is nothing to name. Returns 409 if a manifest already exists — that is also exactly when you want the reader, so use cms_reader_generate for lib/cms-server.ts and cms_create_collection to add real collections; the reader is regenerated on every manifest save, so it always has helpers for every collection. Pages read content ONLY through '@/lib/cms-server'; never hand-roll fs/frontmatter code or add gray-matter.

tools.name: cms_search_entries
tools.description: Full-text search across every CMS collection in a project. Scans every string-valued field on every entry for the query (case-insensitive) and returns matches with collection_id, slug, field_name, and snippet context. Not indexed — fine for projects up to a few thousand entries; switch to FTS at Wikipedia scale.

tools.name: cms_update_collection
tools.description: Update collection-level metadata without touching fields or entries: name, routePattern, defaultSort, group, and hierarchy ({ parentField: <reference field name> } to DECLARE the parent link cms_cascade_duplicate / cms_cascade_reparent walk; null to clear). Fields change via cms_add_field / cms_update_field / cms_remove_field.

tools.name: cms_update_field
tools.description: Patch a field's attributes (label, required, help, default, validation, options, etc.). The `name` is immutable — to rename, remove + add. Changing `type` is allowed but DANGEROUS: existing entries' values may no longer validate.

tools.name: cms_update_manifest
tools.description: Replace the CMS manifest with a new shape (validated server-side).

tools.name: cms_write_entry
tools.description: Upsert a CMS entry by slug. Pass the entry payload as `fields` (canonical) or `data` (alias). Field types must match the collection schema (see cms_field_types / cms_list_collections). `draft: true` writes the entry's DRAFT SHADOW file instead of the live entry — the working copy cms_promote_draft later publishes; draft writes skip validation so partial payloads are fine. Optional top-level `status` (draft/published/scheduled) and `publish_at` (ISO timestamp) are merged into the entry as fields named `status` and `publishAt`; `status` is a plain field the site reads, NOT what makes something a draft — use `draft: true` for that. `publish_at` alone only date-gates rendering; a real scheduled flip needs the schedule endpoint's cron. LIVE writes pass one gate: declared field defaults are applied, values coerced, then required/min/max/length, SELECT MEMBERSHIP (a value outside the declared options is a 422 unless it is the value already stored) and REFERENCE EXISTENCE (a reference or array<reference> slug — top level or nested in object/array<object> — that does not exist as a live entry is a 422 with dangling[]). Drafts skip the gate and meet it on cms_promote_draft.

tools.name: complete_task
tools.description: Mark a task as completed (status=done, completed_at=now, progress_percentage=100). Optional `summary` adds an audit comment on the task.

tools.name: components_add
tools.description: Inject one or more universal components into an existing project. Resolves the full dependency closure automatically — picking a section pulls in the section file, every helper component it imports, the matching client-island bundles, and (when update_package_json is true) adds any missing external npm deps to package.json. Use this instead of project_file_save + manual import bookkeeping when adding a section from the universal catalog. Two ways to specify what to add: • `components: ["HeroEditorial", "PricingToggle"]` — by component name from components_list. • `files: ["components/sections/footer/centered-footer.tsx"]` — by explicit starter file path. Both can be combined in one call. Defaults are safe: `mode: "missing-only"` (won't overwrite existing project files), `dry_run: false`. Always run with `dry_run: true` first on a project you don't want to surprise — the response shows files_to_write + skipped so you can verify before committing. Caps: 16 components, 40 explicit files per call. Splits required for larger adds. Only available on Next.js / internal projects (returns 400 with code="unsupported_project_type" otherwise).

tools.name: components_list
tools.description: Browse the universal section/component catalog — the same registry the designer-mode UI uses. ~220 sections covering hero, pricing, proof, content, CMS, contact, navigation, footer, and category-specific bundles (climate-tech, product-ai, playful-wellness, etc.). The catalog is read from docker/starter-template/components/sections/registry.json at request time, so adding a section to the starter + redeploy makes it instantly browsable here. Each entry: `{component, file, category, styles, intents, best_for}`. Pass `component` strings to `components_add` to inject a section + its dependency closure into a project. Filters compose with AND: category (exact), intent / style (substring against the array), search (substring against name + best_for + file path), template_id (narrows to a template overlay). With no filters the response is paginated 100 at a time — use `facets.categories` from the response to pick a focused subset before iterating.

tools.name: connections_status
tools.description: One-shot integration inventory for the account — SEO (GSC/GBP/Bing), PPC/Ads (Google/Meta/Amazon/Bing/TikTok), email, cold-email, and LLM connections in a single call, each row carrying connection_status / is_active / last_synced_at. Use this FIRST before any Paid Ads / SEO / email work to see what's connected and what's dead, instead of calling the per-department list tools one by one. NOTE: SOCIAL accounts (Meta/IG, LinkedIn, X, TikTok, GBP posting) are NOT included — check those with social_list_accounts. When something the work needs is missing or dead, hand the user the connect link: Google products can be minted via integration_oauth_initiate (returns setup_url); social and Meta/Amazon Ads connect in the dashboard at /<accountId>/dashboard/marketing/social/accounts or /marketing/ppc.

tools.name: content_analysis_phrase_trends
tools.description: This endpoint will provide you with data on all citations of the target keyword for the indicated date range

tools.name: content_analysis_search
tools.description: This endpoint will provide you with detailed citation data available for the target keyword

tools.name: content_analysis_summary
tools.description: This endpoint will provide you with an overview of citation data available for the target keyword

tools.name: content_analytics_get
tools.description: Per-day performance rows for ONE content item. Returns {data:[content_analytics rows: id, content_item_id, account_id, date, views, unique_views, likes, shares, comments, time_on_page, bounce_rate, external_analytics, created_at], content_summary:{id, title, total_views, total_likes, total_shares}, pagination:{page, limit, total, total_pages}}, newest date first. bounce_rate is converted from Decimal to a plain number (null stays null); every other column comes back raw. SILENT FAILURE, read this before you report a zero: nothing in the app writes content_analytics, and content_items.view_count / like_count / share_count are never incremented by any code path, so for effectively every item this returns 200 with data:[] and a content_summary of all zeros. That is a missing collector, not a dead post. Real page performance lives in the tracking and analytics surface; only rows imported from outside (external_analytics) ever appear here. from_date / to_date are passed straight to new Date() with no validation: an unparseable value becomes Invalid Date, the Prisma date filter throws, and you get a generic 500 instead of a 400 naming the field. Use ISO dates. page and limit go through parseInt, so a non-numeric value becomes NaN and also 500s; a numeric limit is clamped to 1..100 (default 30) and page floors at 1. An unknown or cross-account content_id is a flat 404.

tools.name: content_categories_list
tools.description: Lists this account's content categories, each carrying content_count (content_items filed directly under it) and child_category_count, ordered by sort_order ascending, wrapped as {data, pagination:{page,limit,total,total_pages}}. Traps: parent_id takes the LITERAL string 'none' to mean top-level only; any other value is used as a parent UUID, and a well-formed UUID that matches nothing returns an empty page with a 200 rather than an error, while a value that is not a UUID at all fails the Prisma cast and comes back as a generic 500. is_active is compared as a string, so it must be exactly 'true' or 'false'; any other value is silently ignored rather than rejected and inactive categories come back mixed in. limit defaults to 50 and is hard-capped at 100, so a deep taxonomy needs paging. Counts are direct membership only: content filed in child categories is not rolled up, so a parent can read as empty while its subtree holds hundreds of items.

tools.name: content_category_create
tools.description: Creates one content category and returns 201 with the stored row. Traps: slug is NOT an input. The route derives it from name (lowercased, non-alphanumeric runs collapsed to dashes) and de-duplicates it with a -1 or -2 suffix, so a slug you send is dropped without comment; read the returned row to learn the real one. That de-duplication is a check-then-insert with no lock, so two creates of the same name racing each other can settle on the same slug and one loses to the (account_id, slug) unique index as a generic 500. parent_id is neither existence-checked nor account-checked: a UUID matching no row trips the foreign key and surfaces as a 500, while a UUID owned by ANOTHER account is accepted, after which the new category never renders in the builder dashboard, whose tree is built downward from parent_id === null. Coercion here is lossy and differs from content_category_update: sort_order goes through Number(), so a non-numeric string becomes NaN and 500s, and is_active goes through Boolean(), so the STRING 'false' coerces to TRUE. Defaults: sort_order 0, is_active true, every other optional field null.

tools.name: content_category_delete
tools.description: PERMANENTLY deletes one content category. The route supports no confirm field and no soft delete, so when you only want it out of the way call content_category_update with is_active false instead. What it does NOT destroy: child categories are re-parented to null and become top-level rows rather than being deleted, and every content_items row in the category has category_id set to null, so the content itself survives, uncategorised. Both unlinks are irreversible; nothing records the old parent or the old category, so re-creating the category will NOT restore the tree or refile the content, and a re-created category also gets a fresh id, breaking any saved reference. Returns {success:true}, or 404 if the id is not in this account.

tools.name: content_category_get
tools.description: Fetches one category with parent (id, name, slug), children, and content_count, or 404 if the id is not in this account. Traps: the children array is filtered to is_active true and sorted by sort_order, so it is NOT the full child set; call content_categories_list with parent_id set to this id to see deactivated children too. content_count counts direct members only: content filed in child categories is not rolled up, so a parent can read as empty while the subtree holds hundreds of items. The response renames the Prisma relations, so read parent and children, not parent_category and child_categories. Accepts no query params.

tools.name: content_category_update
tools.description: Patches an allow-listed set of fields on one content category and returns the updated row; only keys you actually send are touched, and a 404 means the id is not in this account. Traps: unlike content_category_create this route does NO coercion, so sort_order must be a real number and is_active a real boolean; sending either as a quoted string reaches Prisma raw and comes back as a generic 500 with nothing naming the cause. slug is patchable here but never checked for uniqueness, and (account_id, slug) is a unique index, so colliding with a sibling returns that same opaque 500 instead of a 409. Setting is_active false does NOT hide the category from the builder dashboard, which lists categories with no is_active filter at all; it only affects callers that pass is_active to content_categories_list and the children array of content_category_get. Reparenting is not cycle-checked and not account-checked: pointing parent_id at the row itself or at one of its own descendants still returns 200, after which the row stays readable over the API but disappears from the dashboard tree, which walks downward from parent_id === null.

tools.name: content_comment_create
tools.description: Append one comment to a marketing content item's review thread. Returns {comment:{id, content_item_id, user_name, user_email, comment_text, created_at, status, source}} with HTTP 201. FIRES ONE WORKFLOW EVENT: after the row is written, a content.comment_created trigger fires fire-and-forget (contentCommentCreatedTrigger nodes, filterable by source), so an account with an enabled workflow on that trigger is notified however that workflow says - and an account WITHOUT one is notified of nothing: the comment is then seen only when a human next opens the Collaboration panel on that content item. Do not report that commenting alerted anyone unless such a workflow is known to exist. THE THREAD IS CLIENT-VISIBLE: the row is also shown to anyone holding a live share link for this item, so this is not an internal note. The byline is the fixed literal 'Olympus Agent' and cannot be supplied, and the row is stored with a null author id and null author email on purpose, because a caller-chosen byline on a client-visible thread is an impersonation primitive. comment_text is trimmed then validated: empty or whitespace-only gives 400 'comment_text is required' and over 4000 characters gives 400 'Comment too long (max 4000)'; neither is a 422. status is not an input, every row is created 'open', and this path exposes no edit, resolve or delete verb, so a comment cannot be corrected or withdrawn once written. An unknown or other-tenant content_id answers 404 'Content not found'. Call content_comments_list first to read what has already been said.

tools.name: content_comments_list
tools.description: Read the whole review thread on one marketing content item, oldest first. Returns {comments:[{id, content_item_id, user_name, user_email, comment_text, created_at (ISO), status, source}]}. user_email is OMITTED from the object entirely (not null) when the author had no email, so read it defensively. source is derived ONLY from share_link_id: 'share-link' for a public reviewer, 'in-app' for everything else, so a comment written by an API key serializes as 'in-app' exactly like a human team member's, and user_name is the only signal that no person wrote it. THE THREAD IS CLIENT-VISIBLE: the same rows are shown to anyone holding a live share link for this item, so it is not an internal note surface. There is no pagination, filter or sort control, so a long thread returns in full every time. An unknown contentId and another account's contentId both answer 404 'Content not found', deliberately indistinguishable. status is whatever is stored (every row is created 'open'); nothing on this path can change it. Read-only and costs nothing.

tools.name: content_comments_recent
tools.description: Recent comments across ALL of this account's marketing content items, newest first - the cross-item digest read ('what feedback landed since I last looked'), where content_comments_list is the one-item thread read (oldest first). Returns {comments:[{id, content_item_id, user_name, user_email, comment_text, created_at (ISO), status, source, content_item:{id, title, content_type}}], pagination:{page, limit, total, total_pages}}. Each comment carries its joined content_item so a digest can say WHICH draft got the comment. user_email is OMITTED from the object entirely (not null) when absent, so read it defensively. source is derived ONLY from share_link_id: 'share-link' = a public share-link reviewer (the client-feedback path), 'in-app' = a team member OR an API-key agent - user_name is the only signal which. THE THREAD IS CLIENT-VISIBLE: these same rows render to anyone holding a live share link on the item, so nothing here is an internal note. `since` filters created_at with a STRICT greater-than, so passing the created_at of the last comment you processed will not return it again; an unparseable since is 400, never silently ignored. source outside 'share-link'/'in-app' is 400; a non-uuid content_item_id is 400; an other-tenant or unknown content_item_id simply matches zero rows and answers 200 with an empty comments array, NOT a 404. status matches exactly (every row is created 'open' and no comment path exposes a resolve verb, so other values only exist if something else wrote them). limit defaults 50 and caps at 200; page is 1-based. Read-only and costs nothing.

tools.name: content_create
tools.description: Persists a content row to the CMS. This is a database INSERT — it does NOT generate copy. CRITICAL: Calling this with raw `content` produced without first loading the account context will produce off-brand, generic AI slop. The account has memory, brand voice, customer avatar, and content rules that DO NOT auto-apply when you call this tool directly. CORRECT FLOWS: • Generative work (blog, article, landing-page copy): call `talk_to_department({domain: "content", message: "<the assignment>"})` FIRST. That department agent runs with the full hydrated context (memory, brand, avatar, journey, skills, rules) and returns brand-aligned copy. Then call `content_create` to persist its output. • Pre-written copy from the user: call `account_context_get({domain: "content"})` FIRST, review the brand voice / avatar / rules in the response, then revise the user copy to match, then `content_create`. • Pure CRUD on an existing item: prefer `content_update` for body changes; reserve `content_create` for truly new items. If you call this tool with empty or generic `content`, the account ends up with broken database rows. Don't.

tools.name: content_create_from_cms_entry
tools.description: Imports an entry that already exists in a website project's file CMS into the marketing content module: materializes {collection.path}/{slug}.{mdx|json} into a content_items row (title, body, excerpt, meta fields, tags, featured image, published_at, and the raw entry fields under settings.cms_fields) plus a content_versions row at version_number 1 with change_summary 'Imported from website CMS'. Returns { id, created }: id is the content item that content_get, content_update and content_publish_to_site then operate on. THE TRAP: this is find-or-create, NOT a re-sync. A second call for the same (website_project_id, cms_collection_id, cms_entry_slug) returns the FIRST import's id with created:false and re-reads nothing from the entry file, so any CMS edit made after the first import never reaches the content item and the call still looks like a success. Pull later changes across with cms_read_entry plus content_update instead. An entry whose status field is missing or unrecognized materializes as 'published', not 'draft'. created_at and updated_at are inherited from the entry file's version timestamp and updated_at has no @updatedAt, so a freshly imported row can sort as months old in any recently-updated list. featured_image_url is stored RAW and site-relative (for example /images/foo.jpg); it is not a fetchable absolute URL. Costs nothing: no money, no outbound call, no queued job. Four distinct 404s share one status and differ only in the error text - 'Project not found' (also what a project in another account returns), 'Project has no CMS manifest', 'Collection not found in manifest', 'CMS entry file not found' - and an unparseable entry is 422 with a detail field. A slug race that survives five insert attempts is rethrown rather than converted, so it surfaces as a 500: retry, do not treat it as permanent.

tools.name: content_delete
tools.description: Delete a content item by ID

tools.name: content_get
tools.description: Get a single content item by ID with categories, versions, media, and linked tasks

tools.name: content_get_tasks
tools.description: List PM tasks linked to a content item (with task title/status/due_date).

tools.name: content_link_tasks
tools.description: Link one or more PM tasks to a content item (added to settings.linkedTaskIds).

tools.name: content_link_to_cms
tools.description: Point a content item at the CMS collection entry it publishes to, by setting website_project_id, cms_collection_id and cms_entry_slug on the row. This is the binding content_publish_to_site needs: without it a content item has a body and no destination. content_update cannot reach these three columns. Pass null for any of them to unbind. TRAPS: website_project_id is a website project UUID (sites_list), NOT a PM project, and a project outside this account is a 404 rather than a silent no-op. cms_collection_id is the collection SLUG, a VarChar(120) string like 'blog', not a UUID; cms_entry_slug is VarChar(200). Both are part of the uq_content_items_cms_target unique key, so an over-length value is refused with a 400 instead of being truncated into a key collision, and binding to an entry another content item already owns is a 409 naming the fix. The three fields are independent: sending only cms_entry_slug re-points the entry within the existing project and collection.

tools.name: content_list
tools.description: List marketing content items with filters for status, type, category, tags, and search

tools.name: content_media_attach
tools.description: Register an ALREADY-HOSTED file URL as a media row on one content item. JSON only, no bytes: filename and file_url are required and are rejected with 400 ('filename and file_url are required') when blank or whitespace-only. Upload or register the file first (media_upload / media_library_register_external_url), then pass the resulting URL here. Returns 201 {data: <the created content_media row>}. THE TRAP: this does not change what the published page shows. The publish path maps only content_items.featured_image_url / featured_image_alt into the CMS entry and never reads content_media, so an attachment reaches neither the entry file nor the live site, and no dashboard screen renders these rows; the only readers are content_media_list and content_get. is_featured flags THIS row alone and does NOT set the item's featured_image_url. If the goal is the hero image on the page, call content_update with featured_image_url instead. media_type is cast straight into the enum with no validation: image | video | audio | document | other, defaulting to 'image'. Any other value raises inside the database and returns a generic 500 ('Failed to attach content media'), not a 400 naming the field. Falsy coalescing silently drops values: file_size 0 and duration 0 are stored as NULL, and an empty-string mime_type / alt_text / caption is stored as NULL (an empty original_filename falls back to filename). sort_order and is_featured use nullish coalescing, so 0 and false survive; omit sort_order to append after the current highest.

tools.name: content_media_list
tools.description: List the media rows attached to ONE content item. Returns {data:[{id, filename, original_filename, file_url, file_size, mime_type, media_type, alt_text, caption, dimensions, duration, sort_order, is_featured, created_at, updated_at}], total}, ordered by sort_order ascending. No filters and no pagination: every attached row comes back in one response. Do not confuse this with the account media library. These are content_media rows scoped to one content item; media_library_list reads a different table (media_assets) and the two never mirror each other, so an asset registered in the library is absent here and an attachment here is invisible to the library, to media_usage_get, and to every dashboard screen. An empty data array is the normal answer for most items and does NOT mean the item has no image: the image the published page actually renders is content_items.featured_image_url, which lives on the item itself and is mapped into the CMS entry by content_publish_to_site. Unknown or cross-account content_id returns 404.

tools.name: content_page_views_get
tools.description: Batch pageview traffic for published content, read from ClickHouse: send up to 200 { projectId, path } pairs and get back { stats: { '<projectId>:<normalizedPath>': { views, views30d, visitors } } }. It is a pure read despite being a POST (no money, no queued job, nothing written; one ClickHouse query per request, not per item), and it is the ONLY working content traffic on this surface. Do NOT use content_analytics_get for this: nothing in the product writes content_analytics and content_items.view_count / like_count / share_count are never incremented, so it answers 200 with an empty data array and an all-zero content_summary for effectively every item. SILENT FAILURE: when ClickHouse is down or unconfigured the response is { stats: {}, degraded: true } at status 200, so a caller that ignores 'degraded' reads a full outage as zero traffic everywhere - read the field, not the status. A missing key is never zero-filled and never an error; it means no pageviews recorded, OR the entry was dropped as malformed (projectId not a UUID, or path not starting with '/'), OR the project is not owned by this key's account (omitted on purpose, since an error would confirm another tenant's project id exists). Those cases are indistinguishable from the response. Keys carry the NORMALIZED path - query string and fragment stripped, trailing slash removed except '/' itself - and paths are case SENSITIVE, so match on the returned key rather than the string you sent. Entry fields are camelCase projectId and path, not project_id. The 200 cap is checked on the raw array before dedupe, so 201 copies of one pair is a 400. For a ranked top-pages list instead of named paths use analytics_pages, which reads a different table (analytics_page_metrics) and will not agree with these numbers.

tools.name: content_publish_to_site
tools.description: PUBLISHES. Pushes a CMS-linked content item into its website project through the same canonical path the editor's Publish button uses. This route reads NO body: there is no confirm flag and no dry run, so calling it IS the commit. Confirm with the human first. What it actually changes: it maps the item into the linked collection, FORCES the entry live (fields.status='published' when the collection has a select field named 'status', otherwise fields.published=true), clears 'archived', deletes a FUTURE or unparseable publishAt that would gate the page, validates, then writes <collection path>/<slug>.mdx|json (collection paths already start with content/, for example content/blog/my-post.mdx) into the project's WORKING TREE as a new version. It then updates the row: cms_entry_slug, last_published_to_cms_at, published_at (first publish only; an existing value is preserved), status='published', cms_publish_error=null, settings.published_route. NOT on the internet yet: the entry lands in the working tree, so the page goes live only after a separate deploy of the project. The returned note says so. Re-running is safe and rewrites the same file with a new versionNumber, but this path takes no advisory lock, so a concurrent builder CMS write to the same slug is last-writer-wins. Two side effects that surprise people. (1) Slug collision auto-suffixes: if another item in the same project and collection already holds the slug, this silently publishes at slug-2 through slug-49 and REWRITES cms_entry_slug, so the live URL can differ from the slug you set. Read `slug` and `route` back from the response; do not assume. (2) A brief-born item carrying settings.target_keyword auto-enrolls that keyword in rank tracking against the resolved route; that insert is ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING and wrapped so it never fails the publish, so trackingStarted=false only means it was skipped or already tracked. Returns {data:{filePath, slug, collectionId, versionNumber, unmapped, route, trackingStarted, note}}. ALWAYS read `unmapped`: those content fields had no home in the collection and were dropped from the entry, with a 200. Errors: 404 for a non-UUID or unknown content_id, for a project with no CMS manifest, or for a collection that no longer exists in the manifest; 400 when the item has no website_project_id or no cms_collection_id; 422 when a required CMS field has no source column (details.field names it) or when entry validation fails (details.errors).

tools.name: content_schedule
tools.description: Schedule a content item for publishing or unpublishing at a specific date/time

tools.name: content_schedule_list
tools.description: List the scheduled publishing actions recorded against one content item. Returns {data:[{id, content_item_id, account_id, action_type, scheduled_at, status, executed_at, error_message, retry_count, created_by, created_at}], total}, ordered by scheduled_at ascending. action_type is publish | unpublish | archive | delete; status is pending | completed | failed | cancelled. SILENT FAILURE, and it is the whole reason to read this list carefully: NOTHING EXECUTES THESE ROWS. No cron or worker in the app reads content_publishing_schedule; the only executor that ever existed was a Postgres function in the deprecated saas app's migrations. The scheduler that actually runs is a different table, cms_scheduled_actions, driven by the cms-scheduled-publish cron, which this endpoint cannot see. So a row here still 'pending' with a scheduled_at long past has not failed, it was never picked up, and executed_at will stay null forever. Report these as recorded intent, never as 'it will publish'. content_schedule (POST on this same path) writes into this same inert table. The status filter is assigned raw into an enum column: a value outside pending | completed | failed | cancelled raises in Prisma and returns a generic 500 rather than an empty list. Unknown or cross-account content_id returns 404.

tools.name: content_share_link_create
tools.description: Mints a PUBLIC, no-login URL for one marketing content item. Returns {shareLink:{id, url, label, allow_comments, expires_at, created_at}, reused:boolean}, or 404 'Content not found'. OUTWARD-FACING: url is https://app.hiveku.com/share/content/<token> and the token IS the authorization, so anyone holding or forwarding it reads the item's title, excerpt, FULL BODY, content_format and featured image with no account and no audit trail. Do not call this on a draft that is not meant to leave the building. IDEMPOTENT BY DEFAULT: if any non-revoked, non-expired link already exists it comes back with reused:true, NOTHING is created, and label, allow_comments and expiry_days are SILENTLY IGNORED, so a 200 showing allow_comments:true can be the old link's setting rather than the one you sent. rotate:true forces a fresh token but DOES NOT ROTATE anything: the previous token stays live until content_share_link_revoke revokes it by id, so rotating twice leaves three working URLs. expiry_days is honoured only as a positive NUMBER (floored, capped at 365); a numeric string, 0, or omitting it all mean the link NEVER expires. allow_comments is true unless you send exactly false, and when true any anonymous visitor can read EVERY comment on that item, internal in-app comments included, and post new ones under any name and email with no auth and no rate limit. Costs no money and sends nothing; the cost is one DB row plus permanent exposure until revoked. Run content_share_links_list first to see what is already public.

tools.name: content_share_link_revoke
tools.description: Kills ONE public share link on a marketing content item so its URL stops working: returns {revoked:true} and the public page then answers 410 to everyone still holding that token. This is the only way to close a door opened by content_share_link_create, which leaves every earlier token live when rotate is used, so revoke each id separately. It SOFT-revokes: revoked_at is stamped, the row and all its comments remain in the database, and the item itself is untouched. `id` is the SHARE LINK id from content_share_links_list, NOT the content item id; the route reads it from the query string under exactly that name. Passing the content item id, an already-revoked id, a non-uuid, or an id belonging to another item or another account matches zero rows and returns 404 'Share link not found or already revoked' with NOTHING revoked, so treat a 404 as work still to do and re-read the listing rather than assuming the link was already dead. Omitting id returns 400.

tools.name: content_share_links_list
tools.description: Lists the live PUBLIC share links on one marketing content item. Returns {shareLinks:[{id, url, label, allow_comments, view_count, last_viewed_at, expires_at, created_at}]} newest first, or 404 'Content not found' when the item is not in this account. Every `url` is https://app.hiveku.com/share/content/<token> and needs NO LOGIN: the token IS the authorization, so this output is a list of open doors to the item's full body, and forwarding one hands over the same access. EXPIRED LINKS ARE STILL LISTED: the filter is revoked_at null only, so check expires_at yourself before telling anyone a link works; the public page enforces expiry, this listing does not. view_count is a counter the public reader bumps, not a cap, and it never stops anyone. No paging, no filters, and there is no password or use limit on these rows. Read-only. Call this BEFORE content_share_link_create, which silently reuses an existing live link instead of applying your settings, and use the `id` values here as the input to content_share_link_revoke.

tools.name: content_template_create
tools.description: Creates an account-owned content template (a reusable body scaffold) and returns 201 with the stored row. name and template_content are both required and trimmed; blank or whitespace-only gives a 400. Traps: content_type defaults to 'article' and is cast straight onto content_type_enum with NO validation, so anything outside article, blog_post, page, social_post, email, press_release, case_study, tutorial, faq, landing_page, custom comes back as a generic 500 rather than a 400. is_global (false), is_active (true) and usage_count (0) are hardcoded by the route and any values you send for them are dropped silently, as is created_by, which stays null. template_fields defaults to an empty OBJECT here, overriding the column default of an empty array. Two things to plan around: NOTHING applies a template for you (content_create takes no template_id, no job reads content_templates, and usage_count is never incremented anywhere, so it stays 0 forever), and the only shipped listing tool, marketing_content_templates, takes no paging and returns at most 20 rows ordered by that always-zero usage_count, so a new template can be invisible there. Keep the id from this response and fetch it with content_template_get, then paste template_content yourself.

tools.name: content_template_delete
tools.description: PERMANENTLY deletes one account-owned content template. The route supports no confirm field and this table has no version history, so template_content is gone the moment it returns; when you may want the body back, call content_template_update with is_active false to retire it instead (that preserves the row but does not hide it from the marketing_content_templates listing, which cannot filter on is_active). No reference check runs and none is needed: content_items carries no link to content_templates, so existing content is unaffected and no cascade fires. Global templates cannot be deleted and return 404, the same status code a missing id produces. Returns {success:true}.

tools.name: content_template_get
tools.description: Fetches one template by id and returns the full row including template_content, template_fields and default_settings. Trap: this lookup matches templates owned by this account OR any is_global template, so a template you can READ here may be one you cannot change. content_template_update and content_template_delete re-resolve by account_id alone and answer 404 for a global row, the same status code a genuinely missing id produces, so the 404 will not tell you which happened. Read is_global on the row returned here before planning any edit. This is also the only way to reach a template that the paging-less marketing_content_templates listing never shows you, so hold onto ids. Accepts no query params.

tools.name: content_template_update
tools.description: Patches an allow-listed set of fields on one account-owned template and returns the updated row; only keys you send are touched. Traps: global templates are READ-ONLY, and a PATCH against one returns 404 with a message about not being editable, indistinguishable by status code from an id that does not exist; call content_template_get first and check is_global. content_type is written straight through with no enum validation, so a value outside article, blog_post, page, social_post, email, press_release, case_study, tutorial, faq, landing_page, custom is a generic 500 rather than a 400. template_fields and default_settings are REPLACED wholesale, never merged, so send the complete object or you will silently drop every key you left out. is_global and usage_count are not in the allow-list and are ignored if sent. Setting is_active false is the nearest thing to archiving here, but it hides the template from nothing you can reach today: the shipped marketing_content_templates listing cannot filter on is_active, and no other code in the product reads the flag.

tools.name: content_unlink_tasks
tools.description: Remove one or more PM tasks from a content item.

tools.name: content_unpublish_from_site
tools.description: TAKES A PUBLISHED ENTRY DOWN. The unpublish direction of content_publish_to_site over the same endpoint; the direction is pinned in the request, so this tool can only ever draft an entry, never publish one. Call content_publish_to_site to put it back live. Do NOT reach for content_update status='draft' instead: the site's visibility contract reads the ENTRY FILE, never content_items.status, so that flips the row and leaves the live page exactly where it was. It deletes nothing. It re-maps the item and rewrites the SAME entry file (<collection path>/<slug>.mdx|json) as a NEW version in the project's WORKING TREE with the live signal flipped: fields.status='draft' when the collection has a select field named 'status', otherwise fields.published=false. 'archived' is left as it was and a future publishAt is left alone; only the publish direction clears those. THE PAGE IS STILL UP when this returns 200. Nothing leaves the internet until the project is deployed (deploy_run), and the returned note says exactly that. Do not report a takedown off this response alone. Row changes: status='draft', cms_entry_slug, cms_publish_error=null, settings.published_route, and last_published_to_cms_at is stamped NOW even though nothing was published, so read that column as 'last write through this path', not 'last went live'. published_at is deliberately preserved (a never-published item keeps null). Two things that bite. (1) The slug-collision suffix loop runs in this direction too: if another content item in the same project and collection has claimed the slug since publish, the draft is written at slug-2 and cms_entry_slug is REWRITTEN, leaving the original live file untouched, with a 200. Read `slug` and `filePath` back rather than assuming the live entry was the one drafted. (2) The rank-tracking auto-enroll is not gated on direction, so a brief-born item carrying settings.target_keyword can enroll that keyword against the very route you are taking down; trackingStarted=true here means a keyword was just added to rank tracking, not that anything published. Returns {data:{filePath, slug, collectionId, versionNumber, unmapped, route, trackingStarted, mode:'unpublish', published:false, note}}. Validation still runs on the drafted entry, so a required CMS field that lost its source column 422s and the page STAYS LIVE. Errors: 404 for a non-UUID, unknown or cross-account content_id, a project with no CMS manifest, or a collection missing from the manifest; 400 when the item has no website_project_id or no cms_collection_id; 422 on entry validation (details.errors) or a required field with no source column (details.field).

tools.name: content_update
tools.description: Patch a content row. For metadata-only changes (status flip, slug fix, scheduled_publish_at), use directly. For body rewrites or new content sections: call `account_context_get({domain: "content"})` first, OR delegate to `talk_to_department({domain: "content", message: ...})` for fully brand-aligned copy. Patching with raw text that ignores the account's brand voice / avatar / rules produces off-brand content that the team will then have to rewrite manually.

tools.name: content_version_create
tools.description: Snapshot a marketing content item into a new content_versions row; returns {data: <the created version>} with 201. Send content_id alone to capture the item exactly as it stands, which is the intended use. IT DOES NOT WRITE content_items: title/content/excerpt/meta_title/meta_description/meta_keywords land in the VERSION only, so passing edited values returns 201 while the live item is untouched and you have stored a state the item never had; use content_update to change the item. There is no restore endpoint on this API either, so anything captured here can be read back with content_versions_list but can only be rolled back by a human in the editor. Field merge is `||`, so an empty string for any string field silently falls back to the item's current value, while an empty meta_keywords array is truthy and DOES override to empty. version_number is allocated read-max-then-insert with up to 5 P2002 retries against the unique [content_item_id, version_number]; dashboard autosave writes the same table so numbers interleave with UI saves, and if all 5 attempts lose the race you get a 503 with nothing written.

tools.name: content_versions_list
tools.description: Page through the saved snapshots of a marketing content item, newest version_number first. Returns {data:[{id, version_number, title, content, excerpt, meta_title, meta_description, meta_keywords, change_summary, created_by, created_at}], pagination:{page, limit, total, total_pages}}, or 404 'Content item not found' when the id is not in this account. Unlike content_get, which embeds only the latest 10 versions as metadata, this returns the FULL `content` body of every row, so a long article history is enormous: keep limit small. limit is clamped to 1..100 and defaults to 20; page defaults to 1, and a non-numeric value for either parses to NaN and the route answers a generic 500 'Failed to list content versions' instead of a 400 naming the bad param. created_by is null on every version made through this API; only dashboard saves stamp an author, so a null author is not corruption. Read-only.

tools.name: crawl
tools.description: 🕷️ CRAWL4AI: Multi-URL crawl (Firecrawl-backed)

tools.name: create_task
tools.description: Create a new PM task with title, description, priority, type, assignee, and due date. Field is `title` (NOT `name` — that's the pm_projects field). The route also accepts `name` as a forgiving alias if you forget. Prefer pm_tasks_create going forward; this name is kept for backwards compatibility.

tools.name: crm_account_summary
tools.description: High-level account snapshot: contact/company/deal/pipeline counts, active sequences, suppressions, open-deal $ total. Cheap; use as a first read when the user asks "give me an overview." Contacts, companies and deals count LIVE rows only (soft-deleted rows excluded), the same basis as crm_list_contacts and account_audit_health.crm.contact_count, so those three totals are directly comparable. `counts_basis` in the response states it.

tools.name: crm_activity_leaderboard
tools.description: Activity counts per user (calls/emails/meetings/tasks logged) over a rolling window. Default 30 days.

tools.name: crm_add_lead_source_option
tools.description: Add a custom lead-source option (or un-archive an existing slug).

tools.name: crm_add_lead_status_option
tools.description: Add a custom lead-status option (or un-archive an existing slug). System slugs are reserved.

tools.name: crm_archive_lead_source_option
tools.description: Soft-archive a custom lead-source option. Default sources can't be archived.

tools.name: crm_archive_lead_status_option
tools.description: Soft-archive a custom lead-status option. System rows can't be archived. Existing contacts using this status keep their value.

tools.name: crm_attach_tag
tools.description: Attach a tag to a contact/company/deal. Idempotent — calling twice is safe. Tag scope (object_type on the tag row) is enforced; an account-wide tag (null object_type) attaches to any type.

tools.name: crm_audit_summary
tools.description: Aggregate CRM data-quality audit — the counts behind 'what is wrong with this CRM': missing emails, duplicate contacts, orphaned records and similar. Read-only; run before a cleanup so you act on numbers rather than impressions.

tools.name: crm_calendar_create
tools.description: Create a calendar event. attendees is a list of email addresses; conference=true adds a Google Meet / Microsoft Teams link.

tools.name: crm_calendar_delete
tools.description: Delete a calendar event.

tools.name: crm_calendar_get
tools.description: Fetch one calendar event with full detail (attendees, conference link).

tools.name: crm_calendar_list
tools.description: List upcoming/past calendar events (Google Calendar / Microsoft Graph via the account's connected OAuth). Optional time window + search.

tools.name: crm_calendar_update
tools.description: Update a calendar event (only the fields you pass are changed).

tools.name: crm_calls_list
tools.description: Call activities with recording and transcript detail. Filter by contact_id, company_id, deal_id, has_recording, has_transcript or a free-text search. This is the call history behind a contact — crm_get_contact does not include it.

tools.name: crm_companies_bulk_create
tools.description: Bulk-import companies. Up to 5,000 rows. Dedup precedence: external_id (if provided), then lowercase(name) within the account. Supports the same inline custom_fields + auto_create_fields contract as crm_contacts_bulk_create. Returns the same result shape.

tools.name: crm_contact_email_send
tools.description: Send a REAL 1:1 email to a contact from the account's connected Gmail/Outlook inbox. The recipient is ALWAYS the contact's email on file — there is no arbitrary `to`; cc/bcc add recipients alongside it. Show the operator the exact subject and body and get an explicit yes BEFORE calling — there is no draft state, no recall, and no idempotency key. With no connection_id it falls back to the account's default SENDABLE mailbox (the default is per platform, so a default-Calendar row can never be picked); a read-only-scope or calendar connection 400s cleanly with the reason. Thread a reply with reply_to_message_id + thread_id from crm_thread_for_contact / crm_contact_emails_list. The send self-logs to the contact timeline as an email activity unless log_activity=false — do NOT also write crm_create_activity for the same send.

tools.name: crm_contact_emails_list
tools.description: List the synced 1:1 email activity for one contact (type=email activities: Gmail/Outlook-synced plus manually logged), newest first, paginated. `source` filters to gmail | outlook | manual. This is the per-contact email history read; for the full merged message thread use crm_thread_for_contact.

tools.name: crm_contact_engagement_summary
tools.description: Single-call engagement snapshot for one contact: emails sent/received, opens/clicks, meetings/calls/notes/tasks, last-inbound/outbound timestamps, ratios, active-sequence list. Read-only.

tools.name: crm_contact_merge
tools.description: Merge loser_id INTO winner_id. Reparents activities, deal_contacts, contact_companies, tags, custom_field_values, sequence_enrollments, email_events, and suppressions. Backfills any blank winner field from the loser ("winner wins, loser fills blanks"). Soft-deletes the loser. Single transaction; partial failures don't leave the loser half-merged. DESTRUCTIVE — confirm with the rep before calling. The dashboard typed-name confirmation pattern should gate this from the UI side.

tools.name: crm_contact_score_compute
tools.description: Recompute + persist a contact's lead_score from the last 30 days of engagement. Writes lead_score, lead_score_reason, lead_score_updated_at. Returns the new score (0-100), a reason summary, and the full component breakdown. Same weights as the sales DAO.

tools.name: crm_contact_status_option_create
tools.description: Add a lead-status option (value + label + colour) for the account. Use when a pipeline needs a stage the six defaults do not cover.

tools.name: crm_contact_status_options_list
tools.description: Lead-status options for the account. Seeds six system defaults on first call, so every account has a working baseline. Pass include_archived to see retired options too — useful when a contact carries a status no longer offered.

tools.name: crm_contact_touch_history
tools.description: Chronological merged timeline of activities + sequence email events for a contact. Sorted newest-first, capped at `limit` items across both sources combined.

tools.name: crm_contact_upsert_by_email
tools.description: Idempotent single-contact write keyed on lowercase(email). If a contact with that email exists in the account it's updated (only the fields you pass — existing values are preserved); otherwise it's created with lead_source='upsert'. Use for incremental re-imports + agent flows where you can't tell in advance whether the email is new. Supports inline custom_fields + auto_create_fields like the bulk tools. Returns { action: 'created' | 'updated', id, custom_fields }.

tools.name: crm_contacts_bulk_create
tools.description: Bulk-import contacts into the CRM. Up to 5,000 rows per call; emails are normalized to lowercase before insert and the (account_id, email) unique index prevents duplicates at the DB level. Custom fields can be set inline via per-row `custom_fields: {key: value}`. With `auto_create_fields: true`, unknown field_keys auto-create the crm_custom_fields definition with type inferred from the first value (number→number, true/false→checkbox, ISO date string→date, http(s)://→url, else→text). Default false so typos don't pollute the schema. on_duplicate: • 'skip' (default) — rows whose email already exists in the account are dropped from the batch; results.skipped_duplicates is incremented. • 'error' — the whole batch fails with 409 if any email collides, so the caller can correct the source before retrying. Returns: { created, skipped_duplicates, skipped_invalid, errors[], custom_fields_auto_created[], custom_fields_warnings[] }. For migrations always run crm_import_preflight first.

tools.name: crm_contacts_duplicates
tools.description: Find duplicate-candidate contacts grouped by lowercased email. Name-only matching is intentionally excluded (too many false positives). Returns groups with 2+ contacts each.

tools.name: crm_contacts_gone_cold
tools.description: Contacts who had engagement signals in the last 180 days then went silent for `days` days. Distinct from crm_contacts_stale (which catches "no activity ever"). Highest-ROI re-engagement bucket.

tools.name: crm_contacts_missing_field
tools.description: Contacts missing a standard column value. Use for data-quality sweeps ("which contacts have no phone?"). Valid fields: email, phone, first_name, last_name, job_title, lead_source, owner_id, assigned_to_id, lead_status.

tools.name: crm_contacts_stale
tools.description: Contacts with no recent crm_activities entry. Filters contacts where the latest activity is older than `days` (default 30) OR there are no activities at all.

tools.name: crm_contacts_top_scored
tools.description: Top N contacts by lead_score. Optional lifecycle_stage filter so "hottest leads" works without post-filtering. Excludes contacts whose score has never been computed.

tools.name: crm_contract_template_create
tools.description: Create a contract template. Provide EITHER layout_json (block-based, compiled to HTML server-side) OR source_pdf_s3_key + fields[] (legacy PDF + coordinate fields). signers[] is the role skeleton (e.g. [{role: "Client"}, {role: "Agency"}]).

tools.name: crm_contract_template_delete
tools.description: Archive a contract template (sets is_archived=true). Templates are never hard-deleted — historical envelopes still reference them for audit.

tools.name: crm_contract_template_get
tools.description: Get a single contract template by UUID. Returns layout_json + compiled_html (block path) or source_pdf_s3_key + fields_json (PDF path).

tools.name: crm_contract_template_list
tools.description: List contract templates. By default only non-archived templates are returned; pass archived=true to include archived ones.

tools.name: crm_contract_template_update
tools.description: Update a contract template. Only name, description, and is_archived are mutable here — to change the document body, create a new template (existing envelopes reference the template id for audit).

tools.name: crm_create_activity
tools.description: Log a CRM activity (note, call, email, meeting, or task) linked to a contact, company, or deal

tools.name: crm_create_company
tools.description: Create a new CRM company

tools.name: crm_create_contact
tools.description: Create a new CRM contact with name, email, phone, job title, lifecycle stage, optional company link, and OWNER. owner_id/assigned_to_id are public_users UUIDs validated against your account — pass owner_id to set the rep who owns the lead (assigned_to_id defaults to it). Without owner_id the contact is created unowned (null owner). Use crm_list_users / the account roster to resolve the rep UUID; do NOT hardcode a user id.

tools.name: crm_create_custom_field
tools.description: Define a new custom field on contact/company/deal/etc. field_key must be lowercase alphanumeric + underscore. After creating, write values via crm_set_custom_field_value.

tools.name: crm_create_deal
tools.description: Create a new CRM deal in a pipeline stage with optional value, contact, and company

tools.name: crm_create_email_template
tools.description: Create a new email template. Templates created via Olympus default to is_shared=true (visible account-wide) since service-key callers have no human user. Body/subject support merge tags with fallback syntax ({{first_name|there}}) and spintax for per-recipient variation ({Hi|Hey|Hello}) — see field descriptions.

tools.name: crm_create_pipeline
tools.description: Create a new CRM pipeline with optional stages

tools.name: crm_deal_move_stage
tools.description: Move a deal to another stage in its pipeline (appends to stage_history; the response includes the destination stage and is_closing). When the DESTINATION is a closing (won/lost) stage you can capture why in the same call — the moment the rep actually knows: lost_reason_code (no_decision | price | competitor | timing | no_budget | bad_fit | ghosted | other; unknown codes are a 400) and/or free-text lost_reason (max 500 chars). On a NON-closing move the loss fields are NOT written and the response carries loss_fields_ignored: true — do not treat such a call as having recorded a reason; set it via crm_update_deal after the deal actually closes.

tools.name: crm_deals_at_risk
tools.description: Open deals exhibiting risk signals: stuck in current stage ≥ stuck_days (default 14) OR past their close_date. Returns risk_flags per deal so the agent can prioritize.

tools.name: crm_deals_bulk_create
tools.description: Bulk-import deals. Up to 5,000 rows. Dedup by external_id ONLY — deals don't have a natural uniqueness key. Pipeline + stage are required per-row OR via default_pipeline_id / default_stage_id (both are batch-validated against the account before any insert; mismatches fail fast for the whole batch). Optional contact_id / company_id per row creates the deal↔contact / deal↔company join rows. Same custom_fields + auto_create_fields contract as the other bulk tools.

tools.name: crm_deals_stuck
tools.description: Open deals whose updated_at is older than `days` (default 14). Simpler than crm_deals_at_risk — pure stuck filter without close_date overlay.

tools.name: crm_delete_activity
tools.description: Delete a CRM activity by ID

tools.name: crm_delete_company
tools.description: Delete a CRM company by ID

tools.name: crm_delete_contact
tools.description: Delete a CRM contact by ID

tools.name: crm_delete_custom_field
tools.description: Hard-delete a custom field DEFINITION. Cascades the field's value rows on every object. Destructive — use rarely.

tools.name: crm_delete_deal
tools.description: Delete a CRM deal by ID

tools.name: crm_delete_email_template
tools.description: Soft-delete a template (sets archived_at). In-flight sequence enrollments that reference it still resolve at send time.

tools.name: crm_delete_sequence
tools.description: Hard-delete a sequence — cascades steps and enrollments. Use sparingly. Prefer is_active=false via crm_update_sequence for "stop using this" cases; delete only when truly removing.

tools.name: crm_delete_tag
tools.description: Delete a tag definition. Cascades crm_object_tags (every attachment is removed).

tools.name: crm_detach_tag
