tools.description: Detach a tag from an object. No-op when not attached.

tools.name: crm_email_batch_cancel
tools.description: Cancel all queued rows in a batch (already-sent rows are untouched).

tools.name: crm_email_batch_reschedule
tools.description: Shift the fire time of a batch (all rows in the batch that are still queued).

tools.name: crm_email_send_queue_list
tools.description: List scheduled / sent / cancelled email send-queue rows. Filter by status, batch_id, or contact_id.

tools.name: crm_email_thread_search
tools.description: Search CRM-stored email activities (synced via crm_activities) by subject or body substring. Distinct from crm_ghl_contacts_search / crm_hubspot_contacts_search which hit the external CRM live.

tools.name: crm_enroll_sequence
tools.description: Enroll a contact in a sequence. The sequence must be is_active=true; if it is not, the API returns 400 "Sequence is not active" — check active state via crm_get_sequence first. Returns 409 with duplicate=true if the contact is already enrolled.

tools.name: crm_envelope_add_signer
tools.description: Append a signer to a draft envelope. Refuses (409) if envelope is not draft. Returns the new signer row plus the plaintext access token (not derivable from the stored hash — store it if you need to email a manual link). Signing order is auto-assigned to max+1.

tools.name: crm_envelope_create
tools.description: Create a draft envelope. Provide EITHER layout_json (block-based proposal — compiled server-side to HTML) OR source_pdf_s3_key + fields[] (legacy PDF + coordinate fields). signers[] is required (1-10). The response includes plaintext signer tokens — capture them; they are not derivable from the stored hash. signing_order = parallel | sequential.

tools.name: crm_envelope_delete
tools.description: Soft-delete an envelope (moves status to voided, sets deleted_at). Refuses (409) on completed envelopes — those are immutable for audit reasons.

tools.name: crm_envelope_get
tools.description: Get a single envelope by UUID, including signers, fields, recent events (last 100), and the full CRM linkage: contact (id, name, email, phone), company (id, name), and deal (id, name, value, stage). Response includes an ETag header reflecting updated_at for optimistic-concurrency PATCH.

tools.name: crm_envelope_list
tools.description: List signature envelopes (contracts/proposals). Filter by status (draft/sent/viewed/completed/declined/voided/all), contact_id, company_id, deal_id, or subject_type (estimate/contract/invoice/custom). limit defaults to 50, max 200. Each row includes signers, the linked contact (id, name, email), company (id, name), and deal (id, name, value, stage) so the agent has full CRM context in one call.

tools.name: crm_envelope_list_signers
tools.description: List signers on an envelope. Token hashes are NOT returned — only metadata (status, signed_at, viewed_at, reminder_count, etc.). Use this to check progress on a sent envelope without pulling the full envelope detail.

tools.name: crm_envelope_send
tools.description: Send signer-invitation emails. On first send, status moves draft → sent and per-signer plaintext access tokens are minted server-side. For parallel envelopes every pending signer is emailed; for sequential, only the first pending signer (downstream invites trigger on prior signer completion via the public sign route). Requires the from_email setting on crm_payment_integrations.

tools.name: crm_envelope_update
tools.description: PATCH a draft envelope. Refuses (409) if status != draft. Passing signers replaces the roster but preserves access tokens for signers identified by id. Pass an If-Match header equal to the previous ETag to detect concurrent edits (412 on mismatch). Use contact_id / company_id / deal_id to (re)link the envelope to CRM records — pass null to clear an existing link.

tools.name: crm_envelope_void
tools.description: Void an envelope (status → voided, stamps voided_at and void_reason). Refuses (409) on completed envelopes.

tools.name: crm_estimate_convert_to_invoice
tools.description: Convert an accepted estimate into a fresh draft invoice. Copies line items, totals, notes, and terms; links the invoice back via converted_invoice_id on the estimate; status moves to "converted"; portal tokens are revoked. Returns 409 if already converted.

tools.name: crm_estimate_create
tools.description: Create a draft estimate. Either contact_id OR company_id is required. line_items is an array of { description, quantity, unit_cents, discount_cents?, tax_bps?, sort_order?, product_id?, metadata? }. estimate_number is auto-generated server-side via the atomic doc-number helper.

tools.name: crm_estimate_delete
tools.description: Soft-delete an estimate and revoke its portal tokens. Refuses (409) on accepted/converted estimates — those are immutable for audit reasons.

tools.name: crm_estimate_get
tools.description: Get a single estimate by UUID, including line_items, contact, company, and deal.

tools.name: crm_estimate_list
tools.description: List CRM estimates with optional filters: status (draft/sent/viewed/accepted/declined/expired/converted/all), contact_id, company_id, deal_id, free-text q (matches estimate_number/notes/contact name/email/company name), order (created_desc/created_asc/expires_asc/expires_desc/total_desc/total_asc), pagination via limit/offset. Each row includes the linked contact, company, and deal (id, name, value, stage) so the agent can see CRM context without an extra fetch.

tools.name: crm_estimate_mark_accepted
tools.description: Record operator-side acceptance for an estimate (customer agreed verbally / over email and you're recording it). Stamps accepted_offline=true on the row and renders the acceptance certificate PDF. signer_name is the name the customer agreed under (e.g. "Jane Smith"). Returns 409 if the estimate is declined/expired. Idempotent on accepted/converted — replays return already_accepted=true.

tools.name: crm_estimate_send
tools.description: Send the estimate to the contact via email and/or SMS. Mints a single portal token (TTL 30d) shared across channels. channel = email | sms | both. Pass attach_pdf=true to render and attach the PDF on the email (text + portal link are sufficient otherwise). idempotency_key dedupes accidental re-sends. SMS branch requires the voice add-on enabled on the account.

tools.name: crm_estimate_template_create
tools.description: Create an estimate template. line_items is optional (a design-only template is valid); amount_cents is stamped server-side on each item. design_json is the customizable PDF design (theme/columns/sections/labels) applied when an estimate from this template is rendered. is_default=true makes it the account default (applied to blank estimates) and unsets any other default.

tools.name: crm_estimate_template_delete
tools.description: Soft-delete an estimate template (deleted_at timestamp; not surfaced in list).

tools.name: crm_estimate_template_get
tools.description: Get a single estimate template by UUID.

tools.name: crm_estimate_template_list
tools.description: List reusable estimate templates (name, description, currency, default tax, line items skeleton).

tools.name: crm_estimate_template_update
tools.description: Update an estimate template. Passing line_items replaces the full set. design_json replaces the PDF design. is_default=true makes it the account default (unsets others); is_archived hides it from pickers. Partial updates: only fields present are written.

tools.name: crm_estimate_update
tools.description: Update an editable estimate (status draft/sent/viewed/expired/declined). PATCHing an accepted/converted estimate returns 409 — duplicate it instead. Passing line_items replaces the full set.

tools.name: crm_forecast_weighted
tools.description: Probability-weighted forecast for open deals: SUM(value × stage_probability/100). Returns per-stage breakdown + grand total. Optional pipeline_id.

tools.name: crm_get_company
tools.description: Get a single CRM company by ID with its contacts, deals, and activities

tools.name: crm_get_contact
tools.description: Get a single CRM contact by ID, including their companies, deals, and activities

tools.name: crm_get_custom_field
tools.description: Read a single custom field definition by id.

tools.name: crm_get_custom_field_values
tools.description: Read all custom-field values on a contact/deal/company, keyed by field_key. Use to verify your custom-field writes landed before calling crm_enroll_sequence.

tools.name: crm_get_deal
tools.description: Get a single CRM deal by ID with pipeline, stage, contacts, companies, and activities

tools.name: crm_get_dnc_status
tools.description: Get the DNC (do-not-contact) status for a contact: email suppression, SMS opt-out, lifecycle state, and reasons. Check this before drafting outbound — sending to a DNC'd prospect is a compliance issue.

tools.name: crm_get_email_template
tools.description: Read a single template by id.

tools.name: crm_get_sequence
tools.description: Get a single sequence by id, including steps and current enrollment count.

tools.name: crm_get_user_signature
tools.description: Read a team member's HTML email signature. The full signature body — use when drafting sends from that user's connection.

tools.name: crm_ghl_contact_get
tools.description: Fetch one GHL contact with full custom fields, source, tags, owner.

tools.name: crm_ghl_contact_history
tools.description: Fetch a GHL contact's history: notes + tasks + conversations.

tools.name: crm_ghl_contacts_search
tools.description: Search GHL contacts. query is a free-text match.

tools.name: crm_ghl_opportunities_search
tools.description: Search GHL opportunities (= deals). Filter by pipeline_id, pipeline_stage_id, or contact_id.

tools.name: crm_ghl_pipelines_list
tools.description: List GHL pipelines (and their stages) for the connected location.

tools.name: crm_ghl_status
tools.description: GoHighLevel connection health (location id + name) or { connected: false } if not linked.

tools.name: crm_hubspot_contact_get
tools.description: Fetch one HubSpot contact with all properties.

tools.name: crm_hubspot_contact_history
tools.description: Fetch a HubSpot contact's history: notes + tasks (associated engagements).

tools.name: crm_hubspot_contacts_search
tools.description: Search HubSpot contacts.

tools.name: crm_hubspot_deals_search
tools.description: Search HubSpot deals.

tools.name: crm_hubspot_lists_list
tools.description: List HubSpot static + dynamic lists (for audience selection).

tools.name: crm_hubspot_pipelines_list
tools.description: List HubSpot deal pipelines + stages.

tools.name: crm_hubspot_status
tools.description: HubSpot connection health (portal id, timezone, currency) or { connected: false }.

tools.name: crm_import_preflight
tools.description: Dry-run a bulk import payload without writing anything. Returns a per-payload audit: invalid rows + reasons, intra-batch duplicates, cross-DB duplicates, unknown custom field keys (would_fail_on_unknown_fields=true if auto_create_fields is false). Run this BEFORE every bulk import call when migrating large datasets — surfaces problems at row 0 instead of row 3,000.

tools.name: crm_inbox_connections
tools.description: List all connected inboxes (Gmail / Outlook) for the account — id, email, platform, is_active.

tools.name: crm_inbox_list
tools.description: Return the last N messages from a connected inbox (no search). folder='inbox' | 'sent' | 'all'. Omit connection_id to use the account default.

tools.name: crm_inbox_recent
tools.description: Search a connected inbox with Gmail/Outlook native query syntax. Examples: 'from:logan@x.com newer_than:14d', 'subject:"intro call"', 'to:me has:attachment'. Use crm_inbox_list (no query) for the simple recent-N case.

tools.name: crm_integration_sync_configure
tools.description: Upsert a sync job. source='ghl'|'hubspot'. frequency_seconds clamped to [900, 86400]. plan_json defines the import shape (see crm_ghl_import_analyze / crm_hubspot_import_analyze).

tools.name: crm_integration_sync_disable
tools.description: Disable a sync job (keeps the row for audit). Re-enable via _configure with enabled=true.

tools.name: crm_integration_sync_list
tools.description: List configured external-CRM sync jobs (GHL / HubSpot → Hiveku) for the account.

tools.name: crm_integration_sync_run_now
tools.description: Trigger a sync to run on the next cron tick (zeros last_run_at).

tools.name: crm_invoice_template_create
tools.description: Create an invoice template. line_items is required (min 1). amount_cents is stamped server-side on each item. default_due_days seeds the invoice due date (issue_date + days).

tools.name: crm_invoice_template_delete
tools.description: Soft-delete an invoice template (deleted_at timestamp; not surfaced in list).

tools.name: crm_invoice_template_get
tools.description: Get a single invoice template by UUID.

tools.name: crm_invoice_template_list
tools.description: List reusable invoice templates (name, description, currency, default tax, net terms, line items skeleton).

tools.name: crm_invoice_template_update
tools.description: Update an invoice template. Passing line_items replaces the full set. Partial updates: only fields present are written.

tools.name: crm_lead_triage
tools.description: One-shot lead intake: inbox sweep + prospect parse + CRM dedupe + last-outbound lookup. Provider-agnostic (Typeform/JotForm/Webflow/Instantly/Lemlist/Smartlead/Calendly all work via the same query). Saved query patterns live in memory under domain='lead_intake_query'.

tools.name: crm_link_contact_company
tools.description: Link an existing contact to an existing company. When is_primary=true, the contact's previous primary company is demoted automatically.

tools.name: crm_link_deal_contact
tools.description: Link an existing contact to an existing deal. Idempotent.

tools.name: crm_list_activities
tools.description: List CRM activities (notes, calls, emails, meetings, tasks) with filters

tools.name: crm_list_companies
tools.description: List CRM companies with optional search and industry filter

tools.name: crm_list_contacts
tools.description: List CRM contacts with optional filtering by search term, lifecycle stage, company, with pagination

tools.name: crm_list_custom_fields
tools.description: List custom field DEFINITIONS for the account, optionally filtered by object_type. Returns field_key/label/field_type/options.

tools.name: crm_list_deals
tools.description: List CRM deals with filters for status, pipeline, stage, contact, company, and stale deals

tools.name: crm_list_email_connections
tools.description: List the account's active connected Gmail/Outlook inboxes. Returns id/user_id/email_address/platform. Use to find the connection_id when staging "send from" overrides on sequence enrollments.

tools.name: crm_list_email_suppressions
tools.description: List active email suppressions on the account. Optional ?email=... narrows to one address. Read-only — to ADD suppression use crm_set_dnc (atomic across multiple tables); this is for audit / visibility.

tools.name: crm_list_email_templates
tools.description: List the account's email templates (non-archived by default). Use to find a template_id before referencing it on a sequence step.

tools.name: crm_list_lead_source_options
tools.description: List the account's lead-source attribution options. Returns id/value/label/sort_order/is_default. Call before setting lead_source on a contact.

tools.name: crm_list_lead_status_options
tools.description: List the account's lead-status (operational sub-state within lead lifecycle) options. Returns id/value/label/color/sort_order/is_system. Call before crm_update_contact with a lead_status value.

tools.name: crm_list_pipelines
tools.description: List all CRM pipelines with their stages and deal counts

tools.name: crm_list_sequence_enrollments
tools.description: Paginated list of enrollments on a sequence with status filter. Use to find who's currently in a sequence vs exited/completed.

tools.name: crm_list_sequences
tools.description: List sales-sequence definitions (Cold Email 2, drip sequences, etc.) for the current account. Returns id, name, is_active, step count.

tools.name: crm_list_users
tools.description: List team members on the account (primary users + invited members). Returns id/clerk_user_id/name/email/avatar/has_signature. Use to find owner_id when assigning contacts/deals.

tools.name: crm_pause_sequence_enrollment
tools.description: Pause an active enrollment. The cron engine skips paused rows, but in-flight queue rows still dispatch on their normal tick.

tools.name: crm_pipeline_stage_summary
tools.description: Per-stage open-deal counts and $ totals for a pipeline. Default: first/oldest pipeline if pipeline_id omitted.

tools.name: crm_pipeline_velocity
tools.description: Approximate mean dwell time per stage (in days). Computed from stage_history JSON on each deal — best-effort, depends on stage-change paths populating that array.

tools.name: crm_quota_delete
tools.description: Delete one quota row by UUID (404 when not on this account). To change an amount, call crm_quota_set with the same scope and period instead.

tools.name: crm_quota_set
tools.description: Create or update a revenue quota for a period. user_id omitted/null = the TEAM quota; a user UUID (crm_list_users) = that rep's quota. period_start/period_end are YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive; amount_cents is a non-negative integer in CENTS ($150,000 = 15000000). UPSERTS by (scope, period): the same scope and period is updated, never duplicated (response action: created | updated). 400 on bad dates/amount or a user not on this account. Attainment against these rows is crm_report_attainment.

tools.name: crm_quotas_list
tools.description: List quota rows (scope team | user, period, amount_cents, label). user_id "team" lists only team quotas, a UUID only that rep's; active_on (YYYY-MM-DD) keeps quotas whose period contains that day. Newest period first.

tools.name: crm_reminder_cancel
tools.description: Cancel a scheduled reminder (sets status=cancelled).

tools.name: crm_reminder_list
tools.description: List agent reminders. Filter by ?status=scheduled|fired|cancelled and session_id.

tools.name: crm_reminder_schedule
tools.description: Schedule an agent reminder. fire_at is the ISO timestamp when the reminder fires. prompt is the message the agent will run as a user message at fire time.

tools.name: crm_reminder_update
tools.description: Update a scheduled reminder (cannot edit one that has already fired).

tools.name: crm_remove_dnc
tools.description: Reverse a DNC: soft-remove from suppression lists. Does NOT reset lifecycle_stage or lead_status — set those explicitly if re-engaging. Use sparingly; most "remove from DNC" requests are mistakes.

tools.name: crm_rep_win_leaderboard
tools.description: Reps ranked by closed-won deal count and total value over a rolling window, attributed by deal.owner_id. Won = the account's is_won status slugs plus the literal won / closed_won (echoed as won_statuses_counted). Dated by closed_at, the actual close stamp; rows still without one fall back to updated_at and are counted in dating.fallback_updated_at_rows. Ownerless wins are reported as one `unattributed` line, never dropped.

tools.name: crm_report_activity_summary
tools.description: Activity summary report (calls / emails / meetings / tasks counts over a date range). Defaults: last 7 days.

tools.name: crm_report_attainment
tools.description: "Are we on pace?" as a query. Closed-won value in the window against the crm_quotas rows covering it, per rep and for the team, plus pacing. Window defaults to the current calendar quarter. Returns window, won_statuses_counted, dating { basis: "closed_at", fallback_updated_at_rows }, quotas { team, by_user } (each with period_match exact | overlap and prorated_amount_cents), won { total_cents, deal_count, by_user, unattributed }, attainment { team: { quota_cents, won_cents, attainment_pct, gap_cents, projected_pct } | null, by_user }, pacing { days_elapsed, days_total, expected_share_pct, on_pace, weighted_open_forecast_cents, open_deals_due_in_window }. Won = the account's is_won slugs plus won / closed_won, dated by closed_at (fallback updated_at, counted); attribution = deal.owner_id (ownerless wins are the unattributed line); projected_pct adds the open weighted forecast (value x stage probability) for open deals whose close_date falls in the window. State the dating basis and the quota basis when quoting a number.

tools.name: crm_report_conversion_funnel
tools.description: Pipeline conversion funnel — counts and conversion rates per stage. Optional pipeline_id; omitted = all pipelines.

tools.name: crm_report_loss_reasons
tools.description: Closed-lost deals bucketed by lost_reason_code over a window: { rows: [{ code, count, total_value }] (count desc), uncoded: { count, total_value }, totals, lost_statuses_counted, dating }. `uncoded` is the closed-lost deals with NO code — reported as its own bucket so migration debt stays visible; never fold it into 'other'. Dating: the window filters closed_at, the actual close stamp every writer sets; a lost row still without one falls back to updated_at and dating.fallback_updated_at_rows says how many did (closes from before 2026-08-29 carry a backfilled close_date-or-updated_at stamp). Statuses counted as lost = the account's crm_statuses rows flagged is_lost, plus the literal slugs 'lost' and 'closed_lost'; the exact list used is echoed back as lost_statuses_counted.

tools.name: crm_report_pipeline_summary
tools.description: Pipeline summary — open deal counts and weighted/total $ per stage. Optional pipeline_id.

tools.name: crm_report_stage_transitions
tools.description: Stage-transition events (deal movements) in a date range. Useful for spotting bottlenecks.

tools.name: crm_resume_sequence_enrollment
tools.description: Resume a paused enrollment. The next-step cron picks it up on its next tick.

tools.name: crm_search_contacts
tools.description: Search contacts by name or email (full-text). Use BEFORE crm_create_contact to avoid duplicates. Returns the same shape as crm_list_contacts.

tools.name: crm_sequence_analytics
tools.description: Step-level performance roll-up for one sequence: per-step sent / opens / open_rate / clicks / click_rate / unsubscribes / bounces. Opens + clicks are deduped per enrollment. Plus totals and exit-reason breakdown.

tools.name: crm_sequence_clone
tools.description: Clone a sequence (settings + all steps) as a new inactive sequence. Optionally deactivate the source.

tools.name: crm_sequence_enroll_bulk
tools.description: Bulk-enroll many contacts in ONE sequence in one call. Same gates as single enrollment, applied per contact: suppression/DNC check, re-enrollment policy, the account's cross-sequence cap, and the merge-tag gate (a contact missing a referenced {{tag}} value fails that row, not the batch). The sequence must be is_active=true (400 otherwise) — and enrolling into an active sequence queues REAL email, so show the batch and get explicit approval first. Returns { enrolled, skipped_duplicates, failed: [{contact_id, reason}], enrollment_ids } — read the failed[] list back to the operator instead of reporting the batch as fully enrolled.

tools.name: crm_sequence_spam_check
tools.description: Heuristic deliverability check for sequence step content. Returns score (0-100, lower=better), band (clean / review / likely_filtered), warnings. Two modes: - Inline: pass subject + body (skip step_order) to score ad-hoc content. - Saved-step: pass step_order alone to load the step's content from the DB and score it. Use BEFORE crm_update_sequence_step / crm_update_sequence to avoid saving a cadence that'll tank in spam filters.

tools.name: crm_sequence_status
tools.description: Quick status snapshot of a sequence — name, is_active, step count, enrollment counts by status, and the 10 most-recent enrollments. Cheaper than crm_sequence_analytics when you just need the gist.

tools.name: crm_sequences_compare
tools.description: Side-by-side performance of non-archived sequences on the account. Per sequence: enrolled / active / replies / bookings / unique-opens / unique-clicks + the percentage rates. Sorted by reply_rate desc so the winner bubbles up.

tools.name: crm_set_custom_field_value
tools.description: Set (or clear, with value=null) ONE custom-field value on a contact/deal/company. Identify the field by field_key (slug) OR field_id (UUID). The sequence engine reads these values at send time to substitute {{field_key}} merge tags in email steps — write all required values BEFORE calling crm_enroll_sequence, otherwise enrollment is refused with a 422 listing the missing tags.

tools.name: crm_set_dnc
tools.description: Mark a contact Do-Not-Contact in one atomic write. Suppresses email globally, suppresses SMS (if phone present), flips lifecycle to unsubscribed, and exits any active sequence enrollments. Call this immediately when a prospect signals stop ("unsubscribe", "remove me", "stop emailing"). Idempotent — calling twice is safe.

tools.name: crm_set_user_signature
tools.description: Update a team member's HTML email signature. Pass null/empty to clear. ≤32 KB.

tools.name: crm_thread_for_contact
tools.description: Fetch the full Gmail/Outlook message thread for a specific CRM contact (across all matching emails on file).

tools.name: crm_unenroll_sequence
tools.description: Unenroll a contact from a sequence (sets status=exited). Use when the contact replied, asked to stop, or moved past the lifecycle stage the sequence targeted.

tools.name: crm_unlink_contact_company
tools.description: Remove a contact ↔ company link. No-op when not present.

tools.name: crm_unlink_deal_contact
tools.description: Remove a deal ↔ contact link. No-op when not present.

tools.name: crm_update_activity
tools.description: Update an existing CRM activity

tools.name: crm_update_company
tools.description: Update an existing CRM company

tools.name: crm_update_contact
tools.description: Update an existing CRM contact's details, including reassigning its OWNER. owner_id/assigned_to_id are public_users UUIDs validated against your account (a cross-account id is rejected). Pass unowned:true to clear the owner. Use this to fix a null/incorrect owner instead of asking a human to reassign in the dashboard.

tools.name: crm_update_custom_field
tools.description: Edit a custom field's label, type, options, requiredness, or sort order. The field_key is immutable.

tools.name: crm_update_deal
tools.description: Update a CRM deal — move stages, update value, change status, close date, ownership, and the why-it-closed fields. status: flipping to won/lost stamps closed_at (the actual close timestamp the dated reports filter on); back to open clears it. lost_reason_code is the aggregatable enum (no_decision | price | competitor | timing | no_budget | bad_fit | ghosted | other) — an unknown code is a 400 listing the vocabulary, and crm_report_loss_reasons GROUPs BY it. lost_reason / won_reason are free-text prose, max 500 chars (400 above, never truncated). Pass null to clear any of the three. owner_id / assigned_to_id reassign the deal to a user on this account (crm_list_users); assigned_to_id defaults to owner_id when only the owner is given; unowned: true clears both. stage_id is a stage UUID from crm_list_pipelines, never a stage name.

tools.name: crm_update_email_template
tools.description: Update a template's name/subject/body/category/share flag in place.

tools.name: crm_update_lead_status_option
tools.description: Update label/color/sort_order on an existing lead-status option. Slug is immutable. System rows accept label/color/sort updates.

tools.name: crm_update_sequence
tools.description: Update a sequence in place. Use is_active=true/false to activate or deactivate (no separate verb tool needed). When passing `steps` (full array), the existing steps are REPLACED — caller must include every step. Other fields update in place.

tools.name: crm_update_sequence_step
tools.description: Edit ONE step of a sequence in place (preferred over rewriting the whole steps array via crm_update_sequence when you only need to tweak one step). Use to swap a template_id, change a subject/body, adjust delay, or A/B variant. Subject/body/body_html support merge-tag fallbacks ({{first_name|there}}) and spintax ({Hi|Hey|Hello}) for inbox-fingerprint variation.

tools.name: customer_avatar_create
tools.description: Create a customer avatar (ICP). Accepts the full ICP spec EITHER flat at top level OR inside `avatar_data`. Flat fields: name (required), description, summary, age_range, gender, location, occupation, income_range, education_level, lifestyle, aspirations, typical_quote, background_story, avatar_image_url, background_story_image_url; arrays: values, interests, personality_traits, primary_goals, motivations, pain_points, challenges, frustrations, content_preferences, preferred_channels, tags. **Canonical buying_behavior shape** (rendered in the dashboard avatar editor's Behaviors tab): { trigger: string, // what event finally pushes them to buy decision_cycle: string, // how long the decision takes, with patterns stakeholders: string[], // who's involved (CFO sign-off, spouse, head of ops) preferred_intake: string, // demo / deck / sandbox / case study, etc. budget_range: string, // what they're willing to spend objections: string[] // common pushbacks ('takes too long', 'too expensive') } **Canonical online_behavior shape** (also rendered in the same tab): { social_platforms: string[], // LinkedIn, TikTok, Reddit, etc. device_preference: string, // mobile-first / desktop / mixed content_habits: string, // short vs long-form, video vs text, time-of-day information_sources: string[], // trusted newsletters / podcasts / forums daily_hours_online: string // free-form time estimate } Unknown keys on either object round-trip but don't render. populate_status is server-managed and hidden from responses.

tools.name: customer_avatar_delete
tools.description: Delete a customer avatar. Accepts `id` or `avatar_id`.

tools.name: customer_avatar_get
tools.description: Fetch one customer avatar. Accepts `id` or `avatar_id`.

tools.name: customer_avatar_list
tools.description: List customer avatars (ICPs).

tools.name: customer_avatar_populate
tools.description: LLM-enrich a sparse customer_avatar with GROUNDED context (Firecrawl scrapes + agent notes + brand guide). Refuses with `code: 'context_insufficient'` (400) if the account has no brand_style_guide AND no urls_to_scrape / search_queries / agent_notes are supplied. See entity_populate for the full contract — this is the same tool with entity_type='avatar' hardcoded. Enriches 20+ ICP columns: summary, age_range, gender, location, occupation, income_range, lifestyle, values[], interests[], primary_goals[], motivations[], pain_points[], frustrations[], aspirations, typical_quote, background_story, online_behavior{}, buying_behavior{}, content_preferences[], preferred_channels[]. Flips populate_status to 'populated' on success.

tools.name: customer_avatar_update
tools.description: Update a customer avatar. Accepts `id` or `avatar_id`. Fields can be passed flat or inside `avatar_data`; flat takes precedence. Only the fields you send change — omitted fields are left alone. To CLEAR a field, send it explicitly as [] or "" (populate can no longer do that for you). 5xx responses now name the offending field (e.g. P2000 'value too long for column "X"').

tools.name: customer_avatar_version_create
tools.description: Snapshot a customer avatar's CURRENT PERSISTED row into version history before an ICP rewrite. Returns 201 {data: version} with the allocated version_number (previous max + 1) and the captured avatar_data. The snapshot is read from the database, never from this call's body: change_message is the ONLY field the handler reads, so name, pain_points, buying_behavior or any other key sent here is accepted at 201 and silently dropped, and unsaved edits are NOT captured. Persist with customer_avatar_update first, then snapshot. Usually you do not need this tool at all: customer_avatar_update already writes an 'Auto-snapshot before update' version of the pre-edit row whenever a substantive field changes, so calling this first just adds a duplicate history entry; use it for a deliberately labelled checkpoint. The stored version `name` is copied off the avatar row. Concurrent snapshots contend on the [avatar_id, version_number] unique; the handler retries 5 times and then returns 503 'Failed to allocate version_number after retries', which is retryable rather than a bad request.

tools.name: customer_avatar_version_get
tools.description: Fetch one avatar snapshot in full, including the avatar_data blob that makes paging the list view expensive. Returns {data: {id, avatar_id, version_number, name, avatar_data, change_message, created_by, created_at}}. version_id is the snapshot ROW UUID from customer_avatar_version_list, NOT the integer version_number: passing 3 does not 404, it fails the uuid cast on the id column and comes back as a 500 'Failed to get avatar version'. A real UUID belonging to a different avatar does 404 'Version not found', because the lookup is scoped by avatar_id. avatar_data is the whole avatar row as it stood, including the id, account_id, created_at and updated_at of that moment plus operational columns like populate_status and lock_version; a restore strips exactly those first four and writes every other key back, so read this first to see exactly what customer_avatar_version_restore would overwrite.

tools.name: customer_avatar_version_list
tools.description: List saved snapshots of one customer avatar (ICP), newest version_number first. Returns {data: [{id, avatar_id, version_number, name, avatar_data, change_message, created_by, created_at}], pagination: {page, limit, total, total_pages}}. Every row carries the FULL avatar_data blob (no column selection), so a page of 20 is a heavy payload: take ids here and pull detail with customer_avatar_version_get. Traps: limit defaults to 20 and is silently clamped to 50, so asking for 200 returns 50 with no error, and page is floored to 1. The row's `id` (a UUID) is what version_get and version_restore take, NOT version_number. created_by is nullable and no route on this surface ever writes it, so it is always null. Most rows here are automatic; customer_avatar_update snapshots the pre-edit row by itself on any substantive change unless it was called with snapshot false. An avatar_id from another account returns 404 'Customer avatar not found', not 403; a non-UUID avatar_id fails the uuid cast and comes back 500.

tools.name: customer_avatar_version_restore
tools.description: OVERWRITES the live customer avatar with a snapshot. Every key stored in that version's avatar_data except id, account_id, created_at and updated_at is written straight back onto the row, so pain_points, buying_behavior, online_behavior, tags and any edit made since that snapshot are replaced, and operational columns captured in the blob (is_active, metadata, populate_status, populate_error, populated_at, lock_version) are rewound with them. There is NO confirm parameter and no body is parsed: the first call performs the restore. It is normally recoverable because the handler auto-snapshots the current state first and returns {data: restored avatar, restored_from_version, auto_snapshot_version}, and restoring auto_snapshot_version undoes it. TRAP ONE: if that auto-snapshot loses the version_number race 5 times it is abandoned and the restore proceeds ANYWAY while auto_snapshot_version still reports the number it was trying to use, so confirm the row with customer_avatar_version_list before treating it as your undo. TRAP TWO, wider than this avatar: the restore then nulls icp_matched_at on EVERY visitor row in the account, not only visitors matched to this ICP, forcing an account-wide re-match while each visitor's matched_icp_id is left pointing at its old ICP; that write is wrapped in a catch that only logs, so if it fails the route still returns 200 and stale ICP match timestamps silently survive the persona change. version_id is the snapshot ROW UUID; a version_number passed here fails the uuid cast and returns 500, not 404.

tools.name: customer_journey_avatar_link
tools.description: Attach a customer avatar (ICP) to a journey map and return the full refreshed link list. Writes customer_journey_avatars, the many-to-many table, NOT the legacy customer_journey_maps.target_avatar_id that customer_journey_link_to_avatar sets. Three behaviours worth knowing before you call it: the FIRST avatar linked to a journey is made primary whatever you pass, because a journey must have one; passing is_primary true DEMOTES the current primary in the same transaction; and the write is an upsert on (journey_id, avatar_id), so re-linking an avatar already attached is not an error and changes only is_primary. The avatar must belong to the same account or the call is a 400 'Avatar not found in this account'. Every row written through an API key is stamped added_by_agent true, which is how the dashboard distinguishes agent links from human ones.

tools.name: customer_journey_avatar_list
tools.description: List every customer avatar (ICP) linked to one journey map, as {data: [{id, avatar_id, is_primary, sort_order, added_by_agent, avatar: {name, avatar_image_url, occupation, summary}}]}. READ THIS BEFORE customer_journey_link_to_avatar: there are TWO avatar relationships on a journey and they are not the same thing. customer_journey_maps.target_avatar_id is the legacy single-persona column and is what customer_journey_link_to_avatar and customer_journey_update write; customer_journey_avatars is the many-to-many table with a primary and an explicit order, and this trio is the only way to reach it. This GET is not purely a read: it first backfills the legacy target_avatar_id into the link table, so on a journey that has only ever used the old column the first call materialises that link and returns it. `avatar` is null when the linked avatar row has since been deleted.

tools.name: customer_journey_avatar_unlink
tools.description: Detach one customer avatar from a journey map and return the refreshed link list. Removes the customer_journey_avatars row only; it does NOT clear the legacy customer_journey_maps.target_avatar_id, so a journey can still report a target persona through customer_journey_get after this call, and the next customer_journey_avatar_list will BACKFILL that legacy value straight back into the link table. To detach a persona completely, unlink here and also set target_avatar_id to null with customer_journey_link_to_avatar. An avatar that is not linked is a 404, not a silent success.

tools.name: customer_journey_create
tools.description: Create a customer journey map. Accepts fields flat OR inside `journey_data`. Fields: name (required), description, summary, stages (array of stage objects), metadata, tags, is_active. **Canonical stage shape** (the dashboard UI renders these keys; common synonyms are normalized server-side, but the canonical names are preferred): { name: string, // stage heading. Synonyms: stage, title description: string, emotions: string[], // chip pills. Synonym (singular): emotion pain_points: string[], // chip pills touchpoints: string[], // chip pills. Synonym: channels content_types: string[], opportunities: string[], // chip pills. Synonym: actions images?: [{id, url, prompt}] } Unknown keys are preserved but not rendered.

tools.name: customer_journey_delete
tools.description: Delete a customer journey map. Accepts `id` or `journey_id`.

tools.name: customer_journey_get
tools.description: Fetch one customer journey map. Accepts `id` or `journey_id`.

tools.name: customer_journey_link_to_avatar
tools.description: Link a customer journey map to a customer_avatar by setting target_avatar_id. Convenience wrapper around customer_journey_update — uses the canonical 'this journey is for THIS persona' relationship column. Pass null (or empty string) to unlink. The avatar must belong to the same account; cross-account UUIDs return 400. Mirror of before_after_grid_link_to_avatar.

tools.name: customer_journey_list
tools.description: List customer journey maps.

tools.name: customer_journey_populate
tools.description: LLM-enrich a sparse customer_journey_map with GROUNDED context. Same contract as entity_populate with entity_type='journey' hardcoded. Enriches: summary + stages[] with each stage having {name, description, emotions[], pain_points[], touchpoints[], content_types[], opportunities[]}. Flips populate_status to 'populated' on success.

tools.name: customer_journey_roi_get
tools.description: The ROI funnel for ONE customer journey: what the journey cost, who moved through it, and what it earned. Returns {journey_id, journey_name, window, attribution, funnel_mode, measured_totals, prior, content_sessions_unavailable, published_state, totals, stages[]} plus `iterations` when iterations is set. Each stage carries {stage_id, stage_name, order, contacts_any, contacts_furthest, deals_created, deals_won, spend_cents, revenue_cents, prior_contacts, measured, assets[]}. READ funnel_mode BEFORE QUOTING ANY STAGE NUMBER. 'measured' means journey_contact_enrollments rows exist (the enrollment cron writes them from stage checkpoints) and the stage counts are real progression. 'estimated' means the journey has NO checkpoints, so nothing is measuring it: the stage counts are an attribution proxy (who was touched by an asset attached to that stage), not a measured funnel, and `measured` is null on every stage with measured_totals null too. Null there means NOT MEASURED, not zero contacts. To move a journey to measured mode, put checkpoints on its stages. content_sessions_unavailable: true means the ClickHouse read FAILED and the analytics store was unreachable. It does NOT mean zero sessions. When it is true every content_item asset's metrics.sessions is null for that reason, and a null session count must never be reported or charted as 0. Other nulls, each with its reason: totals.roi is null when spend_cents is 0 (revenue over no spend is Infinity, which helps nobody) and is never 0-by-default; `prior` and every stage's prior_contacts are null when the window has no `from` to anchor a preceding period of equal length, which means 'no comparable period', not 'no movement'; published_state.latest_iteration_number and published_at are null when the journey was never published, and published_state.drift is then false because there is nothing to compare against, NOT because the journey is in sync. totals.mixed_currency true means deals in more than one currency were summed as raw cents, so the total is not a real amount in any single currency. contacts_any counts PARTICIPATION per stage, so one contact appears in every stage that touched them and the per-stage numbers deliberately overlap: never sum them into a total. contacts_furthest counts each contact once at their deepest stage and is what a funnel chart wants. Traps. The window is ALL TIME by default here, while customer_journey_roi_summary defaults to the last 30 days, so comparing the two without pinning from/to compares different windows. attribution defaults to 'last'. A journey_id from another account returns 404, not 403. Heavy payload: every stage lists every enabled asset with its metric chips, so shape it with _fields - but note _fields projects the response's FIRST array-valued property, which is `stages` normally and becomes `iterations` the moment iterations is true.

tools.name: customer_journey_roi_model_get
tools.description: Read a journey's STATED ROI model - the business case it was built against: {investment_cents, time_horizon_days, value_per_conversion_cents, target_conversions, baseline_conversions, assumptions, set_at, set_by}. Returns roi_model: null (with a hint) when none is set; never an empty object pretending to be a model. customer_journey_roi_get returns the same model plus model_vs_actual, so use this only when you want the model alone.

tools.name: customer_journey_roi_model_set
tools.description: Set the journey's STATED ROI model so the ROI report can put projected beside actual. This is the business case, in the account's own numbers: investment_cents (the program cost over the horizon), time_horizon_days (what the target and investment are stated for, 1-730), value_per_conversion_cents (what one won deal is assumed to be worth), target_conversions (wins expected over the horizon), optional baseline_conversions (pace BEFORE the program over the same horizon) and assumptions (free text; say where each number came from). Get these from the human or from account memory - never invent them, a fabricated business case is worse than none. Replaces the whole model; only the roi_model key of metadata is written, so goals and everything else in metadata are untouched. After setting it, customer_journey_roi_get returns model_vs_actual: the window's actual conversions, value and spend, each SCALED to the horizon as a pace (a linear extrapolation, named as such, not a forecast), and the variance against the model. Its `unavailable` list names every null and why: pace needs a bounded window (pass from/to), variance needs a non-zero target, ROI needs non-zero investment. Read it before quoting any of the numbers, and never report a null as zero.

tools.name: customer_journey_roi_summary
tools.description: Cross-journey triage: every non-archived journey on the account with its funnel, totals, prior-period deltas and health issues, in one batched read. Start here, then pull the loser in full with customer_journey_roi_get. Returns {window, truncated, journeys[], summary{journeys, total_spend_cents, total_revenue_cents, total_leads, total_deals_won}}; each journey carries {journey_id, name, description_preview, is_active, updated_at, stage_count, avatars, avatar_count, asset_thumbs, asset_count, funnel_mode, stages[], totals, prior, issues[]}. funnel_mode per journey means the same thing it does on customer_journey_roi_get: 'measured' = journey_contact_enrollments rows exist and the stage counts are real progression; 'estimated' = the journey has no checkpoints, so the counts are an attribution proxy and not a measured funnel. On estimated journeys enrolled_in_stage is null on every stage, and that null means THIS JOURNEY IS NOT MEASURED, not that zero contacts are sitting there. Other nulls: totals.roi is null when spend_cents is 0, never 0; `prior` and every stage's prior_contacts are null when the window has no `from` to anchor a preceding period. THE TRAP THAT MATTERS HERE. This endpoint backs a list page, so it must render something rather than fail: the attribution read, the enrollment rollup, the ppc spend query, the thumbnail lookups and each journey's revenue rollup degrade INDEPENDENTLY to empty on error. `degraded_reads` names which ones did, and it is the field to check BEFORE quoting any number here. Empty means every read succeeded. Non-empty means at least one figure is a floor rather than a fact, and a journey reading 0 leads may simply not have been measured - confirm that journey with customer_journey_roi_get, which does not swallow the attribution read. Other traps: the window defaults to the LAST 30 DAYS when both from and to are omitted, unlike customer_journey_roi_get which is all-time, so pin from/to on both before comparing them. The cap is 24 journeys ordered by updated_at desc with truncated:true when more exist, and there is NO paging parameter, so on a big account this is the 24 most recently touched journeys and nothing else. issues[] is capped at 2 per journey and is a triage hint, not an audit. Heavy payload (every journey's full stage array plus avatars and thumbnails), so shape it with _fields, which projects the `journeys` elements.

tools.name: customer_journey_stage_add
tools.description: Append or insert ONE stage without touching the others. Pass `stage` with the canonical shape {name, description, emotions[], pain_points[], touchpoints[], content_types[], opportunities[]}; `at_index` inserts at a position (default: append). A stage_id is minted for you and returned - do not invent one. Returns 409 lock_conflict if the journey changed while you were composing, in which case NOTHING was written and you should re-read and retry.

tools.name: customer_journey_stage_asset_attach
tools.description: LINK a piece of content that ALREADY EXISTS to a journey stage. asset_type must be one of email_campaign, ppc_campaign, social_post, content_item, email_sequence, cold_email_campaign, site_page (a website page - the CONVERT leg's landing pages) or media_asset (a Media Library video or design), and asset_id must be a record of that type in the same account - a cross-account or missing id is rejected, never silently attached; site_page ownership is checked through the page's project. There is deliberately no lead_magnet type: a lead magnet's materialized form IS a site_page or content_item, so brief it as the type it will become. Use this when the content exists; use customer_journey_stage_asset_propose to write a brief for content that does not. Attaching is what puts the asset into the journey's ROI calculation, since only enabled attachments with a real asset_id can carry attributed revenue. Upserts on (journey_id, stage_id, asset_type, asset_id), so attaching twice is safe.

tools.name: customer_journey_stage_asset_detach
tools.description: Remove one stage asset row - an attachment or a proposal - from a journey stage. `id` is the stage-asset ROW id from customer_journey_stage_assets_list, not the asset's own id, and the underlying content record is NOT deleted; only the link to this stage goes. Prefer customer_journey_stage_asset_materialize with status 'dismissed' when you are rejecting a brief, so the decision stays on the record instead of vanishing.

tools.name: customer_journey_stage_asset_materialize
tools.description: Turn a proposal into a real link, or toggle a stage asset. Three independent things this PATCH can do, by the field you send. `asset_id` MATERIALIZES a proposal: the brief becomes a link to the record you just created, and status flips to 'attached'. It REFUSES to overwrite a row that already references an asset, so it can never silently re-point a live attachment. `enabled` is the canvas checkbox and controls whether the asset counts toward journey ROI. `status` moves a row between attached, proposed and dismissed - dismiss a brief you have decided against rather than deleting it, so the decision stays visible. `id` is the stage-asset ROW id from customer_journey_stage_assets_list, not the asset's own id.

tools.name: customer_journey_stage_asset_propose
tools.description: WRITE A BRIEF for an asset a stage needs but the account does not have yet. This MENTIONS AND WRITES the asset; it does NOT produce it. The row is stored with asset_id NULL and status 'proposed', and someone (human or agent) later creates the real thing and calls customer_journey_stage_asset_materialize to link it. proposal.title is required; brief, channel and cta are the rest of the documented shape, and the brief is where the actual thinking goes - the job this asset does at THIS stage, the key message, the format and length. Write the hook, do not describe it: these briefs are rendered to prospects on the public journey page, so a brief reading 'a case study about results' is a failed proposal. Pass `proposals: [...]` to send 1-50 in one call, which is how you brief a whole stage or a whole journey at once.

tools.name: customer_journey_stage_assets_list
tools.description: List a journey's per-stage assets: both the attachments (asset_id set - real content already in the account) and the proposals (asset_id NULL - a written brief for content that does not exist yet). Pass stage_id to scope to one stage. Each row carries {id, stage_id, asset_type, asset_id, enabled, status, sort_order, proposed_by_agent, proposal, asset} where `asset` is the resolved name/title of a linked record, or null when the target was deleted. THIS IS THE COVERAGE MAP: attachments are what exists, proposals are the gaps someone has written a brief for, and a stage with neither is a gap nobody has even named. Rows whose stage_id no longer appears in the journey's stages blob are filtered out on read rather than returned as orphans. Only `enabled` rows count toward journey ROI.

tools.name: customer_journey_stage_contacts
tools.description: WHO is sitting in one journey stage, longest-waiting first - the drill-down behind a stage's contact count. Returns {journey_id, stage_id, mode, stuck_days, total, capped, contacts[{contact_id, name, email, entered_at, days_in_stage}]}. Use it to turn 'stage 3 is where they die' into a list of people to call. mode is the honesty flag. 'measured' = enrollment rows exist, so these are the CURRENT occupants of the stage (completed journeys excluded, because they are done rather than stuck) and entered_at is the real entered_stage_at. 'estimated' = the journey has no enrollment rows, so these are contacts attributed to that stage's enabled assets and entered_at is their earliest attribution touch, a PROXY for entry: the contact may never have been in that stage at all. Do not describe estimated days_in_stage as time spent in the stage. The estimated branch also ignores dates entirely and reads attribution ALL-TIME, so stuck_days is the only narrowing you get there. intent adds {intent_score 0-100, intent_band, intent_signals} per contact plus a top-level intent_ch_unavailable. intent_band null means scored but below both bands, NOT unscored. intent_ch_unavailable true means the ClickHouse leg of the scorer was unreachable, so the scores were computed WITHOUT session signals and are lower than they should be; it does not mean those contacts had no sessions. If the enrichment fails outright the response comes back with intent:false and intent_error:true and NO intent fields at all rather than a 500 - a missing intent_score is a failed read, never a zero score. Traps: stage_id must be the in-blob stage_id from customer_journey_get, and an unknown one returns 404, it does NOT return an empty list. Hard cap of 200 rows with no paging; `total` and `capped` report the real size, so narrow with stuck_days rather than assuming 200 is all of them. sort:'intent' only re-orders the page ALREADY taken longest-first, so it cannot surface a hot contact sitting at row 201. stuck_days that is non-numeric or <= 0 is silently NO filter rather than an error, and anything above 3650 is clamped. A journey_id from another account returns 404, not 403. _fields projects the `contacts` elements.

tools.name: customer_journey_stage_delete
tools.description: Remove ONE stage from a journey. The response reports stage_assets_orphaned: stage-asset rows keyed to a deleted stage are filtered out on read rather than deleted, so they linger invisibly, and a non-zero count means attachments and briefs just became unreachable. Check customer_journey_stage_assets_list before deleting a stage you did not create. Returns 409 lock_conflict if the journey moved underneath you, in which case nothing was written.

tools.name: customer_journey_stage_list
tools.description: List a journey's stages as a THIN projection: {index, stage_id, name, description, checkpoint_count, image_count, video_count} plus the journey's lock_version. Start here rather than with customer_journey_get when what you need is a stage_id to address a stage by - the full stages blob carries every image, video and checkpoint and is a heavy payload. stage_id is the join key for stage assets, checkpoints and stage video; a stage whose stage_id comes back null is invisible to every tool that addresses stages by id and needs repairing before you can attach anything to it.

tools.name: customer_journey_stage_update
tools.description: Edit ONE stage. Every field you do not send is left exactly as it was, INCLUDING images, videos and primary_media - so this is the safe way to change a description without losing generated media, which a whole-blob PATCH will do if you do not echo everything back. stage_id is deliberately not writable: it is the join key for this stage's assets and checkpoints, and changing it orphans all of them. SETTING CHECKPOINTS IS WHAT MAKES A JOURNEY MEASURABLE. Each checkpoint is {name, is_exit, signal:{type, ...}} where type is page_visit (path, match, project_id), form_submit (form_id), email_click / email_open (campaign_id), call (voice_number_id, direction), deal_stage (pipeline_id, stage_id), deal_won, or asset_touch. AT MOST ONE is_exit per stage - it is the graduation criterion, and two would leave the engine with no single definition of 'moved on'. A journey only reports funnel_mode 'measured' when stage 1 has a checkpoint and some stage has an exit; without that it stays on the attribution proxy. Malformed signals are REJECTED here with invalid_checkpoint rather than accepted and then silently dropped by the engine, which would leave you believing you had set a criterion that never fires. Sending `checkpoints` REPLACES that stage's whole array.

tools.name: customer_journey_stage_video_generate
tools.description: Generate a cinematic AI clip for ONE journey stage and store it on the stage. The prompt is COMPOSED FOR YOU from the stage's own name, description, emotions, pain points and touchpoints plus the journey's primary ICP - pass extra_direction only to steer, not to restate what the stage already says. The stage's hero image drives image-to-video, so the person established in the stage imagery carries into the clip. Writes stage.videos[] {id, url, prompt, posterUrl, createdAt} and sets primary_media to 'video' ONLY when that key is absent, so a user's explicit media choice is never overwritten. 16:9, unlike marketing_generate_video's 9:16 social default. THE BILLING CONTRACT, read before retrying anything. Renders can take minutes. A long one returns {code: 'still_generating', job_id} as a NORMAL 200 outcome - the render is real, BILLED ONCE, and still running. Call this tool again with resume_job_id set to that job_id to pick the SAME render up. A retry WITHOUT resume_job_id starts a second billed render. Never treat still_generating as a failure and never resubmit blind. Gated by the video plan: Premium plus the 20-clip monthly cap, returning 402 - the same meter as marketing_generate_video and a DIFFERENT meter from images (which 429 on the image_generations allowance). An unknown journey_id or stage_id is refused with 404 BEFORE any render starts, so a misaddressed call costs nothing.

tools.name: customer_journey_update
tools.description: Update a customer journey map. Accepts `id` or `journey_id`. Fields flat or inside `journey_data`; flat takes precedence. Only the fields you send change. WRITING `stages` REPLACES THE WHOLE BLOB — re-send each stage’s existing `stage_id`, `images`, `videos`, `primary_media` and `checkpoints` or they are lost, and a changed `stage_id` orphans that stage’s attached assets and checkpoints. To edit one stage, read the journey first and send the full array back with your one change.

tools.name: customer_journey_version_create
tools.description: Snapshot a customer journey map's CURRENT persisted state into a new version row and return it. Takes the row as it stands in the database, not anything you pass: `change_message` is the only body field read, and it is a label for humans reading the history. Call this before any rewrite you might want to undo - especially before customer_journey_update with a new `stages` array, which replaces the whole blob. version_number is allocated MAX+1 with a bounded retry, so concurrent snapshots do not collide.

tools.name: customer_journey_version_get
tools.description: Fetch one journey snapshot in full, including its complete stages blob. `version_id` is the snapshot ROW UUID from customer_journey_version_list, NOT version_number - a version_number here fails the uuid cast and returns 500, not 404. Read this before restoring so you know what the restore will write.

tools.name: customer_journey_version_list
tools.description: List saved snapshots of one customer journey map, newest version_number first. Returns {data: [{id, journey_map_id, version_number, name, description, stages, metadata, change_message, created_by, created_at}], pagination}. Every row carries the FULL stages blob, so a page of 20 is a heavy payload - take ids here and pull one with customer_journey_version_get, or shape this call with _fields. Traps: limit defaults to 20 and is silently clamped to 50; page is floored to 1. The row's `id` (a UUID) is what version_get and version_restore take, NOT version_number. created_by is nullable and no route writes it, so it is always null. A journey_id from another account returns 404, not 403; a non-UUID journey_id fails the uuid cast and returns 500.

tools.name: customer_journey_version_restore
tools.description: OVERWRITES the live journey with a snapshot. name, description, stages and metadata are written straight back onto the row, so every edit made since that snapshot is replaced. There is NO confirm parameter and no body is parsed: the FIRST call performs the restore. Confirm with the human before calling it. The handler auto-snapshots current state first and returns {data, restored_from_version, auto_snapshot_version}, so restoring auto_snapshot_version undoes it - but a returned number is not proof the backup row exists, so verify with customer_journey_version_list before relying on it. RESTORING `stages` RESTORES ITS stage_id VALUES: any stage whose id differs from the live one loses the stage assets and checkpoints keyed to the live id, and any stage added since the snapshot disappears along with everything attached to it. Read customer_journey_version_get first. version_id is the snapshot ROW UUID, not version_number.

tools.name: database_describe
tools.description: Describe one table — column names, types, nullability, defaults.

tools.name: database_execute
tools.description: Run a write SQL statement (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/CREATE/ALTER). Use with care — destructive operations are not sandboxed.

tools.name: database_provision
tools.description: Provision a Hiveku-managed Supabase database for the project. ASYNC: returns 202 with { job_id } within a second (Supabase takes 1-3 minutes to become healthy). Poll job_status_get({ job_id, wait_seconds: 20 }) until terminal; the job result carries projectRef, secretsProvisioned[] and supportsSupabaseClient. Single-flight and idempotent: calling again while the job runs returns the SAME job_id (reused: true); calling after completion returns 200 { alreadyProvisioned: true } and never rotates the database password. Do NOT call database_query/database_execute until the job has succeeded. If a direct-Postgres tool later reports bad_credentials, call database_repair.

tools.name: database_query
tools.description: Run a read-only SQL query against the project database. Returns rows. Refuses DDL/DML — use database_execute for writes.

tools.name: database_repair
tools.description: Re-mint and re-store the Hiveku-managed Supabase Postgres password for the project, then prove the stored DATABASE_URL_* strings authenticate before persisting them. Use when database_status says authenticates:false / a direct-Postgres tool returns code bad_credentials (28P01) — the database is fine, the stored credential is wrong (typically two provision runs raced). Migrations, row tools and the Management-API lanes keep working meanwhile. Pass force:true to rotate even when the current string still authenticates.

tools.name: database_status
tools.description: Get the project's database connection state. Per branch (dev/prod): has_connection (a string is stored) AND authenticates (a live SELECT 1 through it succeeded) — read authenticates; a stored string that fails with bad_credentials means the password is wrong (two provisions raced), call database_repair. Also reports provision_pending when a database_provision job is still running.

tools.name: database_tables
tools.description: List all tables in the project database.

tools.name: dataforseo_labs_available_filters
tools.description: Here you will find all the necessary information about filters that can be used with DataForSEO Labs API endpoints. Please, keep in mind that filters are associated with a certain object in the result array, and should be specified accordingly.

tools.name: dataforseo_labs_bulk_keyword_difficulty
tools.description: This endpoint will provide you with the Keyword Difficulty metric for a maximum of 1,000 keywords in one API request. Keyword Difficulty stands for the relative difficulty of ranking in the first top-10 organic results for the related keyword. Keyword Difficulty in DataForSEO API responses indicates the chance of getting in top-10 organic results for a keyword on a logarithmic scale from 0 to 100.

tools.name: dataforseo_labs_bulk_traffic_estimation
tools.description: This endpoint will provide you with estimated monthly traffic volumes for up to 1,000 domains, subdomains, or webpages. Along with organic search traffic estimations, you will also get separate values for paid search, featured snippet, and local pack results.

tools.name: dataforseo_labs_google_competitors_domain
tools.description: This endpoint will provide you with a full overview of ranking and traffic data of the competitor domains from organic and paid search. In addition to that, you will get the metrics specific to the keywords both competitor domains and your domain rank for within the same SERP.

tools.name: dataforseo_labs_google_domain_intersection
tools.description: This endpoint will provide you with the keywords for which both specified domains rank within the same SERP. You will get search volume, competition, cost-per-click and impressions data on each intersecting keyword. Along with that, you will get data on the first and second domain's SERP element discovered for this keyword, as well as the estimated traffic volume and cost of ad traffic.

tools.name: dataforseo_labs_google_domain_rank_overview
tools.description: This endpoint will provide you with ranking and traffic data from organic and paid search for the specified domain. You will be able to review the domain ranking distribution in SERPs as well as estimated monthly traffic volume for both organic and paid results.

tools.name: dataforseo_labs_google_historical_keyword_data
tools.description: This endpoint provides Google historical keyword data for specified keywords, including search volume, cost-per-click, competition values for paid search, monthly searches, and search volume trends. You can get historical keyword data since August, 2021, depending on keywords along with location and language combination

tools.name: dataforseo_labs_google_historical_rank_overview
tools.description: This endpoint will provide you with historical data on rankings and traffic of the specified domain, such as domain ranking distribution in SERPs and estimated monthly traffic volume for both organic and paid results

tools.name: dataforseo_labs_google_historical_serp
tools.description: This endpoint will provide you with Google SERPs collected within the specified time frame. You will also receive a complete overview of featured snippets and other extra elements that were present within the specified dates. The data will allow you to analyze the dynamics of keyword rankings over time for the specified keyword and location.

tools.name: dataforseo_labs_google_keyword_ideas
tools.description: The Keyword Ideas provides search terms that are relevant to the product or service categories of the specified keywords. The algorithm selects the keywords which fall into the same categories as the seed keywords specified in a POST array. As a result, you will get a list of relevant keyword ideas for up to 200 seed keywords. Along with each keyword idea, you will get its search volume rate for the last month, search volume trend for the previous 12 months, as well as current cost-per-click and competition values. Moreover, this endpoint supplies minimum, maximum and average values of daily impressions, clicks and CPC for each result.

tools.name: dataforseo_labs_google_keyword_overview
tools.description: This endpoint provides Google keyword data for specified keywords. For each keyword, you will receive current cost-per-click, competition values for paid search, search volume, search intent, monthly searches

tools.name: dataforseo_labs_google_keyword_suggestions
tools.description: The Keyword Suggestions provides search queries that include the specified seed keyword. The algorithm is based on the full-text search for the specified keyword and therefore returns only those search terms that contain the keyword you set in the POST array with additional words before, after, or within the specified key phrase. Returned keyword suggestions can contain the words from the specified key phrase in a sequence different from the one you specify. As a result, you will get a list of long-tail keywords with each keyword in the list matching the specified search term. Along with each suggested keyword, you will get its search volume rate for the last month, search volume trend for the previous 12 months, as well as current cost-per-click and competition values. Moreover, this endpoint supplies minimum, maximum and average values of daily impressions, clicks and CPC for each result.

tools.name: dataforseo_labs_google_keywords_for_site
tools.description: The Keywords For Site endpoint will provide you with a list of keywords relevant to the target domain. Each keyword is supplied with relevant, search volume data for the last month, cost-per-click, competition

tools.name: dataforseo_labs_google_page_intersection
tools.description: This endpoint will provide you with the keywords for which specified pages rank within the same SERP. You will get search volume, competition, cost-per-click and impressions data on each intersecting keyword. Along with that, you will get data on SERP elements that specified pages rank for in search results, as well as the estimated traffic volume and cost of ad traffic. Page Intersection endpoint supports organic, paid, local pack and featured snippet results. Find keywords several webpages rank for: If you would like to get the keywords several pages rank for, you need to specify webpages only in the pages object. This way, you will receive intersected ranked keywords for the specified URLs. Find keywords your competitors rank for but you do not: If you would like to receive all keywords several pages rank for, but particular pages do not, you need to use the exclude_pages array as well. This way you will receive the keywords for which the URLs from the pages object rank for, but the URLs from the exclude_pages array do not

tools.name: dataforseo_labs_google_ranked_keywords
tools.description: This endpoint will provide you with the list of keywords that any domain or webpage is ranking for. You will also get SERP elements related to the keyword position, as well as impressions, monthly searches and other data relevant to the returned keywords.

tools.name: dataforseo_labs_google_related_keywords
tools.description: The Related Keywords endpoint provides keywords appearing in the "searches related to" SERP element You can get up to 4680 keyword ideas by specifying the search depth. Each related keyword comes with the list of relevant product categories, search volume rate for the last month, search volume trend for the previous 12 months, as well as current cost-per-click and competition values. Moreover, this endpoint supplies minimum, maximum and average values of daily impressions, clicks and CPC for each result. Datasource: DataForSEO SERPs Database Search algorithm: depth-first search for queries appearing in the "search related to" element of SERP for the specified seed keyword.

tools.name: dataforseo_labs_google_serp_competitors
tools.description: This endpoint will provide you with a list of domains ranking for the keywords you specify. You will also get SERP rankings, rating, estimated traffic volume, and visibility values the provided domains gain from the specified keywords.

tools.name: dataforseo_labs_google_subdomains
tools.description: This endpoint will provide you with a list of subdomains of the specified domain, along with the ranking distribution across organic and paid search. In addition to that, you will also get the estimated traffic volume of subdomains based on search volume.

tools.name: dataforseo_labs_google_top_searches
tools.description: The Top Searches endpoint of DataForSEO Labs API can provide you with over 7 billion keywords from the DataForSEO Keyword Database. Each keyword in the API response is provided with a set of relevant keyword data with Google Ads metrics

tools.name: dataforseo_labs_search_intent
tools.description: This endpoint will provide you with search intent data for up to 1,000 keywords. For each keyword that you specify when setting a task, the API will return the keyword's search intent and intent probability. Besides the highest probable search intent, the results will also provide you with other likely search intent(s) and their probability. Based on keyword data and search results data, our system has been trained to detect four types of search intent: informational, navigational, commercial, transactional.

tools.name: delete_task
tools.description: Delete a task by ID

tools.name: deploy_changes
tools.description: List the files that have changed since the last deploy of the specified tier (dev-preview / staging / production).

tools.name: deploy_diff
tools.description: PREVIEW what a deploy will change — the exact file + route diff between what a deploy WOULD ship and what is currently live on a tier. Read-only; never deploys. Call this before deploy_site to answer 'is it safe to deploy / what am I about to change?'. Sides of the diff: • to-ship (left): omit `local` → the DB is_current text set (exactly what deploy_site ships). Pass `local: [{path,sha256}]` → preview a push you have NOT saved yet. • deployed (right): resolved newest-wins from the exact version manifest of the last deploy, else the post-deploy checkpoint, else a timestamp proxy, else never_deployed. THE CONTRACT — data.has_changes is TRUE | FALSE | null: • false → a CONFIDENT all-clear: exact baseline AND code AND assets all match. Safe to skip the deploy. • true → a concrete change was found (never_deployed ⇒ everything is new ⇒ true). • null → we CANNOT prove no-change: approximate/timestamp basis, GitHub-source project, or an unknown asset baseline. Do NOT treat an empty diff as 'nothing will change' — read data.confidence + data.basis + data.warnings. Returns data.{basis, confidence, source_of_truth, summary{changed,added,deleted,unchanged,total_to_ship}, files{changed,added,deleted}, assets{changed,added,deleted,confidence}, routes{added,modified,removed,details,non_route_file_changes}, warnings}. Routes are a STATIC heuristic from changed src/app files; shared component/lib changes land under non_route_file_changes, not invented routes. warnings may include reserved_cdn_prefix_page_collision — a shipping PAGE sits under a reserved CDN asset prefix (videos/, media/, images/, ...) and will 403 on the deployed URL; rename the route.

tools.name: deploy_doctor
tools.description: DIAGNOSE a deployed environment that isn't serving correctly — 403/404 on the live URL, blank pages, 'deploy said ready but the site is broken'. Read-only; checks the FULL serving path that you cannot see from other tools: • CloudFront wiring — is the default behavior pointing at the right origin kind for this project (Lambda for framework apps, S3 for static)? Leftover static config on an SSR distribution? • The attached CloudFront Function — a static-era function rewriting page paths against a Lambda origin is the classic 'every route 404s but /_next/* chunks work' signature. • Serving diff — the same routes requested through the CDN AND directly against the origin. origin-200/CDN-broken = CloudFront problem; both-broken = build/artifact problem. This distinction is the single most valuable diagnostic: it tells you whether to fix the project or escalate the platform. • Project-tree red flags — framework source without package.json (deploys misclassify as static), reserved-prefix page collisions, suspiciously fast 'builds'. Returns { healthy, findings: [{severity, code, detail, fix}], serving: {cdn, origin_direct}, distribution, recent_deployments }. Relay CRITICAL findings' fix text verbatim — each names the exact next action. Use this INSTEAD of guessing when a deployed URL misbehaves; do not propose deleting/recreating infrastructure without running it first.

tools.name: deploy_get
tools.description: Get one deployment by ID, including URL, status, error, build_logs, and timing. The id slot accepts BOTH forms the deployment row carries: • UUID `id` (what deploy_site / deploy_run return as `deploy_id`) • String `deployment_id` (e.g. 'olympus-1779590857819-6joz6p' — what deploy_history / deploy_status surface) Pass either to `deployment_id`; the route resolves whichever matches. Returns both fields in the response so downstream calls have whatever form they need. Response shape: `{ data: Deployment }` where Deployment is `{ id, deploy_id, deployment_id, environment, status, url, preview_url (===url), error, build_logs, build_time_ms, environment_vars, branch, commit_hash, commit_message, author, triggered_by, started_at, completed_at, created_at }`. `data.status` is always present (column has default='queued'); read it directly. The same per-deployment field set is emitted by deploy_status (under data[] and most_recent) and deploy_site (under data) — one parser handles all three.

tools.name: deploy_history
tools.description: List a project's deployment history with optional filters (environment / status / triggered_by).

tools.name: deploy_run
tools.description: Trigger a DEV-PREVIEW deploy: syncs the project to its Fly preview container, then enqueues a dev build job. The fast path, for iteration. ★ THIS TOOL ONLY DOES dev-preview. It is not a tier selector. The route pins ALLOWED_TIERS to dev-preview and answers 403 for 'production' or 'staging' — the enum used to advertise 'production' anyway, so the one value most likely to be tried was the one guaranteed to fail. For the Lambda + CloudFront tiers use deploy_site({ environment: 'development' | 'staging' | 'production' }). ★ dev-preview HERE IS NOT THE SAME TIER deploy_site means by that name. This is the Fly preview container plus a dev build job; deploy_site builds a separate Lambda artifact and treats dev-preview as a deprecated alias for its own tier. The same token means two different things in the two tools, so read the tool name before the value. agent_codename is an optional audit label recorded on the deployment row. Watch it land with deploy_subscribe({ project_id, deployment_id, wait_seconds: 20 }) or deploy_get.

tools.name: deploy_site
tools.description: Deploy the project to one of the three AWS serverless (Lambda + CloudFront) environments. **GitHub is NOT required** — this pulls files straight from builder_code_versions (the same DB that project_file_save writes to). Works on every project, GitHub-connected or not. Environments — each routes to a distinct deployment service: • development (default, SAFE) — fast turn-around for low-risk experiments.
