Use this first. • staging — must be enabled per project in the hosting dashboard first; calling this on a project where staging_enabled=false returns 412 with code "staging_not_enabled". • production — full CodeBuild → CloudFront. Slowest path; reserve for go-live. NEVER pick this just to "test the deploy flow" — use development for that. END-TO-END LIFECYCLE (preview → production): 1. Edit. project_file_save({sync_preview:true}) or project_files_bulk_save updates the live PREVIEW (Fly container, instant) AND builder_code_versions. 2. Eyeball. preview_screenshot({path:"/..."}) → check the rendered UI before any Lambda spend. 3. Iterate on development. deploy_site({environment:"development"}). Lives at *.development.hiveku-app.com. 4. (Optional) Promote to staging. deploy_site({environment:"staging"}) — requires staging_enabled=true. 5. Go to production. deploy_site({environment:"production"}). This builds a SEPARATE Lambda artifact — production and development DO NOT share code. **Every file change you want in production (including middleware.ts, next.config.js, env-driven changes) requires its own deploy_site({environment:"production"}) call.** There is no auto-promote from development or staging to production. project_file_save reaches the preview INSTANTLY but does NOT touch any of the Lambda environments — those only update when you deploy_site. 6. Custom domain. After the first production deploy succeeds, call project_domains_add({project_id, domain, tier:"production"}) and surface the returned DNS records to the user. Until DNS verifies and SSL issues, the *.hiveku-app.com URL is the only live production address. NOT this tool: the LIVE PREVIEW (Fly container at hvk-<hash>.preview.hiveku.com) is updated INSTANTLY via project_file_save({sync_preview: true}) or preview_sync. That is a separate surface — instant, no build, no Lambda. Use preview_sync for "see my edit live"; use deploy_site only when you want a real Lambda artifact behind one of the three environment subdomains. Returns deployment_id; poll deploy_get({project_id, deployment_id}) for status. READ data.warnings[] when present — e.g. reserved_cdn_prefix_page_collision means a shipping PAGE sits under a reserved CDN asset prefix (videos/, media/, images/, ...) and WILL 403 on the deployed URL; rename the route (see hiveku_docs "Reserved CDN Asset Path Prefixes"). ENGINES REFUSAL (422): the project's package.json is the ONLY source of truth. If engines.node provably excludes the platform's Node (e.g. ">=22" on a Node-20 platform), the deploy is REFUSED up front with {code:"engines_unsatisfied", hint} instead of burning a build that dies later. The fix is in the project: change engines.node to a range that includes Node 20 (e.g. ">=20") or remove a stale constraint — do not retry unchanged. LOCKFILE REFUSAL (422): package.json is the truth. a 422 whose details carry {code:"lockfile_out_of_sync", hint, mismatches:[{package, declared, locked}]} (the proxy nests the route body under details: read details.hint and details.mismatches) means the project's lockfile (pnpm-lock.yaml > yarn.lock > package-lock.json, first found wins) resolves a DIFFERENT framework version (next, react, react-dom, vite) than package.json declares. A lockfile is evidence of a PAST install and is routinely stale on this platform: manifests are edited in the browser and by agents with no local npm, so nothing regenerates the lock. The fix is IN THE PROJECT: update package.json to the versions you actually intend, or delete the lockfile (the project then deploys with a plain install and no lockfile; the preview never writes a lockfile back). NEVER "fix" this by editing the lockfile by hand, and NEVER downgrade package.json to match the lockfile - that is exactly how a healthy Next 16 project gets pinned back into a CVE. Only a PROVABLE disagreement refuses (an exact pin that differs, a locked major the range cannot admit, a locked version below the declared floor, or a framework package the lock does not carry); an unparseable lockfile is reported as uncertain and never blocks. Surface hint and every mismatches row (package: declared vs locked) verbatim to the user; do not retry unchanged. POST-DEPLOY SMOKE VERIFICATION: after the build, the pipeline itself requests the live URL (homepage + sample routes) through the CDN and FAILS the deploy if they return 403/404/5xx — a deploy that reports success is verified actually serving. If a deploy fails with 'live site FAILS verification', the artifacts deployed but the serving path is broken: run deploy_doctor({project_id, environment}) for the diagnosis instead of blindly retrying. WHICH TREE SHIPS (Hiveku-native branches): the environment BINDINGS decide, not this call. Read project_vcs_env_bindings first. production ALWAYS ships `main` and can never be pointed at a branch. development and staging ship the branch they are bound to (project_vcs_env_bind), or `main` when unbound. A bound branch with uncommitted working-tree edits is PROMOTED server-side (a commit is recorded on the branch) before its tree is pinned, so what ships is always a commit. To get branch work into production: open a PR (project_vcs_pr_create), merge it (project_vcs_pr_merge), then deploy_site({environment:"production"}). `branch` here is a CHECK, not a selector: pass the branch you believe the tier serves and the server refuses a mismatch instead of shipping the wrong tree - 409 code "branch_not_bound" (dev/staging: the tier is bound elsewhere, or unbound and tracking main; the hint names project_vcs_env_bind) or 400 code "production_immutable" (any non-main branch on production). A bound tier also refuses deployFromGitHub with 409 "binding_source_conflict". GitHub-connected projects keep the legacy meaning of `branch` (a GitHub branch label).

tools.name: deploy_status
tools.description: List recent deployments for a project, newest first. To check 'what is the status of MY latest deploy', read `most_recent.status` — a singleton convenience that mirrors deploy_get's shape and avoids the data-is-array-not-object trap. Response shape (consistent across calls — same field names as deploy_get + deploy_site): { data: Deployment[] // history, newest first (max 20 by default) most_recent: Deployment|null // === data[0]; null if no deploys ever pagination: { page, limit, total, pages } } Each Deployment object: { id, deploy_id (===id), deployment_id, environment, status, url, preview_url (===url), error, branch, commit_hash, author, triggered_by, started_at, completed_at, created_at }. Use deploy_get when you already have a specific deployment_id (from deploy_site's `deploy_id`). Use deploy_status when polling 'is my latest deploy done?'. Both return the same per-deployment shape so you can write one parser. A row 'building'/'queued' for over 20 minutes carries stale_suspect:true + stale_note — it was likely stranded by a service restart (a later successful deploy or the project's deployment stamp is cited as evidence when present). Trust the note over the raw status; the watchdog closes stranded rows within the hour (benignly as 'cancelled' when the deploy demonstrably completed).

tools.name: deploy_subscribe
tools.description: Wait for a deploy to finish. Pass wait_seconds (max 25) and the SERVER holds the request, checking every 1.5s, answering the moment the deployment reaches a terminal status. One call replaces a client-side sleep-and-poll loop over deploy_get. ★ THIS NO LONGER RETURNS SERVER-SENT EVENTS. The MCP transport buffers a response whole, so it cannot read a stream until it closes - the old SSE contract could only ever time out, and did: no timeoutMs meant the proxy aborted at 60s, and because that abort branch is gated on non-GET a GET fell through to three attempts and ~183s before reporting a network failure. The SSE endpoint still exists for browser clients; it is not reachable from here. Returns { data: { id, deploy_id, deployment_id, environment, status, url, error, started_at, completed_at, build_time_ms, waited_seconds, terminal, succeeded, hint } } - the same per-deployment field set as deploy_get, so one parser handles both. ★ `terminal` is the canonical stop-polling signal, and `succeeded` is a separate question - a failed deploy is terminal too. Do not match on the status string: the vocabulary includes ready, deployed, completed, success, succeeded and partial, and getting that list subtly wrong is exactly how the old stream never closed on ready. Omit deployment_id to track the project's most recent deployment. Typical use: deploy_site, take the id, then deploy_subscribe({ project_id, deployment_id, wait_seconds: 20 }) in a loop until terminal. A production build takes several rounds; a dev-preview usually one or two.

tools.name: design_comment_resolve
tools.description: Mark one review comment on a Creative Studio design as resolved (sets is_resolved true and stamps resolved_at now). Returns only { success: true } - not the comment, not its text, not its new state - so read the thread back with GET /api/olympus/marketing/design/:id/comments if you need to see the result. ONE WAY: no route anywhere un-resolves a comment, and the design canvas renders only unresolved pins and counts only unresolved comments, so a comment resolved by mistake vanishes from the designer's view and can be restored only by direct database access. SILENT NO-OP ON A REPLY: any comment row on the project is accepted, including a reply (one with parent_comment_id set), but the thread read returns isResolved for TOP-LEVEL comments only, so resolving a reply reports success and changes nothing anyone can observe - resolve the parent comment instead. Re-resolving an already-resolved comment also succeeds and overwrites resolved_at with the new time, losing the original resolution time. resolved_by is written NULL for API-key callers, so the row records that it was resolved and when but can never name who did it. A design project that is missing or owned by another account returns 404 'Project not found'; a commentId that is not on that project returns 404 'Comment not found'; an id or commentId that is not a UUID is not guarded here and surfaces as a 500 rather than a 404. Costs nothing: no money, no outbound call, no queued job, no notification, one row update. The handler reads no body and no query string, so anything else sent with the call is ignored.

tools.name: design_comments_list
tools.description: Read the review thread pinned to one Creative Studio design project. Returns { comments: [{ id, commentText, position: { x, y }, userId, isResolved, createdAt, replies: [{ id, commentText, userId, createdAt }] }] }, oldest first, with each top-level comment's replies nested inline, so there is no second call. `position` is the percentage pin on the canvas and reads { x: 50, y: 50 } for any comment stored without one. RESOLVED COMMENTS ARE INCLUDED: the designer's canvas renders only unresolved pins, so filter on `isResolved` yourself or your count will disagree with the 'N unresolved' badge the human is looking at. No filters and no pagination - the entire thread comes back every call. A malformed, unknown or other-tenant id returns 404 'Design project not found', which is NOT the same answer as 200 with an empty comments array. READ ONLY, and no create tool exists or can: design_comments.user_id is NOT NULL and an API key has no user behind it, so posting a comment stays a human action in the dashboard. Resolving is a separate POST to /api/olympus/marketing/design/:id/comments/:commentId/resolve and is one-way - no route un-resolves a comment.

tools.name: design_create
tools.description: Create a new design project. The agent typically provides initialCanvasData (full Fabric.js JSON: { version, objects:[...], background }) and an artboard size — anything created here is immediately editable in the dashboard. Returns id + dashboardUrl so the agent can hand off to the user.

tools.name: design_export_image
tools.description: Flatten a design to a PNG so the user can see the result. Renders one frame of the canvas via the Remotion worker — same CanvasComposition the MP4 path uses, so frame=0 matches what `canvas.toDataURL` would produce in the dashboard editor. For motion designs, set `frame` to capture a specific moment (e.g. frame=60 at fps=30 = 2s in). The agent should: (1) design_update with the canvas, (2) design_export_image to get an S3 PNG URL, (3) include the URL in the chat reply so the user sees the design inline; meanwhile the user can also click design.dashboardUrl to edit. Refuses early if the canvas is empty. Sync poll, ~5-15s typical: the route polls for up to 60s, re-arms once for 25s if the worker restarted mid-job, and runs to a 95s maxDuration; this tool waits 100s. Returns { success, imageUrl, jobId, warnings? }; nothing is registered in the Media Library (use design_publish_to_library for that). BRAND FONTS RENDER SERVER-SIDE: Google-hosted families ride canvas_json.fonts, and the account's CUSTOM brand fonts (brand_custom_fonts rows carrying a css_font_face) are attached to the job automatically, so a layer set in an uploaded family renders in it. A font that cannot be loaded (a failed brand-kit read, an oversized or clipped @font-face, a family the worker could not fetch) DEGRADES to the fallback stack and is reported as a line in `warnings` on the 200 response; it never fails the render. READ warnings before showing the PNG as final: a success carrying a font warning is a brand-wrong image. Errors: 400 missing canvas_json/width/height or an empty canvas, 404 design not in this account, 500 REMOTION_RENDER_URL unset or the render itself failed, 502 the worker rejected the job, 504 the poll budget ran out.

tools.name: design_export_mp4
tools.description: Render a motion-graphic design to MP4 (or GIF) via the Remotion worker. Pass the full canvas_json snapshot the user has been editing (layered Fabric JSON with per-layer `animation` metadata) — the worker uses the same animation vocabulary as the editor so the output matches the in-browser preview exactly. SYNCHRONOUS: the route polls the worker for up to 180s, re-arms once for 60s if the worker restarted mid-job, and runs to a 270s maxDuration; this tool waits 280s. Refuses early if the canvas has no objects. Returns { success, mp4Url, jobId, warnings? }. The MP4 is hosted publicly so it can be embedded directly; after this call, also PATCH the design with `previewVideoUrl` so the dashboard gallery shows an autoplay thumbnail. BRAND FONTS RENDER SERVER-SIDE: Google-hosted families ride canvas_json.fonts, and the account's CUSTOM brand fonts (brand_custom_fonts rows carrying a css_font_face) are attached to the job automatically, so a layer set in an uploaded family renders in it. A font that cannot be loaded (a failed brand-kit read, an oversized or clipped @font-face, a family the worker could not fetch) DEGRADES to the fallback stack and is reported as a line in `warnings` on the 200 response; it never fails the render. READ warnings before publishing or embedding: a success carrying a font warning is a brand-wrong video. Errors: 400 missing canvas_json/width/height/duration_seconds or an empty canvas, 404 design not in this account, 500 REMOTION_RENDER_URL unset or the render itself failed, 502 the worker rejected the job, 504 the poll budget ran out (the worker may still finish; there is nothing here to poll, so do not loop).

tools.name: design_from_testimonial
tools.description: Open a Creative Studio draft on an APPROVED video testimonial's published recording, so the clip can be trimmed, captioned or branded before it is sent back through the testimonial replace-media route. Mints a design_projects row of design_type motion_graphic whose canvas is ONE unmuted HivekuVideo layer sized to the recording (1080x1920 and a black artboard when the row never got its dimensions), plus a media_assets row registering that SAME already-published object BY URL and tagged 'testimonial': no bytes are fetched, copied or re-uploaded, no render is queued, nothing is billed. Returns {ok, created, design_project_id, editor_url (relative /dashboard/marketing/design/<id>), dashboard_url (the absolute, clickable form)} plus asset_id ONLY when created is true. Idempotent: created:false means the draft already existed and came back untouched, and a draft the operator deleted is quietly re-minted. Continue with design_state_get to read the canvas, design_update to edit it, design_export_mp4 to render. APPROVED-ONLY, and it cannot be talked around: status rejected or spam is 409 media_deleted (those rows keep their url columns after the S3 delete, so they LOOK editable while the bytes are gone), any other non-approved status is 409 not_approved, a testimonial whose consent was withdrawn is 409 revoked, and the final linking UPDATE re-checks status approved AND consent not revoked, so approve the testimonial first rather than looking for a way in. Also refused: a written testimonial is 400 not_media, a recording hosted on an external platform is 400 offsite_media, a row with no published recording yet is 409 no_media, and an unknown, malformed or other-account id is a flat 404 not_found. 409 state_changed is a REAL OUTCOME, not a transient error: the testimonial was revoked or unapproved mid-flight, the draft and the asset this call had just written were both deleted again, nothing is attached and nothing leaked, so re-read the testimonial instead of retrying blind. The request body is never read, so the id is the only thing that steers this.

tools.name: design_get
tools.description: Fetch a single design project including full Fabric.js canvasData, artboard, sectionsVersion (the CAS token for design_update's expectedSectionsVersion) and dashboardUrl. Use this for round-tripping: read → mutate → design_update. For an AI-friendly summary instead of raw JSON, use design_state_get. featuredImageUrl: a `data:` URI (the editor's multi-MB inline canvas snapshot) comes back as null with featured_image_inline: true, replaced WHOLE and never truncated; null plus that flag means the thumbnail exists only inline. The fix for a real (S3) thumbnail URL is design_publish_to_library with set_as_featured. canvasData is deliberately NOT screened: it is the exact blob you edit and PATCH back, so an image src that is a data: URI arrives whole here and can be large. When you only need to reason about the canvas, read design_state_get, which elides those.

tools.name: design_list
tools.description: List the account's design projects (graphics + motion graphics) ordered by most-recently-edited. Returns id / title / slug / description / designType / status / featuredImageUrl / previewVideoUrl / tags / createdAt / updatedAt. There is no design_dashboard_url tool: dashboardUrl comes back inline from design_get, design_create and design_state_get. limit is clamped into 1-100 (default 50); a non-numeric limit is a 400, never a silent fallback to the default. INLINE PAYLOADS ARE SCREENED, never shipped: the dashboard editor stores a base64 `data:` canvas snapshot (routinely multiple MB) in featured_image_url, and any design PATCH can stash an inline clip in previewVideoUrl. A `data:` featured image comes back as featuredImageUrl: null with featured_image_inline: true, and a `data:` preview video as previewVideoUrl: null with preview_video_inline: true, each replaced WHOLE and never truncated. So null plus the inline flag means 'a thumbnail exists but only inline', not 'no thumbnail'. The fix for a real (S3) thumbnail URL is design_publish_to_library with set_as_featured.

tools.name: design_publish_to_library
tools.description: Publish a saved design as a flat PNG into the account's Media Library. Reads the design's canvas STRAIGHT FROM THE DB (send no canvas_json), renders one settled frame on the Remotion worker, uploads the PNG to the account's S3 media path and creates a media_assets row tagged creative-studio + published. Returns { success, fileUrl, mediaAssetId, width, height }: fileUrl is the permanent public URL of the PNG, mediaAssetId is the new library row. TREAT THIS AS CREATE, NEVER AS SYNC: nothing dedupes, the filename carries Date.now() and the insert is a plain create with no unique key, so publishing the same design twice leaves TWO S3 objects and TWO library entries, and a retry after a timeout duplicates the same way. Synchronous, polled for up to 90s; on timeout it returns 504 with no job handle to poll while the worker may still finish and orphan a still that never reaches the library, so never loop or auto-retry it. Costs one real still-render job plus one permanent S3 object and one DB row per call; no customer-facing send and no card charge. THE THUMBNAIL PATH: set_as_featured:true also points the design's featured_image_url at the published PNG. An agent-created design has NO gallery thumbnail until this (or a featuredImageUrl design_update) sets one — the editor's own capture only runs in a browser, so a design nobody has opened in the dashboard renders as a blank card. set_as_featured must be a real JSON boolean: any other encoding ('true', 1) is refused 400 invalid_request BEFORE the render, because silently dropping it would bill a render and still leave no thumbnail. With it set, the success payload carries exactly one of featuredImageUrl (thumbnail landed) or featured_image_error (the PNG published and was paid for, only the thumbnail write failed — still a 200; READ THE FIELD and fix with design_update featuredImageUrl, never by re-publishing, which renders and bills again). The featured write leaves sections_version untouched, so it never raises a canvas CAS conflict for an editor mid-save. For a throwaway preview PNG that registers nothing in the library, use design_export_image instead (it also lets you choose the frame; this tool always publishes the settled frame, after enter animations finish, which is frame 0 only for a design with no animation). To register an already-hosted URL without rendering, use media_library_register_external_url. Body is optional in full: with no arguments beyond id it publishes the first page under the design's own title. Failures: 404 unknown design or another account's, 400 empty canvas, a non-boolean set_as_featured, or an unresolvable page_id (the error lists the available page ids and names), 422 the render itself failed, 502 the worker rejected the job or the rendered PNG could not be downloaded, 504 render timed out, 500 REMOTION_RENDER_URL unset on this environment or the S3 upload failed. PM-task linking and custom tags are deliberately not exposed here.

tools.name: design_render_job_get
tools.description: Poll one durable video render job by id and return {jobId, status, progress, progressMessage, url, assetId, width, height, durationSeconds, warnings, error}. This is the recovery path for a paid render whose originating request died: marketing_generate_video and marketing_video_pipeline_retry_scene both reserve a design_render_jobs row and hand back its id, and a 504 or a dropped connection loses the response but NOT the job. Calling this does not just read the row, it ADVANCES it: the handler runs the same pollAndAdvance the reconcile cron uses, so the clip finishes and registers in the media library through this call. Status is one of the RenderJobStatus values and only completed, failed and abandoned are terminal, so keep polling on anything else. The lookup is account-scoped before anything else happens, so another tenant's job id is a plain 404 rather than a leak. `url` and `assetId` stay null until the job reaches completed.

tools.name: design_render_jobs_list
tools.description: List the account's durable render jobs (design_render_jobs) — every video generation, still, composition and pipeline child clip, newest first. This is the RE-DISCOVERY read for a paid render whose response was lost (a 504 on marketing_generate_video, a dropped connection, a fresh session): find the job you already paid for here instead of generating — and billing — again. A PLAIN READ THAT ADVANCES NOTHING: it never calls pollAndAdvance, never talks to the render worker, never finalizes an asset. Poll a SINGLE job with design_render_job_get — that one DOES advance the job on read — using a jobId from this list. Because this list does not poll, a job shown as `rendering` may already be complete on the worker; the row reflects its last recorded poll, not live worker state. Only completed, failed and abandoned are terminal. Each row: { jobId, kind, lane, status, progress, progressMessage, url, assetId, width, height, durationSeconds, designProjectId, billable, error, createdAt, updatedAt } plus top-level total/limit/offset for paging. `url` (result_url) and `assetId` (media_asset_id) stay null until the job is finalized; `updatedAt` is the latest of completed/last-polled/started/created (the table has no updated_at column) — the last time anything was recorded on the row. Filters (all optional, ANDed onto the key's account): status (reserved|queued|rendering|uploading|completed|failed|abandoned), kind (composition|scenes|still|template|generate_video), design_project_id (uuid — a design not in this account simply yields an empty list), limit (1..100, default 20 — ≤100 effective), offset (≥0). A typo'd status/kind or a non-uuid design_project_id is a named 400 invalid_request, never a plausible-looking empty list; non-integer or overflow-length limit/offset also 400.

tools.name: design_state_get
tools.description: Get a human-readable + structured summary of a design's canvas — element-by-element position/size/style/text/animation plus a one-line text summary. Use this before issuing design_update so the agent reasons over a compact view instead of the raw Fabric JSON. Returns featuredImageUrl if a preview thumbnail exists, and `sectionsVersion` — the CAS token to send back as design_update's expectedSectionsVersion. INLINE PAYLOADS ARE ELIDED, never shipped: a featuredImageUrl that is a `data:` URI comes back as null with featured_image_inline: true (the fix for a real thumbnail URL is design_publish_to_library with set_as_featured); an image element's src that is a data: URI reads '[embedded image]'; a pattern fill or stroke whose source is a data: URI comes back with source: '[embedded image]' (a fill or stroke that is itself a data: string reads '[embedded image]' too). The screens are case-insensitive. To get the raw blob, design_get returns canvasData unscreened. MULTI-PAGE DESIGNS (canvasData shaped { pages: [...] }) additionally return a `pages` roster ([{ id, name, index, elementCount }]) and `activePageId`, and the elements described are those of ONE page — the first page by default, or the one named by page_id. The roster's `index` is always a valid page_id even when a page has no id. A single-page design returns the same shape it always did, with both fields absent. This describes the same page save-to-library would render for the same page_id, so read-then-publish stays on one page.

tools.name: design_templates_list
tools.description: List the design templates available to the agent. Returns the rich 52-template library brand-substituted with the account's active brand guide (orange for Locus, purple for Hiveku, etc.) plus artboard size presets grouped by category (Social Media / Presentation / Print / Ads / Email). Each template carries a ready-to-use canvasData payload — pipe it into design_create's initialCanvasData.

tools.name: design_update
tools.description: Save canvas state on a design. Pass `canvasData` (full Fabric.js JSON) to overwrite the canvas — this is the primary write path. The dashboard editor reads from the same column, so user edits later are preserved on next save. Other fields (title/description/status/tags/featuredImageUrl/artboard) update independently. `previewVideoUrl` sets the autoplay-thumbnail URL without touching the rest of canvasData (only fires when canvasData is omitted). Body capped at 10MB. CONCURRENT WRITERS — a human may have this design open in the dashboard editor, so every canvas write is potentially contested. Pass `expectedSectionsVersion` (the CAS token) on canvas-touching writes: on a version mismatch the write is REFUSED with 409 `sections_version_conflict` carrying `serverVersion` and `serverCanvasData` — re-apply your change on top of serverCanvasData and resend with expectedSectionsVersion: serverVersion; NEVER resend the same body blind, that overwrites the very edit the conflict just protected. Token sources: design_get and design_state_get return `sectionsVersion` (read → reason → write with the token), the success response of this tool returns the next `sectionsVersion`, and a 409 carries `serverVersion`. A write without the token still lands and still bumps the version (the editor's next autosave then conflicts instead of silently reverting your work), but the read-first protocol is the correct default. MULTI-PAGE DOCUMENTS: canvasData may also be `{ pages: [{ id, name, canvasData }] }` — each page its own full Fabric canvas. design_state_get reports the page roster, and design_state_get / design_publish_to_library take page_id to work one page at a time. REMOVAL: there is NO design_delete tool and no Olympus DELETE route — `status:'archived'` is the removal verb (it takes the design out of active use and is reversible by setting status back). For full design freedom: arbitrary shapes (rect/circle/triangle/polygon/path/line), text (textbox/i-text with fontFamily/fontSize/fontWeight/lineHeight/charSpacing), images (type:image, src), groups, layer ordering (via objects[] order), positions (left/top/angle/scaleX/scaleY), styling (fill/stroke/strokeWidth/opacity), and per-layer motion via `animation` on the object. THE FIELD NAMES BELOW ARE EXACT: the renderer reads them literally, and an unrecognized key is ignored in silence, so a design saved with the wrong names renders completely static while every tool reports success. This description previously documented `{ preset, delay_ms, duration_ms }`, none of which the renderer reads. `animation: { enter?: 'fade-in'|'fade-up'|'fade-down'|'fade-left'|'fade-right'|'scale-in'|'pop'|'slide-up'|'slide-down'|'slide-left'|'slide-right'|'wipe-up'|'wipe-down'|'blur-in'|'rotate-in', enter_delay_ms?: number (default 0), enter_duration_ms?: number (default 800), enter_distance_px?: number (default 60, for the directional fades and slides), easing?: 'cubic-out'|'quart-out'|'expo-out'|'back-out'|'ease-in-out'|'elastic', exit?: same preset list, exit_at_ms?: number, exit_duration_ms?: number (default 600), loop?: 'pulse'|'wiggle'|'rotate-slow'|'breathe'|'float'|'shimmer' }`. NOTE that `loop` is a SEPARATE FIELD from `enter`, not another preset value: pulse, wiggle, rotate-slow and breathe were previously listed among the entry presets, so putting one in `enter` produces no entry animation at all. Omitting `enter` leaves the layer visible from t=0; omitting `exit` leaves it visible to the end. Canvas-level motion: set `_animation: { duration_ms, fps, loop }` on the root.

tools.name: design_version_create
tools.description: Snapshot the current canvas state into design_versions. Call this BEFORE making large destructive edits so the user can roll back from the dashboard's Version History panel. Mark `isMilestone: true` for named save-points (e.g. 'final approved version').

tools.name: design_version_get
tools.description: Read ONE design version snapshot, including its frozen canvas blob. Returns id, versionNumber, versionName, changeSummary, title, isMilestone, createdAt, plus the two blobs the listing does NOT carry: canvasData (design_versions.sections - the full Fabric.js JSON frozen at snapshot time: objects[] with per-layer geometry, style, text, image src and animation, plus the canvas-level _animation block and any _preview_video_url) and artboard (design_versions.global_settings - width, height, background, gridEnabled, gridSize, snapEnabled, rulerEnabled). Call design_versions_list FIRST: it returns every field here EXCEPT canvasData and artboard, so come here only when the blob is actually needed. SIZE IS THE TRAP: unlike design_state_get, which rewrites an embedded image src to '[embedded image]', this hands back the raw blob, so a canvas carrying base64 data: URIs returns at multiple MB and swamps the agent's context. canvasData is sections || {} over a column that defaults to [], so it can arrive as an object, an empty array, or {} - check before reading .objects. Reading a version does NOT restore it and does not touch design_projects. Restoring is a separate destructive write: send this canvasData to design_update (PATCH on the design), which overwrites design_projects.sections wholesale and increments sections_version - pass expectedSectionsVersion on that call or a human editing the same design loses their unsaved canvas with no error to either side. design_update MERGES artboard rather than replacing it, so pushing this snapshot's artboard back restores the keys it holds and leaves any newer key in place. Costs nothing: two indexed reads, no write, no queued job, no money. Every miss is a 404 - a versionId that belongs to another account, or to a different design in this account, is indistinguishable from one that does not exist.

tools.name: design_versions_list
tools.description: List all version snapshots for a design (most recent first).

tools.name: design_video_capabilities_get
tools.description: Pre-flight for AI video: can this account generate a clip right now, asked BEFORE marketing_generate_video reserves a paid (~$1) render. Returns {videoEnabled} on every outcome, plus {plan, used, limit} once the plan gate runs, plus {reason, message} when blocked. reason is one of not_configured (REMOTION_RENDER_URL is unset on this environment), render_service_unavailable (the render worker did not answer /health within 2s), plan_upgrade_required (the effective plan is not premium), monthly_cap_reached (20 clips per account per calendar month, UTC) or cap_check_unavailable. SILENT FAILURE: all five of those are HTTP 200. There is no error status to branch on, so read videoEnabled and never the status code. cap_check_unavailable is a transient database error and is RETRYABLE, not a real block - do not tell anyone to upgrade or that they are out of clips on it. used and limit are OMITTED on not_configured, render_service_unavailable, plan_upgrade_required and cap_check_unavailable; they appear only on monthly_cap_reached and on success. videoEnabled true is not a guarantee either: worker health is cached process-wide for 60 seconds in BOTH directions, so a worker that just died still reads reachable for up to a minute (the render then fails) and one that just recovered still reads unavailable. used counts only clips already registered in the Media Library after a render finishes, and the cap takes no lock, so an in-flight generation is uncounted and concurrent calls near the boundary can land a clip or two over. Use this rather than marketing_generate_video with dry_run:true as the pre-flight: dry_run reports the same plan and cap gate but runs before the REMOTION_RENDER_URL check and never probes the worker, so it cannot see not_configured or render_service_unavailable, and it still requires a prompt. Free and read-only: nothing is reserved, billed or enqueued. Takes no arguments and always reports the calling key's own account.

tools.name: design_video_rerender
tools.description: Re-render a single Remotion-template video clip with new prop values. Used when a design contains a video element backed by a Remotion template — the user (or agent) edits a slot, this re-runs the render, and the resulting MP4 swaps in place. Canvas position/scale/rotation are preserved by the caller on update. Blocks up to 240s.

tools.name: design_voiceover_create
tools.description: SPENDS MONEY: renders the script through Cartesia, stores the MP3 and writes a billing row. Run design_voiceover_estimate first - that is what it is for - and read too_long, billable and remaining_seconds before calling this. Returns asset_id, url, duration_ms, characters, cost_cents, cached, voice_id and script, and registers the clip in the Media Library. cached: true means an identical (script, voice) render already existed on this account, so nothing new was spent, cost_cents is 0 and no allowance was consumed. asset_id can come back null while url is real audio that has ALREADY been billed, because the library row is best-effort - never treat a null asset_id as a failed render and never retry on it. voice_id must be a Cartesia UUID from design_voices_list: this surface refuses anything else with 400 voice_not_recognised, unlike the browser route, where the shared library silently substitutes the default voice and only writes a server log, turning an unknown id into a paid render in the wrong voice reported as success. voice_id is checked for UUID shape, not catalog membership, so a well-formed id Cartesia does not know still reaches the provider and comes back provider_rejected. Failures carry a machine `error` code plus a human `message`: empty_script and script_too_long are 400, plan_upgrade_required (the plan includes no voiceover) and monthly_cap_reached (ten times the allowance) are 402, and provider_rejected, provider_timeout or upload_failed mean no ledger row was written.

tools.name: design_voiceover_estimate
tools.description: Prices a voiceover script before anything is rendered, and spends nothing: returns characters, max_characters (800), estimated_seconds, too_long, plan, included_minutes, used_seconds, remaining_seconds, billable, overage_cents_per_minute and cost_cents. characters counts the NORMALIZED script - markdown is stripped before it reaches the provider, so a bolded word does not inflate it - and estimated_seconds is a flat 15.5-characters-per-second heuristic, not a measurement. cost_cents is the gross per-character figure the render ledger records (12 cents per 1,000 characters); the monthly invoice bills only whole minutes past included_minutes at overage_cents_per_minute, so cost_cents is not by itself what the customer pays. billable is true when estimated_seconds exceeds remaining_seconds. included_minutes of 0 means the plan (free or hosting) has no voiceover allowance at all and design_voiceover_create will 402 plan_upgrade_required, so check it before writing a script. Omit script to read the allowance on its own.

tools.name: design_voices_list
tools.description: Narrator catalog for Design Studio voiceovers, with a server-scored shortlist on top. Returns { voices: [{ id, name, gender, description, suggested }], suggested_count }, sorted suggested-first then alphabetically, and a voice id here is the value a storyboard or a video render takes. Read brand_guide_voiceovers_get FIRST: that returns the account's APPROVED narrators with the human usage notes on each, and this wider catalog is only for deliberately picking outside that set. Not voice_tts_voices_list, which is the IVR catalog behind the paid phone-plan gate and answers 402 for exactly the marketing-only accounts this one serves. The failure that reads as data: when CARTESIA_API_KEY is unset or the upstream call fails or times out, the response is HTTP 503 carrying voices: [] plus error 'not_configured' or 'voices_unavailable', so an empty array is a broken environment and never an account with no voices - read error before reporting that there are none, and note a failure is not cached so every call retries upstream. suggested_count is the hardcoded constant 8, not a count of the rows returned, and fewer than 8 can carry suggested: true. Takes no arguments at all: no search, no filter, no paging, and the upstream read is one un-paginated page of 100 rows then filtered to non-archived English voices, so this is a slice of the Cartesia catalog and not the whole of it. Costs nothing: it generates no TTS, writes no row, and a successful catalog is cached 10 minutes per process.

tools.name: email_audience_create
tools.description: Create an audience. kind='dynamic' (default) re-evaluates filter_json at send time; 'static' is a manually-maintained list. filter_json vocabulary — the WHOLE list the engine honours (AUDIENCE_FILTER_KEYS in the builder's src/lib/marketing/audience-materializer.ts, which both the send and email_audience_preview resolve through): has_email, include_tags, any_tags, exclude_tags, lifecycle_stages, lead_sources, utm_campaigns, lead_statuses, min_lead_score, max_lead_score, created_after, created_before, has_deal, deal_status, deal_pipeline_id, deal_stage_ids, custom_fields, icp_matched_ids, min_icp_confidence, visited_pages, last_seen_within_days, in_journey_stage, engaged_campaign_ids, not_engaged_campaign_ids, has_shopify_order, min_shopify_total_spent_cents, max_shopify_total_spent_cents, min_shopify_order_count, shopify_last_order_after, shopify_last_order_before. AN UNKNOWN KEY IS NOT REJECTED — it is stored and then ignored. This route validates no key names, so an invented name (min_score, icp_tiers, company_ids, owner_ids, deal_stages, has_open_deal, opened_campaign_ids, clicked_campaign_ids, shopify_min_orders, shopify_min_spend, shopify_ordered_after, unsubscribed, suppressed, groups, filter_version, …) saves with a 201 and then narrows NOTHING: the campaign reaches everyone the remaining keys allow, including the people the operator meant to exclude. Type the names above exactly and read filter_json back before attaching the audience to a campaign. THE ONLY REFUSAL (400, with a contradictions[] body) is a filter no contact can satisfy: a tag both required and excluded, every any_tags value also excluded, an inverted lead-score / shopify-spend / created / last-order range, has_shopify_order=false alongside min_shopify_order_count>=1, the same campaign id in both engaged_campaign_ids and not_engaged_campaign_ids, or conflicting custom_fields predicates. It also fires on email_audience_update when a static audience is flipped to dynamic. Every predicate AND-intersects; there is no OR. Bounds are min_lead_score / max_lead_score (0-100; a NULL lead_score matches neither). has_deal is 'any' | 'open' | 'won' | 'none'; deal_status is ignored under 'open'/'won'. visited_pages and last_seen_within_days resolve against ClickHouse and ARE sized by email_audience_preview — if ClickHouse is unreachable the resolver throws and the preview answers 'Audience not found'. lead_sources and utm_campaigns each match the CURRENT or the FIRST-TOUCH column (lead_source OR original_lead_source, utm_campaign OR original_utm_campaign), by exact case-sensitive equality.

tools.name: email_connect_start

Returns a `setup_url` you HAND TO THE USER (don't open it on their behalf — they need to be in their own browser session to grant Google consent). Other options: - readonly: read email only (no calendar) - send: send email only (no read, no calendar) - modify: read/send/modify email (no calendar) User resolution: passes through to whichever Hiveku user OWNS the connection. Solo-account agents can omit user_email/user_id (auto-picks the only user). Multi-user accounts must specify which user the connection belongs to. Prereq: the account needs a Google OAuth Client registered with `product='crm_email_calendar'`. If the agent gets `code: 'no_oauth_app'`, surface the hint that the account owner needs to register one at /dashboard/settings/oauth-apps first. tools.description: Account's email-service health for the TRANSACTIONAL lane (hk_ API keys, smtp.hiveku.com, /api/v1/email/send). READ sending_enabled FIRST: when false, a `suspension` block carries the reason/timestamp and ALL sending is blocked (SMTP 450s at DATA, /api/v1/email/send refuses) regardless of the healthy-looking reputation numbers below it — domain reputation reflects history, not current sendability. Also returns verified domains, API-key previews, SMTP connection details and code snippets. Suspensions are lifted by Hiveku staff, not by any tool. sending_enabled is a KILL SWITCH, not a readiness check: true means only "not suspended". It does NOT assert a verified domain or an active API key (read `domains` and `api_keys` for those), and it says NOTHING about marketing campaigns, which are provisioned separately. So sending_enabled: true here alongside ready_to_send: false / ses_provisioned: false from marketing_setup_status is normal and both are correct: they measure different lanes. The one thing they share is the suspension gate, evaluated from the same predicate in both, so sending_enabled: false also blocks every campaign send. For campaign sendability use marketing_setup_status; for an end-to-end transactional proof use email_deliverability_check.

tools.name: entity_populate
tools.description: LLM-enrich a sparse marketing entity (customer_avatar / customer_journey / before_after_grid) with GROUNDED context. The agent supplies research — URLs to scrape, web search queries, free-form notes — and the marketing agent server's populate_entity.py merges that with the account's brand_style_guide (if any), calls DeepSeek V4 Pro, and writes the enriched JSON back to the row. **HALLUCINATION GUARDS** (this is not a fancy autocomplete): 1. If the account has no brand_style_guide AND the agent supplies no urls_to_scrape / search_queries / agent_notes / related_research, the script REFUSES to call the LLM and returns `code: 'context_insufficient'` (400). The agent must gather context first. 2. The LLM is instructed to LEAVE FIELDS NULL (strings) or EMPTY [] (arrays) when the context doesn't ground a confident answer. Refusal > fabrication. 3. Response includes a `_meta` block: `{requires_human_review, fields_with_low_confidence[], sources_used[], notes}` — the agent should surface this to the user when populating fresh / sparse accounts. **Recommended grounding pattern for a FRESH account** (no brand guide, no prior research): 1. Get the account's primary website URL (from website_projects.domain or ask the user). 2. Call entity_populate with `urls_to_scrape: ['https://acme.com', 'https://acme.com/about', 'https://acme.com/services']` — Firecrawl scrapes them and the LLM reads the page content. 3. Optionally add `search_queries: ['acme corp business model', 'acme corp customer reviews']` for outside signals. 4. Optionally add `agent_notes: 'B2B SaaS for HVAC contractors, ICP is shop owners with 5-20 trucks'` if you already know something concrete. For a MATURE account: brand_style_guide alone is usually enough. Pass urls_to_scrape only if you want the LLM to lean on specific page copy (a new product page, etc.). Enrichment shape per entity: avatar → 20+ ICP columns: summary, age_range, gender, location, occupation, income_range, lifestyle, values[], interests[], primary_goals[], motivations[], pain_points[], frustrations[], aspirations, typical_quote, background_story, online_behavior{social_platforms[], device_preference, content_habits, information_sources[], daily_hours_online}, buying_behavior{trigger, decision_cycle, stakeholders[], preferred_intake, budget_range, objections[]}, content_preferences[], preferred_channels[] journey → summary + stages[] with each stage having {name, description, emotions[], pain_points[], touchpoints[], content_types[], opportunities[]} grid → transformation_story, key_benefits[], measurable_results[], audience_context, grid_items[] with each item {before:{title, description, pain_points[]}, after:{title, description, benefits[]}, transformation_details} Side effects: UPDATEs the row in place (caller's existing fields are preserved when LLM doesn't return them); flips populate_status to 'populated' / 'failed' / 'context_insufficient'. Takes ~10-60s when scrapes/searches are requested (one Firecrawl scrape ~2-5s; LLM call ~5-20s). Costs ~$0.001-0.005 per call (DeepSeek + Firecrawl combined). Response shape on success: `{ entity_type, entity_id, entity_name, rows_updated, fields_set[], model, enriched, _meta, context_used: {brand_guide, agent_notes, related_research, scrapes_attempted, scrapes_succeeded, searches_attempted, searches_succeeded} }`. On context_insufficient: 400 with a clear hint to gather research first.

tools.name: execute_js
tools.description: 🕷️ CRAWL4AI: Execute JavaScript before scraping (Firecrawl-backed via actions)

tools.name: fetch_url
tools.description: Fetch a public URL and return its body (HTML/JSON/text). Use after web_search to read a specific page, to pull docs, or to inspect a customer-supplied link. GET only. SSRF-safe: refuses private/loopback/link-local hosts and non-http(s) schemes. Returned body capped at 200KB (max_bytes lowers it). CHECKING WHETHER A TAG OR STRING IS ON A PAGE - pass contains and do NOT read the body. contains takes up to 10 case-insensitive PLAIN SUBSTRINGS (not regexes) and returns matches[] of { needle, found, count, matches:[{offset, context}] } instead of the document; with contains set, mode defaults to none so no body comes back at all. That turns a UET/GTM/pixel check into a few hundred bytes instead of a 200KB single-line body you then have to slice. Matching ALWAYS runs against the RAW bytes whatever mode says, and contains raises the SCAN window to 2MB while the returned body stays capped, so it also finds tags past the 200KB point that a plain fetch would have cut off. found IS TRISTATE. true = present. false = absent AND the whole page was read. null = not found in what was read, but the read stopped early (truncated:true, or read_error) - that is NOT evidence the tag is missing, and matches_note says so on the response. Never report a tag as not installed on a null; raise max_bytes, narrow the URL, or use web_scrape. mode: raw (default, full body) | text (tags stripped, whitespace collapsed, for READING prose - it deletes <script> bodies so it can never be used to judge tag presence, and it returns script_srcs[] with the external script URLs it removed) | none (no body). text is GATED on an HTML-ish content type; anything else silently returns raw and says so in mode_note. Byte accounting: byte_count is the RETURNED body, scanned_bytes is what the reader consumed, body_truncated means the returned body was cut to max_bytes, and truncated means the FETCH stopped early (the only one that can invalidate a found:false). For Firecrawl-quality markdown, link discovery, or JS-rendered pages use web_scrape - but its markdown drops script bodies too, so a tag check still belongs here with contains.

tools.name: gallery_apply_jsx
tools.description: Generate ready-to-paste JSX for a responsive image grid. images is [{ src, alt?, caption? }]. Splice the returned JSX into a component file via project_commit.

tools.name: gallery_apply_to_cms
tools.description: Scaffold a CMS gallery collection and write one entry per image (image, alt, caption, order fields). User can then edit/reorder via the CMS panel.

tools.name: generate_image
tools.description: Generate — or in modify mode, edit — a brand-aligned image. Output is a hosted PNG URL AND a media_assets row with `source_type='ai_generated'` so the asset shows up in the Hiveku media library (listable via media_library_list with source_type=ai_generated, taggable, attachable to blogs/emails/etc). The response includes `media_asset_id` for chaining into media_update / media_usage_get, plus `width` and `height` of the delivered image (null only when unmeasurable). BRAND-AWARE BY DEFAULT: the route appends the account's ACTIVE brand guide (palette, fonts, visual voice) to the model prompt unless use_brand:false. Pass false only for deliberately off-brand output. Still load `account_context_get` first so the prompt itself matches the account's voice — the brand suffix styles the render, it does not write the brief. The response says whether the brand actually landed: brand_applied is true only when the ACTIVE guide reached the model prompt, and brand_skipped_reason:'no_active_brand_guide' is set when use_brand was on but the account has no ACTIVE guide (the image generated UNBRANDED and the slot was still spent; activate a guide with the brand_ tools before re-running). A FAILED brand read (DB error) is 503 brand_unavailable, refused BEFORE any quota slot is reserved or any provider is called: never a silently unbranded render. Retry, or pass use_brand:false. TWO RENDER LANES with different knobs: - gemini-3.1 (default) / gpt-5.4 — the editing-capable lane. mode:'modify' edits the referenced images (background swap, style transfer, product recolor) and REQUIRES 1-4 reference_media_asset_ids: Media Library image ids owned by this account (register an external URL first via media_library_register_external_url). A missing, foreign, non-image or unfetchable reference is 404 invalid_reference with details.media_asset_id naming the offender. With target dims this lane renders, then COVER-CROPS to the exact frame (attention-weighted crop: edges may be trimmed, content is never letterboxed or distorted). - flux / flux-pro / recraft — the fal lane. Renders the EXACT requested frame and takes seed (same prompt + same seed = repeatable render) and negative_prompt (≤4000 chars). Both knobs are fal-only: on gemini/gpt they 400 invalid_request, NEVER silently dropped. The fal lane refuses mode:'modify' (400). target_width / target_height: exact output frame in px — both-or-neither, positive integers, ≤4096 per side. Use for pixel-exact placements (email header 1200x600, LinkedIn banner 1584x396). COST: every success debits the account's monthly image-generation quota (429 budget_exceeded at the cap; the slot is refunded when the image generated but storage failed). The fal models additionally bill real compute per image: flux ~$0.025/megapixel and flux-pro ~$0.04/megapixel, ROUNDED UP (1 megapixel = 1024x1024, so a default-size render is one unit); recraft ~$0.04 flat per image. TIMEOUT LADDER: the route runs up to 180s (the fal lane polls the render worker for 120s plus a 35s resubmit window after a worker restart; modify mode fetches reference bytes first) and this tool waits 200s. A slow render can still outlive that: the call is aborted client-side and NOT retried, but the route keeps running and the asset usually still lands — quota spent. After a timeout, check media_library_list (source_type=ai_generated, newest first) BEFORE regenerating, or every timeout becomes a double spend. Errors: 400 invalid_prompt / invalid_request (a fal-only knob on the gemini/gpt lane, one-sided dims, fal+modify, oversized frame — always named, never dropped), 404 invalid_reference, 429 budget_exceeded, 502 storage_error (slot refunded), 503 provider_unavailable, 503 brand_unavailable (the brand guide read failed; nothing reserved or billed). For multiple images in one onboarding/composition pass (avatar + hero + before + after), use `generate_image_set` instead — same quota, same auto-registration, one round-trip, and the same brand-on-by-default (top-level use_brand there sets the batch default, overridable per prompt).

tools.name: generate_image_set
tools.description: Batch image generation — generate up to 10 brand-aligned images in one call. Common onboarding pattern: avatar/persona portrait + landing-page hero + transformation-before + transformation-after, composed against the same brand context. Each prompt can carry its own role, style, aspect_ratio, use_brand, target dims and (optionally) per-prompt model override; top-level `model`/`use_brand`/`target_width`+`target_height` provide the defaults. All successes are auto-registered as media_assets rows (source_type='ai_generated'), so they show up immediately in media_library_list and can be filtered by `tags`/`role` (role is saved into ai_metadata). BRAND-AWARE BY DEFAULT (same 2026-09 decision as generate_image): the route appends the account's ACTIVE brand guide (palette, fonts, visual voice) to every model prompt unless use_brand:false. Top-level use_brand sets the batch default; a per-prompt use_brand overrides it in either direction. Only true/false (or the strings 'true'/'false') are accepted — anything else is a 400, never a silent coercion to TRUE. Each success reports brand_applied, plus brand_skipped_reason:'no_active_brand_guide' when the account has no ACTIVE guide (the normal case on a fresh onboarding account — the images generated UNBRANDED and the envelope says so). A FAILED brand read (DB error) is that prompt's own errors[] row with code brand_unavailable, refused before its slot is reserved; sibling prompts are unaffected. Retry, or pass use_brand:false. target_width/target_height: exact output frame in px — both-or-neither, positive integers, ≤4096 per side. The top-level pair applies to every prompt without a frame of its own; a per-prompt pair REPLACES the top-level pair entirely (never merged half-and-half). NOT accepted per prompt (400 for the WHOLE batch, before any generation or quota debit): mode/reference_media_asset_ids (image editing) and seed/negative_prompt (fal-only knobs) — those are solo-only on generate_image. Per-prompt error handling: one bad prompt does not fail the whole batch — failures land in `errors[]` with the index, role, and code. The account's image quota is debited per successful generation (atomic per-call reservation). Budget exhaustion mid-batch yields `code:'budget_exceeded'` on the remaining entries while the earlier successes still land. The HTTP status is 201 while at least one prompt succeeded and 502 only when every prompt failed, so read summary and errors[], not the status. TIMEOUT LADDER: the route runs up to 180s (maxDuration, sized for the fal lane's 120s poll plus a 35s resubmit window; prompts run in parallel) and this tool waits 200s. A slow batch can still outlive that: the call is aborted client-side and NOT retried, but the route keeps running and the successes usually still land — quota spent. After a timeout, check media_library_list (source_type=ai_generated, newest first) BEFORE regenerating, or every timeout becomes a double spend. Before calling: ALWAYS load `account_context_get` so the prompts reference the account's brand voice + visual style. Compose the prompts up-front from the same context for visual consistency across the set.

tools.name: get_account_info
tools.description: Get the current account information and Olympus configuration

tools.name: get_project
tools.description: Get one PM project (pm_projects table) with its recent tasks and any linked website. ⚠️ THIS IS A PM-PROJECTS TOOL. The id slot wants a pm_projects.id — NOT a website_projects.id. For BUILDER / WEBSITE project details (preview URLs, GitHub state, environments, container status) call `project_get` (single-project) or `sites_list` (all). Calling get_project with a website_projects UUID returns 404 because the row lives in a different table.

tools.name: get_task
tools.description: Get a single PM task by ID. Response `data` includes the task fields plus `annotations` — the browser annotations reviewers dropped on the live preview, each with its SCREENSHOT. Per annotation: { id, annotation_type, priority, annotation_text, page_url, page_title, coordinates, screenshot_url, screenshot_key, screenshot_status, capture_method, viewport_size, created_by_name, created_by_email, created_at, resolved_at }. `screenshot_url` is a directly-fetchable public PNG (no signing/auth needed). `screenshot_status` is ready | capturing | failed | none — a null screenshot_url with status="capturing" means the async capture hasn't finished yet (re-fetch shortly), NOT that it's broken. `annotation_count` gives the total.

tools.name: github_branches_create
tools.description: Create a new branch on the linked repo (defaults to off the project's default branch).

tools.name: github_branches_delete
tools.description: Delete a branch on the linked repo. Use with care.

tools.name: github_branches_list
tools.description: List branches on the project's linked GitHub repo.

tools.name: github_commits
tools.description: Get recent commits on a branch (default: project's default branch).

tools.name: github_compare
tools.description: Compare two commits/branches/tags on the linked repo (base vs head — like a PR diff).

tools.name: github_pr_create
tools.description: Open a pull request: title + head branch + base (default = repo default).

tools.name: github_pr_get
tools.description: Get one pull request by number. Pass include_files=true to also fetch the changed files.

tools.name: github_pr_list
tools.description: List pull requests on the linked repo.

tools.name: github_pr_merge
tools.description: Merge a pull request. merge_method defaults to "squash".

tools.name: github_status
tools.description: GitHub connection status for a project: app installed? repo URL? default branch? last synced SHA?

tools.name: gmail_conversation_history
tools.description: Recent message history with a contact email — used as a duplicate-guard before sending. Returns each touchpoint with direction (inbound/outbound from the mailbox owner's perspective), subject, and snippet.

tools.name: gmail_get_message
tools.description: Fetch a single Gmail message by ID and return parsed fields (from, to, cc, subject, body, bodyHtml, date, labels, snippet).

tools.name: gmail_get_thread
tools.description: Fetch a complete Gmail thread with every message parsed.

tools.name: gmail_inbox_lead_replies
tools.description: Returns inbound prospect replies, pre-filtered to exclude the team on the calling account (resolved per account from its memberships, never a fixed list of names) and noise (calendly, mailer-daemon, DMARC, no-reply). Optionally auto-applies the "ares/pending-review" label, creating it if missing.

tools.name: gmail_list_labels
tools.description: List all Gmail labels (system + user) on the mailbox.

tools.name: gmail_modify_labels
tools.description: Add and/or remove labels on a Gmail message. Accepts label IDs (e.g. INBOX, Label_42) OR human names (e.g. "ares/pending-review"). Set create_missing=true to auto-create label names that do not yet exist.

tools.name: gmail_parse_forward
tools.description: Parse a forwarded email. Returns alias info, prospect info, prospect reply text, and (if present) the original cold email. Splits on Gmail's "---------- Forwarded message ---------" delimiter.

tools.name: gmail_search_messages
tools.description: Search Gmail messages on the connected mailbox using Gmail query syntax (e.g. "in:inbox from:foo@bar.com newer_than:7d"). Returns message ID stubs — call gmail_get_message for full content.

tools.name: helpdesk_automations_get
tools.description: Read the account's helpdesk automation config, always with defaults applied — so an account that has never touched its settings reports what is ACTUALLY running, not an empty object. auto_acknowledge, first_response_sla, resolve_sla, sla_escalation and auto_close all default to ENABLED. Keys: auto_acknowledge, auto_assign, notify_team, first_response_sla and resolve_sla (two separate configs, not one 'sla'), sla_escalation, csat_survey, csat_review_ask, auto_close, reply_channel, reply_routing. Plus the widget config. notify_team.slack_webhook_url is never returned — it is a credential. You get slack_webhook_configured and slack_webhook_last4 instead. Read-only via Olympus; writes go through the dashboard because misconfiguring these has tenant-wide impact.

tools.name: helpdesk_csat_list
tools.description: List individual CSAT responses. Filters: assigned_to_id, since (ISO datetime). Returns ticket_id + rating (great|ok|not_great) + feedback + source.

tools.name: helpdesk_csat_stats
tools.description: Aggregated CSAT stats. Returns totals (great/ok/not_great + csat_score = great / total) plus per-assignee breakdown sorted by csat_score desc and per-source counts. Filter by `since` to scope to a time window (e.g. last 30 days).

tools.name: helpdesk_kb_article_create
tools.description: Create a knowledge-base article. visibility = 'public' (customers + agents), 'internal' (agents only), 'draft' (hidden from search). publish=true sets published_at=now; setting visibility='public' also auto-publishes. body is markdown.

tools.name: helpdesk_kb_article_delete
tools.description: Delete a KB article.

tools.name: helpdesk_kb_article_update
tools.description: Patch a KB article. Allow-listed: title, body, excerpt, visibility, category_id, tags, slug, publish, published_at (null to unpublish, true to publish now, or an ISO datetime). Moving visibility to 'public' from draft or internal AUTO-PUBLISHES, matching create. Re-saving an already-public article does NOT change its publish date, and an explicit published_at always wins — so {visibility:'public', published_at:null} unpublishes.

tools.name: helpdesk_kb_categories_create
tools.description: Create a KB category. Optional parent_id makes it a sub-category. slug auto-derived from name if omitted.

tools.name: helpdesk_kb_categories_delete
tools.description: Delete a KB category. Refuses with 409 category_not_empty (and returns article_count + child_count) when it still holds articles or subcategories — deleting anyway would silently leave every article uncategorised and re-parent every subcategory to the root. Pass reassign_to=<category_id> to move the contents first, or force=true to accept the orphaning deliberately.

tools.name: helpdesk_kb_categories_list
tools.description: List KB categories with parent_id + article/subcategory counts. Caller rebuilds the tree from parent_id.

tools.name: helpdesk_kb_categories_update
tools.description: Rename or re-parent a KB category. Allow-listed: name, slug, parent_id (null moves it to the root), description, sort_order. The slug does NOT change when you rename — it is a live help-centre URL, so renaming never breaks existing links. Pass slug explicitly to change it, or regenerate_slug: true to re-derive it from the new name. Refuses with 400 self_parent or cycle_detected on a move that would create a loop, and 409 duplicate_slug if the slug is taken.

tools.name: helpdesk_kb_read_article
tools.description: Read one KB article (full markdown body). Increments the view counter and returns the POST-increment count. Reads at any visibility, including internal and draft — that is what internal KB is for. Check the returned is_customer_safe (public AND published) before linking it to a customer.

tools.name: helpdesk_kb_search
tools.description: Search OR LIST the helpdesk knowledge base. OMIT q to LIST — this is the only way to enumerate articles (there is no list-articles endpoint), and it is what you want for an audit, a duplicate hunt, or 'what drafts are waiting on review?' (pass visibility: 'draft'). The list form returns total + has_more and takes offset for paging. With q, it is a tokenized match over title/body/excerpt/tags, ranked by relevance (title and tag hits outrank body hits; popularity is only a tiebreak). visibility: public | internal | draft | all. 'all' (the default) means public + internal — DRAFTS ARE EXCLUDED unless you ask for visibility: 'draft' explicitly. Returns matched_keywords so you can see what actually matched, and truncated: true when more candidates existed than were ranked. This returns INTERNAL articles by default: visibility-check by hand before linking anything to a customer, or use helpdesk_kb_suggest_articles, which is customer-safe by construction.

tools.name: helpdesk_kb_suggest_articles
tools.description: Suggest customer-safe KB articles for a customer's question or topic. The safe link-picker for outbound replies: it returns only articles that are BOTH visibility public AND actually published, so it cannot surface an internal doc or an unpublished draft. Takes a natural-language question — it tokenizes and ranks by relevance rather than matching the sentence as one literal string. Returns matched_keywords. Bodies are omitted (excerpt only); use helpdesk_kb_read_article for the full text.

tools.name: helpdesk_macros_create
tools.description: Create a canned-reply macro. Body supports {{template_vars}} like {{contact_first_name}}, {{ticket_short_id}}, {{account_name}}, {{agent_name}}, {{portal_url}}. Use sparingly — tags help the picker stay navigable.

tools.name: helpdesk_macros_delete
tools.description: Delete a macro.

tools.name: helpdesk_macros_get
tools.description: Fetch one macro with its raw body (showing all {{placeholders}}).

tools.name: helpdesk_macros_list
tools.description: List the account's canned-reply macros sorted by usage (most popular first). Filters: is_active (true|false), tag, search (matches title/description/body). Use the macro body verbatim or render it via helpdesk_macros_render to substitute {{vars}}.

tools.name: helpdesk_macros_render
tools.description: Render a macro template by substituting {{vars}}. Returns rendered_body, required_placeholders (everything the template asks for) and unfilled_placeholders. A NON-EMPTY unfilled_placeholders MEANS DO NOT SEND — fill them and re-render. A value you supplied as an empty string counts as unfilled, because sending "Hi ," to a customer is the actual hazard. Unsupplied placeholders render as empty strings, so the raw {{token}} will NOT be visible in the output to warn you. Bumps usage_count so the 'most used' picker sort stays accurate; pass count_usage: false for a dry run. Refuses with 400 if the macro is is_active=false. Use this BEFORE helpdesk_ticket_send_reply / add_message.

tools.name: helpdesk_macros_update
tools.description: Patch a macro. Allow-listed: title, body, description, tags, is_active.

tools.name: helpdesk_queues_add_member
tools.description: Add a user to a queue. Role is a free-form label (e.g. "lead", "shadow"). Accepts any user on the account, including teammates who joined by invitation. Refuses with 409 if they are already a member, and 400 user_not_in_account if they are not on the account at all.

tools.name: helpdesk_queues_create
tools.description: Create a queue. strategy controls auto-assignment: 'round_robin' (cycle members), 'least_busy' (pick the member with fewest open tickets), 'fixed_user' (always assign to fixed_user_id — required for that strategy). Defaults to round_robin.

tools.name: helpdesk_queues_delete
tools.description: Delete a queue. Cascades members. Tickets keep their queue_id pointer (orphaned) — reassign them before deleting.

tools.name: helpdesk_queues_get
tools.description: Fetch one queue with its current active member list.

tools.name: helpdesk_queues_list
tools.description: List queues with member + ticket counts. A queue is a group of agents with a routing strategy (round_robin | least_busy | fixed_user). Tickets can be routed to a queue and the dispatcher picks the assignee per strategy. Filter by is_active to hide retired queues.

tools.name: helpdesk_queues_remove_member
tools.description: Remove a user from a queue. Doesn't affect existing ticket assignments — those stay with the user even after they leave the queue.

tools.name: helpdesk_queues_update
tools.description: Patch a queue. Allow-listed: name, description, strategy, fixed_user_id, is_active.

tools.name: helpdesk_sla_history
tools.description: SLA attainment over a window — the historical complement to helpdesk_tickets_overdue. Includes ALL ticket statuses (a ticket that breached and was later resolved still counts as a breach; overdue only shows live breaches). Window is over created_at: from/to ISO datetimes, default trailing 30 days, max 92 days. Optional scoping by assigned_to_id or queue_id; group_by=assignee|queue adds per-group breakdowns. Each ticket is classified twice — first_response (first_response_at vs first_response_due_at) and resolve (resolved_at vs resolve_due_at) — as met | breached | pending | no_sla. HONESTY CONTRACT: attainment_pct = met/(met+breached); no_sla tickets (no SLA policy applied) and pending tickets (deadline not yet expired) are EXCLUDED from that denominator, and both counts are reported alongside the percentage so the exclusion is visible, never silent. median_first_response_minutes / median_resolution_minutes are computed only from tickets carrying the real timestamps — never imputed. Counts are whole-window, not page-limited.

tools.name: helpdesk_ticket_add_message
tools.description: Add a message to a ticket. direction defaults to "internal" (an internal note). Use helpdesk_ticket_send_reply for customer-visible outbound replies — this tool does NOT send anything on an email or SMS ticket. An internal note never stops the first-response SLA clock, and neither does an outbound row that was not actually delivered.

tools.name: helpdesk_ticket_assign
tools.description: Assign a ticket to a human (assigned_to_id) or a queue (queue_id). Both are validated against the account — including teammates who joined by invitation — and a value that does not belong to it is rejected with 400 rather than silently dropped. Pass null to unassign.

tools.name: helpdesk_ticket_create
tools.description: Create a new helpdesk ticket. Contact resolution precedence: crm_contact_id → contact_email → contact_phone (one is required). If the email/phone isn't on file, a contact is lazy-created with lead_source='helpdesk' (a phone-created contact has no email). Phones are normalized to E.164 before lookup; multiple contacts can legitimately share a phone (shared office lines — there is deliberately NO unique index), so a multi-match resolves to the OLDEST contact and the 201 body includes contact_resolution { matched_by: 'phone', ambiguous: true } — use crm_contact_merge to heal the split rather than ignoring it. Two simultaneous tickets from the same unknown phone can race into twin contacts (same race the email branch has). The ticket fires the helpdesk_ticket_created workflow trigger and runs the account's auto-acknowledge / auto-assign / SLA automations. The 201 body reflects auto-assign and both SLA deadlines — they are applied before it returns. auto_acknowledge and the team notification are still in flight and are listed under automations.pending; re-read with helpdesk_ticket_get if you need to confirm the acknowledgement went out. Optional first_message attaches the customer's initial message in one call (direction defaults to 'inbound'). Channel still defaults to 'email' even when resolving by contact_phone — pass channel: 'sms' when ticketing a texter. Priority defaults to normal. tags are free-form labels.

tools.name: helpdesk_ticket_escalate_to_human
tools.description: Escalate a ticket: forces priority=urgent, optionally assigns to a human/queue, adds the "escalated" tag. RE-CLOCKS THE SLA onto the urgent rung, anchored on the ticket's created_at — so escalating an old ticket can put its deadline in the past and surface it as breached immediately. That is intended: an urgent ticket that is three days old IS breached. Deadlines only ever tighten, never loosen. Omitting assigned_to_id LEAVES THE CURRENT ASSIGNEE IN PLACE; pass null explicitly to unassign.

tools.name: helpdesk_ticket_get
tools.description: Fetch one ticket. Pass include=messages to get the inline message log.

tools.name: helpdesk_ticket_list
tools.description: List support tickets with filters (status, priority, channel, queue, assignee, contact, company).

tools.name: helpdesk_ticket_list_for_company
tools.description: List a company's tickets.

tools.name: helpdesk_ticket_list_for_contact
tools.description: List a contact's tickets (shorthand for helpdesk_ticket_list with contact_id).

tools.name: helpdesk_ticket_merge
tools.description: Merge this ticket into another. `id` is the SOURCE and gets closed; merge_into_id is the TARGET that receives the messages — get them backwards and you close the wrong ticket. Writes a system note on BOTH threads recording the merge, and returns messages_moved plus messages_deduplicated (two tickets from the same email thread can carry the same provider message; the duplicate is discarded rather than duplicated). Moved messages keep their original timestamps. Refuses a self-merge with 400.

tools.name: helpdesk_ticket_messages
tools.description: Convenience: fetch a ticket with its message log inline.

tools.name: helpdesk_ticket_send_reply
tools.description: Send a customer-visible reply to a ticket (direction=outbound). Sends FIRST and records after, so a delivery failure returns an error rather than a row claiming the customer was answered. Refuses with 422 no_recipient on an email or SMS ticket with no reachable address — pass `to` to override the recipient. Stops the first-response SLA clock only when the reply is genuinely delivered by a human or AI author; an auto-acknowledgement never does. author_kind: 'user' (a person) or 'ai_agent' (default). 'human' is accepted as an alias for 'user'.

tools.name: helpdesk_ticket_set_priority
tools.description: Update ticket priority. Re-derives both SLA deadlines from the new priority, anchored on created_at — deadlines only ever tighten, so de-escalating never hands a nearly-breached ticket a fresh window. Rejects anything outside low|normal|high|urgent.

tools.name: helpdesk_ticket_set_status
tools.description: Update ticket status. Auto-sets resolved_at / closed_at when the status flips to resolved or closed, and CLEARS them when it reopens to open/pending. Rejects anything outside open|pending|resolved|closed — the value is stored verbatim and every filter matches it exactly, so a mis-cased status would hide the ticket from every view.

tools.name: helpdesk_ticket_transfer_to_voice
tools.description: Annotate the ticket for a voice transfer. The actual outbound dial is picked up by voice_server.

tools.name: helpdesk_tickets_overdue
tools.description: Surface tickets that have breached SLA — first_response_due_at or resolve_due_at is in the past AND the corresponding actual timestamp is missing. Excludes resolved/closed tickets. Use kind=first_response to focus on missed reply windows, kind=resolve for missed resolutions, kind=both (default) for either.

tools.name: helpdesk_workload
tools.description: Per-agent staffing snapshot — the quantity read beside helpdesk_csat_stats (quality per assignee). For every assignee plus the unassigned bucket: open/pending counts, currently-breached SLA counts (same predicates as helpdesk_tickets_overdue: due date passed, actual timestamp missing, ticket still open/pending), and oldest_open_at. Counts are whole-table grouped aggregates, never page-limited. The unassigned bucket is the null-assignee view the ticket-list API cannot filter for. Assignees whose user record is outside this account return name: null with the id. Optional queue_id scopes every count to one queue.

tools.name: history_cancel_preview_restore
tools.description: Destroy the isolated preview app spawned by history_preview_restore. Pass the preview_session_id from the spawn response. Idempotent — calling against an already-torn-down session returns ok=true + already_torn_down=true. Cleanup is best-effort: per-step failures (Fly destroy / S3 sweep) are reported in the response's `errors` field and the orphan-sweeper cron retries any partial teardown after 1h. If you don't have the preview_session_id, call history_list_preview_sessions first to find active sessions for the project.

tools.name: history_list_preview_sessions
tools.description: List ephemeral preview-restore sessions for a project. Returns active sessions by default (status NOT IN destroyed/failed); pass include_finished='true' for the full history. Use this to (a) find a preview_session_id for an existing session before tearing it down, (b) audit abandoned sessions, or (c) hand a still-running preview_url back to the user mid-conversation.

tools.name: history_preview_restore
tools.description: Spawn an ISOLATED ephemeral preview app for a checkpoint or point-in-time snapshot. The canonical project container is never touched — a broken snapshot can't break the user's working dev environment.
