Returns { preview_session_id, preview_url } the user can open in a browser / iframe. When done, call history_cancel_preview_restore({preview_session_id}) to destroy the isolated app. Spawn takes 30-90s (snapshot upload + Fly app create + machine boot + health poll). On health-check failure the route auto-destroys the half-spawned app and returns 504 with code='preview_unhealthy'. To COMMIT the previewed state to the canonical project, call history_restore_to_time OR project_checkpoint_restore — those write to the canonical DB and container, separate from the isolated preview app. Tearing down the preview session is independent of (and not required before) committing. Exactly one of as_of OR checkpoint_id is required.

tools.name: history_restore_to_time
tools.description: Restore the project to its state at an arbitrary timestamp (point-in-time restore). Unlike project_checkpoint_restore, this works even when no snapshot was taken at the target time — it reconstructs by querying per-row created_at trails and matching the right S3 object versions. Files that exist now but didn't exist at the target time are NOT removed (same semantics as the checkpoint restore). For strict point-in-time recreation, follow with project_files_bulk_save + delete_missing=true using the snapshot from project_state_at. Pairs with history_preview_restore for try-before-commit workflows. The Fly preview is re-synced automatically with every file at the target moment force-pushed past the container's change-detection; the response's `preview` reports liveTextForced / liveTextSynced / liveTextRemaining — liveTextRemaining > 0 means the container is NOT yet a faithful copy, call project_preview_sync again.

tools.name: hiveboard_align
tools.description: Align elements to an edge or centre, and/or space them evenly. ONE tool for both, because they take the same inputs, produce the same deltas, and are almost always wanted together. Re-spacing a row of stickies used to mean computing a dx/dy for each one by hand and sending an elements_patch - a one-click operation everywhere else with no API equivalent. align: left | right | top | bottom | center_x | center_y. distribute: horizontal | vertical, with even GAPS between the current extremes, or a fixed `spacing` if you pass one. Both together applies align first, then distributes the aligned result. Select with element_ids or region. Connectors are excluded from the selection - aligning a line independently detaches it from what it joins - but every connector bound to something that moved is re-anchored, so arrows follow. NO SNAPSHOT is taken, unlike autolayout, and that is the point: the move is fully specified by your own selection and the response returns the exact `deltas` applied, so the inverse call undoes it. Use dry_run to see the deltas first.

tools.name: hiveboard_connect
tools.description: Wire arrows between elements that already exist, by id, with the geometry solved for you. A connector needs two things and they do different jobs. The stored coordinates are what gets DRAWN; the bindings are what keeps the endpoints attached when a human later drags one of the boxes. Building it by hand means resolving each id to a box, which lives in a different field per element type, then picking the right pair of edge anchors. That is why the old way to draw a diagram was two calls with an id-zipping step in between, where one invalid row shifted every id after it and the arrows attached to the wrong boxes. Each connection picks the anchor pair the relationship implies: side to side when the two boxes are mostly apart horizontally, bottom to top otherwise, matching what the editor's own connection mode does. A text element has no stored width or height anywhere, so its box can only be estimated server-side; connecting to one is the case you cannot do correctly from outside. Connecting TO an arrow or line is refused. Returns connector_ids and a `skipped` list with the reason for each. Additive.

tools.name: hiveboard_create
tools.description: Create a new Hiveboard (Miro-style canvas). Optionally attach to a project. Use this for sitemaps, brainstorms, sales flows, customer journey maps, etc. After creating, add content via hiveboard_element_create / hiveboard_elements_bulk_create, OR call hiveboard_sitemap_scaffold to auto-place a tree of pages, OR call hiveboard_import_miro to ingest an existing Miro JSON export.

tools.name: hiveboard_delete
tools.description: Delete a Hiveboard. Cascades to every element on the board.

tools.name: hiveboard_duplicate
tools.description: Clone a Hiveboard + every element into a new board (same account, optionally renamed).

tools.name: hiveboard_element_create
tools.description: Add a single element to a Hiveboard. Element types: "rectangle", "circle", "diamond", "triangle", "hexagon", "text", "sticky-note", "frame", "arrow", "line", "pen", "image". Position {x, y} is the element's TOP-LEFT corner, not its centre: the builder sets start={x,y} and end={x+width,y+height} (hiveku_builder/src/lib/hiveboards/element-builder.ts:130-135). This description previously said "center-origin", which put every generated element off by half its size (80x50 at the default 160x100) and left connector arrows pointing at corners instead of edges. To centre a shape on a point, subtract half the width and height yourself. element_data is type-specific (e.g. {text, width, height} for shapes; {points: [...]} for pen; {startConnection, endConnection} for arrow). Sticky notes are the exception to colour: element_data.color must be one of yellow, blue, green, pink, purple, orange. Anything else (a hex, most obviously) is coerced to yellow, because the renderer looks the name up in a table and used to CRASH the whole board on a miss. Additive - does NOT touch other elements on the board. For many elements use hiveboard_elements_bulk_create.

tools.name: hiveboard_element_delete
tools.description: Remove one element by id.

tools.name: hiveboard_element_update
tools.description: Patch ONE element. Allow-listed: element_type, element_data, position, z_index, rotation, color, fill_color, stroke_width, font_size, locked, hidden. element_data is REPLACED wholesale, never merged, and the renderer needs the complete typed element: sending {label: 'New name'} strips start/end and breaks that element on the canvas. Read the element first (hiveboard_elements_find with include_data), change the one field, send the whole object back. For a MERGE, and for a move that also drags the attached connectors along, use hiveboard_elements_patch instead. Style fields are now mirrored into element_data for you, so color/z_index/locked and friends take effect. They previously wrote a column the renderer never reads, which returned 200 and changed nothing on screen. `hidden` is still read by no renderer at all.

tools.name: hiveboard_elements_bulk_create
tools.description: Add up to 5000 elements in one call. Each element is the same shape as hiveboard_element_create. Additive — does NOT delete existing content. Returns {created, invalid, errors[]}.

tools.name: hiveboard_elements_find
tools.description: Find elements on a board by type, by the text they show, or by the region they sit in, without pulling the whole board. Returns a projection: id, element_type, z_index, box {x,y,w,h}, and the text. Text matching is one field whatever the type keeps it in: a shape shows its `label`, a text element and a sticky show their `content`. Getting that distinction wrong by hand is why a search for a card by its caption used to come back empty. Set include_data true when you are about to call hiveboard_elements_patch: that tool merges into the stored element_data, so you need to see what is already there. Leave it off otherwise; raw element_data is what makes a board read expensive. Region is JSON {x, y, w, h} and matches anything OVERLAPPING it, not only what is fully inside. Read-only.

tools.name: hiveboard_elements_patch
tools.description: Update many elements at once, and the ONLY correct way to move something on a board. Three things separate it from hiveboard_element_update. (1) element_data MERGES here instead of being replaced, so changing one label cannot strip an element's geometry and break it on the canvas. (2) A move is a real move: shapes carry their position in start/end, stickies and text and images carry it in position, a pen carries every point, and patching the position column alone moves nothing. (3) Connectors follow: every arrow bound to something that moved has its endpoints translated by the same delta, across the WHOLE board, because the arrows that break are exactly the ones you did not name. Moving a FRAME: pass include_children: true on that update and everything inside the frame moves with it, by the same majority-of-area rule the editor uses when you drag one. Off by default, so an existing move is unchanged. Call hiveboard_frames first to see what would come along. Use `text` rather than guessing the field: it writes `label` on a shape and `content` on a text or sticky. Style fields are mirrored into element_data so they take effect. Returns updated, connectors_repaired, skipped (with reasons) and not_found. An id belonging to another board simply does not resolve and comes back in not_found.

tools.name: hiveboard_elements_prune
tools.description: DESTRUCTIVE. Remove many elements from a board at once, by ids, by type, by region, or the whole canvas. The board itself survives; use hiveboard_delete for that. This is what makes a generated board fixable. Every scaffold is additive, so re-running one stacks a second copy on the first, and until this existed cleanup was one call per element: a 200-element mistake cost 200 calls to undo. It snapshots the board into version history first and returns snapshot_version_id. If that comes back NULL the delete was NOT recoverable, and you should say so rather than assume a rollback exists. confirm: true is required. An empty filter is never treated as 'everything': clearing the canvas has to be asked for with all: true, by name. Returns deleted, the recomputed element_count, and any requested ids that were not on this board.

tools.name: hiveboard_flow_scaffold
tools.description: Build a directed flow diagram in one call from nodes and edges: a process map, a user flow, an onboarding flow, or a swimlane handoff map. Those are one drawing with different nouns, so this is one tool. YOU PASS RELATIONSHIPS, IT DERIVES THE LAYOUT. Each node is ranked one layer after its latest predecessor, so the flow reads in dependency order however you listed it, and within a layer nodes are ordered by their predecessors' positions to stop the arrows crossing. A node with TWO parents works here, which is the thing hiveboard_sitemap_scaffold structurally cannot express. Cycles are fine. A rework loop ('failed review' back to 'draft') is drawn dashed and curved and does not flatten the layout; the response lists back_edges so you can see which ones it treated that way. Node types map to the shapes readers actually parse: start/end become terminator circles, decision becomes a diamond, handoff becomes a hexagon, step becomes a card. Label a decision as a question and label both edges leaving it. Pass `lanes` to draw swimlanes. The lane then decides the cross axis instead of the crossing-minimised order, because a swimlane diagram exists to say WHO does each step. A frame is a visual grouping only: it contains nothing in any data sense. An edge naming an unknown node is a 400, not a silently missing branch. Additive. Returns node_to_element_id and node_ranks.

tools.name: hiveboard_frames
tools.description: What is inside each frame on this board. CORRECTS THE DOCS: "a frame contains nothing in any data sense" is true of the schema and false of the product. The editor has always dragged a frame's children with it, using a majority-of-area rule; that rule is now reachable from the API. An element belongs to a frame when at least half its area is inside it. Pair with include_children on hiveboard_elements_patch to move a frame and its contents together. `straddler_ids` is the second answer worth having: elements overlapping a frame but not mostly inside it, so they will NOT move with it. Almost always an accident, and invisible until someone drags the frame.

tools.name: hiveboard_funnel_scaffold
tools.description: Build a whole conversion funnel in one call: a card per stage, its metric beside it, a connector carrying the conversion rate, and a drop-off callout beside every leak. The stage that loses the most is highlighted automatically. YOU PASS COUNTS, IT DERIVES THE RATES. Step conversion, step drop-off in both percent and absolute contacts, overall top-to-bottom conversion, and the single biggest leak all come back in the response, so you can quote the same numbers you just drew. Pull the counts from crm_pipeline_stage_summary or the analytics tools rather than inventing them; a funnel with unattributed numbers is a liability. A missing count is not a zero: the connector says 'no data' rather than drawing a confident 0% that reads as a catastrophe. width_mode 'proportional' tapers each card by its share of the top stage, which is what makes a funnel look like a funnel. Widths are floored so a 2% stage stays readable. Additive: it never deletes existing content, so a second call stacks on the first unless you move the origin. Returns stage_to_element_id and the full conversion table.

tools.name: hiveboard_get
tools.description: Fetch a Hiveboard's metadata + every element (z-indexed). Returns elements: [{id, element_type, element_data, position, z_index, color, fill_color, ...}] plus workshop_state, which carries the live dot-vote ledger ({active, budget, frozen, votes:[{elementId, userId}]}) and the session timer. A frozen tally is what a facilitated workshop leaves behind, so that field is how you report what the room actually chose. This returns EVERY element with its full element_data and takes no filters, so on a large board it is expensive. To read a board as a diagram use hiveboard_outline; to find specific elements use hiveboard_elements_find.

tools.name: hiveboard_grid_scaffold
tools.description: Build any board that is content binned on two axes: a customer journey map (stages across, facets down), a retro, a kanban snapshot, a SWOT, a RACI, an affinity wall. One drawing, different nouns, one tool. IT SIZES ITSELF TO THE CONTENT. A sticky note is the only element whose text wraps, and text past its box scrolls INTERNALLY, so the overflow is invisible until someone clicks the note. Each row is therefore sized from its longest cell, and any cell still too long comes back in `truncated` rather than being silently swallowed. Shorten or split those; do not assume they rendered. A row typed 'scores' is drawn as a curve with a dot and a reading per column, auto-scaled to its own range, which is how an emotion line gets onto a journey map without you picking a scale. It is a line, never a filled area: the canvas has no fill primitive outside its six shapes, so there are no pie or area charts here at all. Every row's cells array must be exactly as long as columns, in column order, with null for an empty cell. A length mismatch is a 400 naming both counts, because padding it would slide every later cell one column left and look plausible. Sticky colour is a NAME (yellow, blue, green, pink, purple, orange), never a hex. Additive. Returns cell_to_element_id keyed '<row> <column>'.

tools.name: hiveboard_import_miro
tools.description: Import a Miro board export into Hiveku. Accepts the raw JSON from Miro's REST API (GET /v2/boards/<id>/items) — the {board, items: [...]} shape. Mapping handles shape/sticky_note/text/frame/image/paint; unsupported types (mindmap_node, card, kanban, etc.) are skipped with warnings. Miro's items endpoint doesn't include connectors, so imported boards have content but no arrows. Use hiveboard_element_create afterward to wire connections, or hiveboard_sitemap_scaffold if the import was a sitemap. Either creates a NEW board (omit board_id; name defaults to the Miro board's name) or APPENDS to an existing one (pass board_id). Returns {board_id, created, inserted, summary: {by_type, converted, skipped}, warnings}.

tools.name: hiveboard_list
tools.description: List Hiveboards in the account, newest-edited first. Returns summary cards: id, name, project_id, background_type, element_count, created/edited timestamps. Use `search` to find a board by name rather than listing and matching yourself: the list is capped at 200 and truncates silently, so on an account with many boards a client-side match can miss the one you want.

tools.name: hiveboard_outline
tools.description: Read a board as a STRUCTURE rather than a pile of elements: nodes with their labels and boxes, plus the edge list joining them. The edge list is the point, because it exists nowhere in the data. A connector is a row whose element_data names two other element ids, and nothing joins them back up, so without this the only way to learn what is connected to what is to pull every element through hiveboard_get and rebuild the graph yourself. On a large board that is tens of thousands of tokens for one question. unbound_connectors is the diagnostic worth reading: an arrow drawn between two boxes with no bindings only LOOKS like a relationship. It does not survive a human dragging either box and it is invisible to any structural read. A board full of them needs re-wiring with hiveboard_connect. Read-only. Also returns orphan_count and the board's extent, which is what you need to pick an origin that does not land a new diagram on top of the old one.

tools.name: hiveboard_render
tools.description: SEE a board. Returns a PNG of the board and INLINES it as an image content block, so you look at what you built instead of verifying it by coordinate arithmetic. This is a screenshot of the REAL canvas - the same renderer a human opens - not a server-side re-drawing of element_data. So it cannot disagree with what the client sees. WORKFLOW: scaffold or edit -> hiveboard_render -> look at it. Overlapping labels, text bleeding out of a card, a funnel that does not read as a funnel and elements invisible against the board background are all things no amount of checking x/y/width/height will catch. FRAMING: by default the whole board is fitted to the viewport. Pass `region` {x,y,w,h} OR `element_ids` (not both) to frame part of it, and `scale` to force a zoom instead of fitting. On a big board, fitting everything makes text unreadable - render a region. `overflow[]` is the payoff beyond the picture: every shape label wider than its box and every sticky whose text scrolls invisibly, measured in the real browser from the same paint. `visible_bleed` a reader will notice; `hidden_scroll` they will not, because a sticky hides its overflow until clicked. A FAILED RENDER NEVER RETURNS AN IMAGE. If the page could not prove it finished painting you get a non-2xx with a `reason` and a `hint`, because a blank picture beside a 200 is indistinguishable from an empty board. `blank: true` on a SUCCESS means the board genuinely has no elements. Costs a headless capture per call and takes ~5-15s, so it is a write-scoped tool rather than a free read.

tools.name: hiveboard_restore_version
tools.description: Put a board back to a saved version. Deletes every element and recreates from the snapshot, so `confirm: true` is required. IT IS ITSELF REVERSIBLE: the current canvas is snapshotted first, in the same transaction, and the new version id comes back as `pre_restore_version_id`. A null there means the board was empty, not that you cannot get back. Refuses with 409 restore_would_be_lossy when more than a fifth of the snapshot is of a type no renderer draws, because those rows come back invisible and a recovery you cannot trust is worse than one that fails loudly. Pass accept_lossy: true to take a partial restore anyway - often the right call, but it should be a decision. `restored` is what was ACTUALLY inserted and `degraded` says what came back diminished. Check both: a 200 does not mean the board looks like it did.

tools.name: hiveboard_sequence_scaffold
tools.description: Build an outreach sequence or cadence board in one call: a card per touch, the wait carried on the connector between them, a decision diamond wherever the path forks on a reply, and a goal terminator at the end. YOU PASS WAITS, IT DERIVES THE CALENDAR. Per-step waits are accumulated into an absolute day offset and stamped on every card, and the schedule comes back in the response. Nobody reading a cadence wants 'wait 3 days' five times; they want to know the last touch lands on day 21. The wait on a step is the gap BEFORE it, which is how every sequence tool on the platform models it, so the input maps straight onto email_sequence_get's step list. This is deliberately not hiveboard_flow_scaffold with different words: that one takes a graph and has no time semantics, and using it here would mean building the nodes, the edges and the day arithmetic yourself. on_reply forks the path: a diamond goes on the main line, the outcome card sits on its own row above it clear of everything, and the sequence resumes from the fork. Additive. Returns step_to_element_id, the derived schedule, and total_span_days.

tools.name: hiveboard_sitemap_scaffold
tools.description: Build a whole tree on a Hiveboard in one call: a sitemap, an org chart, a taxonomy, a decision tree. Pass `pages` either as a flat list with `parent` refs OR as a nested tree with `children`; the server detects which shape you sent. Each node becomes a frame labelled with its title, with `path` rendered as a caption underneath it. Parent-to-child arrows are wired automatically with real connections, not floating lines. SET pack_subtrees: true FOR ANYTHING UNBALANCED. The default layout groups nodes by depth and orders each depth by sibling index, so at depth 2 with several parents the subtrees interleave and the arrows cross. pack_subtrees runs a tidy layout instead: every subtree gets a contiguous band and a parent sits centred over its own children. It is off by default only so existing boards do not change shape. Additive: it never deletes existing content, so a second call STACKS another tree on the first unless you pass a different origin. Returns title_to_element_id, which is the only cheap way to patch one node later. Duplicate titles are a hard 400 and nothing is created, because titles are the join key. A parent naming a title that does not exist is silently treated as a root, so check arrows_created against the number of nodes that had a parent. Example flat input: {pages: [{title:"Home",path:"/"}, {title:"About",parent:"Home"}, {title:"Team",parent:"About"}]}

tools.name: hiveboard_update
tools.description: Update a Hiveboard's metadata. Allow-listed: name, description, background_type, background_color, is_public, project_id. Never touches elements. is_public does NOT mean public to the internet. The board is already scoped to its account, so it means any member of THIS account may open it without being granted access to it individually. Pass project_id to attach the board to a project after the fact, or null to detach it. A project_id from another account is a 404, not a silent re-home.

tools.name: hiveboard_validate
tools.description: Lint a board. Almost every defect this surface produces returns 200 and looks successful, so counting elements proves nothing - this is the class worth checking against. CHECKS: malformed_elements (no derivable box - THE CRASHING ONE, see below) - invisible_elements (an element the same colour as the ground it sits on, including the default near-black on a dark board) - text_overflow (a label wider than its box, or a sticky whose content will not fit) - dangling_connectors (bound to an id that is no longer on the board) - unbound_connectors - collisions - backwards_edges. malformed_elements is the one to act on first. A partial hiveboard_element_update REPLACES element_data wholesale, so sending {label:"x"} to a rectangle erases its start/end; the renderer then dereferences shape.start.x and the WHOLE BOARD fails to render, after that update returned 200. Use hiveboard_elements_patch, which merges. text_overflow reports `visibility`: visible_bleed means a label runs past its card and a reader will see it; hidden_scroll means a sticky is scrolling internally and nobody will ever notice. backwards_edges is INFO, never an error. Author intent is not recorded anywhere, so a deliberate feedback loop and a mistake look identical. `ok` is true when nothing structural is broken; warnings can be fine. Costs nothing and works on a board far too large to photograph legibly - use hiveboard_render for what it LOOKS like, this for what is wrong with it.

tools.name: hiveboard_version_get
tools.description: One version, and what restoring it would COST - before you restore it. `would_degrade` is the important field. A snapshot can contain rows whose element type no renderer draws; those restore as database rows that never appear on the canvas, so the board comes back visibly emptier. It also counts rows that would stack at the origin for want of a position, and rows that would fall back to black. `snapshot_format` is columns | wire | mixed. Two formats exist in real data and restore accepts both; `mixed` means the same board was written through both paths. The snapshot payload is OFF by default because it is unbounded - a large board is tens of thousands of tokens. Pass include_snapshot only when you actually need to read the elements.

tools.name: hiveboard_versions_list
tools.description: Board history, newest first. THIS IS THE UNDO. Without it every scaffold, prune and layout change is a one-way door, which is why the guidance used to be "do not plan to reposition". Versions are written by the dashboard autosave and by the pre-prune snapshot, so an agent-built board that nobody has opened may legitimately have none. `author_name` is "Automatic" when no human did it - an autosave, or a snapshot taken by an API key, which has no profile. The page size is 50 and is NOT configurable; `truncated` tells you when you are seeing only the newest 50.

tools.name: hiveku_batch
tools.description: Run up to 25 tool calls in ONE round trip. Reach for it whenever you need several independent reads - an audit, a status sweep, gathering context before a decision. Each separate call is a round trip, a transcript entry and a permission decision; batched they cost one of each, and the rate limiter charges a batch far less than the same calls made singly. calls: [{ label?, tool, args }]. Results come back IN INPUT ORDER - read each `ok`, because one member failing does not fail the batch. stop_on_error:true aborts after the first failure. ★ IT DOES NOT WIDEN WHAT YOU MAY DO: every member is checked against this connection's key scope and tool profile exactly as a direct call would be, and a refused member comes back ok:false while the rest still run. ★ Members run in parallel ONLY when every one is a read. Any write makes the whole batch sequential - concurrent identical writes would collide on the idempotency key and one would replay the other's response, reporting two successes for one write. Over 25 calls the batch is refused and NOTHING runs; it is never silently trimmed. hiveku_batch cannot be nested. ★ A TOOL THAT RETURNS A PICTURE CANNOT SHOW IT FROM INSIDE A BATCH: a batch result is one JSON text block, so an inlined image (project_annotation_screenshot, preview_screenshot) cannot travel in it. That member comes back with `uncarried_content` naming the block and its size - and with `result: null`, meaning could-not-be-carried, if the tool returned no text either. Call those directly, outside the batch. Response shape: { batch_id, count, ok_count, failed_count, stopped_early, executed_in, results[{label,ok,status,bytes,duration_ms,result|error,uncarried_content?}] }. max_bytes_per_result (default 2048) caps each payload.

tools.name: hiveku_docs_get
tools.description: Get full documentation for a single Hiveku/Olympus endpoint — path params, query params, request body schema, response example, and notes (gotchas, duplicate detection, workflow triggers). Use this AFTER hiveku_docs_search has narrowed you down to a candidate endpoint, before you call the corresponding MCP tool.

tools.name: hiveku_docs_search
tools.description: Search the Hiveku/Olympus API documentation. Returns matching endpoint summaries (path, methods, description, category, tags). Use this BEFORE guessing — it covers every CRM, marketing, SEO, helpdesk, PM, voice, and integration endpoint. Filter by keyword (search) or category (crm, marketing, seo, helpdesk, pm, voice, integrations, etc.). Call hiveku_docs_get with a specific path to see request/response shapes.

tools.name: hiveku_playbook_get
tools.description: Get full detail for a single playbook by id — every step, sample arguments, prerequisites, related endpoints, and gotchas. Use this when hiveku_playbooks_list surfaced a candidate and you want the actual sequence to execute.

tools.name: hiveku_playbooks_list
tools.description: List Hiveku how-to PLAYBOOKS — named chained-workflow recipes. Each playbook bundles 3-7 tool calls into a complete task: "edit a file and ship it", "estimate → invoice", "rollback a project", "debug a failed deploy", etc. Use playbooks BEFORE composing your own multi-step flow — they encode the canonical Hiveku sequence and call out the right tools in the right order. Beats stitching things together from `hiveku_docs_search` results. Categories: sites, files, deployments, preview, crm, content. Filter with `playbooks_category` if you only want one bucket.

tools.name: hiveku_tool_schema
tools.description: Return the EXACT parameter schema for one or more tools - the signature, not the prose. Use it the moment you are unsure what a tool takes, and ALWAYS before retrying a call that failed on argument shape. hiveku_find_tools and hiveku_docs_search return descriptions; neither returns a signature, so the only way to learn a parameter name was to guess and read the error. Guessing produced query for sql, template_slug for slug, variables for overrides, projectId for project_id, a string array where an object array was required - each costing a call and a retry. Per tool you get: name, method, path, description, required[], properties (the real JSON Schema, including nested item shapes), and forwarded_as. ★ forwarded_as is the field that exists nowhere else. It maps each declared argument to where it actually goes - body, query or path - so it states positively what is accepted and, by omission, what is not. An argument absent from it is DROPPED BY THE PROXY before the request leaves, which is why a call can fail complaining about a field you believe you just set. Pass `names` (up to 20 exact tool names) or `search` (a substring, max 20 results). A tool this key cannot call comes back as { name, available:false, reason } rather than being omitted - an omission reads as 'no such tool' and sends you hunting for a name that exists. Response shape: { tools: [{ name, available, method, path, description, required, properties, forwarded_as, shaping_supported }], count, not_found[] }.

tools.name: html
tools.description: 🕷️ CRAWL4AI: Extract rendered HTML (Firecrawl-backed)

tools.name: ice_score
tools.description: ICE prioritization scoring (Impact × Confidence × Ease) — pure math, no persistence. Use to rank growth experiments, findings, SEO action items, pm_tasks, etc. against a consistent framework instead of inventing per-call scoring. Two modes: 1. Single — pass {impact, confidence, ease} → {score (1-1000), normalized_score (0-1), components} 2. Batch — pass {items: [{label, impact, confidence, ease, ...passthrough}]} → {items: [{...passthrough, score, rank, input_index}], summary: {count, top_score, mean_score}} Batch mode preserves every input field on each item (notes, evidence, action_url, etc.) so you can round-trip a list through the scorer without losing context. Sorted by score desc, stable tiebreak on input order. Each component clamped to [1,10] with a per-item warning when out of range. Formula: score = impact * confidence * ease. Range 1-1000. Normalized: score/1000.

tools.name: integration_connect_link_create
tools.description: Mint the link a human clicks to connect or re-authenticate ANY provider for the bound account: a Hiveku URL (https://app.hiveku.com/connect/oauth/<token>) that lives ttl_hours (default 24, max 168), explains the connection in plain language, and sends them to the provider's consent screen when they press Continue — the account + connector + OAuth client are resolved server-side at click time, so the 5-minute consent window starts when THEY are ready, not when you called this. Uses the account's own OAuth app when one is tagged for the product, otherwise Hiveku's platform app (the same client the dashboard's Quick connect uses) — so a missing oauth_apps row is no longer a dead end for Google Analytics, Search Console, Business Profile, Google Ads, Calendar or Microsoft Ads. Gmail and Outlook stay bring-your-own-client and need owner_user_email (whose CRM inbox it is). RECONNECT (dead refresh token, missing scope such as analytics.edit, 'Account has been deleted'): pass target_connection_id = the existing row id (integration_connectors_list → connections[].id, or seo_connections_list / ppc_connection_list / crm_list_email_connections / social_list_accounts). Credentials are replaced IN PLACE under the client that minted the row (a Hiveku-native row stays native, a BYOK row stays on its app), bindings are kept, status goes back to connected. Never delete-and-recreate to fix a token. CREATE: omit target_connection_id. Optional bindings: google_ads customer_id / manager_id / developer_token (required when the account's OWN Google app is used; not needed on the Hiveku app), google_search_console site_url, google_business_profile gbp_account_id + gbp_location_id, google_analytics ga_property_id, shopify shop_domain (required) + project_id, outlook tenant, gmail/outlook scope_label (readonly | send | modify | modify_with_calendar, default modify_with_calendar) + consumers (['crm'] | ['helpdesk']). Bindings not given are picked after consent (the status reports needs_binding). Returns {link_id, url, expires_at, connector, provider, table, mode, client_source, oauth_app_id, connection_id, handoff{headline, what_they_will_see, pick_hint, permissions[], after_consent, next_step}, polling, instructions}. THE URL IS SHOWN ONCE (only a hash is stored) — hand it over now, on its own line, with what they will see and which account to pick. Then poll integration_connect_link_status({ link_id, wait_seconds: 8 }) when they say they are through. source ('plugin' | 'vscode' | 'app' | 'agent') only changes the 'return to ...' copy on the done page. Errors: 400 connector_unknown (lists the vocabulary; aliases like ga4, gsc, gbp, bing_ads, facebook, twitter work), 422 connector_not_linkable (no consent flow; diagnostic.dashboard_path), 402 plan_upgrade_required (connecting a NEW X account needs the Premium plan; reconnect is allowed), 412 no_oauth_client (nothing can front the consent; hint says exactly what to register; diagnostic.existing_apps), 400 owner_required (gmail/outlook: pass owner_user_email; diagnostic.candidates), 400 bindings_required (BYOK Google Ads without developer_token + customer_id), 404 target_connection_not_found. Do not mint unprompted: offer, and mint when the user picks it.

tools.name: integration_connect_link_list
tools.description: This account's connect links, newest first — status, connector, outcome, opened/completed timestamps, note. THE URL IS NEVER HERE (only a hash is stored): to hand someone a link you no longer have, revoke and mint a fresh one. Filters: connector (slug or alias), status (pending | opened | completed | failed | expired | revoked), limit (default 50, max 200). Read-only.

tools.name: integration_connect_link_revoke
tools.description: Kill switch for a connect link: the public page stops opening immediately and permanently. Use when a link leaked, went to the wrong person, or was superseded. A connection the link already completed is untouched. Returns {link_id, revoked:true}; 404 connect_link_not_found when the id is unknown, foreign, or already revoked.

tools.name: integration_connect_link_status
tools.description: Where a connect link stands. Pass wait_seconds (max 8) to long-poll server-side instead of hammering. Returns {link_id, connector, label, table, mode, status, terminal, client_source, connection_id, email, needs_binding[], error, opened_at, opened_count, completed_at, failed_at, expires_at, hint}. status: pending (nobody opened it), opened (they pressed Continue and are at the provider), completed (done — connection_id is the DOMAIN row in `table`; needs_binding lists what still has to be chosen, e.g. ga_property_id / site_url / gbp_location_id / customer_id, via the discover + update tools), failed (consent denied or the callback errored — error says why; the SAME link can be retried until it expires), expired, revoked. terminal:true means stop polling. Poll when the user says they are through; do not sit in a tight loop for 15 minutes.

tools.name: integration_connectors_list
tools.description: The connector catalog for THIS account — call it before offering to connect or reconnect anything. One row per connector Hiveku can run a consent for (google_analytics, google_search_console, google_business_profile, gbp_social, google_ads, gmail, google_calendar, outlook, microsoft_ads, meta_ads, meta_social, linkedin_social, linkedin_ads, tiktok_social, tiktok_ads, x, shopify, amazon_ads, vibe_ctv) with: linkable (a connect link can be minted for it), ready (linkable AND an OAuth client is available: the account's own app tagged for the product, else Hiveku's platform app), client.would_use ('byok' | 'hiveku' | null), client.byok_apps, client.native_available, client.how_to_get_ready (the exact prerequisite when nothing can front the consent), owner_required (gmail/outlook/google_calendar rows belong to one Hiveku user), the existing connections[] for that connector ({id, display, status, client_source, bound}) — the id is what target_connection_id takes on a reconnect — and dashboard_path for the manual fallback. summary.ready / needs_oauth_client / dashboard_only group the slugs. Read-only.

tools.name: integration_create
tools.description: Create an integration. Only API-KEY providers (bing_webmaster, dataforseo) can be created from CLI/MCP — OAuth providers return 422 with a dashboard URL the user must visit. Idempotent: re-running with the same provider returns the existing row updated with the new credentials and existed:true.

tools.name: integration_delete
tools.description: Soft-delete an integration (sets is_active=false). The row is preserved for audit history; downstream tools that look up by provider_slug + active will stop finding it. Accepts `integration_id` or `id`.

tools.name: integration_get
tools.description: Get one integration by id, including masked credentials_preview and last_synced_at. Accepts `integration_id` or `id`.

tools.name: integration_list
tools.description: List all account integrations (Google + marketing/sales connections). Filter by provider_slug or is_active. Returns credentials_preview (masked tokens) for confirmation only; never returns raw secrets.

tools.name: integration_oauth_check
tools.description: Poll the status of an OAuth flow started by integration_oauth_initiate. Pass setup_token (BYOK setup-token lane) OR link_id (when initiate answered with connect_link:true). Status values: pending (not completed yet), completed (setup_token lane: integration_id is the account_integrations row — the DOMAIN row id is connection_id from the initiate response; link_id lane: connection_id is returned here), failed (consent denied or the callback errored — error has the reason; a connect link can simply be retried, a setup_token needs a new initiate), expired (15 min for setup_token; the link's expires_at otherwise). With link_id you may pass wait_seconds (max 8) to long-poll server-side. Recommended interval otherwise: 5 seconds.

tools.name: integration_oauth_initiate
tools.description: Start an OAuth flow for google_ads / google_search_console / google_business_profile / google_analytics. Returns setup_url, setup_token (for polling), oauth_app_id, and (for ads/gsc/gbp) connection_id. ⚠️ DO NOT USE FOR GMAIL OR CALENDAR. Use `email_connect_start` instead — Gmail + Calendar + Meet share a single consent flow that writes to email_connections (the table CRM calendar/inbox/triage tools read). This route will return code='wrong_tool_for_provider' if you pass google_gmail or google_calendar. THREE PATHS: 1) FIRST-TIME SETUP (recommended for agents driving setup end-to-end). For google_ads pass {provider_slug, customer_id, manager_id?, developer_token} — the route creates the ppc_connections row with those bindings populated, then OAuth fills in refresh_token and status auto-promotes to 'connected'. The agent collects the three Google Ads fields from the user in conversation (developer_token from the MCC's API Center, customer_id of the client account, manager_id of the MCC), calls this tool ONCE, hands the setup_url to the user. Same for google_search_console (pass site_url) and google_business_profile (pass gbp_account_id + gbp_location_id) — but those bindings are usually discovered POST-OAuth via seo_gsc_discover_sites / seo_gbp_discover_locations, so omit them and discover later. 2) RE-AUTH (dead refresh_token, or a token missing a scope such as analytics.edit). Pass target_connection_id pointing at the existing ppc_connections / seo_connections row — google_analytics connections are seo_connections rows too (seo_connections_list shows them). Credentials get replaced in place, bindings are preserved, status auto-promotes back to 'connected'. Symptom that triggers this: integration_test reports 'Account has been deleted', or sync starts failing with OAuth errors. 3) BARE INITIATE (no pre-bindings). For google_analytics, or when you want to bind fields later via seo_connection_update / ppc_connection_update. PREFER integration_connect_link_create for anything a human has to click: it covers every connector (not just these four), returns a durable Hiveku URL (hours, not 5 minutes), never dead-ends on a missing OAuth app when Hiveku's own app can front the consent, and has one status tool. This tool remains for callers that already drive the setup_token loop. OAuth app resolution: 1. body.oauth_app_id (if supplied) — validates account ownership + product match 2. First per-account oauth_apps row tagged with the product (provider=google, products contains <the product for provider_slug>) 3. The app the EXISTING connection was minted with (its seo_connections / ppc_connections row, then the account_integrations mirror), even if it is no longer tagged for the product — the response carries oauth_app_note asking you to tag it with oauth_app_update add_products 4. Hiveku's OWN app (the same client the dashboard's Quick connect uses, and the client every dashboard-made connection with a NULL oauth_app_id was minted with). When this lane is taken — including whenever target_connection_id points at such a native row — the response has connect_link:true, setup_token:null, link_id, and setup_url is a Hiveku page (https://app.hiveku.com/connect/oauth/...) valid until expires_at; poll integration_connect_link_status({ link_id }) (or integration_oauth_check({ link_id })) instead of a setup_token. Only when none of the four resolves: 412 code='no_oauth_app_for_product' WITH diagnostic.existing_apps[] — extend one via oauth_app_update({ oauth_app_id, add_products: [<product>] }) (additive) then retry; call oauth_app_create only when the account has no Google app at all. Setup-token lane (BYOK): the setup_url is Google's consent URL and now really lasts 15 minutes (it used to die at 5 while claiming 15). A denied consent now flips the setup_token to status='failed' with the reason instead of sitting 'pending' until expiry. google_analytics re-auth via target_connection_id now refreshes the seo_connections row the GA4/GTM tools read (it previously only wrote account_integrations). After consent: poll integration_oauth_check until status='completed', then verify with integration_test (oauth/api) or ppc_connection_test (google_ads) + run the sync.

tools.name: integration_providers_list
tools.description: List available integration providers. Returns slug, name, description, auth_type ("oauth" or "api_key"), and can_create_from_cli. Use this BEFORE integration_create to discover valid slugs and check whether OAuth-required.

tools.name: integration_test
tools.description: Live-test an integration. For OAuth providers (Google *), runs an actual token refresh — success means refresh_token is still valid and the access_token gets rotated. For API-key providers, sanity-checks that credentials are present. Updates last_synced_at on success. Accepts `integration_id` or `id`.

tools.name: integration_update
tools.description: Update an integration's settings, identifier, or is_active flag. Credentials cannot be updated here — rotate via OAuth (dashboard) or re-POST for API-key providers. Accepts `integration_id` or `id`.

tools.name: job_cancel
tools.description: Cancel an in-flight async job. Idempotent on terminal jobs (returns 409 with the current status). v1 handlers don't poll for cancellation — they finish whatever they were doing — so this is best treated as 'stop charging me for this future polling round-trip' rather than a hard kill switch. For long-running jobs that haven't fully started yet (status='queued'), cancel is immediate. Once status flips to 'running', the in-process handler completes regardless.

tools.name: job_status_get
tools.description: Check any Olympus async job. PREFER LONG-POLLING: pass wait_seconds (max 25) and the server holds the request, returning the moment the job goes terminal — ONE call replaces a client-side sleep-and-poll loop (MCP calls are rate-limited; poll loops are the #1 budget burner). Typical pattern: job_status_get({ job_id, wait_seconds: 20 }) in a loop until `terminal` is true. Returns status / progress / progress_message / result / error / elapsed_ms / terminal. Large string fields in the echoed `input` are replaced with <field>_bytes stubs (you already have what you sent). The `terminal` flag is the canonical 'stop polling' signal — true when status is succeeded / failed / cancelled / timed_out. Retention: rows are kept ~90 days. After that, polling a stale job_id returns 404. To cancel a queued/running job, call job_cancel({ job_id }).

tools.name: kb_documents_get
tools.description: Fetch one knowledge-base document by id. Returns `data` with the full row: content, metadata, created_at, updated_at. It does NOT return chunks, despite what this tool used to claim. The stored vectors live in Qdrant keyed by metadata.upload_id and are reachable through kb_search, not here. The `embedding` column is a pgvector type Prisma cannot select, so it is absent from the response whether or not the document was embedded; absence is NOT evidence it is unindexed. Scoped through the KB: a document_id that exists under a DIFFERENT knowledge base 404s rather than leaking, so pass the kb_id the document actually belongs to.

tools.name: kb_stats

There is NO chunk count and this tool will never return one: chunking happens on the way into Qdrant and the vectors are addressed there by metadata.upload_id, while Postgres holds one row per indexed document. document_count is that row count, NOT a chunk count. Read sources_by_status before concluding a KB is small. A KB that looks under-populated is usually one whose sources are stuck 'pending' or 'failed' rather than one nobody fed, and document_count alone cannot tell those apart. last_indexed_at is the newest DOCUMENT created_at, so it stops moving the moment ingest stalls even while sources keep arriving.

The `github_repo_full_name` field on pm_projects is usually null even when GitHub IS connected on the website side — sites_list reads the canonical GitHub state.

tools.name: marketing_agent_actions_list
tools.description: List every script and read action marketing_agent_read can run, with a total count. Call this before guessing a script or action name. Read-only.

tools.name: marketing_agent_read
tools.description: Run one READ action from the marketing agent's own Python implementations — 131 actions across 24 scripts covering PPC (Google, Meta, TikTok, LinkedIn, Microsoft, Amazon), SEO (GSC, Bing Webmaster, GBP, audits, keywords, local) and Social. WHEN TO USE: reach for the cross-platform ppc_*, seo_* and social_* tools FIRST — they work from a connection id regardless of platform, and are the only surface with social calendar/hashtags/pillars/comments and connection lifecycle. Use this when you need per-platform DEPTH they cannot express (asset groups, experiments, split tests, lead forms, targeting facets, auction insights). DISCOVER: GET this endpoint (no body) returns every script and its allowed actions. Pass { script, action, connection_id?, args? }, e.g. { script: 'ppc_google_ads', action: 'search-terms', connection_id: '…', args: { 'date-range': 'LAST_30_DAYS' } }. READ-ONLY, and not an oversight: writes spend money or mutate platform state, and the marketing agent wraps them in a daily-budget ceiling, paused-on-create and staged approval that live ABOVE these CLIs. For writes use the ppc_*/seo_*/social_* write tools or talk_to_department({ domain: 'marketing' }).

tools.name: marketing_call_attribution_breakdown
tools.description: The same question for CALLS, which are most of a local-services advertiser's conversions. Groups this account's calls by source/medium/campaign and by day, the way a PPC platform aggregates, so the two can be laid side by side. AND IT REPORTS CALL QUALITY, WHICH THE PLATFORM STRUCTURALLY CANNOT. Google Ads counts a call as a conversion once it passes a minimum duration, regardless of whether it was a lead — so a 12-second wrong number is a conversion. This returns the duration distribution against THIS ACCOUNT'S own configured threshold, the disposition mix, and how many calls reached voicemail, were missed or were abandoned. Learning that 18 of 40 'conversions' were under 30 seconds is the point. Returns no call rows and no transcripts. ALWAYS read the caveats in the response before reporting a discrepancy: this is OUR record, not the platform's record of a conversion, and the two legitimately differ — view-through conversions have no click and can never appear here, cross-device joins are invisible to us, the platform dates by CLICK while we date by the event, and the platform also counts conversions that are not this type at all.

tools.name: marketing_call_attribution_list
tools.description: The breakdown from marketing_call_attribution_breakdown PLUS a page of individual calls. Each carries its source/medium/campaign, the tracking DID that rang and the pool session that credited it (dynamic-number insertion attributes through both), its duration bucket, whether it meets the account's own conversion policy, and has_transcript / has_summary. Returns NO transcripts and never touches storage — use marketing_call_transcript_get for a specific call. include_summaries inlines each AI summary; leave it off for a wide sweep. Breakdown percentages cover up to 5000 scanned calls: totals.truncated says when the window is larger, and totals.calls_matching is the uncapped count.

tools.name: marketing_call_transcript_get
tools.description: Read ONE call's verbatim transcript and AI summary by call id (the id field from marketing_call_attribution_list). DELIBERATELY A SEPARATE, COSTLIER STEP: the transcript is an object in the encrypted recordings bucket, so this pays a storage round trip a list sweep must never pay implicitly. Call it for calls you have a specific question about, not across a result set. THE TEXT IS VERBATIM AND UNREDACTED. A transcript contains whatever was said aloud, including card numbers, dates of birth and health details. Treat it as the most sensitive class of customer data and do not paste it anywhere it would outlive the question. When there is no transcript, transcript_state says WHICH of five situations it is, and none of them means 'empty': never_recorded (no recording ever existed, so nothing failed), pending (still processing), failed (the retry window has closed and nothing will retry it), purged (it WAS transcribed and retention later deleted it — the ai_summary is the surviving record), unreadable (the stored object is missing or will not read).

tools.name: marketing_design_export_image
tools.description: Render one frame of a design canvas to a flat PNG via the Remotion render worker; the same route as design_export_image (design_id here is its id). SYNCHRONOUS: the route polls the worker for up to 60s, re-arms once for 25s if the worker restarted mid-job, and runs to a 95s maxDuration; this tool waits 120s. Send the full Fabric.js canvas_json plus artboard width/height; the canvas must contain at least one layer. frame=0 matches what the dashboard editor would export, so use it to show the user a preview of agent-made designs; for a motion design set frame = seconds * fps. Returns { success, imageUrl, jobId, warnings? }; nothing is registered in the Media Library (use design_publish_to_library for that). BRAND FONTS RENDER SERVER-SIDE: Google-hosted families ride canvas_json.fonts, and the account's CUSTOM brand fonts (brand_custom_fonts rows carrying a css_font_face) are attached to the job automatically, so a layer set in an uploaded family renders in it. A font that cannot be loaded (a failed brand-kit read, an oversized or clipped @font-face, a family the worker could not fetch) DEGRADES to the fallback stack and is reported as a line in `warnings` on the 200 response; it never fails the render. READ warnings before showing the PNG as final: a success carrying a font warning is a brand-wrong image. Errors: 400 missing canvas_json/width/height or an empty canvas, 404 design not in this account, 500 REMOTION_RENDER_URL unset or the render itself failed, 502 the worker rejected the job, 504 the poll budget ran out. A paid render is sent ONCE: the transport never replays a 502/504, so check the design before calling again.

tools.name: marketing_design_export_mp4
tools.description: Render an animated design (per-layer keyframes) to MP4 or GIF via the Remotion render worker; the same route as design_export_mp4 (design_id here is its id). SYNCHRONOUS: the route polls the worker for up to 180s, re-arms once for 60s if the worker restarted mid-job, and runs to a 270s maxDuration; this tool waits 290s. Send the full Fabric.js canvas_json plus width/height and duration_seconds; the canvas must contain at least one layer. The worker uses the same animation vocabulary as the editor, so the output matches the in-browser preview. Returns { success, mp4Url, jobId, warnings? }. The MP4 is hosted publicly so it can be embedded directly; after this call, also PATCH the design with previewVideoUrl so the dashboard gallery shows an autoplay thumbnail. BRAND FONTS RENDER SERVER-SIDE: Google-hosted families ride canvas_json.fonts, and the account's CUSTOM brand fonts (brand_custom_fonts rows carrying a css_font_face) are attached to the job automatically, so a layer set in an uploaded family renders in it. A font that cannot be loaded (a failed brand-kit read, an oversized or clipped @font-face, a family the worker could not fetch) DEGRADES to the fallback stack and is reported as a line in `warnings` on the 200 response; it never fails the render. READ warnings before publishing or embedding: a success carrying a font warning is a brand-wrong video. Errors: 400 missing canvas_json/width/height/duration_seconds or an empty canvas, 404 design not in this account, 500 REMOTION_RENDER_URL unset or the render itself failed, 502 the worker rejected the job, 504 the poll budget ran out (the worker may still finish; there is nothing here to poll, so do not loop). A paid render is sent ONCE: the transport never replays a 502/504.

tools.name: marketing_design_get
tools.description: Get one Creative Studio design project by ID — returns the full Fabric.js canvasData, artboard settings, metadata, sectionsVersion (the CAS token for a canvas PATCH), and a dashboardUrl for the user to open it in the editor. A featuredImageUrl that is a `data:` URI (the editor's multi-MB inline canvas snapshot) comes back as null with featured_image_inline: true, replaced whole and never truncated; the fix for a real (S3) thumbnail URL is design_publish_to_library with set_as_featured. canvasData is NOT screened (it is the round-trip blob), so an inline image src arrives whole; design_state_get is the elided read.

tools.name: marketing_design_list
tools.description: List Creative Studio design projects (design_projects) with title, type, status, featured image, and preview video URL. Filter by design_type and status. A featuredImageUrl that is a `data:` URI (the editor's multi-MB inline canvas snapshot) comes back as null with featured_image_inline: true, and a `data:` previewVideoUrl as null with preview_video_inline: true, each replaced whole and never truncated: null plus the flag means the thumbnail exists only inline, not that there is none. The fix for a real (S3) thumbnail URL is design_publish_to_library with set_as_featured. limit is clamped into 1-100; a non-numeric limit is a 400.

tools.name: marketing_form_attachment_download_url
tools.description: Mint a SHORT-LIVED signed download link for ONE form attachment, by attachment id from marketing_form_attachments_list. The link is a Hiveku-signed URL that streams the file as a forced download; it expires after expires_in seconds (default 900, max 900) and cannot be revoked early. Call this only when the operator explicitly asks to read or fetch a specific file, one file per call. NEVER paste the returned URL into a document, a task, a CRM note, a chat message, a report, or a transcript summary: anyone holding the link can download the file until it expires, and the file is a visitor's personal document (a resume, an ID, a medical form). Fetch it, use it, and refer to the file by name and attachment id afterwards. Every mint is audit-logged against the calling key. Returns { url, expires_at, file_name, size_bytes, content_type }. A purged attachment returns 410 with state purged; a file that belongs to another account does not exist (404).

tools.name: marketing_form_attachments_list
tools.description: List the files visitors uploaded through forms on this account's Hiveku sites (resumes, photos, PDFs, quote attachments). Every <input type="file"> inside a captured form uploads automatically to Hiveku's private attachment store and is bound to the resulting submission; nothing on the site needs wiring, and no site ever needs an upload endpoint, an S3 client, or Supabase storage for it. Filter by ONE of submission_id (the files on a single form fill), contact_id (every file that CRM contact ever sent, newest first, with the form label and submitted date), or project_id (every attachment on one website project). With no filter, the account's newest attachments. Paginate with cursor from the previous response's next_cursor. METADATA ONLY: id, submission_id, contact_id, form_key, field, name, size, mime, state (bound | purged), created_at. No download link is minted here. To read a file, pass its id to marketing_form_attachment_download_url; a purged attachment (retention elapsed, or its submission was deleted) still lists with state purged so the record explains the gap, but it cannot be downloaded. Files are retained per the project's policy (marketing_form_upload_settings_get), 30-365 days.

tools.name: marketing_form_conversion_audit
tools.description: Answer 'the platform says 40 conversions, the CRM shows 22 — where did the other 18 go?' for FORM fills. Returns submissions with their source attribution (UTMs, click ids, channel, landing page), aggregated the way a platform aggregates (source/medium/campaign, and by day in the ad-account timezone), plus named discrepancy buckets that SUM TO THE TOTAL: deleted, duplicate, spam, archived, workflow_failed, no_attribution, unpaid_attribution, counted. Use buckets.counted as OUR number and explain the gap with the rest — '40 vs 22, and here are 11 spam, 4 duplicates, 3 with no UTMs' answers the question; a bare number does not. Unlike the dashboard Forms tab this INCLUDES spam, deleted and duplicate rows and labels them, because they ARE the answer. has_click_id isolates submissions tied to a paid click, recovered from utm_params OR the landing-page URL — which catches real paid clicks the CRM recorded as organic. Defaults to the last 30 days, UTC days, and NO field data. ALWAYS read the caveats in the response before reporting a discrepancy: this is OUR record, not the platform's record of a conversion, and the two legitimately differ — view-through conversions have no click and can never appear here, cross-device joins are invisible to us, the platform dates by CLICK while we date by the event, and the platform also counts conversions that are not this type at all. CLICK TIMING splits into what is KNOWN and what is guessed — read `click_window` before quoting either. `click_window.click_dated` is how many counted rows carry the REAL click instant (embed v3.4+). Of those, `clicks_before_range` provably clicked before the range, so the platform credited them to an EARLIER period — that is a FINDING explaining part of the gap, not a hedge. `boundary_risk` covers only rows with no dated click. A row is never in both. CRITICAL: if `click_dated` is 0, then `clicks_before_range: 0` means NOT MEASURABLE, not zero — never report it as 'no clicks fell outside the window'. Each submission also carries `attribution.first_touch_at` with `click_time_is_exact`; only an exact one dates a click, the rest merely bound it. Compare against the conversions figure from ppc_metrics (or a single conversion action's total).

tools.name: marketing_form_upload_settings_get
tools.description: Read one website project's form-upload policy: whether file inputs on its captured forms upload to Hiveku at all (enabled, default true), which file extensions are accepted (allowed_ext), the per-file size cap in MB (max_file_mb, default 25, platform ceiling 100; files over 10 MB upload in parts automatically), how many files one submission may carry (max_files, ceiling 10), and how long files are kept before they are purged (retention_days, 30-365). Also returns the platform ceilings and the account's storage usage against its cap, so a 'why did the upload fail' question can be answered from one call: a rejected type, an oversized file, or an account at its stored or daily quota. Read this before promising a client that a form will accept a given file, and before tightening anything with marketing_form_upload_settings_update.

tools.name: marketing_form_upload_settings_update
tools.description: Change one website project's form-upload policy. Fields are merged: only the keys you pass change. enabled false turns uploads OFF for every form on the site (file inputs then submit as before but no file is stored, and the notification email carries none); allowed_ext narrows the accepted extensions (a subset of the platform list, e.g. ['pdf','docx','jpg','png']; anything else is refused at upload time as type_not_allowed); max_file_mb sets the per-file cap (1-100, default 25); max_files lowers the per-submission count (1-10); retention_days sets how long files are kept before the purge (30-365). The policy can only be NARROWED below the platform ceilings, never widened above them; a value outside its range is a 400 naming the field. WRITE. Confirm with the operator before disabling uploads or shortening retention: a shorter retention purges existing files on the next sweep and the purge is not reversible. Read the current policy first with marketing_form_upload_settings_get and echo the merged result back after the change.

tools.name: marketing_frequency_cap_get
tools.description: The 7-day rolling per-contact send cap. Recipients already emailed this many times in the last week are SILENTLY SKIPPED at dispatch (skipped_frequency_cap) — this is usually why a send under-delivers. 0 = unlimited.

tools.name: marketing_frequency_cap_set
tools.description: Set the 7-day rolling per-contact send cap (0 = unlimited). Useful as a blast-radius limiter while testing.

tools.name: marketing_funnel_appearance_get
tools.description: Read one review funnel's fully resolved look and feel, what each field falls back to, and whether anything is actually overridden. Returns appearance (logo_url, primary_color, background, background_color, background_image_url, surface_color, text_color, muted_text_color, corners, layout, font_heading, font_body, headline, subhead, show_attribution), inherited_from_brand (the brand-guide value behind primary_color, text_color, background_color, logo_url, font_heading, font_body, plus logo_url_source 'brand_guide' | 'account' | null), is_inherited, share_url, status, font_choices, contrast_ratio, rating_style and rating_styles. CALL THIS BEFORE marketing_funnel_appearance_update: that write REPLACES the whole appearance object rather than merging, so this response is the base you must edit and send back. appearance is the account brand guide (with accounts.logo_url as the logo backstop) merged UNDER the funnel's own overrides, so most fields are values nobody chose for this funnel; is_inherited true means surveys.settings.appearance does not exist at all and a reset would be a no-op. contrast_ratio is the WCAG ratio of the auto-picked black-or-white button label against primary_color ONLY, rounded to one decimal; it says nothing about text_color on background_color, and below 4.5 those buttons are unreadable. Nothing enforces it, so a funnel can already be live and failing. share_url is RELATIVE ('/s/' + share_token) and is a PUBLIC capability link: anyone holding it can submit to this funnel, and that page 404s unless status is 'active'. survey_get returns the same link absolute, so the two tools disagree on the string by design. rating_style is null when the funnel's first scoring step is not a star step (an nps, csat or scale step, or no scoring step at all), which is also exactly the case where the update tool silently ignores rating_style. Find funnel_id with survey_list, which returns review funnels as type 'review' alongside nps and csat surveys. 400 invalid_id for a non-UUID, 404 for an id outside the calling account or for a survey that is not type 'review'.

tools.name: marketing_funnel_appearance_update
tools.description: Restyles a LIVE PUBLIC PAGE: no draft, no preview, no publish step, so what this writes is what a visitor on /s/<share_token> sees next. It spends no money and queues no job. Returns { ok, appearance (sanitised, as stored), rating_style }, plus contrast_ratio on every path EXCEPT reset:true. THE TRAP: appearance is a WHOLE-OBJECT REPLACE, not a merge. Every key you OMIT silently reverts to the brand value or the product default instead of keeping what was stored, so read marketing_funnel_appearance_get first and send its appearance back edited. SILENT SUBSTITUTION: nothing invalid is rejected. A colour that is not #rgb or #rrggbb, a font outside font_choices and a url that is not http(s) all fall back with no error, and headline/subhead are trimmed to 200/400 chars; compare the returned appearance against what you sent. show_attribution:false strips 'Powered by Hiveku' from that public page; documented as a higher-plan unlock but NO plan gate exists here, so it works on any account. reset:true DELETES the override so the funnel follows the brand guide again including future edits; it ignores any appearance sent with it and does not reset rating_style, though a rating_style in the same body is still applied. rating_style is NOT part of appearance: it writes survey_questions.config.display and changes what the funnel ASKS. SILENT NO-OP: it applies only when the funnel's first scoring step is a 'star' step, so on an nps, csat or scale funnel it is accepted, ignored and answered ok:true with rating_style null. LOSSY: 'faces' and 'thumbs' force star_count to 5 and switching back to 'stars' does not restore a 10-star scale. An unrecognised value is a 422 naming the allowed set; a body naming none of reset, appearance or rating_style is a 422 nothing_to_update. surveys.settings is read-modify-written WHOLE, so a concurrent survey_update landing between this read and write is lost. Archived funnels are NOT excluded and can still be restyled. 400 invalid_id for a non-UUID; 404 outside the account or for a survey that is not type 'review'.

tools.name: marketing_generate_entity_image
tools.description: Generate an image AND file it onto a customer journey stage or a before/after grid item in one call. USE THIS instead of generate_image whenever the image belongs to a journey or a grid: plain generate_image hands back a URL and leaves you to hand-assemble the {id, url, prompt, createdAt} entry and PATCH the whole stages/grid_items blob back, which is both fiddly and the shape that loses the other images. This routes the image server-side, the way the marketing department agent has always done it. It also carries ACTOR ANCHORING on journeys: stage 2 onward reuses the person established in an earlier stage's image, so one recognisable customer walks through the whole journey instead of a different face per stage. JOURNEYS: pass journey_id + stage_id (get stage_id from customer_journey_get; an unknown one is refused BEFORE the image is generated and billed, so you are never charged for a misfile). Deliberately no stage_index: it is positional, so a concurrent reorder files the image onto the wrong stage. GRIDS: pass grid_id + image_type. before/after also need grid_item_index (0-based); story_before/story_after write the grid's own transformation-story slots and take no index. Billing is the account's image_generations allowance, returning 429 when exhausted - a different meter from video (a Premium plan gate plus a 20-clip month, returning 402).

tools.name: marketing_generate_video
tools.description: Generate a short AI video clip (720p, up to 10s; model 'auto' resolves worker-side, to the fal Kling lane when fal is configured and otherwise to Gemini Omni Flash) from a text prompt — for social posts, Reels/Shorts, and ad creative. Optionally image-to-video via reference_image_url or reference_media_asset_id (a Media Library image; pair with generate_image for a still → "animate this" flow). The clip is auto-registered in the Media Library (tags ai_generated + creative-studio) and the returned asset_id attaches straight to posts via media_asset_ids. COST + LIMITS — treat clips as expensive: each generation is PAID at roughly $0.10 per second (~$1 for a full 10s clip), Premium-plan only, capped at 20 clips/account/month, and platform capacity is limited (429 video_quota_exhausted = try again after the overnight reset). duration_seconds (clamped 2-10, rounded to whole seconds) is the direct cost lever — a 4s loop costs well under half a default-length clip; omit it for the model default. DURATION SNAPPING: duration_seconds is a HINT, several lanes snap it to the steps their provider bills in, and billing follows the RENDERED length. kling-2.5-turbo (the default 'auto' lane when fal is configured) renders ONLY 5s or 10s (hint > 7 -> 10s, else 5s; omitted -> 5s), so a 9s request IS a 10s bill; veo-3.1-fast / veo-3.1-lite (fal) render 4s/6s/8s (hint <= 5 -> 4s, <= 7 -> 6s, else 8s; omitted -> 8s); veo-3.1-google does not snap (the rounded hint capped at 10s is forwarded and the provider enforces its own 4-8s bounds, so a hint outside them can error upstream); omni-flash honors any 1-10s; kling-avatar-v2 follows the driving audio and ignores the hint. Which lane 'auto' resolves to is worker-side config and cannot be predicted here, so the response reports it (duration_requested / duration_effective / duration_note, see Response). ALWAYS call with dry_run:true FIRST to check {allowed, used, limit} before promising a video, prefer reusing existing assets (marketing_media_list), and NEVER retry a generation that succeeded. REFERENCES — reference_mode picks how a reference feeds the clip. Default 'animate': the image IS the scene (classic image-to-video). 'compose': the image model FIRST builds a scene still WITH the reference (logo on a shirt, product in a setting), then that still is animated — video models cannot composite a reference into a new scene themselves. compose requires a reference (400 without one), spends ONE image-generation credit BEFORE the video step (gated by the monthly image quota, 429 image_generation_limit_reached, and the AI budget, 402 ai_credits_exhausted), and a compose failure is FATAL (500 compose_failed) rather than a silent fallback to animating the raw reference. When compose succeeded but the video step then failed, the failure body carries composed_still_asset_id — that still is already paid for and in the library, so retry by animating IT (reference_media_asset_id + reference_mode 'animate'), never with a second compose. STATEFUL REVISION — the success response includes interaction_id when, and only when, the clip can be revised (the Omni lane). Feed it back as previous_interaction_id with a prompt that is the EDIT INSTRUCTION ("make it dusk, keep everything else"); the reference and the brand suffix are then skipped. ONLY pass an interaction_id this tool returned to THIS account: a fal| handle is refused 400, and every other handle is checked against this account's own design_render_jobs.provider_operation, the ONLY ownership proof: it is written from the worker's poll and the runner's completion claim, never from a request body, and the reconciler derives the asset's interaction_id FROM it, so every revisable clip has it. The clip asset's ai_metadata.interaction_id is deliberately NOT consulted (the media create doors copy caller ai_metadata verbatim, so an asset-side match would only prove the caller wrote the handle down). A handle that is unknown, belongs to another account, or names a clip older than the durable job row (before 2026-08-08, so no provider_operation) is refused 400 invalid_request, so a guessed or foreign id no longer submits a fresh, separately-billed generation dressed as a cheap edit. design_project_id links the paid render job to a Design Studio project (account-scoped — an id not in this account is a 404, and the clip then renders on no design page). Brand-aware by default (use_brand:false to opt out; skipped automatically on a stateful revision). aspect_ratio: 9:16 (default, Stories/Reels/TikTok) or 16:9 (YouTube/X/LinkedIn). Platform duration ceilings still apply at post time (X 140s, Reels 90s, Shorts 60s). Response: { asset_id, mp4_url, width, height, duration_seconds, duration_requested?, duration_effective?, duration_note?, render_job_id, interaction_id?, reference_used?, composed_still_asset_id? }. duration_seconds and duration_effective are the worker-MEASURED output length and are null (never 0) when the worker did not measure it: a 0 from the worker is its ffprobe failure sentinel, not a zero-length clip, so never re-generate off a null. When duration_seconds was sent, duration_requested echoes the clamped hint and duration_note explains the difference whenever the rendered length is not the one requested (the lane snapped it). composed_still_asset_id is returned on the FAILURE bodies too (402 monthly_cap_reached, 400 invalid_request) once a compose still was produced, so the retry can animate it. seed: null and an empty string mean absent (never coerced to seed 0); any other non-finite value, or a boolean, is 400 invalid_request "seed must be a finite number", never a silent drop, and it is validated before compose so a doomed request spends nothing. Errors: 400 invalid_request (compose without a reference, a non-public reference URL, a fabricated, unknown or foreign previous_interaction_id, a garbage seed, an unusable reference), 400 prompt is required, 402 plan_upgrade_required | monthly_cap_reached (with used/limit) | ai_credits_exhausted, 404 reference image / design project not found, 429 video_quota_exhausted | image_generation_limit_reached, 500 compose_failed | REMOTION_RENDER_URL unset | render failed, 501 video_generation_not_configured, 502 worker unavailable | asset_save_failed (with render_job_id), 503 brand_unavailable (use_brand on, the default, but the brand guide READ failed; refused BEFORE any paid work, never a silent unbranded clip: retry, or pass use_brand:false) | cap_check_unavailable (the monthly cap could not be read; retry, it is not a plan wall), 504 timeout WITH render_job_id — the clip may still finish and register; poll design_render_job_get with that id instead of regenerating. Generation takes ~30-90s — this call blocks until done.

tools.name: marketing_knowledge_bases_list
tools.description: List marketing-specific knowledge bases (separate from general kb_*).

tools.name: marketing_knowledge_bases_search
tools.description: Semantic search across marketing knowledge bases.

tools.name: marketing_mailing_address_get
tools.description: The account's physical postal address + `can_spam_complete`. CAN-SPAM requires a real mailing address in every marketing email; footer validation FAILS without one, so no campaign can send until this is set.

tools.name: marketing_mailing_address_set
tools.description: Set the account's physical postal address (CAN-SPAM). ALL of address, city, state, zip_code, country must be present or every send is refused at footer validation. Confirm the address with the owner — it appears in the footer of every marketing email they send.

tools.name: marketing_media_folders
tools.description: List folders in the marketing Media Library (media_assets folders) with asset and child-folder counts. Pass parent_id="root" for top-level folders. NOT related to website builder-project assets_* paths.

tools.name: marketing_media_get
tools.description: Get one marketing Media Library asset (media_assets) by ID, including its folder, collections, and recent usage tracking. This is the media library used by social posts and designs — NOT the website builder-project assets_* tools (use assets_info for project files).

tools.name: marketing_media_list
tools.description: List assets in the marketing Media Library (media_assets) — the account-level library that social posts and designs pull images/videos from. NOT the website builder-project assets_* tools (those are per-project files on S3); for website project files use assets_list/assets_upload. Filters: folder_id ("root" for top level), media_type, tags (comma-separated), search (title/filename), ai_generated, collection_id. Paginated.

tools.name: marketing_media_register_external_url
tools.description: Register an existing http(s) URL as a marketing Media Library asset (media_assets) without uploading bytes — for AI-generated S3 URLs, CDN/stock URLs, or bulk imports. This is the library social posts and designs use — NOT the website builder-project assets_* tools. media_type and mime_type are inferred from the URL extension when omitted; title falls back to the filename in the URL.

tools.name: marketing_media_upload_base64
