tools.description: Upload a file (base64 bytes, max 50MB) into the marketing Media Library (media_assets) — S3-backed, account-level, used by social posts and designs. NOT the website builder-project asset store; to ship an image into a website project use assets_upload instead. mime_type is inferred from the file extension when omitted; a data: URI prefix on content is stripped automatically.

tools.name: marketing_offline_conversion_actions_list
tools.description: List the EXISTING conversion actions on a connected ad account that the offline lane could be designated to. Hiveku never creates a conversion action; designation always points at one that already exists on the platform. What 'conversion action' means per platform: google_ads = a ConversionAction resource name the connection's ad account owns; microsoft_ads = the OfflineConversionGoal NAME (exact match); meta_ads = the CAPI event name (e.g. Lead, Purchase).

tools.name: marketing_offline_conversions_designate
tools.description: Map a conversion source to an EXISTING conversion action on a connected ad account, so discovered conversions from that source upload against it. Use marketing_offline_conversion_actions_list to see candidates; Hiveku never creates one. source: crm_deal_won | form_lead | shopify_order. value_mode: source_value (the deal/order amount) | fixed_value (operator-configured per-lead value, requires fixed_value). match_mode: click (stored gclid/gbraid/wbraid/msclkid/fbclid) | enhanced (hashed email/phone, Google enhanced-conversions-for-leads; REFUSED for meta_ads — that lane sends only the fbc click parameter, never PII). Click-age windows are enforced at enqueue (google/microsoft 90 days, meta 7 days) and conversions older than 63 days are refused rather than queued. A single conversion value above 1,000,000 in the mapping currency is REFUSED, never clamped (max_value can lower that ceiling per mapping). Pass enabled: true to arm the mapping; a designation with enabled false exists but does not run.

tools.name: marketing_offline_conversions_opt_in
tools.description: Enable (or disable) the offline-conversion lane for this account. Enabling from off ALWAYS lands in validate-only mode: uploads are proven against the platform and record nothing until a human goes live. THE GO-LIVE FLIP IS NOT AVAILABLE HERE. Passing validate_only: false returns 403 — an account owner/admin does that in the dashboard after reviewing a validate-only run. Calling this on an account a human already took LIVE preserves live mode (it will not silently un-arm it); the response note states the actual mode, read it back to the user verbatim. lookback_days (1-90, default 30) bounds how far back discovery looks for conversions.

tools.name: marketing_offline_conversions_preview
tools.description: Dry-run discovery: what WOULD be enqueued from a source over the lookback window, with a sample of up to 10 rows and per-reason skip counts. Writes nothing and sends nothing to any platform, ever — the dry-run flag is pinned server-side. Run this before marketing_offline_conversions_run and relay the skip reasons: a conversion refused for click age (windows: google/microsoft 90d, meta 7d) or the 63-day import horizon is not an error, it is the lane refusing an upload that could only fail.

tools.name: marketing_offline_conversions_queue
tools.description: Read the offline-conversion outbox (newest first). Filters: source (crm_deal_won | form_lead | shopify_order), status (queued | validated | uploaded | failed | skipped), limit 1-100 (default 25). Read-only. click_id and email/phone hashes come back MASKED — they are per-visitor tokens and platform match keys, not data for a model to copy around. 'validated' rows are proof the payload works in validate-only mode; they upload for real only after a human goes live and marketing_offline_conversions_requeue re-arms them. error_code/last_error on failed rows name the platform's reason.

tools.name: marketing_offline_conversions_remove_mapping
tools.description: Remove a source→conversion-action designation. Returns { removed, cancelled_rows }: queued outbox rows for that mapping are cancelled, not uploaded. Rows already uploaded to the platform are NOT retracted — nothing can un-send a recorded conversion.

tools.name: marketing_offline_conversions_requeue
tools.description: Re-arm rows that finished as 'validated' during validate-only runs so the next run uploads them for real. Only meaningful AFTER a human takes the account live in the dashboard; 409 with the reason otherwise. Returns { requeued }.

tools.name: marketing_offline_conversions_run
tools.description: Discover AND dispatch offline conversions: enqueue new rows from the source, then work the outbox (limit 1-500, default 500). Gated: 409 not_opted_in without opt-in, 409 source_not_designated without an enabled designation. MODE DECIDES WHAT THIS DOES. validate_only: true (the default state) proves every payload against the ad platform and records NOTHING — the response says so. On an account a human took LIVE, this records real conversions that reach the client's automated bidding and CANNOT be un-sent; treat it like any other money write: preview first, run once, read the dispatch tallies back. outcome: 'clean' | 'partial' — partial means some rows failed permanently or a connection errored; read the dispatch counts, do not retry in a loop.

tools.name: marketing_offline_conversions_status
tools.description: Offline-conversion lane status for this account: opt-in state, validate_only mode, designated conversion actions per connection/source, and outbox tallies by status (queued | validated | uploaded | failed | skipped). READ THIS FIRST before any other marketing_offline_conversions_* call. validate_only: true means uploads are proven against the ad platform but NOTHING is recorded; false means the account is LIVE and uploads influence the client's automated bidding for real. Takes no parameters.

tools.name: marketing_offline_conversions_validate_only
tools.description: Put a LIVE offline-conversion account back into validate-only mode. The SAFE direction only: validate_only must be true; anything else is a 403 (turning it off is the go-live step, a human dashboard action). 409 not_opted_in when the lane was never enabled. changed: false when the account was already in validate-only. NOTE: conversions already uploaded stay on the ad account and keep influencing automated bidding — this does not retract them.

tools.name: marketing_qr_style_get
tools.description: Read the account-wide QR appearance that every reputation surface draws with. Returns style (the stored values merged over the defaults, i.e. the thing to draw), defaults, stored (ONLY the fields this account has actually chosen, so a client can label a field 'inherited' instead of inferring it from equality), warnings, and account_logo_url (accounts.logo_url, so logo_mode 'account' can be previewed without a second call). warnings is the half an agent can act on and is reachable no other way: inverted_colors, low_contrast_margin (under 7:1), large_logo (a logo over 0.25 of the width), detached_modules. Reading is deliberately TOLERANT and never fails on a bad row: each invalid stored value falls back to its own default silently, so a value in style may be a fallback rather than what is on the row, and stored is the field that tells the two apart. A colour pair below the 3:1 write floor can therefore sit here quietly while it blocks every write (see marketing_qr_style_update). SETTINGS ONLY: there is no server-side QR renderer anywhere in the product, so no tool can render, download or eyeball a QR image; the code only exists once a human opens the funnel QR studio in a browser. Takes no arguments, costs nothing, two point reads.

tools.name: marketing_qr_style_update
tools.description: Merge a partial QR style into the account's reputation settings. Returns ok, style (the full merged result), defaults, stored, warnings and dropped; it does NOT return account_logo_url, unlike marketing_qr_style_get. SETS STYLE ONLY: there is no server-side QR renderer, so this cannot produce, preview or verify a QR image - a code is drawn only when a human opens the funnel QR studio in a browser. SILENT PARTIAL WRITE, the trap that bites: any key outside the eight below is DROPPED rather than rejected, and as long as one recognised key is present the call still returns 200 ok:true with the misspelling visible only in dropped, so always read dropped back. (A body whose keys are ALL unrecognised is a 400 no_changes instead, never a 200 that stored nothing.) logo_size is CLAMPED into 0.05 to 0.35 rather than rejected, so 0.9 returns 200 with 0.35 stored; read the echoed style. Every other field errors instead, and a blank-string logo_size is an error rather than zero. Cross-field validation runs on the MERGED RESULT, not on your patch, so a row already under the 3:1 contrast floor, or in logo_mode 'url' with no usable logo_url, rejects EVERY patch with 400 invalid_qr_style - including patches that never mention those fields - until one call carries the fix as well. Account-wide with no per-funnel override: one call restyles the whole fleet, and these values end up printed on counter cards and van doors where a print run cannot be patched. No money, no outbound call, no queued job. Known dead ends today: the studio hydrates the module colour from a 'dot_color' key this API never returns, so dots_color is stored and drawn by nothing, and logo_url is stored but the studio takes its logo from the funnel brand, leaving dot_style, corner_square_style, corner_dot_style, background_color, logo_size and logo_mode as the only fields that currently change what a human sees. Call marketing_qr_style_get first for the current values, what is inherited, and the warnings.

tools.name: marketing_report_create
tools.description: Create a scheduled CLIENT REPORT — the shareable, branded results page the client opens (marketing report: leads, deals won, traffic, spend, SEO, rankings movement, search-term wins, AEO, local, work log; social report: posts, impressions, engagement). Returns the row including its public_token: marketing reports are PUBLIC BY DEFAULT (the share link is the point) and next_scheduled_at is stamped so the scheduler cron actually delivers on cadence. delivery_config.recipients (email addresses) is who marketing_report_send emails. After creating, call marketing_report_regenerate to populate the numbers, then marketing_report_share_link for the URL. THE PAID-MEDIA CLIENT REPORT IS THIS TOOL, NOT A SEPARATE TYPE: report_type 'marketing' with include_sections ['overview','ppc','search_terms','calls','work_log'] renders a branded PPC-only page. The ppc section carries per-platform totals, top campaigns, a daily cost/conversions/CPA trend, and a month pacing block (spend to date, the monthly target summed from each active connection's budget target, a straight-line projection; the target is null when no connection carries one or the connections disagree on currency). A disapproved-ad count is not in the section yet: disapprovals are read live (ppc_disapprovals_list), never synced.

tools.name: marketing_report_pdf
tools.description: Download a client MARKETING report as a PDF, rendered server-side from the STORED last_report_data blob — the exact numbers the public share page and the report email show (marketing_report_regenerate is the only way they change). Returns { filename, content_type, size_bytes, generated_at, data_base64 } — decode data_base64 to get the PDF bytes. 409 when the report has never been generated: call marketing_report_regenerate first, then retry. Social reports are not supported (400) — share their public link instead. A plain browser GET on the same route (no format param) streams raw application/pdf with a download filename.

tools.name: marketing_report_regenerate
tools.description: Rebuild the report's numbers NOW and store them (last_report_data) — the public page and the emailed summary render this stored blob verbatim, so regenerate is the only way numbers change. Does NOT email anyone and does NOT advance the schedule (the cron owns cadence). Marketing reports accept days: 7 or 30 (window). Can take a while: the marketing assembly includes live Google Ads pulls (search terms, change history). Run this after create and before send/share.

tools.name: marketing_report_send
tools.description: Email the report to its recipients — REAL MAIL LANDS IN THE CLIENT'S INBOX, so this is confirm-gated. First call WITHOUT confirm: you get a preview (report title + the exact recipient list + the public URL that will be mailed) — show it to the user. Re-call with confirm: true (strict boolean) to actually send. Marketing reports email the CURRENT stored numbers (regenerate first if stale) and require an existing public link. Pass recipients to replace delivery_config.recipients before sending. Never advances the cron schedule.

tools.name: marketing_report_share_link
tools.description: Fetch the report's public share URL (/public/marketing-report/[token] or /public/social-report/[token]) — the link the client opens, no login required. Returns url: null with a fix-it note when the report is not public (use marketing_report_update with is_public: true to mint the link). Read-only; never mints.

tools.name: marketing_report_update
tools.description: Update a client report's config: rename, change cadence (schedule change re-stamps next_scheduled_at so the cron stays in sync), section list, recipients (delivery_config), active flag, or the share link. is_public: true mints a public_token when the row has none; is_public: false on a marketing report REVOKES the link outright (social keeps its token so re-enabling restores the same URL). To turn a cross-channel report into the paid-media deliverable, set include_sections to ['overview','ppc','search_terms','calls','work_log'] and regenerate; the ppc section includes month pacing.

tools.name: marketing_setup_status
tools.description: RUN THIS FIRST, before building anything. One call listing every condition that SILENTLY blocks a MARKETING CAMPAIGN send: marketing enabled, not paused, not suspended, SES tenant provisioned, a VERIFIED sending domain, and the CAN-SPAM mailing address. Returns ready_to_send + blockers[], with a `fix` on each FAILING check (passing checks carry no fix text). Skipping it is how agents build a perfect campaign and then discover it can never send. Scope: campaign and sequence dispatch through the account's SES tenant. It is NOT the transactional lane, which email_service_status reports as sending_enabled (hk_ API keys, smtp.hiveku.com, /api/v1/email/send). The two are provisioned independently, so ready_to_send: false here with sending_enabled: true there is normal and both are correct. The only shared gate is not_suspended, read from the same predicate in both, so a suspension shows up as false on both sides.

tools.name: marketing_storyboard_create
tools.description: Draft a storyboard for a multi-scene marketing video and park it awaiting the user's approval. Use this instead of one-off marketing_generate_video whenever the ask is "make me a video" (Reel/TikTok/promo/explainer/testimonial/listing tour), not just one clip. FREE AND FAST — it validates, prices, and stores; NOTHING is reserved, billed, or enqueued until a human approves. Pass EXACTLY ONE of: `storyboard` (a full hiveku.storyboard.v1 document you authored) OR `template_id` (a genre template the builder renders server-side: social-short, product-promo, explainer, testimonial, listing-tour, event-promo). With a template, fill `substitutions` ({slot: value}); optionally set style_id (clean-professional, bold-social, premium-minimal, warm-documentary), profile_id (tiktok, instagram_reels, youtube_shorts, youtube_landscape, linkedin_feed, linkedin_square, website_hero), voice_id (a Cartesia voice UUID), music (generate|stock|none), and model (auto|kling-2.5-turbo|veo-3.1-fast|veo-3.1-lite|omni-flash). A hand-authored `storyboard` may carry the look fields inline: board-level style_id, transition (none|fade|slide-left|slide-up), transition_ms, brand, captions.style, and per-scene camera. There is no `look` block on create — nothing to patch yet; to restyle a template-built board, create it and then call marketing_storyboard_set_look. On a validation failure the response carries validation.errors naming the exact bad field per scene — fix those with marketing_storyboard_update. THE AGENT CANNOT APPROVE: after creating, submit for approval and stop.

tools.name: marketing_storyboard_delete
tools.description: Delete a storyboard that never ran. IRREVERSIBLE. For cleaning up a board the user rejected or a duplicate created by mistake — in practice only two boards delete: one still in draft/awaiting_approval that was never approved, and a canceled/failed one that never reserved a clip. THIS IS NOT HOW YOU STOP A RUN — marketing_video_pipeline_cancel is. An approved or mid-run board returns 409 pipeline_running: cancel it first (that releases its reserved clips), then delete. A board that generated anything returns 409 pipeline_has_render_jobs — those render jobs carry the billing record and the platform keeps them on purpose, so that board is permanent. Neither refusal is something to work around; a 404 usually means it was already deleted.

tools.name: marketing_storyboard_get
tools.description: Read one storyboard/pipeline row: status, the document, per-scene generation state, and the final result when ready. Same row and snapshot as marketing_video_pipeline_status — the storyboard artifact and the run record are one row.

tools.name: marketing_storyboard_set_look
tools.description: Change a storyboard's LOOK by name — style, brand, captions, transition, music, per-scene camera — WITHOUT resending the document. PREFER THIS over marketing_storyboard_update for any appearance change: a full replace makes you restate every field you are not changing, and a field you forget is a field you silently delete. IT IS NOT A LIGHTER-WEIGHT WRITE. It bumps the storyboard version, recomputes the checksum, and CLEARS EVERY APPROVAL STAMP exactly like a full replace — a one-colour change re-drafts an approved board and the user must approve again. That is the gate working. Only a draft/awaiting_approval board is editable (else 409 pipeline_already_started). The agent still cannot approve. submit defaults true — the revision goes straight back to awaiting_approval so the user sees the re-priced card; pass submit=false only to park a draft you are not ready to show. Every `look` key is optional: absent = leave alone, a value = set, and null = DELETE that field ON THE KEYS THAT ACCEPT NULL. Null is NOT universal — three fields are required on the board and reject null with a 400: `captions.enabled`, `music.mode`, and `scenes[].on_screen_text` (clear on-screen text with the empty string "", which is its no-text value). Unknown keys are REJECTED (400 invalid_look), not ignored, so a misspelled knob is reported instead of silently doing nothing. - style_id: clean-professional | bold-social | premium-minimal | warm-documentary | null. Applied FIRST, so an explicit knob in the same call overrides the playbook for that field. - brand: {primary_color, accent_color, font_family, logo_url, inherit_account_brand} with #rrggbb colours, or null to remove the block. PRECEDENCE, PER FIELD: (1) inherit_account_brand=false means the account brand guide is not read at all, for any field; (2) a field set here always wins; (3) a field left unset is filled from the account brand guide at compile time. Set ONLY the field being overridden — restating the account's own colours freezes them and the board stops following the brand guide when it changes. - captions: {enabled (required on the board, no null form), style|null merged key-by-key}. Style keys: emphasis (bold|medium|light), placement (lower-third|centered|upper-third), highlight (fill|scale|underline|none), uppercase, font_family, font_weight 100-900, font_scale 0.02-0.12, position (top|center|bottom), fill/color, accent/highlight_fill, stroke (#rrggbb), stroke_width 0-20. Renderer keys (font_weight/position/fill) win over playbook keys (emphasis/placement). - transition: {kind: none|fade|slide-left|slide-up|null, transition_ms: 0-2000|null}. "none" forces 0ms. - music: {mode: generate|stock|none (required on the board, no null form), brief, stock_track_id, duck_under_vo_db -60..0}. - scenes: [{id, camera, transition_out, on_screen_text}], max 20, matched BY SCENE ID and never by index — an unknown id is a 400 listing the ids that DO exist. on_screen_text is a string up to 500 chars with NO null form: pass "" to clear it. camera = {zoom_from 1-3, zoom_to 1-3, pan_x_pct -50..50, pan_y_pct -50..50, origin: center|top|bottom|left|right|top-left|top-right|bottom-left|bottom-right}; setting it opts that scene OUT of the automatic move entirely (omitted axes become no-move, so a lone zoom_from is a hold at that scale), and camera=null restores the automatic move. A non-zero pan requires zoom headroom (max zoom > 1) or it is a 400. House-safe motion is a 0.08-0.20 zoom delta; keep |pan_pct| under (max_zoom - 1) x 50 or the frame slides past its own edge.

tools.name: marketing_storyboard_submit_for_approval
tools.description: Put the storyboard's approval card in front of the user — THE HAND-OFF, then STOP. It parks the board in awaiting_approval and surfaces the approval card (storyboard table, pre-viz, itemized cost). THE AGENT CANNOT APPROVE OR START THE RUN — only a signed-in human clicking Approve does. After this, tell the user what was built (scenes, runtime, estimated cost), ask them to review and approve, and end the turn. Do NOT then generate scenes one at a time to work around the gate.

tools.name: marketing_storyboard_update
tools.description: Replace a storyboard's document (PRE-APPROVAL ONLY) and re-validate. A FULL REPLACE — whatever the document omits is gone; use it when the SCENES change (add/remove/reorder a scene, rewrite a prompt, vo_line, or duration). For an appearance change (style, brand, captions, transition, music, a scene's camera or on-screen text) use marketing_storyboard_set_look instead, which edits by name so a field you did not restate cannot be silently dropped. ANY edit VOIDS a prior approval and re-prices — that is the checksum gate working; the user must approve again after a change. submit defaults true (send it back to awaiting_approval); pass submit=false to park a draft. A 409 pipeline_already_started means it is past approval and can no longer be edited (cancel and re-create, or retry a failed scene). The agent still cannot approve.

tools.name: marketing_template_archive
tools.description: Archive a marketing template (soft — campaigns keep their reference; never hard-deleted).

tools.name: marketing_template_create
tools.description: Create a template a CAMPAIGN can use (marketing_template). Author it EITHER way: 1. `layout_json` — the visual builder's block tree. Compiled to HTML/text server-side via MJML, so the template stays EDITABLE in the Hiveku visual builder afterwards. Prefer this. Shape: { version: 1, styles: {...}, blocks: [ { type, ...props } ] }. Block types: heading | text | image | button | divider | spacer | hero | social | columns | footer | quote | card | list | stats. 2. `compiled_html` (+ optional `compiled_text`) — paste-in raw HTML. Faster, but NOT editable in the visual builder. The body MUST carry an unsubscribe link and the account's physical address to pass CAN-SPAM footer validation at send time ({{unsubscribe_link}} is substituted per-recipient). Run marketing_setup_status first if unsure. ⚠️ Do NOT use email_template_create for campaigns — that writes the TRANSACTIONAL template store (/api/v1 send API) and a campaign cannot reference it.

tools.name: marketing_template_get
tools.description: Fetch one marketing template, including its layout_json block tree and compiled HTML/text.

tools.name: marketing_template_list
tools.description: List MARKETING templates — the ones a campaign's template_id can reference, and what the Templates tab shows. NOT the same store as email_template_list (that's transactional templates for the /api/v1 send API, which a campaign cannot use).

tools.name: marketing_template_update
tools.description: Update a marketing template. Passing layout_json recompiles the HTML/text from the block tree; passing compiled_html/compiled_text alone edits the raw body without touching the tree.

tools.name: marketing_testimonial_media_replace
tools.description: OUTWARD FACING AND IRREVERSIBLE. On success the new video is live on every public Hiveku surface (widgets, testimonial galleries, share pages) instantly: there is no staging step and no undo in this call. It promotes a COMPLETED Creative Studio MP4 render to be an APPROVED testimonial's published video by server-side copying the whole file (can be ~100 MB) to a new public immutable key and then repointing the row. Get render_job_id from design_export_mp4 (its jobId) and confirm the job reads status completed with design_render_job_get BEFORE calling: a job that is unfinished, is a still image, is not an .mp4, or belongs to another account is render_job_invalid (400). Returns { ok, public_video_url, quote_needs_re_review, cms, note }. quote_needs_re_review true means the published quote was lifted from an AI snippet of the OLD recording, so a trim may have cut the exact words the quote claims were said; the row is stamped body_source snippet_stale and a human must re-check it. That is an FTC 16 CFR Part 255 exposure, so report the flag to the operator and never swallow it. SILENT FAILURE on the site half: cms is null when the row has no CMS projection, and even cms.ok true can mean the site never got the new video - cms.reason unchanged, or videoUrl listed in cms.droppedFields, means the target collection does not declare the video field. A clean site write is still NOT live: the customer's site keeps serving the old video until a deploy runs. COSTS every call: the S3 copy, one more public object that nothing ever cleans up (the old keys are only parked in import_meta.replaced_media for a future sweep), and a fresh Deepgram transcription plus AI snippet, sentiment and topic regeneration. NOT IDEMPOTENT: a second call with the same render_job_id mints a second live key and a second transcription. Approved media testimonials only - text is not_media (400), pending or rejected is not_approved (409), withdrawn consent is revoked (409), and state_changed (409) means a takedown landed during the copy and nothing was replaced; none of those are retryable. Right after success the transcript, ai_snippets, ai_sentiment and ai_topics fields read empty, poster_url is null and processing_status is back to submitted - that is the deliberate reset, not a second bug to chase.

tools.name: marketing_testimonial_widget_archive
tools.description: Take one testimonial proof widget off the air. This is a SOFT ARCHIVE: it writes status 'archived' on the reputation_widgets row and destroys nothing - the row, its configuration and its public_token all survive, and marketing_testimonial_widget_update with status 'active' republishes at the SAME token. Never report it as a deletion or as unrecoverable; there is no hard delete for a widget on this API. Returns { ok: true, archived: true, widget } with the archived row. OUTWARD-FACING and immediate: the iframe /embed/testimonials/<token> and the hosted wall /t/<token> stop serving the moment this returns (a not-available notice and a 404 respectively), so anything embedded on a third-party page goes blank - confirm with the operator before archiving a widget that is live. The JSON feed /api/public/testimonials/wall/<token> is edge-cached (s-maxage=300, stale-while-revalidate=60) and can keep answering with content for up to about six minutes; calling this again does not speed that up, since it is idempotent and an already-archived widget still answers ok. FAILURES: 400 invalid_id on a non-UUID; 404 not_found means no such widget IN THIS ACCOUNT, covering both not-yours and does-not-exist, and never that it was already deleted. Costs nothing: one UPDATE, no money, no outbound call, no queued job.

tools.name: marketing_testimonial_widget_create
tools.description: Creates one embeddable testimonial gallery and returns { widget }: the new row including its freshly minted public_token (24 random bytes as hex, permanent, and the entire embed snippet). IT PUBLISHES NOTHING. status is always 'draft' and all three public readers require 'active', so the widget serves nothing anywhere until a separate PATCH to /api/olympus/marketing/reputation/widgets/[id] sets status 'active'. This call is step one of two; telling an operator their gallery is live after it is false. kind is 'wall' when omitted and must be one of wall, grid, carousel, single, badge, popup, collector, otherwise 400 invalid_kind with the allowed list. 'collector' is the leave-a-testimonial launcher rather than a gallery: it needs collector.survey_id pointing at a review funnel in this same account that is active and not archived or the frame shows a not-configured notice, and it renders as a collector only when the frame is opened with ?mode=collector, falling back to a wall on a direct open. name IS PUBLIC COPY, not an internal label: /t/<public_token> renders it as the heading of a deliberately indexable page, so a widget called 'test 3' publishes that heading to search engines. It becomes 'Testimonials' when omitted and is silently TRUNCATED at 120 characters rather than rejected. filters decides whether a live wall is full or nearly empty: filters.include is the source picker over testimonial, google, facebook, yelp, trustpilot, tripadvisor and an absent or empty include means ALL of them; with no filters.min_rating, synced reviews are floored at 4 stars while first-party testimonials have no floor; featured_only true, or a kinds list that omits 'text', excludes every synced review; filters.limit defaults to 30 and is clamped to 1-100; filters.order and filters.languages appear in the schema comment but no reader implements them. style keys that are actually read: accent_color (hex), card_radius (0-32), columns (1-4), show_rating, show_company, show_video, show_avatar, show_date. allowed_origins IS NOT ACCESS CONTROL: it is an anti-leech Referer check enforced only on the iframe page, an absent Referer fails OPEN, the JSON feed ignores it entirely, and an omitted or empty list means embeddable anywhere. filters, style and collector must be JSON objects; a string or an array is silently replaced with {} and still answers 200. No money, no outbound call, no queued job, but there is NO UNDO: the sibling DELETE only archives and public_token can never be rotated, so every call permanently adds a row and permanently burns a token. Do not loop on this to retry.

tools.name: marketing_testimonial_widget_update
tools.description: Reshape one testimonial proof widget (a reputation_widgets row) and, when status is sent, publish or unpublish it. Returns { ok: true, widget }: the FULL row AFTER the write, so the status just set is readable without a second call. OUTWARD-FACING: status 'active' starts serving testimonials and synced platform reviews immediately, with no further confirmation anywhere, on every page already carrying this widget's public_token - the iframe /embed/testimonials/<token>, the search-indexable hosted wall /t/<token>, and the JSON feed /api/public/testimonials/wall/<token>. 'draft' or 'archived' takes it down; the two pages flip at once, but the JSON feed is edge-cached (s-maxage=300, stale-while-revalidate=60) and can keep serving for up to about six minutes, so wait rather than re-flipping. WHOLESALE REPLACEMENT is the trap that empties live walls: filters, style, collector and allowed_origins each overwrite the stored object entirely and are never merged. Read the current row first (GET /api/olympus/marketing/reputation/widgets returns full rows) and send the complete object back - a partial filters silently drops the operator's include source picker, which decides whether the wall shows synced Google reviews as well as first-party testimonials, the difference between a full wall and an empty one on a customer's site. An EMPTY allowed_origins means ALLOW EVERYWHERE, not block everything; entries are trimmed and lowercased, and only the iframe page enforces them (a Referer check that fails OPEN on an absent Referer, so it is anti-leech, not access control), so a wrong hostname list turns an already-live embed into a refusal notice. kind and public_token are NOT settable and are ignored without error if sent: rotating the token would break embeds nobody can reach. FAILURES: an empty patch is 400 no_fields and writes nothing; a non-UUID id is 400 invalid_id; an unrecognised status, a name over 120 chars, more than 20 origins, or a non-object filters/style/collector is 422 invalid_body with issues - rejected, never truncated or silently dropped. 404 not_found means no such widget IN THIS ACCOUNT, never that one was deleted. Costs nothing: one UPDATE, no money, no outbound call, no queued job.

tools.name: marketing_testimonial_widgets_list
tools.description: Returns { widgets: [...] }: this account's embeddable testimonial widgets as full reputation_widgets rows (id, name, kind, status, public_token, filters, style, collector, allowed_origins, created_at), newest created_at first. HARD-CAPPED AT 100 with no cursor, no offset and no filter argument of any kind, so widget 101 is invisible here while still serving publicly on customer sites. Never report this list as the account's complete set. Only status 'active' widgets serve anything: 'draft' and 'archived' rows render a not-available page on /embed/testimonials/<public_token> and /t/<public_token> and answer 404 on the public JSON feed, so a row appearing here is not evidence that anything is live. public_token is returned in full and that is correct, because it is the public embed id the snippet carries rather than a credential, but it is also all anyone needs to read /api/public/testimonials/wall/<public_token>, which applies NO origin check at all, so share it exactly as freely as the embed code and no more freely. Read-only: no writes, no money, no queued job. To publish, rename or retarget a widget, PATCH /api/olympus/marketing/reputation/widgets/[id]; that route's DELETE only archives, it destroys nothing.

tools.name: marketing_testimonials_list
tools.description: The testimonial moderation queue for the account, newest first, keyset-paginated. Returns { testimonials, next_before }; each row carries id, kind (video|audio|text), status (pending|approved|rejected|spam|archived), collected_via, rating, headline, body, body_source, author { name, role, company, name_public }, transcript, ai_snippets, ai_sentiment, ai_topics, processing_status, processing_error, media { playable, url, poster_url, mime_type, duration_seconds, width, height, unavailable_reason }, is_public, featured, tags, created_at. This is the ONLY way to obtain a testimonial id: the id feeds the two testimonial tools that take one, over POST /api/olympus/marketing/reputation/testimonials/:id/edit-in-studio (opens a Creative Studio draft of an approved clip) and POST .../:id/replace-media (publishes a rendered clip back over it). NO MEDIA URL FOR ANYTHING UNAPPROVED, EVER. Unlike the moderation UI this tool does not return preview_url (a six-hour AWS presigned GET for the private, unapproved original recording) and never mints a signed poster either, because a presigned string is a bearer capability and a tool response lands in a transcript, a prompt cache and a log line. media.playable is only 'live' or 'none' here, never 'signed'; media.url and media.poster_url are non-null only for an approved, consented, published row. Otherwise unavailable_reason is 'text_only', 'media_deleted' or 'no_permission', and 'no_permission' is PERMANENT on this surface rather than a grant that could be widened, so do not retry, do not treat it as a transient error, and do not go looking for another media URL: there is none to find. Also deliberately absent: author.email (a PRIVATE column that is never projected off the server) and the consent record (consent_granted / consent_at / consent_revoked_at). is_public is the stored derivation of (approved AND consent granted AND not revoked), so is_public plus status fully answers 'may I publish this' without the legal evidence trail. author.name is the display-safe name: a customer who set name_public false reads as 'Sarah K.' here, and that shortened string is what may be published. transcript, body, rating and headline ARE returned for pending rows. That is unreviewed third-party speech about the tenant: summarise it, but do not republish any of it until status is 'approved'. PAGINATION TRAP: next_before is the last row's created_at whenever the page came back full, so an exact-fit final page hands back a cursor that fetches an empty page; stop on an empty testimonials array, not on next_before being null. The cursor is created_at-only with a strict less-than, so any row sharing the exact created_at of a page's last row is SKIPPED. Bad filters fail loudly rather than returning a misleading empty page: an unknown status or kind is a 400 (invalid_status / invalid_kind) listing the allowed values, a non-UUID survey_id is a 400 (invalid_survey_id) instead of a 500, and an unparseable before is a 400 (invalid_before) instead of silently serving page 1 forever. Costs nothing: one indexed Postgres read capped at 100 rows, no S3 request, no outbound call, no spend.

tools.name: marketing_video_pipeline_cancel
tools.description: Cancel a run. Unsubmitted clips release their monthly-cap slots; a clip already generating was already paid for and is left to finalize (its asset is kept — paid work is never discarded). A run that already finished/failed/was canceled returns 409 pipeline_already_terminal.

tools.name: marketing_video_pipeline_list
tools.description: List the account's storyboard boards (design_video_pipelines), newest first — the discovery read that finds an EXISTING board before you create another. Duplicate boards are the observed failure mode: an agent that lost the create response, or a fresh session, makes a second board for the same ask and the user sees two approval cards. Check here first; filter by design_project_id for the design the user has open, or status:'awaiting_approval' for boards already parked at the human gate. SUMMARIES ONLY: each row is { pipelineId, status, progress, progressMessage, designProjectId, storyboardVersion, sceneCount, approvedAt, pausedUntil, resultMediaAssetId, error, createdAt, updatedAt } plus top-level total/limit/offset. The storyboard DOCUMENT never ships on this list (no prompts, VO scripts or scene assets) — fetch one board with marketing_video_pipeline_status / marketing_storyboard_get for its content. sceneCount is computed server-side from the stored document. LISTING APPROVES NOTHING and advances nothing: no approval field is written, no render is polled — approval remains a human dashboard action with no Olympus twin, so a board listed as awaiting_approval is waiting for a person and listing it does not move it. Filters (all optional, ANDed onto the key's account): status (draft|awaiting_approval|approved|generating_assets|compositing|completed|failed|canceled), design_project_id (uuid — a design not in this account simply yields an empty list), limit (1..100, default 25 — values above 100 are clamped, ≤100 effective), offset (≥0). A typo'd filter is a named 400 invalid_request, never a plausible-looking empty list; non-integer or overflow-length limit/offset also 400.

tools.name: marketing_video_pipeline_retry_scene
tools.description: Re-generate EXACTLY ONE failed clip scene (0-based index from marketing_video_pipeline_status). Only a clip whose latest attempt FAILED can be retried; completed scenes keep their paid-for assets and are never regenerated — the route refuses a retry on a scene that already landed rather than double-billing it. A 402 monthly_cap_reached means the single retry clip will not fit the remaining allowance.

tools.name: marketing_video_pipeline_start
tools.description: Resume an ALREADY-APPROVED run that went idle. This does NOT approve or bypass the gate — approval already starts the run automatically; this is a manual re-kick for the rare stall (a per-minute reconcile cron is the automatic backstop). Against a board the user has not approved it returns 409 storyboard_not_approved, the correct answer — call marketing_storyboard_submit_for_approval and wait for the user.

tools.name: marketing_video_pipeline_status
tools.description: Snapshot an approved run: status, per-scene state (static/pending/reserved/generating/completed/failed), quota pauses (paused_until — the run resumes itself; not a failure), and the final media asset once compositing finishes. Returns immediately — check in, do NOT poll in a tight loop; a full board takes minutes and the platform drives it on its own.

tools.name: marketing_workspace_get
tools.description: Fetch the marketing workspace (active sub-departments, persona configs, dashboards).

tools.name: mc_decision_check
tools.description: Cheap polling endpoint for agents waiting on a HITL decision. Returns a tiny payload — just status, resolved (true if status=done OR decision_answer is set), the structured answer if any, who decided, and a `retry_after_seconds` hint derived from priority (P0=30s, P1=2m, P2=15m, P3=6h). Honor the hint so we don't get hammered. Prefer this over mc_task_get when all you need is 'did the human answer yet?'. Agent workflow: 1. Create card via mc_task_create with decision_options. 2. Loop: call mc_decision_check, if !resolved sleep retry_after_seconds. 3. On resolve: read answer.chosen_key (and answer.text when chosen_key='OTHER') and continue.

tools.name: mc_decision_to_memory
tools.description: Promote a resolved Mission Control card's decision into the account's durable memory. Closes the HITL loop — instead of the answer disappearing into card history, it lives in account_ai_memory where future agents working that account inherit the call. Card must be resolved (decision_answer set); returns 412 with code='not_resolved' otherwise. By default composes a memory entry from card.title + chosen option label + answer.text + decider + date. Supply `summary` to override. Returns the memory_entry_id so callers can link further. The card's meta.memory_links grows with each promotion; a `memory_promoted` event is emitted for the audit trail.

tools.name: mc_decisions_pending
tools.description: Convenience query for digest jobs: returns cards with status='awaiting_human', grouped by priority (P0/P1/P2/P3 buckets). Cheaper than mc_tasks_list + client-side filter; the grouped response shape is ready to feed straight into a digest template.

tools.name: mc_intake_classify
tools.description: Server-side LLM classifier for a Mission Control intake. Given title + body + source, returns suggested {account_slug, type, priority, assignee, estimate_min, reasoning} with a confidence score. Use this standalone to pre-classify a request before deciding whether to call mc_intake_external (or to enrich an existing card via mc_task_update). If you want intake to be atomic-with-classification, just call mc_intake_external with `auto_route_above` set instead of two calls. Model: Sonnet 4.6 via OpenRouter (more conservative about confidence than Haiku, which matters when account_confidence drives auto_route_above). Returns 503 with code='llm_unavailable' if OPENROUTER_API_KEY isn't configured.

tools.name: mc_intake_external
tools.description: Generic external intake — Slack, email, webhook, anything. Creates a card with a source chip and source_ref so the original context is traceable. OPTIONAL LLM AUTO-TRIAGE: pass `auto_route_above` (a confidence threshold 0-1) to call the classifier inline. If the LLM's account_confidence >= threshold, the new card lands in the Doing lane with the suggested priority + assignee applied. Below threshold (or if the classifier fails) it lands in Intake unchanged — the classification still gets stamped in meta so the human sees what the LLM thought during triage. Recommended threshold: 0.8 for auto-routing, 0.0 to always classify-but-keep-in-inbox.

tools.name: mc_lane_create
tools.description: Create a new Kanban column for the account. Name must be unique within the account; conflicts return 409 with code='duplicate_name'. display_order is auto-appended after the current max if omitted.

tools.name: mc_lane_delete
tools.description: Hard-delete a lane. Cards in the lane have their lane_id set to NULL (no card is lost — they appear as 'Uncategorized' on the board). Prefer mc_lane_update { archived: true } if you want the lane label to remain in event history.

tools.name: mc_lane_update
tools.description: Rename, recolor, reorder, or archive a lane. Pass { archived: true } to soft-hide a lane from the default board view (cards in it keep their lane_id; archived lanes appear in the lane editor for un-archiving).

tools.name: mc_lanes_list
tools.description: List the account's Mission Control Kanban columns (lanes), ordered by display_order. Each lane: { id, name, description, color, display_order, archived, counts: { open, in_progress, awaiting_human, awaiting_agent, done } }. First read seeds the default lanes (Intake, Decisions, Discoveries, Doing, Done) if the account has never used Mission Control before. The response also includes `uncategorized_counts` for cards with no lane_id.

tools.name: mc_schedule_create
tools.description: Create a recurring-card schedule. The cron worker ticks the table and fires matches; each fire spawns one card per matching account from the named template. Example: cron='0 9 1 * *', timezone='America/New_York', template_name='ppc.monthly_review', defaults={priority:'P2', assignee:'pi-ppc'} — on the 1st of every month at 9am ET, spawn a P2 'Monthly PPC review' card assigned to pi-ppc using the ppc.monthly_review template. target_account_filter supports: { account_ids: [...] }, { tag: 'cb-google-ads' } (saas-admin only), { all: true }. Per-account olympus path scopes to the schedule's own account.

tools.name: mc_schedule_delete
tools.description: Delete a schedule. Spawned cards are unaffected.

tools.name: mc_schedule_fire
tools.description: Manually fire a schedule now — spawn cards for the matching accounts using its template. The cron worker auto-calls this when the cron matches; use it for backfills, replays, or to verify a new schedule's plan before letting the cron drive it. Dry-run mode previews the plan without spawning. Pass accounts_override to fire against an explicit list of account ids (bypasses target_account_filter — useful when you want to backfill just one account).

tools.name: mc_schedule_get
tools.description: Fetch one schedule by id with its current state (last_fired_at, last_fire_summary).

tools.name: mc_schedule_update
tools.description: Update a schedule. Pass only the fields to change. enabled=false pauses; flipping it back resumes.

tools.name: mc_schedules_list
tools.description: List recurring-card schedules for the account. Each schedule pairs a cron expression with a template_name; the cron worker fires them on cadence and spawns cards for each matching account using mc_template render.

tools.name: mc_sla_breached
tools.description: Cards past their priority-derived SLA. Default SLAs (overridable per call): P0 = 1h (urgent revenue/SLA blocker) P1 = 4h (blocking a cadence) P2 = 24h (can wait a day) P3 = 168h (FYI / weekly) Excludes resolved/archived cards and those snoozed via auto_confirm_until in the future. Response carries age_hours, sla_hours, and over_by_hours per card so digests can render 'P0 alert created 6h ago — 5h over SLA.' Override per call with sla_P0_hours / sla_P1_hours / sla_P2_hours / sla_P3_hours if a tenant runs a different escalation rhythm.

tools.name: mc_task_comment
tools.description: Append a comment to a Mission Control card. Comments are append-only; the conversation between agents and the human stays linear and auditable. Author is free-form (agent slug or user id). THREADING: pass `parent_comment_id` to reply in-thread to a specific prior comment (fetch comments via mc_task_get to find the id). The server validates the parent belongs to this task and refuses 400 with code='parent_not_on_task' otherwise. Omit the field to leave a new top-level comment. The UI indents replies under their parent so an agent's nested back-and-forth with the user reads as a thread instead of an interleaved log.

tools.name: mc_task_comments_list
tools.description: List the comment thread on one Mission Control card, oldest first. Returns every comment with its free-form author, which may be an agent slug or a user id, so do not assume a human wrote any given line. Pair with mc_task_comment to append. The card id must be a UUID or the route 400s before touching the database. A card belonging to another account is a 404, not an empty list, so an empty array genuinely means the card exists on this account and nobody has commented.

tools.name: mc_task_create
tools.description: Create a Mission Control card. Common patterns: • Decision needed: status='awaiting_human', priority='P1', body uses a decision template (what was I doing / where I'm stuck / what I need / options / my recommendation / next steps). • Discovery (FYI, non-blocking): status='open', priority='P3', body describes what was found. • Hand-off to another agent: assignee=<agent slug>, status='awaiting_agent'. lane_id is optional — if omitted, the card lands as uncategorized; the UI surfaces these so the human can route them. Use mc_lanes_list to see the account's columns first if you want to drop into a specific one. Body is free-form markdown; Hiveku doesn't enforce a template, but agents should be consistent within their org so the human always finds the right info in the right place. DECISION OPTIONS: pass `decision_options: [{key, label, description?}]` to give the human structured radio choices. The UI auto-appends an OTHER row so the human can always type a custom answer. When the human submits, the answer is stamped on the card as { chosen_key, text? } — readable via mc_task_get or the cheaper mc_decision_check. The 'OTHER' key is reserved (don't send it as your own option key). Best practice: ≤6 options, short labels, longer description for the trade-off.

tools.name: mc_task_decide
tools.description: Submit a structured decision answer on a Mission Control card. Use this when the agent is the courier for a human's choice — Slack reply parsed into an option, Telegram quick-action, in-chat 'I pick A' reply, an auto_confirm policy firing. Validates chosen_key against the card's decision_options (or accepts 'OTHER' + text). By default transitions to status='done' and stamps decided_by_user_id with the human you're acting as. ACCOUNTABILITY: • Pass acting_as_user_id (a public_users.id from the task's account, NOT a Clerk id) to attribute the decision to a real human. That value becomes decided_by_user_id — identical to a human answering via the Mission Control UI. • Omit acting_as_user_id only for non-human auto-confirms (auto_confirm_until policy firing, scheduled escalation). The card resolves with decided_by_user_id=null; the event log captures the agent slug and notes "agent_relay: true" so audits can see the agent acted unilaterally. CLAIM CONTENTION: if the card is claimed by a user other than acting_as_user_id, returns 409 with code='claim_held_by_other' unless force=true. Forced takeovers are audit-logged in meta. MULTI-STEP DECISIONS: set also_resolve=false to record the answer without flipping to done — useful when the choice unblocks the agent but the larger workflow isn't finished. Auto-posts a comment '✅ Decision: <label>' on the card unless you supply your own via the `comment` field.

tools.name: mc_task_get
tools.description: Fetch one Mission Control card by id with full body, comments timeline, recent events, and the lane it sits in. Use this before mc_task_transition, mc_task_update, or mc_task_comment so you know the current state. COMMENTS shape — each entry: { id, author, body, parent_comment_id, created_at }. parent_comment_id=null is a top-level comment; non-null points to the parent comment in the same task and forms a reply thread. To reply in-thread, pass that id back to mc_task_comment as parent_comment_id. The events array carries claim / decision / status_changed / linked / spawned_pm_task / memory_promoted rows for the audit timeline. Decision audit fields (claim_by, decided_by) are included when set so an agent can see 'human X is on it' or 'human X resolved with answer Y' before acting.

tools.name: mc_task_link_pm
tools.description: Link a Mission Control card to an existing pm_task. The MC card represents the decision/intake; the pm_task is the actual work on the project board. After linking, mc_task_get shows related_account_task_id and pm_task_get_mc_link shows the reverse. Idempotent on the same link — if the card is already linked to that pm_task, returns 200 with was_already_linked: true. If linked to a DIFFERENT pm_task, returns 409 unless { force: true }. force replaces the link and emits both an unlinked and linked event.

tools.name: mc_task_mirror_from_pm
tools.description: Sync the MC card's status from its linked pm_task. Mapping: pm.queued → mc.open pm.in_progress → mc.in_progress pm.qa | pm.ready_for_review | pm.blocked → mc.awaiting_human pm.done → mc.done pm.cancelled → mc.archived Idempotent — if the MC status already matches the derived target, returns no_change: true with no event emitted. Returns 412 if the MC card has no linked pm_task. Use after any pm_task status change to keep the kanban view consistent without per-pm-task-change webhooks.

tools.name: mc_task_spawn_pm
tools.description: One-shot: create a NEW pm_task from a Mission Control card and link them. Use this when you need the MC decision-context PLUS a trackable work item on the project board. Defaults: title and description carry over from the MC card; priority maps P0→urgent, P1→high, P2→medium, P3→low; task_type defaults to 'marketing'; status starts at 'queued'. Override any field via the body. The new pm_task carries an ai_metadata.spawned_from { kind: 'mission_control', mc_task_id } back-reference so a later agent picking up the pm_task can pull the decision context via pm_task_get_mc_link. Refuses with 409 if the MC card is already linked to a pm_task; pass { force: true } to replace.

tools.name: mc_task_transition
tools.description: Ergonomic status push — single call to move a card forward with optional comment. Equivalent to mc_task_update with just { status, comment } but cheaper and clearer. Use this when an agent is reporting 'I picked it up' (open → in_progress), 'I need human input' (in_progress → awaiting_human), or 'I'm done' (* → done). Setting status='done' also stamps resolved_at automatically. IMPORTANT: if the card has decision_options (a structured-choice request) and the human's answer is what's closing it, use mc_task_decide instead — that captures the chosen key + free-form text into decision_answer and stamps decided_by_user_id correctly. Using mc_task_transition(done) on a decision card silently discards the structured-answer slot and leaves polling agents (mc_decision_check) seeing answer: null.

tools.name: mc_task_unlink_pm
tools.description: Clear the pm_task link from a Mission Control card. Idempotent — if the card isn't linked, returns 200 with was_linked: false. The pm_task itself is untouched.

tools.name: mc_task_update
tools.description: Patch a Mission Control card. Send only the fields you want to change — anything omitted is untouched. Changes to status, priority, lane_id, and assignee emit audit events so the digest jobs and UI can render a clean 'what moved today' trail. When to prefer something else: • Simple status push → mc_task_transition (lighter contract, optional comment in one call) • Closing a card with a structured human answer → mc_task_decide (captures decision_answer + decided_by_user_id; this PATCH cannot write either field) • Linking to a PM task → mc_task_link_pm (validates the pm_task exists in the same account) • Claim ownership → /workspaces claim flow (human-only; agents can read claimed_by_user_id but not write it) related_account_task_id IS settable here for back-compat, but mc_task_link_pm gives you validation + audit-event semantics.

tools.name: mc_tasks_aged
tools.description: Find Mission Control cards that have been in a status for too long — the canonical 'what got forgotten' signal. Default behavior: status='awaiting_human' older than 24h. Aging is measured against updated_at so a card that recently got a comment or status nudge doesn't keep flagging. Perfect for the morning digest's 'stalled decisions' section.

tools.name: mc_tasks_list
tools.description: List Mission Control cards for the account. Filterable by status, priority, assignee, lane_id; supports free-text search across title + body. Cards are the universal HITL surface — agents drop decisions / discoveries / hand-offs here so a human sees them in one spot. Status vocabulary is fixed (open | in_progress | awaiting_human | awaiting_agent | done | archived); lanes are the per-account customizable Kanban columns. Use mc_tasks_next instead if you're an autonomous agent polling for work — that endpoint pre-filters to ready-to-work statuses and orders by priority.

tools.name: mc_tasks_next
tools.description: Polling endpoint for autonomous agents — 'what should I work on next?'. Returns up to `limit` cards in priority order that are ready to work (status in open / awaiting_agent / in_progress). Filter by assignee (recommended; otherwise you'll see everything in the account, which is rarely useful). Optional lane filter by name or UUID. Designed for cron-driven pollers running every N minutes — cheap, indexed, no side effects.

tools.name: mc_tasks_stalled
tools.description: Cards with NO activity (events: status changes, comments, claim ops) in N hours. Stricter than mc_tasks_aged — that one measures task.updated_at which gets bumped by any mutation. This one inspects the event log, so a card whose only update was an agent claim counts as stalled if no human has acted since. Returns hours_since_last_event so digests can sort by 'most stale first'. Pair with a status filter for finer queries ('all in_progress cards with no events in 72h').

tools.name: mc_template_create
tools.description: Create a tenant template. Name is lowercase a-z 0-9 with . _ - separators (e.g. 'wct_intake', 'ppc.monthly_review'). Body is markdown with {{var}} markers — variables can be nested ({{account.name}}, {{today}}). If `variables` isn't passed, it's auto-extracted from the {{...}} markers in body. Cannot create platform built-ins from olympus — those are saas-admin-only.

tools.name: mc_template_delete
tools.description: Delete a tenant template. Platform built-ins are untouched. After deletion, mc_templates_get for that name falls back to the built-in if one exists.

tools.name: mc_template_update
tools.description: Update a tenant template. Cannot mutate platform built-ins — use mc_template_create to shadow them with a tenant copy first.

tools.name: mc_templates_get
tools.description: Fetch one template by name. Returns the tenant override if one exists, otherwise the platform built-in.

tools.name: mc_templates_list
tools.description: List Mission Control templates visible to the account. Templates are reusable markdown bodies with {{var}} markers — define a 'wct_intake' or 'decision_required' template once and every card created from it stays consistent. Returns both account-owned templates and platform-wide built-ins; when both define the same name, the tenant version wins (is_tenant_override: true).

tools.name: mc_templates_render
tools.description: Server-side render a template's body with the provided variables. Resolves tenant override > built-in. Lenient by default — missing variables stay as literal {{markers}} in the output and are reported in the `missing` array. Pass strict=true to error on missing. Typical agent flow: render the template, pipe the rendered markdown straight into mc_task_create's body. Saves having to do string formatting in the agent's language.

tools.name: md
tools.description: 🕷️ CRAWL4AI: Generate markdown from web content (Firecrawl-backed)

tools.name: media_ai_enhance_prompt
tools.description: Turns a rough social post idea into one image-generation prompt. Returns { success, enhancedPrompt, originalContext }: enhancedPrompt is 1-2 sentences of plain prose meant to be passed straight to generate_image or generate_image_set, originalContext echoes the first 100 characters of the trimmed postContent so a caller enhancing many posts can match responses to requests. It WRITES NOTHING of its own - no media_assets row, no social post, no CRM change - so whatever you generate from the prompt still has to be registered separately. COSTS MONEY ON EVERY CALL: it runs a full tool-enabled social department agent turn (hydrated with the account's memory, rules and brand voice, minted into turn history and metered against the account's AI spend), so budget a few cents and several seconds to tens of seconds of latency; it returns 504 if the turn passes 120s and 500 'No prompt generated' if the agent streams back an empty string. Brand context is hydrated server side, so account_context_get is not a prerequisite here. SILENT FAILURE: the anti-repetition block (image prompts read from the 30 newest ai_generated social_posts, at most 15 shown to the model) sits in its own try/catch that only logs a warning, so a 200 does NOT prove fatigue avoidance ran and you can get back a near copy of last week's image prompt. Only the first 500 characters of postContent steer the prompt. tone is matched against a fixed table (professional, friendly, witty, inspirational, educational, conversational, bold, empathetic, humorous, authoritative); any other value is accepted with no error and simply drops the tone guidance block, though the raw string is still shown to the model.

tools.name: media_bulk_move
tools.description: Reassign the folder of 1 to 200 media library assets in one filtered updateMany. Returns { result: { success, updatedCount, movedAssets, targetFolderId }, skipped_asset_ids }: movedAssets and updatedCount cover ONLY the ids that belong to this account, and every id you sent that does not is returned in skipped_asset_ids, so a 200 carrying a short updatedCount is a PARTIAL move and skipped_asset_ids is the only field that names what was dropped - always read it. targetFolderId separates a missing key from an explicit null: OMITTING the key is a 400, an explicit null moves the assets to the library root, and a uuid must name a folder in this account or the call 404s having moved nothing. Nothing is written unless the whole input validates: a non-uuid entry, an empty array, or more than 200 ids is a 422, and if none of the ids exist in this account it is a 404. Get a real destination id from media_folders_list first. Cheap and reversible: no money, no queued job, no file is touched, and moving them back undoes it. This is pinned to the move operation and cannot delete; removing an asset is media_delete, one at a time. For a single asset media_update with folder_id is fewer moving parts, but that route does NOT verify the destination folder is yours.

tools.name: media_collection_add_item
tools.description: Add an asset to a collection. Idempotent — duplicate add returns the existing row.

tools.name: media_collection_create
tools.description: Create a collection. cover_asset_id is the thumbnail shown in the UI.

tools.name: media_collection_delete
tools.description: Delete a collection. Cascade-removes membership rows (does NOT delete the underlying assets).

tools.name: media_collection_get
tools.description: Fetch one collection by id with every asset it contains (in sort_order).

tools.name: media_collection_items_list
tools.description: List just the membership rows of one media collection, ordered by sort_order asc. Returns { data: [{ id, sort_order, added_at, asset }], total }. media_collection_get returns the same items plus the collection row and its cover asset, so use that when you also want the collection metadata and this when you only want the contents. The row-level `id` is the MEMBERSHIP row id, NOT the asset id: pass asset.id to media_collection_remove_item or media_library_get, because an item id matches no asset and comes back 'Asset not in collection' 404. The embedded asset is a PARTIAL projection (id, filename, original_filename, file_url, file_size, mime_type, media_type, width, height, title, alt_text, tags, created_at); description, caption, duration, folder_id, source_type, ai_generated and usage_count are absent, so call media_library_get for full metadata rather than concluding those fields are empty. Traps: this route reads no query params at all, so there is no pagination and a large collection returns every row in one payload; and media_collection_add_item writes sort_order 0 by default, so a collection that was never explicitly ordered comes back in arbitrary order despite the orderBy. An unknown collection id, or one owned by another account, returns 404 'Collection not found', which is a different signal from an empty collection: empty is 200 with data: [] and total: 0.

tools.name: media_collection_remove_item
tools.description: Remove an asset from a collection. Doesn't delete the asset itself.

tools.name: media_collection_update
tools.description: Rename a collection / change its cover / toggle is_public. Use add/remove tools for asset membership.

tools.name: media_collections_list
tools.description: List curated media collections (album-style groupings of assets, distinct from folders). Each collection has a cover_asset_id + sort_order. Multiple collections can include the same asset.

tools.name: media_create
tools.description: Register an already-hosted file as a media_assets row. Pure INSERT: uploads no bytes, never touches S3, never fetches file_url. Returns 201 { data: <new asset row> } with file_size coerced from BigInt to a number. Prefer media_library_register_external_url for ordinary imports (only file_url required, media_type inferred); use this to set every column yourself. filename, file_url and media_type are required together, else 400 'filename, file_url, and media_type are required'. Traps: a dead, private or expired file_url persists as a healthy-looking row that renders a broken thumbnail wherever it is later attached; folder_id is NOT checked against the account here (the multipart upload route does check it), so a bogus or foreign folder UUID trips an FK violation the catch swallows into a bare 500 'Failed to create media asset' naming no field; the same opaque 500 is all you get for an out-of-enum media_type or source_type, or a non-integer file_size (BigInt() throws). ai_generated and is_public go through Boolean(), so any non-empty string, including the string 'false', stores as true. file_size 0 is falsy and stores as NULL. No unique index and no dedupe on file_url: calling twice creates two rows. This route also skips the updateMediaStorageUsed call the upload routes make, so the storage meter does not move.

tools.name: media_delete
tools.description: Delete an asset (hard-delete + S3 purge). Refuses with 409 in_use if the asset has any media_usage_tracking rows (i.e. it's referenced by an email, page section, CMS entry, etc.) — pass force=true to delete anyway and accept the orphan. Call media_usage_get first to see exactly what would break.

tools.name: media_folder_create
tools.description: Create a media folder. Optional parent_id makes it a sub-folder. Slug + name unique per (account, parent). description / color / icon are UI hints only.

tools.name: media_folder_delete
tools.description: Delete an empty folder. Refuses with 409 if the folder contains assets or subfolders — move them first via media_update (folder_id) and media_folder_update (parent_id).

tools.name: media_folder_get
tools.description: Fetch one media folder with parent_folder {id, name, folder_path}, child_folders [{id, name, slug, color, icon}] in sort_order, and the derived asset_count + child_folder_count. It returns NO assets: those are counts only, so list the contents with media_library_list(folder_id). Both counts are DIRECT children only, so asset_count 0 does not mean the subtree is empty and is not a safe green light for deletion: DELETE on this same route does NOT refuse a non-empty folder the way the media_folder_delete description claims. It updateMany-unparents every child folder (parent_id null) and every asset (folder_id null) to root, then deletes, so the assets survive but the organisation is gone with no undo and no 409. Unknown id and another account's folder are indistinguishable here: both return 404 'Folder not found'. Note also that a rename through media_folder_update recomputes slug and folder_path on this folder alone, so descendants can report a stale folder_path until they are reparented.

tools.name: media_folder_update
tools.description: Rename / reparent / restyle a folder. Allow-listed fields: name, slug, parent_id, description, color, icon.

tools.name: media_folders_list
tools.description: List media folders with hierarchy + asset count per folder.

tools.name: media_image_quota
tools.description: The pre-flight read the media skill cites BEFORE a batch generation (generate_image_set) and before media_upscale: how many AI image generations this account has left in the current period. It reads the SAME account_credits counter the generation path's atomic reserve debits, so it is exactly what the next generate_image / generate_image_set / media_upscale call is gated on (one counter, two refusals: the generate tools answer 429 budget_exceeded at the cap, media_upscale answers 402 quota_exceeded). generate_image_set debits one slot per SUCCESSFUL generation (failures refund), so `remaining` is the number of images the next batch can still produce. Takes no arguments; the account is the key's account. Costs nothing: one indexed read. ALWAYS 200 with failures-as-fields (same style as design_video_capabilities_get): read the fields, never the status. Shape: { used, limit, unlimited, remaining, stored_used, stored_remaining, period: { interval: 'monthly', resets_at, lapsed } | null, reason?, message?, note? }. limit 0 means UNLIMITED (unlimited: true) and remaining is then null, never a fabricated 0. reason: 'read_failed' (with message) means the DB read threw and EVERY numeric field is null: a failed read is never serialized as 0 or as 'nothing left', so a null remaining means UNKNOWN, not empty; retry. A no-credits-row account reports used 0 at the default limit of 10 with a note (the posture the first generation will meet). A LAPSED period (resets_at in the past, stored counter not rolled yet) reports the post-reset posture the next generation will actually meet (used 0, remaining = limit) with period.lapsed true and a note, while stored_used / stored_remaining always carry the raw stored counter, which lapse-blind surfaces (generate-video's compose step, the usage meter) still gate on.

tools.name: media_import_url
tools.description: Copy an EXTERNAL image into the account's own Media Library. The bytes are downloaded, verified as a real image, uploaded to the account's S3 media path and registered as a NEW media_assets row (source_type 'import', the origin URL kept on external_url), so the asset OUTLIVES the origin. That is the difference from media_library_register_external_url, which only stores a POINTER at somebody else's URL and renders a broken thumbnail the day that origin dies. Use it for a client-supplied image, a stock download, or an asset generated elsewhere that has to survive. NOT a generation: no image-generation quota slot is reserved or spent and no model runs. It costs one fetch, one S3 object and one row, and counts against media_storage_limit_mb. The fetch is SSRF-guarded (private, loopback and unresolvable hosts are refused as invalid_url), streamed under a 25MB cap (Content-Length is not trusted), and IMAGE-ONLY: a non-image Content-Type or bytes that do not decode are refused, and SVG is refused as unsupported_format because this bucket is served inline. folder_id must name a folder in this account. Returns 201 { data: { id, file_url, s3_key, filename, title, width, height, bytes, mime_type, source_type, origin_url, created_at } }. Nothing dedupes on origin_url: importing the same URL twice makes two rows. Failure codes (every failure carries `code`): 400 invalid_request (body not an object, title not a string, tags not an array), 400 invalid_url (empty, unparseable, non-http(s) or SSRF-blocked), 400 not_an_image, 400 unsupported_format (SVG), 403 storage_limit_reached (details.used_mb / limit_mb), 404 not_found (folder_id is not a UUID or not in this account), 413 too_large (over 25MB), 500 register_failed (the bytes ARE on S3 but the row insert failed: check media_library_list before re-importing), 502 fetch_failed (network error or non-2xx from the origin), 502 storage_error (fetched but the S3 upload failed), 503 database_error (the folder lookup could not be READ: retry shortly, it does not mean the folder is gone).

tools.name: media_library_get
tools.description: Fetch one media asset by UUID. Returns full metadata + folder + collections + usage_count.

tools.name: media_library_list
tools.description: List media library assets in the account. Filters: media_type (image|video|audio|document|archive|other), tags (comma-separated), folder_id, collection_id, source_type (upload|pexels|ai_generated|import|url), ai_generated, search (free-text against title/filename/alt). Account-scoped; account-wide library shared across all projects.

tools.name: media_library_register_external_url
tools.description: Register a pre-hosted URL (S3, CDN, third-party) as a media_assets row WITHOUT uploading bytes. Useful for: (1) backfilling older generate_image outputs that weren't auto-registered, (2) importing a list of pre-existing image URLs in bulk (cheap INSERT — no round-trip), (3) tracking external CDN assets so they show up in media_library_list / are taggable / searchable. Body: file_url (required), title, source_type (ai_generated|upload|pexels|import|url — default 'url'), media_type (auto-inferred from extension), mime_type (auto-inferred), tags[], description, alt_text, caption, ai_generated, ai_metadata, external_id, width/height/duration if known. Returns the new asset row.

tools.name: media_library_register_external_url_batch
tools.description: Batch variant of media_library_register_external_url — register N pre-hosted URLs as media_assets rows in a single call. Up to 100 per batch; chunk client-side for larger imports. Per-row error handling: one bad URL doesn't fail the whole batch — successful rows come back in `asset_ids[]` and failures in `errors[{index, file_url, error}]`. Same field contract per asset as the solo endpoint: file_url required; title / source_type / media_type / mime_type / tags[] / ai_metadata{} / alt_text / caption / description / ai_generated / external_id / folder_id / width / height / duration / is_public all optional with the same defaults.

tools.name: media_stock_video_search
tools.description: The only stock FOOTAGE search on this surface: free video from Pexels and Pixabay, the picker behind a `stock` storyboard scene. Returns { success, results, providerErrors, licenses: { pexels, pixabay } }. Each result carries id (the provider-prefixed handle, e.g. "pexels:13736675", which is what a storyboard scene stores in stock_video_id), provider, providerVideoId, previewUrl, downloadUrl (the mp4 the render worker fetches), width, height, durationS, attribution, author, pageUrl, license, and sizeBytes when the provider reports it. READ providerErrors ON EVERY CALL. A provider whose API key is unset or whose call failed is listed there, contributes zero rows, and the response is still 200 with success:true, so half a catalogue looks like the whole catalogue. An unrecognised provider value is IGNORED rather than rejected: the search silently widens to both providers, so check the provider field on the rows you actually got. width and height are the storyboard FRAME the footage will fill, not a post-filter, but they do shape the search: they set the orientation hint sent to Pexels and a minimum-dimension floor for Pixabay, they order results by aspect fit, and they pick the mp4 rendition closest to that frame instead of the largest file. The route defaults them to 1080x1920 and caps each at 4096. min_duration and max_duration are SECONDS and are silently dropped unless they parse as positive numbers; min_duration also cannot exclude a clip whose provider reports a duration of 0. per_page defaults to 15, is capped at 50 and floored at 3. A missing or blank query is a 400. Costs nothing: no render job, no monthly clip-cap slot, no database write, and nothing lands in the media library (results are catalogue handles only). It does make one outbound call per provider. For STILLS use stock_photos_search, which searches Unsplash and Pexels over a different route and cannot return video.

tools.name: media_transform
tools.description: Deterministic pixel edits (crop, resize, re-encode) on an image asset this account already owns. Always creates a NEW media_assets row and never mutates the source: the derivative carries ai_metadata.parent_media_asset_id plus the operations applied, an '(edited)' title suffix, the source's folder and its ai_generated flag. FREE: no image-generation quota slot is reserved or spent and no model runs; it is sharp on bytes you already have, so the only cost is one S3 object and one row against media_storage_limit_mb. OPS (at least one of resize, crop, format is required; quality requires format): crop { left, top, width, height } is expressed in SOURCE pixels and is bounds-checked (400 naming the overflow); resize { width, height, fit } with fit 'cover' (attention-weighted crop to the exact frame, the same crop the generation lanes use) or 'contain' (letterboxed: white for jpeg, transparent otherwise); format 'png' | 'jpeg' | 'webp' (default keeps the source format; a source that is none of the three re-encodes to png); quality 1-100. The order of operations is fixed: crop (against the source) -> resize -> encode. Caps: output at most 4096px per side (a format-only transform of a larger source is refused: include a resize or crop), the source fetch at 25MB, the source decode at 24 megapixels (source_too_large). Returns 201 { data: { id, file_url, s3_key, width, height, bytes, mime_type, title, parent_media_asset_id, created_at } }; width/height are measured from the output bytes and null only when unmeasurable.
