Pass `commit: true` to also push the restored content to GitHub via the same path as project_commit (recommended when the project is GitHub-connected so the rollback shows in the commit history with a clear message). Use project_file_versions first to find the version_number to roll back to.

tools.name: project_file_save
tools.description: Write/replace a single file's content in the project. THIS IS THE PRIMARY EDIT TOOL. Writes to builder_code_versions (the project's working DB store) and creates a new version row, so version history stays intact. ⚠️ **SOURCE-OF-TRUTH RULE (read first before assuming you are done editing):** ON A BRANCH (`branch` set to a Hiveku-native branch other than main): the branch WORKING TREE is the source of truth and GitHub is irrelevant. The save updates the branch tree only, never touches main or builder_code_versions.is_current, and is NOT a commit - call project_vcs_commit({project_id, branch, message}) with no files to promote the accumulated edits into a commit. Whether a live branch preview picks this single-file save up is NOT reported here (sync_preview targets the main container, which never sees branch edits); for a batch that must reach the branch preview use project_files_bulk_save({branch}), which returns `preview_effect`, or resync via project_vcs_branch_preview. ON MAIN, when the project HAS GitHub connected (check sites_list → github.connected), the DB is a WORKING BUFFER, not the source of truth — GitHub is. Any save to builder_code_versions that is not committed to GitHub WILL be overwritten the next time the project syncs from GitHub (i.e. webhook push from VSCode OR pre-deploy sync). To make your edits persist past the next sync you MUST follow up with project_commit. The /v3 chat agents auto-commit at session end; MCP agents are responsible for calling project_commit themselves. ON MAIN, when the project does NOT have GitHub connected, the DB IS the source of truth and edits persist on save — project_commit is unnecessary and would fail with `github_not_connected`. OPTIMISTIC CONCURRENCY: pass `expected_hash` (the sha256 you read for this path, from project_files_bulk_get / project_files_status / a prior save) and the route refuses with 409 code "content_conflict" ({path, expected, actual}) when the stored content no longer matches - on main AND on a branch. You are not the only writer; use it whenever you edit a file you read earlier in a session. When to use which write tool (per project state): • project_file_save (this one) — single-file edit. Always writes the DB. • project_commit — batch save N files AND push to GitHub. REQUIRED FOR PERSISTENCE on GitHub-connected projects; fails with code="github_not_connected" on DB-only projects. Recommended flow per project state: GitHub-connected: project_file_save (×N) → project_commit → preview_sync → deploy_site DB-only: project_file_save (×N) → preview_sync (or sync_preview: true) → deploy_site Live preview sync (orthogonal — does not affect persistence): • Set `sync_preview: true` for a one-shot edit — the saved file is pushed into the running Fly preview container immediately, so the next preview_screenshot reflects your change. • For multi-file batches: leave sync_preview off, save N files, then call preview_sync ONCE at the end (cheaper — preview_sync scans every file). • Either way, the preview container must be running. If sites_list shows live_preview.container_status != "running", call preview_start first. Pre-deploy sync gate: when GitHub IS connected, deploy_site runs a reconciliation against GitHub HEAD before queuing the build. If your DB has uncommitted edits AND GitHub has a different change to the same file, the deploy returns 409 with code="github_sync_conflict" and a list of the conflicting files. Resolve via project_commit (push your version) or pass acceptGitHubOverwrite to let GitHub win.

tools.name: project_file_save_async
tools.description: Same as project_file_save but returns immediately with a job_id. The save runs in the background; poll with job_status_get until terminal. Use when writing many files in parallel — fires N saves without blocking the agent's tool socket for N×3s. Idempotency: pass `idempotency_key` (any string ≤128 chars). Retries with the same key return the SAME job — no duplicate writes. Without a key, every call enqueues a new job. Response: 202 Accepted with { job_id, status: 'queued', reused, poll_url }. Watch job_status_get for status transitions: queued → running → succeeded|failed|cancelled|timed_out. Terminal status carries `result` (on success) or `error` (on failure). For ONE file, prefer the sync project_file_save — round-trip is ~3s and you skip the polling loop. Async wins on batches of 5+ saves.

tools.name: project_file_versions
tools.description: List the version history for a single file in a project. Returns each row's version_number, is_current, file_size, language, commit_message, git_commit_hash, git_branch, created_at, created_by, and `actor` — no content (use project_file_diff or project_file_restore for the actual bytes). `actor` says WHO wrote the version: { kind: 'user'|'dashboard_agent'|'mcp_key'|'system', id, label }, derived server-side from the writer's credential (never from any caller-supplied byline); null on rows written before attribution existed — display 'unknown'. Newest first. Use this before project_file_restore so you know which version_number to roll back to.

tools.name: project_files_bulk_delete
tools.description: Soft-delete MANY files by explicit path list in ONE call (up to 500) — replaces N single project_file_delete calls that burn the rate limit. Soft-only: every byte stays in version history (revive via project_file_restore); the same Fly-volume + S3 fan-out as the tree-replace runs so stranded physical files cannot shadow new routes. A full pre-op checkpoint is taken by default (checkpoint:false to skip); dry_run reports what would be deleted. not_found_paths in the response lists requested paths that were not current files.

tools.name: project_files_bulk_get
tools.description: Download EVERY current file in a project in one call — replaces (project_files_list + N×project_file_get). Returns an array of {path, content, encoding, size, language, version}. Binary files come back with encoding="base64". Default scope: CODE + CONFIG only. Binary assets (images/fonts/video/pdf/etc.) are excluded by default and surfaced separately in excluded_asset_paths[] so a multi-MB hero image cannot starve the byte cap and silently drop tsconfig.json. Set include_assets=true to include them in the main files[] payload. Caps: per-file 1MB (oversized files marked truncated, fetch via project_file_get), total payload 20MB (response carries partial=true + next_cursor; pass cursor back to resume). Set include_content=false for a paths-only manifest. Use cases: clone-to-local, "show me everything", template extraction. BRANCH: pass `branch` to download a Hiveku-native branch's WORKING TREE (uncommitted branch edits included) instead of the live project. Same cursor and caps; entries carry `version: null` (tree entries, not builder_code_versions rows); include_assets still reads the shared asset store. The response gains `branch` and `basis: { kind: "branch", working_tree_etag }` - RECORD working_tree_etag at pull and compare it against project_vcs_branches before you push, so a save by someone else on the branch is detected instead of overwritten. Omit `branch` (or pass "main") for the live project, byte-identical to before.

tools.name: project_files_bulk_save
tools.description: ⚠️ FOR A WHOLE PROJECT / LARGE BATCH, PREFER project_import_presign → PUT tarball → project_import_finalize: it is BYTE-EXACT (nothing re-emitted through the model, so no escaping/newline/truncation corruption), lane-routes binaries automatically, and returns a per-file sha256 manifest to verify against. Use THIS tool for small inline batches you just authored. Save MANY files in one call — replaces N×project_file_save. Each file: {path, content, encoding?}. Writes go through the same version-tracking pipeline as project_file_save, so version history stays intact. encoding semantics: 'base64' on a TEXT file is DECODED server-side and stored as text (undecodable payloads reject the request with the offending file named — never silently-stored garbage). 'base64' on a real binary stores the internal binary form, but CDN-servable binaries (public/<subdir>/…) trigger a response warning: they belong in the presign asset lane or they will vanish on deploy. Never base64 text 'to be safe'. Caps: max 500 files per call, 20MB combined payload. Splits required for larger batches. The whole batch is validated upfront (path traversal, content type) — any one bad entry rejects the entire request before any write happens. Per-file write failures (post-validation) come back in results[] with ok=false; succeeded files still land. Duplicate paths in files[] are deduped last-write-wins; summary.duplicates_dropped surfaces the count. TREE-REPLACE MODE (delete_missing=true): use this for "upload my entire local project in one shot". Paths in the project that are NOT in files[] are SOFT-DELETED (is_current flipped to false; bytes stay in builder_code_versions forever). Before any mutation, an automatic full checkpoint is taken (files + S3 assets + DB). If the checkpoint can't be created the operation aborts with code="checkpoint_failed" before touching anything. Without delete_missing, orphaned files persist (additive-only — safer for partial syncs). DRY-RUN (dry_run=true): returns the plan {to_create, to_update, to_delete} + counts without writing, without taking a checkpoint. Always run this first when delete_missing=true so you can confirm what will be removed. RECOVERY PATHS if the tree-replace produces a broken site: 1) Whole-tree rollback: call project_checkpoint_restore with the checkpoint_hash from this response. Restores files + S3 assets + DB to the pre-op snapshot. Any edits made after the tree-replace are discarded. 2) Single-file revive: for any path in the response's soft_deleted_paths, call project_file_versions(file_path) to list the history, pick the most-recent version_number (the one that was current right before the delete), and call project_file_restore — this writes a new is_current=true version with that content, "un-deleting" the file. saveProjectFile computes the next version_number from the full history (no is_current filter), so the math is correct even though all existing rows are is_current=false. 3) Selective revert: same as #2 but pick an earlier version_number from project_file_versions if you want to roll the file back further than its pre-delete state. CAVEAT on discovery: project_files_list and project_files_bulk_get both filter is_current=true, so soft-deleted paths are invisible to them. The reliable way to find what was deleted is the soft_deleted_paths field in THIS response (capture it) or project_checkpoint_get(checkpoint_hash).file_snapshots diffed against the current file list. Does NOT push to GitHub. Use project_commit for the GitHub-connected batch path; this tool works on every project (GitHub or not). BRANCH: pass `branch` to save the batch into a Hiveku-native branch's WORKING TREE. It updates the branch tree only - NOT a commit (project_vcs_commit({project_id, branch, message}) with no files promotes it), never touches main or builder_code_versions.is_current, and syncs a live branch preview if one exists (response `preview_effect` says whether it did, or that you should start one with project_vcs_branch_preview). Response gains `branch`, `uncommitted: true` and `working_tree_etag`; `checkpoint_hash` is null with a `note`. delete_missing on a branch takes NO checkpoint: the branch's last commit is the rollback (project_vcs_revert). dry_run is honored on a branch. Omit `branch` (or pass "main") for the live project, byte-identical to before.

tools.name: project_files_finalize
tools.description: Register assets uploaded via project_files_presign into builder_project_assets — the CDN lane every deploy tier serves. Call this AFTER PUTting the bytes to the presigned URLs; the bytes are already in S3, this only confirms them (HeadObject), writes the public/ mirror when needed, and creates the versioned is_current asset row (exactly what assets_upload does, minus the upload hop). Without this step the uploaded bytes are orphaned and invisible to deploys. Returns per-file `results[]` ({file_path, ok, asset_id?, version_number?, error?}) + a `summary`. Idempotent — re-finalizing a path bumps its version. Retry any `ok:false` entries.

tools.name: project_files_list
tools.description: List the current files in a Hiveku project (paths + metadata, no content). Use to enumerate what to pull. Paginated two ways: • page + limit (1-indexed page numbers) • offset + limit (0-indexed item offset — alias) Response carries `pagination.next_offset` so you can chain calls without recomputing math. `has_more: true` means there's another page. On most projects pass `limit=5000` for a one-shot dump; only projects with >5000 files need to chain via next_offset. If you submit a limit higher than 5000, the response sets `pagination.limit_clamped_from` and `limit_clamped_to` so silent truncation is impossible to miss.

tools.name: project_files_presign
tools.description: Get presigned S3 upload URLs to push BINARY ASSETS (images, fonts, video, audio) to a project WITHOUT base64-through-JSON-RPC — the reliable path for large / many assets (100MB+ sets that assets_upload one-at-a-time is slow for and bulk_save chokes on). WHY a separate lane: CDN-servable assets live in builder_project_assets + S3 and are served via CloudFront on every deploy tier. Pushing them through project_file_save/bulk_save/vcs_commit puts them in builder_code_versions instead — they show in the Fly preview but are DROPPED from the deploy bundle, so they go missing on deploy. Flow: (1) call this with the files you want to upload; (2) for each returned upload, PUT the raw bytes to `upload_url` replaying EXACTLY the `required_headers` (Content-Type + Cache-Control — a mismatch = 403); (3) call project_files_finalize to register them. Key = `<projectId>/<file_path>`. Use file_path like "public/images/cdn/hero.jpg". For a FEW small assets, assets_upload is simpler; code/text files use project_files_bulk_save.

tools.name: project_files_search
tools.description: Full-text search across all current files in a project — `grep -rn` for the codebase. Use this INSTEAD OF listing files + reading each one when you're looking for a symbol, string, or pattern. Examples: • Find every use of an API: { query: "useAccountContext" } • Scoped to TSX: { query: "TODO", glob: "src/**/*.tsx" } • Regex (typed handlers): { query: "use[A-Z]\\w+", is_regex: true } Returns matches with line numbers + before/after context. Capped at 500 matches.

tools.name: project_files_snapshot
tools.description: Build a tarball of every current file in the project and return a short-lived signed S3 URL the caller can curl. ~3-5x smaller than the equivalent JSON from project_files_bulk_get (no per-file overhead, no base64 explosion on binaries). The tarball includes a `.hiveku-manifest.json` at the root mapping paths to version_numbers. When to use: 'I need a complete local copy of the project' or 'I want to test-build offline against the canonical state.' For 'does it currently build?' prefer project_test_build with use_db_state=true — same source, no download required. Default behavior excludes binary assets (images / fonts / etc.) to keep the payload small; pass include_assets=true to include them. Extract with: `curl -sSL '<download_url>' | tar -xz -C /target/dir` (or `-x` for compress='none'). Signed URL is short-lived (default 15min, max 1h). S3 lifecycle policy on the snapshots/ prefix should expire objects within 24h.

tools.name: project_files_snapshot_async
tools.description: Async project_files_snapshot. Returns a job_id immediately and builds the tarball in the background; poll job_status_get({ job_id, wait_seconds: 20 }) until status is 'succeeded', then read download_url from the job's `result` (same body the sync tool returns). USE THIS FOR ANY LARGE PROJECT, and whenever the sync call has already timed out. The synchronous tool cannot serve a big project at all: Cloudflare closes the connection at 120 SECONDS regardless of server or client timeouts, surfacing as an edge HTTP 524 — so a project needing longer than that is unreachable synchronously no matter how the request is configured. A project with hundreds of MB of inline binaries is well past that line. Pass idempotency_key to make retries safe — the same key returns the existing job instead of rebuilding the tarball. ttl_seconds defaults to the 3600 maximum here (unlike the sync tool's 900), because a polled job may sit before the caller uses the URL.

tools.name: project_files_status
tools.description: Diff a local file manifest against a chosen layer of the project in Hiveku. Send [{path, sha256}] for everything you have locally; returns categorized lists: changed (different content), only_local (untracked locally), only_remote (deleted locally or never pulled), plus same_count. No file content is transferred — fast even on big projects. target (optional, default "current"): • "current" — builder_code_versions is_current, i.e. the DEPLOY SOURCE (what deploy_site ships). Byte-identical to the historical behavior. • "main" — the Hiveku-native VCS main HEAD (project_vcs_commit). Between commits this runs BEHIND current, so this shows "what have I changed since my last commit". • "branch:<name>" — a Hiveku-native branch's WORKING TREE (uncommitted branch edits included), hashed from the tree itself, so basis is "branch" with confidence "exact". This is the drift check for a branch loop: diff your local copy against the branch before project_files_bulk_save({branch}). • "deployed" / "deployed:<env>" — what is actually live on that tier (env = development|staging|production; bare "deployed" = development). Always read data.basis.confidence: "exact" is byte-accurate; "approximate"/"unknown" (e.g. a GitHub-source project, or a tier with no deployed manifest yet) means the diff is best-effort — only_remote/deletions may be incomplete. Unknown target values coerce to "current" with a warning (never an error). ★ `local` IS THE WHOLE INPUT, and omitting it is NOT an error even though the schema marks it required — that constraint is not enforced. Measured 2026-08-29 against a 222-file project: calling with only `project_id` returned success, `total_local: 0`, `same_count: 0`, and all 222 files under only_remote. This tool diffs a manifest YOU send, so with no `local` it compares the project against nothing. That is the single most common way to misread it — the answer looks like "the project is empty" or "everything is remote-only" when it means "you sent no manifest". If `total_local` is 0 and you did not intend an empty manifest, you did not hash your files: walk the working tree, sha256 each file's BYTES, and send [{path, sha256}] for every one before drawing any conclusion.

tools.name: project_files_validate_orphan_routes
tools.description: Scan the project's current files for internal route references (href=, <Link href=>, router.push, router.replace, redirect) and report any target path that doesn't resolve to a matching App Router page (`src/app/<segments>/page.tsx|jsx|ts|js`). Server-side reflection of the kind of check you'd write client-side as a migration QA — catches dead links AFTER a wf2next conversion or major refactor BEFORE the deploy. Dynamic segments handled: `[slug]` matches any single segment, `[...rest]` matches catch-alls, `[[...optional]]` matches optional catch-alls. Route groups like `(marketing)` are stripped (App Router convention — they don't appear in URLs). Trailing slashes + query strings + hash anchors are normalized before lookup. ALSO REPORTS ROUTE-OWNERSHIP COLLISIONS via `route_collisions[]`: two route files that can produce the SAME URL (e.g. `app/blog/my-post/page.tsx` beside `app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx` whose generateStaticParams emits `my-post`). Next.js renders exactly ONE of them and silently drops the other, with NO build error, because its own conflict guard covers the Pages Router only. The dynamic route usually wins, so the dedicated page stops being served and editing it changes nothing on the live site. IMPORTANT: `orphans: 0` does NOT mean routing is healthy. The orphan scan only asks whether a link resolves to a page, and a `[slug]` route matches any single segment, so a URL owned by TWO files still resolves and still counts as zero orphans. Always read `route_collisions` too. To ask about one specific URL instead, use `project_route_owner`. Response: `{ orphans: [{source_file, line_number, snippet, route, kind}], route_collisions: [{route, served_by, shadowed_file, note}], routes_found: string[], app_router_pages: string[], summary: {files_scanned, references_found, unique_routes, orphans, route_collisions, pages_indexed} }`. Pass `include_external: true` to ALSO get a list of `https://` / `mailto:` / `tel:` link targets if you want a full audit.

tools.name: project_folder_create
tools.description: Make an empty folder "exist" in the project tree by writing a .gitkeep placeholder at the given path. Idempotent — returns created=false with reason "already_exists" if .gitkeep is already there. Useful when you want to scaffold a directory layout before saving real files into it (e.g. set up src/lib/ before generating its contents).

tools.name: project_folder_delete
tools.description: Soft-delete every file and asset whose path starts with folder_path. Reversible per-file via project_file_restore (use project_file_versions on each path to find the version_number before the delete). Use project_folder_move to rename rather than delete+recreate. Safety: this operates on the prefix as-given. Passing folder_path="src" deletes everything under src/. Always verify with project_files_list ?search=<prefix> before calling.

tools.name: project_get
tools.description: Get full detail for ONE website/builder project — preview URLs (dev/staging/prod), Fly preview state, custom domain, GitHub settings, deployment metadata. This is the per-project version of sites_list; use sites_list when you want the full account list, project_get when you already have a UUID and want the rich detail without the list overhead. Response shape (VERIFIED live 2026-08-29): `{ data: { id, name, subdomain, custom_domain, status, detected_project_type, tiers, github, counts, created_at, updated_at } }`. The URLs are NESTED: `tiers.development.url`, `tiers.staging.url`, `tiers.production.url`, each alongside `enabled`, `status`, `deployment_type`, `distribution_id`, `lambda_function`. GitHub is the nested `github` object (`connected`, `repo`, `default_branch`, `auto_deploy`, `branches`), not flat fields. ★ There are NO flat `dev_preview_url` / `staging_url` / `deployment_url` / `github_repo_url` fields. This description claimed them until 2026-08-29 and they never existed; an agent that looked for them found nothing, concluded the tool could not answer, and went to a memory file instead. ★ WHEN THE DEV URL IS null — that is the normal state, not an error. dev/staging/prod are serverless (Lambda + CloudFront) and a tier has no URL until it is deployed; `tiers.development.status` says "not deployed". The URL you can open RIGHT NOW is the Fly preview container, and it is only on sites_list, as `live_preview.url`. So the ladder for "what is the development URL" is: `tiers.development.url` → if null, `sites_list` → `live_preview.url` (call `preview_start` first if `container_status` is not "running") → if both are empty, say the site has never been deployed rather than reporting the tool as broken. For PM (pm_projects) detail call get_project instead — that lives in a different table.

tools.name: project_github_configure
tools.description: Update a project's GitHub auto-deploy + branch-mapping settings. Use to toggle which tiers auto-deploy (dev/staging/production) and to set which branch maps to each tier. Only the fields you pass are updated. CANNOT do via this tool (require human dashboard action): • Install the Hiveku GitHub App on a repo (user OAuth flow) • Connect a different repo (user must re-link in /settings/github) • Disconnect GitHub entirely For everything else (toggle auto_deploy_production from off to on, change the staging branch from "staging" to "release/v2", etc.) this is the tool. Pair with project_deploy_preflight to verify the new configuration before relying on it.

tools.name: project_hosting_options_get
tools.description: One read answering "what is enabled on this website project, per tier?" — annotations overlay, review share, cookie consent, accessibility, SEO enhancements, security headers, PWA, form captcha (+ spam level), Hiveku badge (+ position), minification level, staging_enabled, deployment types, custom-code entry count. Each family is keyed development/staging/production. ★ Every toggle here applies at DEPLOY time — a change is live only after the next deploy of that tier. ★ Per-tier password protection does not exist on the platform — never promise it.

tools.name: project_import_finalize
tools.description: Step 2 of the byte-exact bulk import: extracts the uploaded tarball server-side and lands every file EXACTLY as archived — text into builder_code_versions (verbatim; no write-path sanitizers), binaries into the CDN asset lane (S3 + builder_project_assets + code-lane shadow tombstones, so images survive deploys). A single wrapping root directory is stripped automatically; node_modules/.git/dist inside the archive are skipped. VERIFY WITH THE MANIFEST: the response carries per-file { path, sha256, lane } computed from the bytes ACTUALLY STORED — compare against your local sha256s instead of re-downloading. A mismatch means re-import that file. delete_missing:true = tree-replace (code-lane paths absent from the archive are soft-deleted; a full pre-op checkpoint is MANDATORY and its checkpoint_hash is your one-call rollback). ALWAYS dry_run:true first with delete_missing. The preview container AND cold-boot storage are synced automatically on success (response carries preview_synced — only if false do you need a manual preview_sync). Then project_test_build before deploying.

tools.name: project_import_presign
tools.description: Step 1 of the BYTE-EXACT bulk code import — THE way to get a whole project (or any large file set) into Hiveku without corruption. Flow: `COPYFILE_DISABLE=1 tar czf site.tar.gz -C <dir> .` (EXCLUDE node_modules/.git/.next; COPYFILE_DISABLE=1 keeps macOS AppleDouble ._* junk out — the server skips it regardless) → PUT the archive to the returned upload_url (replaying required_headers) → project_import_finalize with the returned key. Why this over bulk_save for big sets: file bodies never pass through the model or JSON, so nothing gets HTML-escaped, newline-trimmed, or truncated; binaries are lane-routed to the CDN asset store automatically; and finalize returns a per-file sha256 manifest you verify against local hashes. Archive cap: 200MB compressed.

tools.name: project_logs_get
tools.description: DEPLOYED-environment logs — Lambda / ECS / build / deployment-event logs across the project's hosting surfaces. This is the 'Vercel-like Functions tab' for Hiveku-deployed sites. Use this when: • A page on staging or production threw an error and you want the request log • A deploy is stuck or failed and you want the build output • You want to see what recent traffic looks like For ad-hoc commands in the dev preview (npm test, ls, tsc) use preview_exec. For preview-container stdout use preview_logs. Three sources: • runtime — Lambda or ECS container logs from CloudWatch (live request traces) • build — recent build sessions with full output (deploy debugging) • deploy — high-level deployment lifecycle events (status + error_message) Filter via `level` (error|warning|info|all) to focus on what matters. `filter` supports CloudWatch FilterPattern syntax for runtime logs. Output is account-scoped; AWS log group / infra detail is intentionally stripped. `since` applies to every source; build and deploy events are windowed on their FINISH time. When no build finished inside the window the response carries window_empty:true + showing:'latest' with one labeled event.

tools.name: project_redirect_create
tools.description: Add a single redirect rule. The route validates against duplicate sources, self-loops, trailing-slash-only redirects, and circular chains up to depth 10. Defaults: status_code=301 (permanent), match_type="exact", is_active=true. After creating rules, call project_redirects_deploy to push them to CloudFront — until then they're only stored in the DB.

tools.name: project_redirect_delete
tools.description: Delete one redirect rule by id. The DB row is removed but CloudFront keeps serving the old set until you call project_redirects_deploy.

tools.name: project_redirect_update
tools.description: Update a single redirect rule by id. Allow-listed: from_path, to_path, status_code, match_type, is_active, notes. Re-runs the same loop-detection validation as project_redirect_create.

tools.name: project_redirects_deploy
tools.description: Push the project's redirects out to CloudFront. Nothing you changed takes effect until this runs. It deploys BOTH kinds: the path rules from project_redirect_create, AND the domain redirects derived from the attached domains — every non-primary domain 301s to the primary. So after project_domains_add or flipping is_primary, call this or the change is stored but not live. Domain redirects apply to the PRODUCTION tier only. Uses CloudFront Functions for ≤150 rules; auto-switches to Lambda@Edge above that. Optional body {tier} — "development" | "staging" | "production" (default production). ★ SLOW BY NATURE - 60-120s is normal. It reads the CloudFront distribution config, updates it (retrying up to 3 times on an ETag conflict when another deploy is in flight), then issues an invalidation. The route may run the full 300s; the tool budget is 290s, so a contended deploy can time out HERE while it is still succeeding on CloudFront. A timeout from this tool is NOT a failed deploy - do not re-send it. Read project_redirects_list and check the live URL after 10-15 minutes instead. Returns { success, deployed_count, deployment_target, invalidation_id, message, tier, deploymentMethod, functionName, projectType, activeRedirects, deploymentNote, warning? }. deployed_count is the number of ACTIVE rules pushed; deployment_target is "cloudfront-function" or "lambda-edge". A `warning` means the shared-function path failed and the distribution kept its existing function - the redirects may be stale until the next successful deploy, so report it rather than silently retrying. ★ PROPAGATION IS NOT INSTANT: a 200 means CloudFront accepted the change; it goes live globally in 10-15 minutes. Do not curl the URL immediately and conclude the deploy failed.

tools.name: project_redirects_list
tools.description: List a project's redirect rules. Returns {redirects: [{id, from_path, to_path, status_code, match_type, is_active, created_at, notes?}], hosting_config}. Rules live in website_projects.redirect_rules; serve via CloudFront once project_redirects_deploy is called.

tools.name: project_review_link_get
tools.description: Get the client review share link for a website project — THE ONLY URL WHERE ANNOTATING WORKS. The injected bridge is deliberately inert outside an iframe, so handing someone the raw dev URL yields a page where nothing can be pinned; the annotate page is app.hiveku.com/review/share/<token>?branch=… which iframes the tier and hosts the overlay UI. Returns share_url plus ready-made annotate_urls for development/staging (the share page's branch values are dev|staging — the development→dev mapping is already done). Production is NOT a reviewable tier and gets no annotate URL. Strictly read-only: if no token exists yet it says so — mint one with project_review_link_set {enabled:true}.

tools.name: project_review_link_set
tools.description: Enable/disable the review share link, or rotate its token. {enabled:true} turns sharing on and mints a token if none exists; {enabled:false} turns it off; {regenerate:true} issues a NEW token — ★ every previously shared link dies immediately, so only regenerate when revoking access is the point. After enabling, hand the user the annotate URL from the response (or project_review_link_get), never the raw tier URL.

tools.name: project_route_owner
tools.description: Answer "which file actually renders this URL?" for one route. USE THIS FIRST when a page will not change no matter what you edit, or when content looks stale/generic/wrong and you are about to blame CSS, caching, or a build. More than one route file can produce the same URL (a dedicated page beside a `[slug]` sibling that prerenders the same slug). Next.js renders ONE and silently drops the other with no build error, so the file you are editing may simply never ship. There is no other way to see this: the files all exist on disk and the build succeeds. Returns `served_by` (the file to edit), `owners[]` (everything claiming the URL), and `shadowed[]` (files that are NOT on the live site). If `has_collision` is true, fix the ownership before editing anything: remove the slug from the dynamic route's generateStaticParams(), or delete the redundant dedicated page. For a whole-project sweep instead of one URL, use `project_files_validate_orphan_routes` and read its `route_collisions[]`.

tools.name: project_secrets_apply_to_preview
tools.description: Push the project's ALREADY-STORED secrets into the running Fly dev preview WITHOUT sending any values — the route reads Secrets Manager server-side, applies the dev-tier resolution (_DEV wins; _STAGING/_PROD skipped) and restarts the machine (~11s). Returns key NAMES only. Use this when a secret exists (set earlier, by the dashboard, or by database_provision) but the preview container predates it — never re-send a stored value through project_secrets_set just to reach the preview. NEXT_PUBLIC_* keys are compile-time inlined: rebuild defaults to true when any are present so they reach the browser bundle.

tools.name: project_secrets_delete
tools.description: Delete one secret by key. ★ Omitting `key` no longer wipes anything: a total wipe now requires `all: true` explicitly (irreversible; refuses with 400 otherwise). Deletes propagate to the deployed Lambda env on the next deploy.

tools.name: project_secrets_list
tools.description: List a project's environment variables / secrets (stored in AWS Secrets Manager, NOT in builder_code_versions). Returns { secrets: { KEY: value, ... }, entries, sensitive_keys, metadata }. Pass metadata_only=true to get { keys: [...], count, sensitive_keys, metadata } with no values — use that whenever you only need to check key existence, to avoid pulling plaintext values over the wire. IMPORTANT — variables marked SENSITIVE are OMITTED from `secrets` entirely and listed by name in `sensitive_keys`. Their values are write-only and cannot be retrieved by this or any other tool, by you, by the account owner, or by Hiveku staff. Do not retry, do not try another tool, and do not try to read them out of a .env file, a build log, or the preview container: those paths are closed too. If you need such a variable changed, call project_secrets_set with a NEW value, or ask the user to set it in the dashboard. A key appearing in `sensitive_keys` IS configured — treat it as set, never as missing. Secrets are the source of truth for environment configuration. The dashboard /settings → Environment Variables UI writes to the same AWS Secrets Manager record. For web projects, .env is auto-generated from these at deploy time; for Expo native projects, .env is also written to builder_code_versions because mobile bundles need env vars baked in at local EAS build time.

tools.name: project_secrets_set
tools.description: Upsert one or more secrets. Body: { secrets: { KEY: value, ... }, tier? }. Auto-syncs to deployed Lambda envs (non-blocking). **TIER SCOPING — read before setting anything.** A bare key applies to EVERY tier, PRODUCTION included: setting `STRIPE_KEY` while 'testing on dev' changes the production Lambda env. Pass `tier: 'dev' | 'staging' | 'production'` to scope the write (the route suffixes the keys _DEV / _STAGING / _PROD for you; explicit suffixes also work). The response's `scope.applies_to` lists exactly which tiers each key reached, and `scope.note` calls out any production hit — check it. **Auto-applies to the running dev preview by default.** Fly machine env is baked at create time, so a plain SecretsManager write previously did NOT reach a running preview container — agents had to hand-write .env.local as a workaround. Now, after the secrets write, this route pushes the new env into the Fly machine (stop → updateMachine → start ≈ 11s downtime) so the dev server sees the values on next request. Response includes `preview_env_applied: true|false` + `preview_env_apply_reason` (one of: 'no_preview_machine', 'only_non_dev_keys_set', or a Fly error like 'restart_failed') so you can confirm propagation. _DEV-suffixed keys (e.g. DATABASE_URL_DEV) are stripped to the base name (DATABASE_URL) before being injected into the preview machine, matching the same resolution rule preview_start uses. _PROD / _PRODUCTION / _STAGING suffixed keys are SKIPPED for the preview (they're for the deployed Lambda envs, not the dev container). Pass `apply_to_preview: false` to skip the bounce — use this when setting multiple secrets in a row (skip on all but the last call), or when you only need the value in deployed Lambdas not in the live preview. To apply secrets that are ALREADY STORED without re-sending their values (e.g. keys written by database_provision or the dashboard), use project_secrets_apply_to_preview instead. **NEXT_PUBLIC_* auto-rebuild**: keys prefixed with `NEXT_PUBLIC_` are inlined into the build at compile time by Next.js. A runtime restart alone keeps the cached `.next` bundle and the new value stays `undefined` in the browser. Whenever any NEXT_PUBLIC_ key is in the secrets payload, this route AUTO-TRIGGERS a `preview_sync` afterward so the new value reaches the browser bundle on the next page load. Force the same behavior for non-NEXT_PUBLIC keys by passing `rebuild: true`. Response includes `preview_synced: true|false` and `preview_sync_reason` so you can confirm the rebuild fired.

tools.name: project_site_orphan_sweep
tools.description: Delete STALE BUILD OUTPUT from the project's SITE bucket under explicitly named top-level prefixes — the lane nothing else sweeps. Preview first: the dry run returns a `confirm_token`, and confirm:true without it is refused 400 confirm_token_required. Use when project_cdn_behaviors_list shows behaviors backed ONLY by site_bucket_objects (asset_rows:0, asset_bucket_objects:0): typically old-framework output (Vite era) that deploys sync WITHOUT deleting, which re-backs route-shadowing CloudFront behaviors (403s) on every deploy. DRY-RUN by default — returns per-prefix counts, newest LastModified, and a `confirm_token` minted for exactly the objects listed. Re-call with confirm:true AND that token to delete; confirm:true alone is refused 400 confirm_token_required. ★ If the set moved in between the call is refused 409 stale_plan (the check is over the exact key set, not the count), and a token expires after 15 minutes. Hard guards: nextjs (Lambda-served) projects only — on static-export projects the bucket IS the site and the call refuses; reserved/runtime prefixes refused; any prefix with asset-lane backing refused (clean that lane first). After a confirmed sweep run project_cdn_behaviors_prune then project_cdn_invalidate — and future deploys stop regenerating the behaviors, ending the prune-after-every-deploy treadmill.

tools.name: project_state_at
tools.description: Reconstruct the project's state at an arbitrary timestamp WITHOUT touching anything — read-only dry run for the PIT machinery. Returns the file list (paths, sizes, version_ids), asset list (with resolved S3 versionIds), and the set of paths that were tombstoned by that time. Use this to (a) preview what 'restore to time X' would produce before committing, (b) extract a single file at time X by setting include_content=true and picking the path you want, (c) inspect drift between current state and an earlier snapshot. Cheaper than project_checkpoint_list when you already know the timestamp you care about.

tools.name: project_test_build
tools.description: Run Hiveku's exact build pipeline WITHOUT deploying. Two input modes: • use_db_state=true (RECOMMENDED for 'does the current canonical state still build?'): Skips the upload entirely — the builder pulls all current files from builder_code_versions itself. Removes the 'my bulk_get returned 424/538 files' completeness dependency that bit agents on big projects. Perfect for pre-deploy sanity checks after a sequence of project_file_save calls. • files[] (caller-supplied snapshot): Use when you want to verify a candidate change set that's NOT yet in the canonical DB. Must include package.json. Omit node_modules / .next/ / build/ / dist/ / .git/. Pass exactly one — they're mutually exclusive. RECOMMENDED PATTERN — polling (wait=false, default): 1. const { build_session_id } = await project_test_build({ project_id, use_db_state: true }); 2. loop: { const { status } = await project_test_build_log_get({ project_id, session_id: build_session_id }); if (status !== 'running') break; await sleep(10_000); } 3. inspect logs, fix code, repeat. ALTERNATIVE — inline wait (wait=true): the route blocks up to 5 MIN server-side. Most MCP clients have a SHORTER timeout (httpx default 120s; many agent harnesses 60s). On a 500+ file project with a cold build cache the build runs 119s and the client gives up even though the server succeeds. Polling sidesteps this entirely. Use wait=true only on small projects or when you know the build cache is warm. MANIFEST GATES (2026-09-02): a test build runs the SAME engines.node and lockfile verdicts as deploy_site, before any build spend, so it cannot report green on a project whose deploy would be refused. A refused build ends with status 'failed' and a log line '[Test Build] refused before any build spend: <message> <hint>' (the codes are engines_unsatisfied and lockfile_out_of_sync). lockfile_out_of_sync means the project's lockfile resolves a different framework version (next, react, react-dom, vite) than package.json declares: package.json is the truth, and a lockfile that disagrees with it is stale (evidence of a PAST install; routinely stale here because manifests are edited without a local npm). The fix is IN THE PROJECT: update package.json to the intended versions or delete the lockfile (the project then builds with a plain install and no lockfile; the preview never writes one back). Never hand-edit the lockfile and never downgrade package.json to match it. Typical timing: 90-180s cold, ~30-60s warm cache. BRANCH: `use_db_state: true` + `branch` builds the Hiveku-native branch's WORKING TREE (uncommitted branch edits included) with the same pipeline - the pre-merge / pre-deploy check for branch work. `files[]` + `branch` is refused with 400 (mutually exclusive: a caller-supplied snapshot has no branch). Omit `branch` (or pass "main") to build the live project, byte-identical to before.

tools.name: project_test_build_log_get
tools.description: Fetch the full log transcript for a test build by its session ID. Returns the auto-fixes Hiveku applied, npm install output, next build output, and any TypeScript/route-validator errors. Status is one of 'running' | 'succeeded' | 'failed', derived from sentinel log lines. Call this after project_test_build (especially when wait=false). When the line_count hits the cap (10,000), the truncated flag is true.

tools.name: project_vcs_branch_create
tools.description: Create a Hiveku branch off `from` (default `main`) so work can be done off to the side WITHOUT touching the live project. Branch content lives in Supabase/S3 — `main` and the web builder are untouched until you merge. Commit to the branch with project_vcs_commit({branch}), preview it on Fly with project_vcs_branch_preview, and merge it back with project_vcs_merge. Branch names: letters/numbers/. _ / - only, and keep them short (preview machines cap the name).

tools.name: project_vcs_branch_delete
tools.description: Delete a Hiveku-native branch REF — DESTRUCTIVE: once the ref is gone, a later project_vcs_prune treats its tree as an orphan and destroys the bytes. Requires confirm: true (400 confirm_required without it). Refuses when the branch is `main` (400), is bound to an environment (409 — clear the binding with project_vcs_env_bind first), has an OPEN pull request (409 — merge or close it first), or is a STASH branch (pending/*, stash/* — 409: those hold scooped customer work; merge them back first, or pass force: true only when the user explicitly says to discard it). Only delete a branch the user asked to clean up or whose PR you just merged. NOT the same as project_vcs_prune (storage GC of orphaned trees).

tools.name: project_vcs_branch_preview
tools.description: Spin up a live preview of a BRANCH at its own URL, in its own isolated app — the project's main preview is untouched and the branch tree never enters the project's files. Use it to look at off-to-the-side work before merging. Returns { previewUrl, status, previewSessionId, filesSynced }. status is 'ready' (serving now — open previewUrl) or 'starting' (the app is up but still installing/compiling, usually another 30-90s). On 'starting' do NOT call this again — that spawns a second app; poll project_vcs_branch_preview_status with the previewSessionId. Previews are reaped automatically; call project_vcs_branch_preview_teardown when done to free it sooner.

tools.name: project_vcs_branch_preview_status
tools.description: Check a branch preview started by project_vcs_branch_preview. Returns { status, ready, previewUrl, branch }. Re-probes the container, so a preview that finished compiling since you started it flips to ready here. Poll this instead of starting another preview — starting again spawns a second app. Omit session_id to list every live branch preview for the project.

tools.name: project_vcs_branch_preview_teardown
tools.description: Destroy a branch preview and its isolated app now. Optional — previews are swept automatically once they age out — but tear down when the review is finished so several open previews do not pile up. Irreversible: start a fresh preview to look again.

tools.name: project_vcs_branches
tools.description: List a project's Hiveku-native branches (default `main` first), backed by Supabase. Calling this also lazily initializes the project's VCS (`main` ref + initial commit), so the dev extension calls it right after downloading a project to ensure version control is ready. No GitHub involved. Each branch carries `ahead` (its commits since the merge-base) and `behind` (main's commits since the merge-base), so you can spot a stale branch WITHOUT fetching two trees with project_vcs_compare - which answers what differs, not who moved. ★ Both are null on `main` itself and on a branch with no base commit: null means the question does not apply, where 0 would read as 'in sync'. A freshly merged branch correctly reads 0 behind, because the merge-base moves on merge exactly as git's does. Each branch also carries `uncommitted` (true when its WORKING TREE has edits not yet promoted into a commit - saves made through project_file_save / project_files_bulk_save / project_file_delete with `branch`) and `working_tree_etag` (a short fingerprint of the working tree; null when unknown). RECORD the etag when you pull (project_files_bulk_get({branch}) returns the same value) and COMPARE it here before you push: a changed etag means someone else saved on this branch since your pull - re-pull and reconcile instead of overwriting. `uncommitted: true` on a branch you are about to deploy or merge is fine: promotion happens server-side.

tools.name: project_vcs_checkout
tools.description: Return a branch's full working tree as { files: [{path, content, encoding}] } so you can materialize it LOCALLY. For `main` this returns the live project state; for a branch it returns the branch's off-to-the-side content (uncommitted working-tree edits included). `encoding` is 'base64' for binary files. `data` also carries head_commit_id, working_tree_etag and uncommitted. ★ THIS CHANGES NOTHING SERVER-SIDE. It is a read: it does not switch the project, the editor, or any deployed tier onto that branch, and no tool does. That is deliberate - materializing a branch into the live project IS what project_vcs_merge does, so a 'checkout' that did it would make main become the branch. To WORK on a branch you do not switch anything: pass `branch` to the file tools - project_files_bulk_get / project_file_get to read, project_file_save / project_files_bulk_save / project_file_delete to write its working tree, project_test_build to build it, preview_screenshot / preview_http_get to look at its branch preview - then project_vcs_commit({branch, message}) with no files to promote the edits into a commit. For a plain download, project_files_bulk_get({branch}) is the same data with cursoring and caps. To make a branch actually SERVE somewhere: project_vcs_env_bind points development or staging at it (the next deploy ships that branch's pinned tree), or project_vcs_branch_preview spins a throwaway preview of it. project_branch_switch is a different thing entirely - it switches the tracked GITHUB branch and 400s without a GitHub repo.

tools.name: project_vcs_commit
tools.description: Hiveku-native commit (default `main`, or any branch via `branch`) — saves file edits/deletions AND records a commit entirely in Supabase (NO GitHub needed). This is the dev-flow equivalent of `git commit && git push`, used by the VSCode extension and by Claude Code working in a downloaded project folder. Works on EVERY project (GitHub-connected or DB-only) — unlike project_commit, which is GitHub-only. Committing to `main` saves the files via the normal versioned path (the live project changes), snapshots the new state as a checkpoint, and advances `main`. Committing with `branch` set stores the work off to the side in Supabase/S3 WITHOUT touching the live project — the work-in-progress lane; create the branch first with project_vcs_branch_create. `main` is bootstrapped lazily the first time you commit/list — nothing to set up. When to use: 'commit my local changes back to Hiveku', 'save this edit session with a message'. After committing to main, trigger a deploy with deploy_site if you want it live. BODY: message (required) + files: [{path, content, encoding?}] (encoding 'base64' for binaries; `file_path` accepted as an alias for `path`). Optionally deletedFiles: [path] and branch (target branch, default main). Returns the new commit { id, message, branch_name, checkpoint_hash, revertable, revert_blocked_reason, recovery, files_committed, files_deleted, promoted, created_at }. ★ A commit on `main` snapshots the project and carries a checkpoint_hash you can pass to project_checkpoint_restore. A commit on a NON-MAIN BRANCH has checkpoint_hash null and revertable false — branch content lives in an S3 tree and never enters the live project until merge, so there is nothing to restore. That is by design, not a failure: read `recovery` for the path that does work. Revert main commits via project_checkpoint_restore using the commit's checkpoint_hash; revert a BRANCH to one of its earlier commits with project_vcs_revert. PROMOTE (no files): on a branch, the branch-aware file tools (project_file_save / project_files_bulk_save / project_file_delete with `branch`) write the branch's WORKING TREE without committing. Calling this with `branch` and NO files / deletedFiles PROMOTES that working tree into a commit (no bytes are re-uploaded; the tree pointer becomes the commit). The response carries `promoted: true` in that case. A clean branch (nothing uncommitted) answers 409 code "nothing_to_commit" - not an error to retry. A branch that moved under you (someone else saved or committed mid-call) answers 409 "branch_changed" (the head moved; re-read project_vcs_branches and retry), and 409 "branch_busy" means another writer holds the branch write lock (retry shortly). The builder does not replay VCS commits: two identical promote calls both execute and the second simply answers 409 nothing_to_commit, so do NOT pad `message` with timestamps or etags to defeat a replay - keep messages meaningful, they are permanent history.

tools.name: project_vcs_compare
tools.description: Compare two branches' working trees file-by-file (status relative to going from `from` → `to`). Either side may be `main`. Returns { from, to, added, removed, modified, entries: [{path, status}] }. Use to review what a branch changed before merging.

tools.name: project_vcs_diff_file
tools.description: Both sides of ONE file across two Hiveku-native branches' working trees - the per-file drill-down for project_vcs_compare (which lists paths and statuses but no content). Returns { data: { from, to, path, status: 'added'|'removed'|'modified'|'same', base: {content, encoding, hash}|null, head: {content, encoding, hash}|null } } where `base` is the file on `from` and `head` the file on `to`; a side is null when the path does not exist there. Either side may be `main`. Sides over 1 MB come back with tooLarge instead of content. PR REVIEW: a pull request diff is from: <target_branch>, to: <source_branch> - call project_vcs_compare once for the path list, then this tool per changed path you want to read. Uncommitted working-tree edits on either branch ARE included (a branch's working tree may run ahead of its last commit).

tools.name: project_vcs_env_bind
tools.description: Bind the development or staging environment to a Hiveku-native branch — its next deploy ships that branch's PINNED tree instead of main — or clear the binding so the tier tracks main again by passing branch "main" (or ""). `branch` is REQUIRED so a mis-built call can never clear a binding by accident. production is refused with 400 production_immutable: `main` IS production, permanently. ★ IF THE PROJECT HAS A CMS, BINDING ARMS A SILENT TRAP and the response says so in `warning`: every CMS write goes to main, with no branch awareness anywhere, so once a tier serves a branch an entry edited in the CMS panel will NOT appear on that tier, and a scheduled publish reports success while never going live. Relay that warning to the user - keep CMS work on an unbound tier, or merge the branch before relying on CMS content there. (Scheduled publishes are now HELD rather than falsely completed while a tier is bound.) Binding does NOT deploy; trigger the tier's deploy (deploy_site) to put the branch live. A later branch delete is refused while a binding points at it. Returns the full bindings object (same shape as project_vcs_env_bindings).

tools.name: project_vcs_env_bindings
tools.description: Read which branch each deploy environment serves (Hiveku-native VCS environment→branch bindings). Returns { development: {branch, bound}, staging: {branch, bound}, production: {branch: 'main', bound: false, locked: true} }. `bound: false` means the tier tracks `main` (today's default behavior). production is PERMANENTLY `main` and can never be rebound. NOT the same as project_env_matrix (environment VARIABLES) or the legacy GitHub branch-deployments mapping.

tools.name: project_vcs_history
tools.description: List Hiveku-native VCS commit history (newest first) for a project, backed by Supabase. Each entry: { id, branch_name, message, actor, checkpoint_hash, files_committed, files_deleted, created_at }. `actor` says WHO made the commit — { kind: 'user'|'dashboard_agent'|'mcp_key'|'system', id, label } — derived server-side from the writer's credential at commit time (an MCP/agent commit shows kind 'mcp_key' with the API key's id + name; a dashboard commit shows kind 'user' with the user's id). `actor` is null on commits from before attribution existed — display 'unknown'; it is not inferable. Bootstraps `main` lazily, so even a never-before-committed project returns its initial commit. Each entry also carries revertable, revert_blocked_reason and recovery. A `merge` commit also carries merged_branch, merged_into and auto_merged, which is how you answer "was branch X ever merged" without a PR - the direct/agent merge lane creates no PR row at all. ★ An 'already up to date' merge writes NO commit, so absence here is not proof a branch was never merged. ★ FILTER ON `revertable` BEFORE OFFERING A ROLLBACK. Only a commit with a checkpoint_hash can be restored with project_checkpoint_restore, and a commit on a NON-MAIN BRANCH always has checkpoint_hash null and revertable false — by design, because branch content lives in an S3 tree and never enters the live project until merge. `recovery` names the path that does work for that commit (checkout/compare on a branch; the merge commit once merged).

tools.name: project_vcs_merge
tools.description: Merge a branch into ANY target branch (`into`, default `main`) with 3-way conflict flagging. Non-conflicting changes are applied as a `merge` commit on the target; files changed on BOTH sides (to different content) are returned in `conflicts` and left for you to resolve — they are NOT overwritten. PARTIAL semantics: the clean portion merges even when some files conflict. For all-or-nothing merging, open a pull request (project_vcs_pr_create) and merge it with project_vcs_pr_merge, which is STRICT — any conflict refuses the whole merge. The source branch is never deleted, so you can fix conflicts and merge again. ★ The merge commit lands on the target WITH a checkpoint_hash (kind 'merge'), so a merge IS revertable even though the branch commits behind it were not — revert the merge commit to undo the whole branch's work in one step. Merging into `main` changes the live project; merging into another branch only updates that branch. Returns { merged_into, applied, deleted, conflicts, commit } — `deleted` counts deleted FILES applied by the merge, not branches.

tools.name: project_vcs_pr_close
tools.description: Close an open Hiveku-native pull request WITHOUT merging. The source branch is untouched. 409 if the PR is not open. A closed PR can be reopened with project_vcs_pr_reopen (a merged one cannot).

tools.name: project_vcs_pr_create
tools.description: Open a Hiveku-native pull request: source_branch → target_branch (default `main`). Works on EVERY project — no GitHub needed (for GitHub repos use github_pr_create instead). The PR records merge intent and shows a live diff (project_vcs_pr_get); merge it atomically with project_vcs_pr_merge. 409 when a PR for the same source→target pair is already open. Returns the PR { id, number, status, source_branch, target_branch, title, ... } — `number` is per-project.

tools.name: project_vcs_pr_get
tools.description: Get one Hiveku-native pull request by its per-project number, INCLUDING a live diff recomputed on every read ({ added, removed, modified, entries }). A merged/closed PR whose source branch was deleted still returns, with diff: null and a diff_error explaining why. Use before merging to review exactly what will change.

tools.name: project_vcs_pr_list
tools.description: List Hiveku-native pull requests for a project (project_pull_requests-backed — NOT GitHub PRs; those are github_pr_list). Filter by status open | merged | closed. Each entry: { id, number, status, source_branch, target_branch, title, description, created_at, merged_at, closed_at, ... }. ★ Each PR carries source_branch_recreated: true means a branch by that name exists now but was created AFTER the PR - the name was deleted and reused, so this PR's history does NOT describe the branch currently wearing it. null means not checked (the branch is gone, or the lookup was unavailable); never read null as an assurance.

tools.name: project_vcs_pr_merge
tools.description: Merge an open Hiveku-native pull request — STRICT and atomic: if ANY file conflicts, NOTHING is merged (409 code merge_conflicts; the PR stays open; resolve on the source branch and retry). ★ READ THE CONFLICTS AT THE TOP OF THE ERROR BODY: `conflicts`, `conflict_details` and `conflict_count` sit beside `error`, which through this proxy means `details.conflicts` - the same depth as the direct lane. They are ALSO still under `details.data.conflicts` for older callers; do not report a conflict-free failure because you only looked in one place. This is the all-or-nothing counterpart to project_vcs_merge's partial semantics — prefer it for reviewed changes. Merging a PR whose target is `main` changes the live project. The source branch is NOT deleted; delete it afterwards with project_vcs_branch_delete if it is finished. `merged` is terminal — a merged PR cannot reopen.

tools.name: project_vcs_pr_reopen
tools.description: Reopen a CLOSED Hiveku-native pull request (merged PRs are terminal and cannot reopen). 409 if the PR is not closed, or when another PR for the same source→target pair is now open.

tools.name: project_vcs_prune
tools.description: Prune orphaned branch-tree storage for a project — S3 tree objects not referenced by any branch or commit (accumulated from superseded branch commits). SAFE BY DEFAULT: runs as a dry run and only reports what WOULD be deleted unless you pass dry_run=false. Returns { scanned, referenced, orphaned[], deleted, dry_run }.

tools.name: project_vcs_revert
tools.description: Move a Hiveku-native BRANCH back to one of its own earlier commits. Writes a NEW commit (kind 'revert') whose tree is the target commit's tree and moves the branch head to it - history stays linear, nothing is deleted, and the branch's uncommitted working-tree edits are discarded as part of the move (they were what you are reverting). This is the rollback for branch work: a branch commit carries no checkpoint, so project_checkpoint_restore does not apply there. For MAIN, keep using project_checkpoint_restore with the commit's checkpoint_hash (project_vcs_history). GUARDS: `commit_id` must be a commit ON THIS BRANCH of this project (400 not_revertable otherwise - a foreign branch's commit is refused); `main` is refused (400 main_not_allowed). Pass `expected_head_commit_id` (the head you observed via project_vcs_branches / project_vcs_history) and the revert is refused with 409 branch_changed ("branch moved since this turn") if the branch head is no longer that commit - always pass it when reverting on behalf of a user so a concurrent save is not silently thrown away. Returns the new commit { id, message, branch_name, kind, created_at }. A live branch preview is NOT resynced automatically - re-run project_vcs_branch_preview (or its resync) to see the reverted tree.

tools.name: project_vcs_stash
tools.description: Scoop everything PENDING on an environment — work that differs from what is provably live — onto a new branch, so the environment's source matches exactly what it serves. Per environment: 'production' moves undeployed editor/is_current changes to a branch and aligns `main` to the proven deployed baseline (refuses when what-is-live cannot be proven — deploy once, then retry); 'development'/'staging' bound to a branch moves that branch's undeployed commits to a new branch and resets it to the deployed pin; an UNBOUND tier returns 409 tier_tracks_main (its pending work IS main's — stash production instead). DRY RUN IS THE DEFAULT: without dry_run: false this only REPORTS { status, fileCount, modified, ... } and writes NOTHING. Statuses: clean (nothing pending) | stashed | skipped (reason says why — e.g. active editors, unprovable baseline) | failed. Apply mode notifies the account owners and returns the branch holding the work; merge it back later with project_vcs_merge (production stash → into main; branch stash → into ITS bound branch, never main).

tools.name: project_version_log
tools.description: Combined chronological timeline of file edits, checkpoints, restores, and deploys for one project. One call answers 'what happened to this project today?' without juggling four separate endpoints. Each event has the same shape: { type, at, title, subtitle, ref_id, metadata }. Newest-first. Edit events carry metadata.actor = { kind: 'user'|'dashboard_agent'|'mcp_key'|'system', id, label } saying WHO made the edit — derived from the writer's credential at write time; null on rows from before attribution existed (display 'unknown'). Pass the response's `oldest_event_at` as `until` on the next call to paginate older events. Filters: • since / until — ISO timestamps for date-range scoping • file_path — limit to edits of one file (forces type=edit) • types — CSV of event types to include (edit, checkpoint, restore, deploy) • limit — max events (default 100, max 500) ★ Pass _fields:["type","at","title"] to drop the per-event metadata objects, and _max_bytes to cap the payload; both trim honestly and report what was omitted.

tools.name: redesign_homepage_approve
tools.description: Mark the project's homepage as approved, unlocking the rest of the redesign workflow. Sets website_projects.redesign_homepage_approved_at — until this is set, redesign_start refuses with 409 "Homepage not approved". Call exactly once after the user confirms the homepage looks good.

tools.name: redesign_import
tools.description: Start the background scrape of all selected pages — fires Firecrawl per page and stages results in the 7-day scraper bucket. Returns 202 immediately; poll redesign_status to watch pages transition through scraping → assets_imported. After that, call redesign_promote per page (with the user-approved subset of asset URLs) to move them into durable storage.

tools.name: redesign_promote
tools.description: Move a staged redesign page from the scraper bucket (7-day TTL) into durable project storage. Downloads the agent-approved subset of discovered asset URLs into the project bucket as builder_project_assets rows, S3-copies HTML+markdown into the durable brand-assets/ prefix, and writes .hiveku/redesign/<slug>.json into the project workspace for the agent to read on its redesign turn. Pass assetUrls to filter; omit/null = promote all discovered.

tools.name: redesign_restart
tools.description: Abandon the current redesign session (status → partial_failed with reason="Aborted by user") so the next redesign_start opens a fresh row. Completed sessions cannot be restarted.

tools.name: redesign_select_pages
tools.description: Replace the selection set on a redesign session. Set pageIds to the array of builder_redesign_pages.id values the user chose. Passing an empty array clears the selection and the session falls back to status="pages_discovered".

tools.name: redesign_start
tools.description: Kick off page discovery for a redesign session. Calls Firecrawl /map on the source URL, persists each discovered page as builder_redesign_pages rows, and returns the list for the user to pick from. Refuses with 409 if redesign_homepage_approved_at is null. Returns {session:{id,status,total_pages}, pages:[{id,source_url,path,slug,title,screenshot_url}...]}.

tools.name: redesign_status
tools.description: Get the redesign session + all per-page rows in one call. Use as a polling endpoint while pages are mid-scrape or mid-promote. Without sessionId returns the most-recent session for the project (handy for "where did I leave off").

tools.name: room_async_jobs_await
tools.description: Convenience: poll for completed async jobs in a room. Shorthand for room_async_jobs_list with status='completed'. Use after firing delegate_to_department_background to gather results.

tools.name: room_async_jobs_list
tools.description: List orchestrator async-delegation jobs for a room (jobs fired by delegate_to_department_background). Filter by status / department.

tools.name: room_note_append
tools.description: Append to a room note (creates it if missing).

tools.name: room_note_delete
tools.description: Delete a room note by key. kind defaults to "note" (use "asset" or "resource" for those entry types).

tools.name: room_note_read
tools.description: Read one room note by key.

tools.name: room_note_write
tools.description: Write (replace) a room note.

tools.name: room_notes_list
tools.description: List notes scoped to an agent room (e.g. a marketing-strategy chat thread).

tools.name: room_rename
tools.description: Rename a room (orchestrator session). Truncated to 500 chars server-side. Use sparingly — only when the topic is stable enough that a title would help find it later.

tools.name: screenshot
tools.description: 🕷️ CRAWL4AI: Capture page screenshot (Firecrawl-backed)

tools.name: seo_add_competitor
tools.description: Add a competitor domain to an SEO tracking project (seo_competitor_analysis row). Needs project_id from seo_list_projects and competitor_domain (bare host like competitor.com; `domain` is accepted as an alias). Returns 201 { data: { id, project_id, competitor_domain, ...metric columns null } }; 409 when that domain is already tracked on the project. Adding a competitor stores the domain only: it does NOT fetch metrics or start any comparison. Fill the metric columns with seo_competitor_update after running seo_research action domain-overview, or compute gaps with seo_research action keyword-gap.

tools.name: seo_aeo_audit_get
tools.description: Read the LATEST persisted AEO audit results for a domain. No DataForSEO calls — pure DB read from seo_serp_features. Returns per-keyword AI-overview / featured-snippet / PAA presence + whether the domain is cited, plus ai_overview_references (top 20 per keyword: the sources the AI Overview actually cites, each {source, domain, url, title}, with ai_overview_reference_count for the uncapped total) — so 'who is AI citing instead of us' is answerable from stored history without paying for fresh probes. Same summary stats as seo_aeo_audit_run. `since` filters to only rows newer than that ISO date — handy for trend analysis.

tools.name: seo_aeo_audit_run
tools.description: Run an AEO (Answer Engine Optimization) audit for a domain. For each keyword, calls DataForSEO's organic SERP and parses the AI Overview, Featured Snippet, and People Also Ask blocks — records whether each feature is present AND whether the target domain is cited in them. PERSISTS every probe to seo_serp_features (append-only, so history works) and upserts seo_featured_snippets rows for keywords where a snippet exists. Returns a summary (readiness %, top opportunities) plus the per-keyword breakdown. Use this BEFORE recommending AEO changes so you have concrete data. Each keyword = 1 DataForSEO SERP call; cap at ~25 to control cost.

tools.name: seo_aeo_brand_audit
tools.description: Run the multi-provider LLM brand interrogation — asks several AI models about the brand and records how they answer, so you can see how the brand is represented in AI results. Requires a configured aeo_brand_profiles row (400 if none). Shares the SAME per-UTC-day audit budget the dashboard enforces, so it can refuse when the day is spent.

tools.name: seo_aeo_brand_audit_history
tools.description: Read the stored brand-audit history (aeo_brand_audits) — latest audit + up to `history` prior runs (default 12 ≈ a quarter of weekly sweeps, max 100), newest first. Pure DB read, no LLM spend — this is how you trend the core AEO KPI (overall_avg score movement, per-provider recognition/sentiment/share-of-voice dimensions in provider_scores, competitors_mentioned evidence, inaccuracies) without re-running the audit. Run a FRESH audit with seo_aeo_brand_audit (costs real LLM spend, budgeted per UTC day).

tools.name: seo_aeo_brand_profile_get
tools.description: Read the account's AEO brand profile (aeo_brand_profiles) — the audit subject config that gates the entire brand-audit engine: brand_name, domain, category, industry, region, and the competitor set that anchors share-of-voice scoring. Returns { profile: null } when the brand hasn't been configured yet — in that state seo_aeo_brand_audit 400s and the weekly brand-audit sweep cron skips the account, so create the profile with seo_aeo_brand_profile_upsert before any brand-audit work. One profile per account.

tools.name: seo_aeo_brand_profile_upsert
tools.description: Create or update the AEO brand profile — the required setup step for the brand-audit engine (seo_aeo_brand_audit 400s and the weekly sweep cron skips the account until this exists). Same field contract as the dashboard settings form. FULL-REPLACE semantics: brand_name, domain, and category are required on EVERY call (this is not a partial patch — read the current profile first with seo_aeo_brand_profile_get when editing). competitors may be omitted or empty — the first brand-audit run AI-seeds them from the engine's suggestions, and they stay editable here afterwards (max 10, each {name, domain?}).

tools.name: seo_aeo_rankings_sync
tools.description: Track keywords across AI engines. For each (keyword × search_engine) combination, ensures a website_rankings row exists (creates if missing, reuses if present), then queries DataForSEO's LLM Mentions API to populate the current citation position + ai_mentioned + mentions_count + ai_search_volume on each row. After this runs, the dashboard's AI ranking columns light up. Supported engines: • ai_overview — Google's generative SERP (most reliable AEO signal) • chatgpt — DataForSEO platform='chat_gpt' • perplexity — currently routed through 'google' (DataForSEO doesn't have a direct Perplexity platform yet) Each (keyword × engine) costs one DataForSEO LLM Mentions call. To create tracking rows without paying the per-keyword cost upfront, pass skip_sync=true; you can call seo_aeo_rankings_sync again later (or trigger sync via the existing ranking-sync cron) to populate them.

tools.name: seo_aeo_readiness
tools.description: Zero-cost AI-readiness check for a domain: llms.txt, robots.txt AI-crawler directives, homepage JSON-LD / meta / h1, and sitemap. Plain HTTPS fetches — spends nothing and persists nothing, so it is always safe to run first, before any credit-spending AEO audit.

tools.name: seo_ai_visibility
tools.description: How often the account's domains are cited by AI answer engines, aggregated from rank checks ALREADY STORED (no external call): per engine (chatgpt, perplexity, claude, gemini, ai_overview) tracked keywords, mentioned count, mention rate, average citation position and last check from website_rankings; a 30-day per-engine trend of mentions from website_ranking_history; serpFeatures (AI Overview presence per keyword and featured-snippet ownership written by the AEO audit); lastChecked; domains. Optional domain narrows to one target_domain. Returns { engines, trend, serpFeatures, lastChecked, domains }. GOTCHA: keywords created before the AI engines existed have NO AI lanes, so tracked 0 means 'not tracked', never 'not cited'; add lanes with seo_rankings_platforms_set (about $0.10 per keyword per engine per check). A lastChecked weeks old means the checks stopped (DataForSEO balance), not that visibility froze.

tools.name: seo_analytics_discover_properties
tools.description: List the GA4 properties a google_analytics connection's OAuth user can see (Analytics Admin accountSummaries), so the right one can be bound. Needs id from seo_connections_list (platform google_analytics). Returns { properties: [{ property_id: 'properties/<id>', label, account }], summary: { property_count } }; 400 when the connection has no refresh token yet (authorize first) or the token refresh fails; 502 on an Analytics Admin API error. Then bind with seo_connection_update { id, ga_property_id } which promotes the row to 'connected'; until a property is bound seo_ga4_report has nothing to query. Mirrors seo_gsc_discover_sites / seo_gbp_discover_locations. One live Google call, no metering.

tools.name: seo_audit_get
tools.description: Fetch one persisted site audit by audit_id OR task_id (both come back from seo_run_audit / seo_audit_start; seo_list_audits rows carry them as id and task_id). While the crawl is running the route checks DataForSEO and persists the progress, so polling this is how an audit completes: status (queued / processing / completed / failed), pages_crawled vs total_pages, crawl_progress, then on completion `results` = the stored audit payload { overall_health_score, crawled_pages, issues_found, errors, warnings, notices, issues[] (each with affected URLs), core_web_vitals }. Returns { data: { id, task_id, status, target_url, pages_crawled, total_pages, crawl_progress, started_at, completed_at, error_message, results } } plus `progress` while in progress; 404 when neither id is on this account; 402 when the DataForSEO cap is hit mid-poll; with DataForSEO unconfigured the stored row comes back with a warning. Poll every 30 to 60 seconds, not in a tight loop; a completed or failed row is served from the DB without a DataForSEO call.

tools.name: seo_audit_list
tools.description: Narrower-param alias of seo_list_audits (same route; this one has no domain or status filter). Lists the persisted site audits (site_audit_tasks) on the account, newest first, each row { id, task_id, target_url, status, pages_crawled, total_pages, crawl_progress, started_at, completed_at, error_message }. project_id (seo_list_projects) narrows to that project domain. Returns { data, pagination }. An empty list means no crawl was ever started, never a clean site; start one with seo_run_audit and poll seo_audit_get.

tools.name: seo_audit_start
tools.description: Same call as seo_run_audit: start a DataForSEO site crawl for an SEO tracking project and persist it as an audit row (site_audit_tasks). ONE crawl type, no audit_type. Needs project_id from seo_list_projects; target_url defaults to https://<project domain>; max_crawl_pages default 50, max 500 (each page metered). Returns 202 { data: { audit_id, task_id, target, status: 'queued', project_id, max_crawl_pages }, hint }; a `warning` with audit_id null means the crawl started but the row could not be saved (keep task_id). Poll seo_audit_get with audit_id or task_id every 30 to 60 seconds; a 50-page crawl completes in 1 to 5 minutes. The task_id is also the `target` for seo_research crawl actions (redirect-chains, duplicate-content, non-indexable, internal-links, keyword-density). 402 = DataForSEO balance or cap exhausted, 503 dataforseo_unconfigured = no credentials; neither means clean.

tools.name: seo_automated_report_delete
tools.description: Delete a scheduled client-report configuration. Needs report_id from seo_automated_reports. Returns { success: true }; 404 when the id is not on this account. Hard delete, no undo: the schedule stops, the public share link (public_token) stops resolving for the client, and generated report history attached to the row is no longer reachable. To pause instead, seo_automated_report_update { is_active: false } or { schedule: 'none' }. Confirm with the user before calling.

tools.name: seo_automated_report_get
tools.description: Fetch one scheduled client-report configuration (seo_automated_reports): report_name, report_type (marketing | social), domain, schedule (weekly | monthly | none), include_sections, delivery_method (email | link), delivery_config (recipients etc.), is_active, is_public, public_token, next_scheduled_at, last_generated_at.
