Needs report_id from seo_automated_reports (data[].id). Returns { data: <row> }; 404 when the id is not on this account. public_token is the share-link secret: do not paste it into chat or memory. Generating or sending the report itself is the seo_report_* family.

tools.name: seo_automated_report_update
tools.description: Update a scheduled client-report configuration: report_name, domain, schedule (weekly | monthly | none; a change recomputes next_scheduled_at from now, and 'none' clears it so the cron never fires), include_sections (validated against the report type's section vocabulary; unknown names are silently dropped), delivery_method (email | link), delivery_config, is_active, is_public. Needs report_id from seo_automated_reports; only the fields sent change and values outside the allowed vocabularies are ignored rather than rejected. Returns { data: <the updated row> }; 404 when the id is not on this account. is_public: true mints a public_token when the row has none; is_public: false on a MARKETING report REVOKES the token (the share link the client has dies), while a social report keeps its token so re-enabling restores the same link.

tools.name: seo_automated_reports
tools.description: List the scheduled client-report configurations on the account (seo_automated_reports: report_name, report_type 'marketing' | 'social', domain, schedule weekly | monthly | none, include_sections, delivery_method email | link, delivery_config, is_active, is_public, public_token, next_scheduled_at, last_generated_at), ordered by next_scheduled_at. Account-scoped, no project id: filter with domain (contains), is_active (STRING 'true' / 'false'), report_type, page, limit (max 100). Returns { data, pagination }. A row with schedule 'none' or is_active false never fires. Use the returned id for seo_automated_report_get / seo_automated_report_update / seo_automated_report_delete; generation and sending are the seo_report_* tools.

tools.name: seo_backlink_opportunities
tools.description: List the link-building opportunities stored for the account (seo_backlink_opportunities: target_domain, source_domain, source_type, domain_rating, domain_traffic, contact_email, contact_name, opportunity_score, difficulty_score, estimated_value, topical_relevance, status, notes, outreach_attempts, acquired_url), ordered by opportunity_score. Account-scoped, no project id: filter with domain (exact target_domain), status, source_type, min_score (opportunity_score >=), page, limit (max 100). Returns { data, pagination }. Rows get here only through seo_backlink_opportunity_create (or the dashboard); nothing discovers opportunities automatically, so an empty list means none were recorded. Find candidates with seo_research action link-gap or backlinks-competitors, then record the ones worth pursuing.

tools.name: seo_backlink_opportunity_create
tools.description: Record a link-building opportunity worth pursuing (seo_backlink_opportunities). Needs target_domain (your site), source_domain (the site that could link) and source_type (e.g. 'guest_post' | 'resource_page' | 'broken_link' | 'directory' | 'partner'); optional domain_rating, domain_traffic, contact_email, contact_name, opportunity_score, difficulty_score, estimated_value, topical_relevance, status (default 'new'), notes. Returns 201 { data: <row, outreach_attempts 0> }; 409 when that source_domain is already recorded for the target_domain on this account. This is a pipeline record, not discovery: find candidates with seo_research action link-gap / backlinks-competitors first. Contact details are stored in plain text; only record what the user has a legitimate basis to hold.

tools.name: seo_backlink_opportunity_delete
tools.description: Delete a link-building opportunity record. Needs opportunity_id from seo_backlink_opportunities. Returns { data: { deleted: true } }; 404 when the id is not on this account. Hard delete, no undo, and the outreach history stored on the row (attempts, dates, notes) goes with it; to keep the record set status 'rejected' with seo_backlink_opportunity_update instead. Confirm with the user before calling.

tools.name: seo_backlink_opportunity_get
tools.description: Fetch one link-building opportunity (seo_backlink_opportunities) with its pipeline fields: status, notes, contact_email, contact_name, social_profiles, outreach_attempts, last_outreach_at, acquired_at, acquired_url, acquired_anchor, scores. Needs opportunity_id from seo_backlink_opportunities (data[].id) or seo_backlink_opportunity_create. Returns { data: <row> }; 404 when the id is not on this account.

tools.name: seo_backlink_opportunity_update
tools.description: Move a link-building opportunity through the pipeline: status, notes, contact_email, contact_name, social_profiles, outreach_attempts, last_outreach_at, acquired_at, acquired_url, acquired_anchor, opportunity_score, difficulty_score, estimated_value, topical_relevance, domain_rating, domain_traffic. Needs opportunity_id from seo_backlink_opportunities; only the fields sent change. Returns { data: <the updated row> }; 404 when the id is not on this account. outreach_attempts is a plain counter you set, not incremented for you (read the row, add one); when a link lands set status 'acquired', acquired_at, acquired_url and acquired_anchor, and add it to the manual tracker with seo_backlink_tracker_add. target_domain, source_domain and source_type are fixed after create.

tools.name: seo_backlink_tracker_add
tools.description: Record a link you built or are pursuing in the manual link-building tracker (seo_tracked_backlinks). Needs url (the page that links, or will link, to you); optional title, target_url (your page), target_anchor, link_type (e.g. 'guest post' | 'directory' | 'citation' | 'partner'), status (published | unpublished, default published), date_published (ISO), page_authority, domain_authority, notes, project_id (a WEBSITE project id from sites_list; 404 when it is not on this account). Returns 201 { data: <row with website_projects { id, name }> }. This records your own claim; nothing verifies the link exists or is dofollow. Verify with fetch_url on the url, or seo_research action referring-domains, before reporting it as live.

tools.name: seo_backlink_tracker_delete
tools.description: Remove a row from the manual link-building tracker. Needs backlink_id from seo_backlink_tracker_list. Returns { data: { deleted: true } }; 404 when the id is not on this account. Hard delete of the record only, no undo; the link on the other site is of course untouched. Confirm with the user before calling.

tools.name: seo_backlink_tracker_get
tools.description: Fetch one manual link-building tracker row (seo_tracked_backlinks) with its website project { id, name }. Needs backlink_id from seo_backlink_tracker_list (data[].id) or seo_backlink_tracker_add. Returns { data: <row> }; 404 when the id is not on this account. Stored claim only; nothing here re-checks the link.

tools.name: seo_backlink_tracker_list
tools.description: List the MANUAL link-building tracker (seo_tracked_backlinks): links you built or are pursuing, entered by hand, each with url, title, target_url, target_anchor, link_type, status (published | unpublished), date_published, page_authority, domain_authority, notes and the website project it belongs to. Filter with project_id (a WEBSITE project id from sites_list, not the SEO tracking project), status, link_type (contains), search (url / title / target_url / anchor contains), page, limit (max 100). Returns { data, pagination }. Not DataForSEO data: for links Google's index actually shows use seo_research action referring-domains or backlinks_bulk_new_lost_backlinks. seo_new_lost_backlinks reads the same route.

tools.name: seo_backlink_tracker_update
tools.description: Update a manual link-building tracker row: url, title, target_url, target_anchor, link_type, status, date_published, page_authority, domain_authority, notes, project_id. Needs backlink_id from seo_backlink_tracker_list; only the fields sent change (project_id: null clears the project link). Returns { data: <the updated row> }; 404 when the id is not on this account. Typical use is flipping status from unpublished to published with a date_published once the link goes live, after verifying it with fetch_url.

tools.name: seo_backlinks_list
tools.description: Read the STORED backlink profile of an SEO tracking project (seo_backlink_profiles summary: total_backlinks, referring_domains, dofollow/nofollow, new/lost 30d, toxic_score, avg_domain_rating, link_velocity, last_updated) plus its stored individual backlinks (seo_backlinks: source_domain, source_url, anchor_text, domain_rating, is_dofollow, is_active), ordered by domain_rating. Needs project_id from seo_list_projects; filter with min_authority (domain_rating >=), search (source_domain or anchor contains), is_dofollow and is_active (STRING "true"/"false"), page, limit (max 100). Returns { data: { profile, backlinks }, pagination }; profile null and backlinks [] when nothing has been imported for the project. Nothing refreshes this table on a schedule: for live backlink data use seo_research action domain-backlinks / referring-domains or the backlinks_* vendor tools.

tools.name: seo_bing_backlinks
tools.description: Live Bing Webmaster GetLinkCounts: inbound-link COUNTS per page of one property (the pages of the site with the most links pointing at them), not a list of the linking pages themselves. site_url defaults to the Bing connection's site_url; limit caps the rows (default 100); 412 when no Bing connection with an API key exists. Returns Bing's raw payload. For individual referring pages, anchors and new/lost links use seo_research action referring-domains / backlinks-anchors or the backlinks_* vendor tools.

tools.name: seo_bing_crawl_stats
tools.description: Live Bing Webmaster GetCrawlStats: Bingbot's recent crawl activity for one property (pages crawled, crawl errors, blocked by robots, HTTP status buckets, per day). site_url defaults to the Bing connection's site_url; 412 when no Bing connection with an API key exists. Returns Bing's raw payload. Crawl errors here are Bing's view only; Google's index state is seo_gsc_inspect_url / seo_gsc_index_coverage. A 404 spike here after a redesign usually means missing redirects: check project_redirects_list.

tools.name: seo_bing_inspect_url
tools.description: Inspect one URL's crawl/index state in Bing (GetUrlInfo) — the GSC seo_gsc_inspect_url analog.

tools.name: seo_bing_keywords
tools.description: Live Bing Webmaster GetKeywordPerformance: per-keyword impressions, clicks and average position for one property, optionally scoped by country (default 'us') and language (default 'en-US'). site_url defaults to the Bing connection's site_url; 412 when no Bing connection with an API key exists. Returns Bing's raw payload. These are the keywords Bing reports performance for, not the queries traffic actually came from: that list is seo_bing_query_stats. Not comparable with GSC numbers; keep Bing and Google totals separate.

tools.name: seo_bing_list_sitemaps
tools.description: List the sitemaps and feeds registered for one Bing property (Bing Webmaster GetFeeds) with their type, submission date, last crawl and URL counts. site_url defaults to the Bing connection's site_url; 412 when no Bing connection with an API key exists. Returns Bing's raw payload. A sitemap missing here was never submitted to Bing even if Google has it; register it with seo_bing_submit_sitemap. Google's equivalent is seo_gsc_list_sitemaps.

tools.name: seo_bing_list_sites
tools.description: List the sites verified in this Bing Webmaster account (GetUserSites) — the GSC seo_gsc_list_sites analog. No site_url needed.

tools.name: seo_bing_pages
tools.description: Bing top pages for a property (GetPageStats). Bing's analog of seo_gsc_top_pages. Pair with seo_bing_query_stats to triangulate which queries drive which pages.

tools.name: seo_bing_period_comparison
tools.description: Compare two periods on Bing. Fetches the daily GetRankAndTrafficStats series once, then aggregates each window server-side: total clicks/impressions/CTR, impression-weighted avg position, daily rollups. Use for the same MoM / WoW / pre-vs-post-launch questions that seo_gsc_period_comparison answers, but for Bing traffic. Position deltas are signed Bing-style (lower = better; negative position_delta = improved). Limitations vs GSC: Bing's API has no dimensions param, so this is site-level only (no per-query/per-page diff). The daily_a + daily_b arrays let the agent reconstruct a trend chart, and seo_bing_query_stats / seo_bing_pages give the keyword / page detail if needed.

tools.name: seo_bing_query_stats
tools.description: Bing top user search queries for a property (GetQueryStats). Different from seo_bing_keywords (which is keyword-performance for tracked terms) — query_stats returns the queries Bing's traffic actually came from. Bing's analog of seo_gsc_search_queries.

tools.name: seo_bing_stats
tools.description: Live Bing Webmaster GetRankAndTrafficStats: the daily series of impressions, clicks and average impression / click position for one property. site_url defaults to the Bing connection's own site_url (seo_connections_list, platform bing_webmaster); 412 when the account has no Bing connection with an API key. Returns Bing's raw payload (a { d: [...] } list of daily rows, dates as /Date(ms)/ strings). Site-level only: Bing's API has no query or page dimension here (seo_bing_query_stats / seo_bing_pages for those). Bing keeps roughly 6 months of daily history.

tools.name: seo_bing_submit_sitemap
tools.description: Register a sitemap with Bing Webmaster (SubmitSiteMap) so Bing crawls it on its own schedule. Needs sitemap_url (full URL, e.g. https://example.com/sitemap.xml); site_url defaults to the Bing connection's site_url; 412 when no Bing connection with an API key exists. Returns Bing's raw acknowledgement. Bing does not validate the sitemap synchronously: a 200 here says the URL was accepted, not that it parsed; check seo_bing_list_sitemaps a day later for its status. The sitemap must be live first (seo_generate_sitemap, deploy_site, then fetch_url to confirm).

tools.name: seo_bing_submit_url
tools.description: Ask Bing to (re)crawl one URL now: Bing Webmaster SubmitUrl. Needs url (the full page URL); site_url defaults to the Bing connection's site_url and the url must belong to that property; 412 when no Bing connection with an API key exists. Returns Bing's raw acknowledgement (an empty object on success). Bing rate-limits submissions per site per day (the quota is in the Bing dashboard), so submit changed pages, not the whole site; for bulk use seo_bing_submit_sitemap. Submission is not indexing: confirm later with seo_bing_inspect_url.

tools.name: seo_cannibalization
tools.description: Detected keyword cannibalization (multiple pages competing for the same query). Data source: computed every Sunday by the seo-analysis-sweep cron — queries where 2+ pages of the same domain each drew 50+ impressions (200+ combined) in the last 28 archived days. Empty (with a note) until GSC is connected and the first weekly run completes.

tools.name: seo_citations_audit
tools.description: Run a citation audit for a Google Business Profile connection: pulls the canonical NAP (name/address/phone/website) from the synced GBP listing, runs ONE DataForSEO Business Listings search for the business's public listings footprint, diffs every listing attributable to the business (primary + duplicates) for NAP consistency (normalized: phone digits-only, address tokenized with abbreviation canonicalization, name fuzzy), and checks a fixed major-directory list (Google, Yelp, Facebook, Bing Places, Apple Maps, BBB, Yellow Pages, Foursquare, Tripadvisor where category-relevant) using in-app signals. Returns directories_found / consistent / inconsistent (with per-field their_value vs expected) / missing_major (entries carry a basis field — 'no_signal' means presence is UNVERIFIED, not confirmed absent) and persists the snapshot. SPENDS DataForSEO CREDITS: one Business Listings search per run, metered under the account's monthly SEO research cap (same read-spend class as seo_research — no confirm step). A 24h server-side cooldown returns 429 with retry_at plus the stored audit. AUDIT ONLY — this never writes to any directory (citation submission is not offered). Get connection_id from seo_connections_list (platform google_business_profile). Read the stored snapshot for free with seo_citations_get.

tools.name: seo_citations_get
tools.description: Read the STORED citation-audit snapshot for a GBP connection (canonical NAP, directories_found/consistent/inconsistent with per-field diffs, missing_major with per-directory basis, audited_at). Free, DB-only — never calls DataForSEO. Omit connection_id for a row per active GBP connection (audit: null = never audited; run seo_citations_audit to compute one).

tools.name: seo_competitor_changes
tools.description: Read the competitor activity feed stored in seo_competitor_changes (change_type, description, urgency, requires_response, our_domain, competitor_domain, change_detected_at), newest first. Account-scoped, no project id: filter with domain (exact our_domain), competitor_domain (exact), urgency, requires_response (STRING 'true' only), from_date (change_detected_at >= ISO date), page, limit (max 100). Returns { data, pagination }. Rows are written by the weekly analysis sweep for accounts with a connected data source; an empty feed means nothing was recorded, not that competitors were idle. For a live look use seo_research action competitors or ranked-keywords on the competitor domain.

tools.name: seo_competitor_delete
tools.description: Remove a competitor row from an SEO tracking project. Needs competitor_id from seo_list_competitors. Returns { data: { deleted: true } }; 404 when the row belongs to another account. Hard delete of the row and its stored metrics, no undo; the competitor_changes feed rows for that domain are account-scoped and stay. Confirm with the user before calling.

tools.name: seo_competitor_get
tools.description: Fetch one tracked competitor row (seo_competitor_analysis: competitor_domain, domain_rating, organic_keywords, organic_traffic, shared_keywords, keyword_gap, backlinks_count, referring_domains, competition_level, market_share, trend_direction, last_analyzed). Needs competitor_id from seo_list_competitors (data[].id). Returns { data: <row> }; 404 when the row belongs to another account. The metrics are stored values, last written by seo_add_competitor or seo_competitor_update; nothing refreshes them on a schedule.

tools.name: seo_competitor_update
tools.description: Write metric columns onto a tracked competitor row after researching it: competitor_domain, domain_rating, organic_keywords, organic_traffic, shared_keywords, keyword_gap, backlinks_count, referring_domains, competition_level, market_share, trend_direction. Needs competitor_id from seo_list_competitors; only the fields sent change and last_analyzed is stamped now. Returns { data: <the updated row> }; 404 when the row belongs to another account. Source the numbers from seo_research action domain-overview / competitors / keyword-gap and state the date in your report; this tool records, it does not fetch.

tools.name: seo_competitors_list
tools.description: Narrower-param alias of seo_list_competitors (same route; this one has no page/limit). Lists the competitor domains tracked on an SEO tracking project with their stored metric columns. Needs project_id from seo_list_projects. Returns { data, pagination }. Metrics are whatever seo_add_competitor / seo_competitor_update last wrote; nothing refreshes them.

tools.name: seo_connection_create
tools.description: Create an SEO data-source connection (BYOK). BING WEBMASTER is the simplest — just { platform: 'bing_webmaster', site_url, api_key } (the key from bing.com/webmasters -> Settings -> API access; no OAuth). GOOGLE SEARCH CONSOLE: { platform: 'google_search_console', site_url, client_id, client_secret, refresh_token } (scope https://www.googleapis.com/auth/webmasters — the FULL scope, not .readonly, or sitemap submit/delete will 403). GOOGLE BUSINESS PROFILE: { platform: 'google_business_profile', client_id, client_secret, refresh_token } then set gbp_account_id/gbp_location_id via seo_connection_update. After create, call the connection's test/sync (seo_sync) to verify. For a Bing Webmaster site not yet in the tool, the user can one-click 'Import from Google Search Console' at bing.com/webmasters first.

tools.name: seo_connection_delete
tools.description: Soft-delete an SEO connection (sets is_active=false). Preserves the row for audit history; downstream tools that filter by is_active will stop finding it. To clean up a phantom or stuck pending row created during OAuth setup.

tools.name: seo_connection_get
tools.description: Fetch one SEO data-source connection (seo_connections) without its credentials: id, platform (google_search_console | bing_webmaster | google_business_profile | google_analytics), display_name, site_url, gbp_account_id, gbp_location_id, ga_property_id, is_active, connection_status (pending | connected | error), last_synced_at, last_error, settings, gtm_container_path / gtm_container_public_id (the Tag Manager pin), created_at. Needs id from seo_connections_list. Returns { data: {...} }; 404 when the id is not on this account. connection_status tracks AUTH only: a 'connected' row can have stopped receiving data weeks ago, so read seo_connections_health for freshness. Credentials are never returned.

tools.name: seo_connection_test
tools.description: Probe an SEO connection's credentials with one lightweight call to the platform (GSC: refresh the token and list sites; Bing: GetUserSites; GBP: list accounts; GA4: list property summaries). Needs id from seo_connections_list. Returns { success, message, platform, details } where details carries the sites / accounts / properties the credential can reach and message warns when the configured site_url or ga_property_id is not among them. WRITES connection_status: success sets 'connected' and clears last_error; ANY failure sets 'error' and stores the message, and the 6-hour sync cron only picks up rows whose status is 'connected', so a TRANSIENT failure (Google 5xx, a timeout, an expired token that refreshes on the next try) PAUSES that connection's data pull until a later test passes or seo_connection_update resets it. Do not run this in a loop or as a routine health check; use seo_connections_health (read-only) for that and call this only when you intend to act on the result. Platforms with no probe are left unchanged (success false, message says so).

tools.name: seo_connection_update
tools.description: Update an SEO connection — set the chosen site_url (GSC), gbp_account_id + gbp_location_id (GBP), ga_property_id (GA4, from seo_analytics_discover_properties), display_name, or is_active. When the final identifier lands (site_url for GSC; both gbp_account_id + gbp_location_id for GBP; ga_property_id for GA4), connection_status auto-flips from 'pending' to 'connected' so the sync route picks it up. Credentials reset status to 'pending' on update.

tools.name: seo_connections_health
tools.description: Read-only data-freshness verdict for every active SEO connection on the account, driven by the NEWEST DATA ROW each connection has produced rather than by connection_status (which only tracks auth): healthy (data within 3 days; GBP 7, its API backfills late), stale (connected but data older than that), error (connection_status 'error', last_error set), needs_setup (authorized but never configured, e.g. GBP with no location picked), pending (never synced). Connections the operator marked not-applicable are omitted. No arguments. Returns { connections: [{ id, platform, display_name, connection_status, last_error, last_synced_at, data_through, days_stale, health }], summary: { healthy, stale, error, needs_setup, pending } }. Writes nothing, unlike seo_connection_test. A stale GSC row is the usual cause of 'the report shows zero'; the fix is seo_sync (or seo_connection_test then seo_sync when status is error).

tools.name: seo_connections_list
tools.description: List connected SEO data sources (DataForSEO/GSC/Bing Webmaster/Google Business Profile).

tools.name: seo_content_decay
tools.description: Pages with declining organic traffic (good refresh candidates). Data source: computed every Sunday by the seo-analysis-sweep cron from the permanent Search Console query/page archive (last 28 archived days vs the prior 28; floors 100 impressions + 5 clicks). Empty (with a note) until GSC is connected and the first weekly run completes; rows a human re-statused are preserved across re-runs.

tools.name: seo_content_gaps
tools.description: Read the stored content-gap rows (seo_content_gaps) for an SEO tracking project, ordered by priority_score - one row per analyzed competitor with { competitor_domain, missing_keywords, content_opportunities, traffic_potential, priority_score, analysis_date }. Needs project_id from seo_list_projects; page and limit (max 50) paginate. Returns { data: [...], pagination }. Rows are written by seo_content_gaps_compute: this is the compute-then-read pair, so run the compute first and read here. An empty list means no compute has run for this project yet, not that there are no gaps. For a one-off live look without persisting, seo_research action keyword-gap still works.

tools.name: seo_content_gaps_compute
tools.description: Compute and PERSIST content gaps for an SEO tracking project: runs the DataForSEO Labs domain-intersection of a competitor's domain against the project's domain (intersections:false, so only keywords the COMPETITOR ranks for - true gaps) and writes one seo_content_gaps row per competitor ({ competitor_domain, missing_keywords, content_opportunities, traffic_potential, priority_score, analysis_date }), replacing that competitor's previous row for the project. Needs project_id from seo_list_projects. competitor_domain (bare host like competitor.com) analyzes just that one; omit it to analyze the competitors tracked via seo_add_competitor - the top 3 by organic traffic per call, the rest listed in meta.skipped_competitors (call again with each skipped domain); 400 when neither yields a competitor. limit caps keywords stored per competitor (10-300, default 100). Location is fixed to the US (location_code 2840); language follows the project's target_language. SPENDS DataForSEO credits (one Labs intersection call per competitor, metered against the monthly SEO research cap, no confirm step): 402 = research cap reached, 503 = DataForSEO credentials not configured on the server, 502 = the DFS call failed; none of those mean 'no gaps'. Returns { data: [the new rows], meta }. Read the persisted rows back with seo_content_gaps (compute-then-read).

tools.name: seo_core_web_vitals
tools.description: Core Web Vitals for any URL, field + lab in one call. FIELD = Chrome UX Report real-user p75 LCP/INP/CLS — the numbers Google actually ranks on (GSC's CWV report has no API; this is the only programmatic source). LAB = PageSpeed Insights Lighthouse: performance/accessibility/best-practices/SEO scores plus the top improvement opportunities ranked by estimated savings. Platform API key, no per-account connection — works on any URL including competitors. If field data 404s for an exact URL (thin traffic), retry with origin= for site-level data. include=field skips the slow (~20-60s) Lighthouse run.

tools.name: seo_create_project
tools.description: Create a new SEO project to track a domain with target country/language

tools.name: seo_cro_audit
tools.description: Heuristic conversion-rate (CRO) audit of ONE landing page — v1 is audit only, NOT experiment tracking (run experiments as pm_tasks for now). Fetches the page (SSRF-guarded), then scores five sections 0-100: speed (CrUX real-user p75 + PageSpeed lab), clarity (H1/title/meta, image alt coverage), friction (form field counts, labels, a conversion path existing at all), trust (testimonials, reviews, guarantees, badges, social-proof numbers, visible phone), and cta (action-verb copy + an above-fold heuristic: header/hero or first 35% of the page). Returns named findings each carrying {issue, why_it_costs_conversions, fix} plus a quick_wins shortlist of cheap edits. Pure read: nothing persisted, no credit spend, works on any public URL including competitors. If the web-signals key is missing only the speed section degrades — the rest still audits.

tools.name: seo_deliverable_delete
tools.description: Permanently delete a saved SEO deliverable. Needs id from seo_deliverable_list. Returns { data: { deleted: true } }; 404 when the id is not on this account. Hard delete with no undo and no version history; if the document might be wanted again set status to 'archived' with seo_deliverable_update instead.

tools.name: seo_deliverable_get
tools.description: Fetch one saved SEO deliverable (seo_deliverables: a report, audit write-up, keyword plan or strategy document the workspace keeps) with its full content object, recommendations, target_keywords, tags, status and timestamps. Needs id from seo_deliverable_list or seo_deliverable_save. Returns { data: { id, title, slug, deliverable_type, status, target_domain, target_keywords, summary, content, recommendations, tags, created_at, updated_at } }; 404 when the id is not on this account. content is free-form JSON written by whoever saved it; do not assume a schema across deliverable types.

tools.name: seo_deliverable_list
tools.description: List saved SEO deliverables (audits, content briefs, strategy docs, etc.).

tools.name: seo_deliverable_save
tools.description: Create a saved SEO deliverable (seo_deliverables) so work done in chat survives the session and shows in the dashboard. Needs title, slug (unique per account, e.g. 'ranking-report-2026-05') and deliverable_type; optional status (default 'draft'), target_domain, target_keywords[], summary, content (object), recommendations[], tags[]. Returns 201 { data, existed: false }. Idempotent on slug: when a deliverable with that slug already exists the call returns 200 { data: <the existing row>, existed: true } WITHOUT changing it, so update it with seo_deliverable_update instead of re-saving. Deliverables are documents, not the sheet: rows for the workspace sheet go through seo_sheet_add_rows.

tools.name: seo_deliverable_update
tools.description: Update fields on a saved SEO deliverable. Needs id (seo_deliverable_list / seo_deliverable_save) plus at least one of title, slug, deliverable_type, status, target_domain, target_keywords, summary, content, recommendations, tags (400 when none is given). Returns { data: <the updated row> }; 404 when the id is not on this account. Every field is a full replacement, so send the complete content object or recommendations array, not a patch of it; read the current row with seo_deliverable_get first. Changing slug to one another deliverable uses fails on the unique key.

tools.name: seo_eeat_scores
tools.description: E-E-A-T (Experience/Expertise/Authority/Trust) scores for the account's top Search Console pages (up to 10/account, re-scored monthly by the Sunday seo-analysis-sweep). Pages are fetched live and LLM-scored (account-metered, budget-gated) with a static-signal fallback — check *_signals.method ('llm' vs 'heuristic_only') for scoring depth. competitor_scores is not computed. Empty (with a note) until GSC is connected and the first sweep completes.

tools.name: seo_entity_check
tools.description: AEO entity audit via the Google Knowledge Graph: does this brand/person/topic resolve to a KG entity? Returns kg_id, canonical name, types, description and resultScore per match. A brand with no entity is a string, not a citable source — that absence is itself an audit finding. Use kg_id + official_url in schema.org sameAs/mainEntityOfPage markup, and compare resultScore against competitors as an entity-strength signal. Platform API key, works for any query.

tools.name: seo_featured_snippets
tools.description: Featured-snippet opportunities (keywords where the snippet is winnable).

tools.name: seo_ga4_admin_scopes
tools.description: Does this Google Analytics connection's token carry the analytics.edit scope? Read-only preflight — call it before a write wave to learn the customer must reconnect, instead of discovering it from a 403 halfway through a change.

tools.name: seo_ga4_conversion_audit
tools.description: START HERE for GA4 conversions. Which key events exist, which URL rules feed them, and which recorded NOTHING in the window. A key event with zero events is a Google Ads conversion action (origin GOOGLE_ANALYTICS) reporting zero with no error shown anywhere — the Ads side looks configured and simply never fires. Many Ads conversions ARE imported GA4 key events, so this is where an 'Ads conversion stopped recording' investigation starts.

tools.name: seo_ga4_data_streams_list
tools.description: List a GA4 property's data streams (name, type, defaultUri, measurementId). Event create rules hang off a STREAM, not the property, so this is the lookup that makes every rule action possible.

tools.name: seo_ga4_event_create_rule_create
tools.description: TURN A URL INTO A CONVERSION. GA4 cannot mark 'a page_view whose URL contains /thank-you' as a conversion — only a whole event name — so the chain is: this rule creates a distinct event, then seo_ga4_key_event_create marks it, then Google Ads imports it. TWO TRAPS THIS TOOL HANDLES FOR YOU. GA4 has NO page_path parameter: the URL lives in page_location, which is the FULL url including host and any ?utm_ query string — so EQUALS never matches a bare path, and CONTAINS is the right default. And a rule with no event_name condition fires on nearly EVERY event GA4 collects; this pins the source event automatically. GA4 never backfills, so a new rule starts at zero. v1alpha, and rules hang off a DATA STREAM, not the property.

tools.name: seo_ga4_event_create_rule_delete
tools.description: DESTRUCTIVE AND IRREVERSIBLE. GA4 stops creating the destination event entirely, so any key event on that name — and any Google Ads conversion imported from it — records nothing from that moment on, with no error anywhere. TWO-STEP CONFIRM: the first call does NOT delete; it returns requires_confirm with a preview and issues no write. Repeat with confirm: true (strict boolean). v1alpha.

tools.name: seo_ga4_event_create_rule_update
tools.description: Change a GA4 event create rule's destination event, conditions, parameter copying or mutations. conditions is a REPEATED field — a patch REPLACES the whole list, it does not append, so send every condition you want to keep. Renaming the destination event leaves any key event on the OLD name receiving nothing, silently flatlining its imported Google Ads conversion. v1alpha. TWO-STEP CONFIRM, because unlike GTM (where a write is a draft that serves nothing until publish) a GA4 change is LIVE ON RETURN and propagates into every Google Ads conversion imported from it. The first call writes nothing and returns a preview naming each field's current value, new value and consequence. Repeat with confirm: true.

tools.name: seo_ga4_event_create_rules_list
tools.description: List GA4 event create rules — the URL-driven rules that turn a thank-you-page URL into a distinct event. They live on a DATA STREAM (properties/{p}/dataStreams/{s}/eventCreateRules), NOT the property, and the resource exists only in Admin API v1alpha, so it can change without notice. Sweeps every stream unless data_stream is given.

tools.name: seo_ga4_key_event_create
tools.description: Mark a GA4 event as a key event (a conversion). Google Ads conversion actions imported from GA4 read this. GA4 ACCEPTS A KEY EVENT FOR AN EVENT NAME IT HAS NEVER RECEIVED, and it then records nothing forever with no error — confirm the event actually arrives with seo_ga4_conversion_audit. If the conversion is a page URL rather than an existing event, create the event first with seo_ga4_event_create_rule_create. counting_method matters: ONCE_PER_SESSION for lead forms (a reloaded thank-you page counts once), ONCE_PER_EVENT for purchases. default_value and default_currency must be sent TOGETHER — GA4 rejects a value with no currency. Needs the analytics.edit scope; a connection authorized before it was requested must reconnect.

tools.name: seo_ga4_key_event_delete
tools.description: DESTRUCTIVE AND IRREVERSIBLE. Un-marks a GA4 event as a conversion. Any Google Ads conversion action imported from it stops recording immediately and SILENTLY — the Ads conversion action keeps existing and flatlines, and if it sits in a bidding goal, Smart Bidding loses that signal. TWO-STEP CONFIRM: the first call does NOT delete — it returns requires_confirm with a preview and issues no write at all. Repeat the identical call with confirm: true (a strict boolean; the string 'true' only previews).

tools.name: seo_ga4_key_event_update
tools.description: Change a GA4 key event's counting method and/or default value. eventName is IMMUTABLE — renaming means create + delete. Both changes propagate AUTOMATICALLY to Google Ads conversions imported from this key event, shifting reported volume or value without anyone touching Google Ads, which moves CPA and forces Smart Bidding to relearn. Not retroactive. The response names the consequence. TWO-STEP CONFIRM, because unlike GTM (where a write is a draft that serves nothing until publish) a GA4 change is LIVE ON RETURN and propagates into every Google Ads conversion imported from it. The first call writes nothing and returns a preview naming each field's current value, new value and consequence. Repeat with confirm: true.

tools.name: seo_ga4_key_events_list
tools.description: List GA4 key events (the conversions) with countingMethod and defaultValue — the two settings that make an imported Google Ads conversion wrong. GA4 Admin API v1beta properties/{p}/keyEvents. (conversionEvents is the deprecated name for the same thing.)

tools.name: seo_ga4_report
tools.description: Pull NUMBERS from a client's GA4 property — one Google Analytics Data API runReport. Every other seo_ga4_* tool is Admin API configuration (key events, streams, rules); this is the only one that returns sessions, landing pages, revenue. The GA4 PROPERTY ALWAYS COMES FROM THE CONNECTION ROW (seo_connections.ga_property_id) — there is no property input; a connection whose property is not the one you want cannot be redirected. Quickest path is a preset (ONE param): channel_sessions (sessionDefaultChannelGroup x sessions/engagedSessions/keyEvents), landing_pages (landingPage x sessions/keyEvents/engagementRate), ecommerce_revenue (date x purchaseRevenue/transactions). Explicit dimensions/metrics override the matching half of a preset, so preset 'ecommerce_revenue' + dimensions ['itemName'] is revenue by product (then use metrics ['itemRevenue','itemsPurchased'] — purchaseRevenue is order-scoped). Without a preset, pass dimensions (0-9) and metrics (1-10). Names are CASE SENSITIVE GA4 Data API names and are checked against a shape regex AND an allowlist before anything reaches Google; an unknown name is a 400 naming the offender and the response carries allowed_dimensions / allowed_metrics. Custom definitions use customEvent: / customUser: / customItem: prefixes. keyEvents is the current name for what GA4 called conversions (both accepted). dimension_filter is a GA4 FilterExpression ({ filter: { fieldName, stringFilter|inListFilter|numericFilter|betweenFilter } } or andGroup/orGroup/notExpression) rebuilt from known keys only — an unknown key is refused, never silently dropped. Dates default to the last 30 COMPLETE days ending yesterday (GA4 only serves complete days); a date_to of today is accepted with a warning that the last row is partial. limit 1-1000, default 100; total_row_count is Google's count BEFORE the limit and totals cover every matched row, so a truncated report says so. GOOGLE'S ERRORS COME BACK VERBATIM AND ARE NOT RETRIED: a 429 is the property's hourly Data API token quota and the full Google message plus the parsed google_error object are returned as-is — retrying inside the hour only burns the rest of it. property_quota in every success shows tokens consumed/remaining. Warnings flag thresholding (rows withheld for privacy, so rows do not sum to totals), '(other)' row folding, sampling, and zero-row results (a property that never sent purchase events returns zero rows, not an error). Metric values are numbers; engagementRate is a 0-1 ratio.

tools.name: seo_gbp_attributes
tools.description: Location attributes for a GBP connection, in one round-trip: `current` (attributes actually set), `available` (the full catalog Google offers for the location's category), and `audit` (completeness summary + the missing list). Unset attributes are invisible to Google's filtered local searches ('wheelchair accessible', 'outdoor seating') — filling them is usually the cheapest local-visibility win. Live Google call. Get connection_id from seo_connections_list (platform google_business_profile). Apply changes with seo_gbp_attributes_update.

tools.name: seo_gbp_attributes_update
tools.description: Patch location attributes on a GBP connection. Changes publish DIRECTLY to the client's live listing — they alter how the business appears in Google's filtered local searches. TWO-STEP CONFIRM: the first call (without confirm) does NOT apply — it returns a preview (attribute names + count, connection name) with requires_confirm: true. Repeat the IDENTICAL call with confirm: true to apply. Each entry: { name: 'attributes/<id>', values?: [...], repeatedEnumValue?: {...}, uriValues?: [...] } per the Business Information Attributes resource — only the named attributes change (attributeMask derives from them). Discover attribute ids + gaps with seo_gbp_attributes (its audit.missing list). Get connection_id from seo_connections_list (platform google_business_profile).

tools.name: seo_gbp_discover_locations
tools.description: List Google Business Profile accounts + locations accessible to a connection. Returns an 'accounts' array; each account has a 'locations' array with location_id (resource name) + location_title. After picking, call seo_connection_update with both gbp_account_id AND gbp_location_id — status auto-flips to 'connected' once both are set.

tools.name: seo_gbp_insights
tools.description: Daily Google Business Profile insights: website clicks, call clicks, direction requests, mobile/desktop impressions on Maps vs Search.

tools.name: seo_gbp_listing
tools.description: Full GBP listing snapshot: Listing Score with per-field breakdown, NAP block, verification + duplicate status, and score history. Reads the synced DB snapshot (no live Google call — the 6h sync cron keeps it warm). Get connection_id from seo_connections_list; omit it to return a row per active GBP connection (needs_setup connections return state-only rows).

tools.name: seo_gbp_location
tools.description: Live Business Information read for a GBP connection's location: title, phone, categories, website, address, hours, service area, open status, place metadata. Also refreshes the cached listing snapshot. Get connection_id from seo_connections_list (platform google_business_profile). Edit the core listing fields (NAP / hours / categories / description / website) with seo_gbp_location_update.

tools.name: seo_gbp_location_update
tools.description: Edit the core Google Business Profile listing fields — the NAP/hours/categories lane: title (business name), phoneNumbers, profile (description), regularHours, specialHours, categories, websiteUri, storefrontAddress. Changes publish DIRECTLY to the client's live listing, and name/address/category edits can trigger Google re-verification. TWO-STEP CONFIRM: the first call (without confirm) does NOT apply — it returns a preview (the fields + values being changed, the connection name, the cached listing title) with requires_confirm: true. Repeat the IDENTICAL call with confirm: true to apply. Only the fields present in `updates` change (the PATCH updateMask derives from them); unknown fields are rejected with a 400. Field shapes follow Google's Business Information API Location resource: title and websiteUri are strings; phoneNumbers = { primaryPhone, additionalPhones? }; profile = { description }; regularHours = { periods: [{ openDay, openTime: { hours, minutes? }, closeDay, closeTime }] }; specialHours = { specialHourPeriods: [...] }; categories = { primaryCategory: { name: 'categories/gcid:...' }, additionalCategories? }; storefrontAddress = a postalAddress object. Read current values first with seo_gbp_location. Get connection_id from seo_connections_list (platform google_business_profile). For attribute toggles use seo_gbp_attributes_update instead.

tools.name: seo_gbp_media
tools.description: The GBP location's public photo gallery (live read, no DB cache): each item's media_id (feed it to seo_gbp_media_delete), category (COVER / PROFILE / LOGO / EXTERIOR / INTERIOR / PRODUCT / AT_WORK / FOOD_AND_DRINK / MENU / COMMON_AREA / ROOMS / TEAMS / ADDITIONAL), format, googleUrl/thumbnail, dimensions, view count — plus total_media_item_count. Get connection_id from seo_connections_list (platform google_business_profile). Add photos with seo_gbp_media_add.

tools.name: seo_gbp_media_add
tools.description: Add a PHOTO to the GBP location's gallery from a public https URL. The photo publishes PUBLICLY on the client's live listing (Google fetches it from source_url). Categories COVER / PROFILE / LOGO REPLACE the listing's primary imagery instead of appending to the gallery — use them deliberately. TWO-STEP CONFIRM: the first call (without confirm) does NOT publish — it returns a preview (category, source_url, media_format, whether primary imagery is replaced) with requires_confirm: true; URL and category validation run at this step, so a bad input fails before confirm. Repeat the IDENTICAL call with confirm: true to publish. source_url must be https and resolve to a public host; videos are rejected (photo-only). Get connection_id from seo_connections_list (platform google_business_profile).

tools.name: seo_gbp_media_delete
tools.description: Permanently remove one media item from the GBP location's live public gallery (deleting a COVER / PROFILE / LOGO item removes the listing's primary imagery). TWO-STEP CONFIRM: the first call (without confirm) does NOT delete — it fetches the live item and returns a preview (category, format, googleUrl/thumbnail, create time, view count) with requires_confirm: true, so you see exactly what is being removed; a bad media_id fails at this step. Repeat the IDENTICAL call with confirm: true to delete. Get connection_id from seo_connections_list (platform google_business_profile); get media_id from seo_gbp_media.

tools.name: seo_gbp_overview
tools.description: Cached GBP dashboard overview for one connection: insights totals + daily trend (last `days`, default 30), review stats (count / average rating / unreplied count), and the cached listing snapshot. DB-only — no live Google call. Get connection_id from seo_connections_list (platform google_business_profile).

tools.name: seo_gbp_posts
tools.description: Google Business Profile posts (localPosts) for one GBP connection, from the seo_gbp_posts cache: post_name, post_id, topic_type (STANDARD | EVENT | OFFER), summary, state (LIVE | REJECTED | PROCESSING), search_url, media, cta_type, cta_url, event, offer, create_time, update_time, newest first. Needs connection_id from seo_connections_list (platform google_business_profile). refresh '1' (or 'true') pulls the live list from Google first and upserts the cache (one GBP API call, quota-limited: once per session, never per read); limit caps the rows (default 90, max 500). Returns { data: { posts: [...], refreshed, connection_id, display_name } }; 400 without connection_id, 404 when it is not a GBP connection on this account. A post missing without refresh means the cache is behind, not that Google removed it. Publishing a new post goes through social_create_post with platform google_business_profile, not through this tool.

tools.name: seo_gbp_review_reply
tools.description: Publish the business-owner reply on a Google Business Profile review. The reply POSTS PUBLICLY on the client's live listing (and replaces any existing owner reply). Max 4096 characters. TWO-STEP CONFIRM: the first call (without confirm) does NOT publish — it returns a preview (the reply text + length, the review being replied to, the connection name) with requires_confirm: true. Repeat the IDENTICAL call with confirm: true to publish. Get connection_id from seo_connections_list (platform google_business_profile); get review_id from seo_gbp_reviews. Remove a reply with seo_gbp_review_reply_delete. NOTE: GBP POSTS (What's New / offers / events) deliberately have NO direct tool in this lane — publish them via the social lane: social_create_post with platform google_business_profile (goes through the approval queue).

tools.name: seo_gbp_review_reply_delete
tools.description: Permanently remove the public business-owner reply from a GBP review on the client's live listing. TWO-STEP CONFIRM: the first call (without confirm) does NOT delete — it returns a preview (the existing reply, the review) with requires_confirm: true. Repeat the IDENTICAL call with confirm: true to delete. Get connection_id from seo_connections_list (platform google_business_profile); get review_id from seo_gbp_reviews.

tools.name: seo_gbp_reviews
tools.description: Google Business Profile reviews from the synced seo_gbp_reviews cache (filled by seo_sync and the 6-hour cron, not fetched live here), newest first: reviewer, rating, comment, review_time, and the existing reply text and time when one was posted. Optional connection_id (seo_connections_list, platform google_business_profile) scopes to one location; min_rating / max_rating (1 to 5) filter; limit default 90, max 500. Returns { data: rows }. A review missing here means the cache is behind (check last_synced_at in seo_connections_health, then seo_sync), not that it was deleted. Reply with seo_gbp_review_reply (two-step, publishes publicly).

tools.name: seo_gbp_services
tools.description: The GBP location's service menu (live Business Information read): serviceItems — structured services (Google-defined serviceTypeId for the category) and free-form services (merchant-defined label under a category), each optionally priced — plus title/categories context for picking valid category ids. Services show publicly on the listing and feed Google's 'services' local-search filters. Get connection_id from seo_connections_list (platform google_business_profile). Edit with seo_gbp_services_update.

tools.name: seo_gbp_services_update
tools.description: Replace the GBP location's service menu. This REPLACES the ENTIRE service list on the client's live listing — every current service missing from service_items is REMOVED, and an empty array removes ALL services. The menu publishes publicly. TWO-STEP CONFIRM: the first call (without confirm) does NOT apply — it returns a live diff summary (current_count / new_count / added / removed / kept service names) with requires_confirm: true. Repeat the IDENTICAL call with confirm: true to apply. Each item has EXACTLY ONE of structuredServiceItem ({ serviceTypeId, description? } — serviceTypeId comes from the category's Google-defined service types) or freeFormServiceItem ({ category: 'gcid:...', label: { displayName, description?, languageCode? } }), plus optional price ({ currencyCode, units?, nanos? }). Read the current list first with seo_gbp_services (it also returns the location's categories for free-form category ids). Get connection_id from seo_connections_list (platform google_business_profile).

tools.name: seo_generate_sitemap
tools.description: Generate sitemap.xml content from the project's published website_pages (honors show_in_sitemap unless includeNoIndex is set in sitemap_settings). Returns { file_path: 'public/sitemap.xml', content }. Commit via project_commit to save.

tools.name: seo_gsc_delete_sitemap
tools.description: Remove a sitemap from Google Search Console — DELETE /sites/:site/sitemaps/:feedpath. Use during template/structure migrations when an old sitemap URL is no longer canonical.

tools.name: seo_gsc_discover_sites
tools.description: List the GSC-verified sites accessible to a connection's OAuth user. Returns 'sites' (queryable: siteOwner / siteFullUser) and 'restricted_sites' (siteRestrictedUser — appears in /sites but returns 403 on data queries). After picking one, call seo_connection_update with {site_url: '<picked>'} — that flips status to 'connected'. If the user has only delegated read access and 0 sites appear, the hint will tell the agent to use sc-domain:<domain> directly.

tools.name: seo_gsc_get_sitemap
tools.description: Per-sitemap detail for one feedpath — lastSubmitted, lastDownloaded, isPending, isSitemapsIndex, errors[], warnings[], contents[]. Use this when seo_gsc_list_sitemaps shows a sitemap with submitted > indexed to find out what's wrong.

tools.name: seo_gsc_index_coverage
tools.description: Best-available substitute for GSC's Index Coverage report. Google's public API has NO bulk coverage endpoint — this tool fans out URL Inspection per URL and buckets the results by coverage_state (e.g. 'Submitted and indexed' | 'Discovered - currently not indexed' | 'Crawled - currently not indexed' | 'Duplicate without user-selected canonical' | ...). Use to surface index health for a known URL set (sitemap entries, top-traffic pages, new launches). Capped at 50 URLs per call — split into batches for larger sites.

tools.name: seo_gsc_inspect_url
tools.description: Run GSC's URL Inspection on a specific page. Returns indexability + mobile-usability + rich-result analysis. NOTE: Google's public API only inspects the indexed snapshot — there is no liveTest equivalent, and manualActions / securityIssues are not exposed in this response (they're UI-only in Search Console).

tools.name: seo_gsc_list_sitemaps
tools.description: List sitemaps registered in GSC for a property + their submission state.

tools.name: seo_gsc_list_sites
tools.description: List the Search Console properties the account's GSC connection can see: Google's owner-verified sites (siteUrl, permissionLevel) merged with the account's seo_connections rows for google_search_console, including pending rows whose site_url is still unset. No arguments. Returns the site list plus the connection rows so you can tell 'verified in Google' from 'bound in Hiveku'. Needs at least one google_search_console connection with a working refresh token (seo_connections_list); with none, or an expired token, the route answers 4xx rather than an empty list. To bind a property to a pending connection use seo_gsc_discover_sites then seo_connection_update { site_url }.

tools.name: seo_gsc_period_comparison
tools.description: Compare two time periods on the same site and return winners/losers + rank climbers/droppers. Fetches both periods, joins on the supplied dimensions, computes click/impression/position deltas. Top use cases: post-launch review (period_b=after, period_a=before), algorithm-update analysis, MoM/WoW reporting. Position deltas are signed Google-style (lower = better; rank_climbers have negative position_delta).

tools.name: seo_gsc_search_analytics
tools.description: Full multi-dimension Search Analytics query — the canonical GSC report tool. Pass dimensions as ANY combination of date | query | page | country | device | searchAppearance (e.g. ['query','page'] answers 'which query drives which page?'). Filters support equals | notEquals | contains | notContains | includingRegex | excludingRegex. Up to 25000 rows per call; paginate with start_row.

tools.name: seo_gsc_search_queries
tools.description: Top queries from GSC for a property (dimensions: query). Default window: last 28 days. search_type: 'web'|'image'|'video'|'discover'|'googleNews'.

tools.name: seo_gsc_submit_sitemap
tools.description: Submit a sitemap to Google Search Console — PUT /sites/:site/sitemaps/:feedpath. Use after a redeploy that added or changed indexable URLs. Idempotent — re-submitting an existing sitemap is fine.

tools.name: seo_gsc_time_series
tools.description: Daily clicks/impressions/CTR/position time series. Convenience wrapper over seo_gsc_search_analytics with dimensions=['date']. Use to answer 'did my change help?' — overlay a deploy date on the trend. Accepts the same filters[] (e.g. {dimension:'page', expression:'/blog/', operator:'contains'} to scope the trend to one section).

tools.name: seo_gsc_top_pages
tools.description: Top pages from GSC (dimensions: page). Same params as seo_gsc_search_queries.

tools.name: seo_gtm_install
tools.description: Install a GTM container's snippet into one tier's site-wide custom code — the <script> block in HEAD and the <noscript> iframe in BODY. GTM needs BOTH; a head-only install silently loses no-JS and some privacy-blocked traffic. STRICT TWO-STEP CONFIRM: the first call (confirm omitted, or anything other than the boolean true) returns requires_confirm with a preview and changes NOTHING. Repeat the identical call with confirm: true to write. NEVER DUPLICATES, BUT DOES REPAIR. It is a no-op only when the container is FULLY installed site-wide (both halves). Otherwise it fixes what is wrong, writing only what is missing and leaving what is present byte-for-byte: a half install gets its missing box added (and the response says which, since an iframe-only install means the container never loads at all, while a script-only one merely undercounts no-JS traffic), and a container living only in page overrides is MOVED site-wide in one transaction. If a page override box holds other code alongside the snippet, the call refuses and names the page rather than splicing customer HTML. SAVED IS NOT LIVE: the write takes effect on the NEXT DEPLOY of that tier, and the preview tier additionally requires run_in_preview (see project_custom_code_preview_toggle).

tools.name: seo_gtm_install_status
tools.description: Is the GTM container the agent is editing actually installed on the site? Reports per tier (preview / development / staging / production), head and body separately: not installed, installed, installed-but-a-different-container, or installed more than once. ALWAYS call this before and after seo_gtm_tag_create / seo_gtm_publish. A published container that is not installed fires on nobody, and every tag call still reports success — that failure is invisible from both ends. The three findings that cost money: WRONG CONTAINER (the site runs a container the agent is not editing; both ids are named, and conversions recorded is zero), DUPLICATE INSTALL (the same container twice on one rendered page, which DOUBLE-COUNTS every conversion — it reads as performance improving and corrupts every downstream CPA and ROAS), and TIER DRIFT (verified on staging, never installed on production). Also flags a head-only install (loses no-JS traffic) and a row that is disabled or over the injection cap — which reads as installed in the UI and ships on no deploy, ever. SCOPE: reads project_custom_code. A container hardcoded in the site's own source is invisible here — use analytics_diagnose_tracking for that. Reports the SAVED state, never the LIVE one.

tools.name: seo_gtm_publish
tools.description: Publish a GTM container version — THE step that CHANGES THE CLIENT'S LIVE SITE: every tag in the version starts serving to real visitors immediately. TWO-STEP CONFIRM: the first call (without confirm) does NOT publish — it returns a preview (container name + public id, the version's tags, what is currently live, and the workspace's pending changes with a note that those are NOT in this version) with requires_confirm: true. Repeat the IDENTICAL call with confirm: true to publish. Get version_id from seo_gtm_version_create. Requires the Tag Manager publish scopes (tagmanager.edit.containerversions + tagmanager.publish, requested since 2026-08-23) — a connection authorized before then gets a reconnect-Google-Analytics error naming the fix. Remember the documented failure mode this pipeline exists to close: a container whose conversion tags were never published recorded nothing for months. CONTAINER PINNING: the first time a container is used successfully on a connection, that container is claimed from Google's own answer and stored on the connection. A later call naming a DIFFERENT container is refused with a 403 naming both — the connection's Google user can legitimately reach containers belonging to other tenants, so the pin is what stops one account editing another's container. Retrying the same call will not help; either use the pinned container, or clear the pin deliberately with seo_connection_update (gtm_container_path: null) and let the next successful call re-claim it.

tools.name: seo_gtm_status
tools.description: Google Tag Manager status for a Google Analytics connection (GTM rides the SAME seo_connections row — one Google authorization covers both). Without container_path: lists the GTM accounts + containers the connection's Google user can see (container_path + public GTM-XXXXXX id). With container_path: the publish preview for that container — container name, the default workspace's PENDING CHANGES (what the next version would contain), a draft-vs-live tag split (draft_only tags are NOT serving), the currently-live version, and a loud warning when the container has NEVER been published (the documented failure mode: a never-published container silently losing every Ads conversion). Also returns triggers[] — every trigger in the workspace, the live version and the built-ins, each with trigger_id, name, type, filters, load_only and spa_safe, and each tag's firing_triggers[] resolved BY NAME rather than as a bare numeric id. That is what lets you bind a conversion tag to a click trigger a human already built, without creating a duplicate. Also returns variables[] — variable_id, name, type, type_label, reference (the {{Name}} form) and data_layer_key (the dataLayer key it actually reads, which is independent of its display name). variable_id is what seo_gtm_variable_get / _update / _delete take, and nothing else emits it. Built-in variables are excluded because they have no numeric id. Read this before seo_gtm_tag_create and before seo_gtm_version_create / seo_gtm_publish. Get connection_id from seo_connections_list (platform google_analytics). CONTAINER PINNING: the first time a container is used successfully on a connection, that container is claimed from Google's own answer and stored on the connection. A later call naming a DIFFERENT container is refused with a 403 naming both — the connection's Google user can legitimately reach containers belonging to other tenants, so the pin is what stops one account editing another's container. Retrying the same call will not help; either use the pinned container, or clear the pin deliberately with seo_connection_update (gtm_container_path: null) and let the next successful call re-claim it.

tools.name: seo_gtm_tag_create
tools.description: Create a tag in a GTM container's default workspace — a WORKSPACE DRAFT ONLY: nothing serves until the container is published (seo_gtm_version_create then seo_gtm_publish), and an unpublished conversion tag records nothing however complete it looks in GTM. No confirm gate for that reason. TAG TYPES: 'ga4_event' (measurement_id 'G-XXXXXXXXXX' + event_name), 'ads_conversion' (conversion_id + conversion_label from the Ads conversion action's tag setup), 'bing_uet' / 'bing_uet_event' (uet_tag_id), 'meta_pixel' / 'meta_event' (meta_pixel_id), 'custom_html'. Bing and Meta are emitted as templated Custom HTML because GTM has no first-party type for them; bing_uet and meta_pixel are BASE tags that fire once per document load. CONVERSION VALUE: pass conversion_value + currency_code (+ transaction_id to deduplicate) as a literal or a '{{Variable}}' reference. Omit them and the tag sends NO VALUE — the conversion still records, but every one is worth the same, so tROAS bids against a constant. Create a dataLayer variable with seo_gtm_variable_create and reference it here. FIRING TRIGGERS: pass firing_trigger_ids (existing ids from seo_gtm_status, which now returns every trigger's name/type/filters so you can bind to a click trigger a human already built) OR create_trigger. 'all_pages'; 'page_path' (+ trigger_page_path, e.g. /thank-you), which defaults to trigger_type 'both' — one pageview AND one historyChange trigger, because on a Next.js site a form submit is a client-side route change a pageview trigger never sees while a hard landing is a document load historyChange never sees, and either alone has a silent blind spot; or 'click' / 'link_click' / 'form_submit' (+ trigger_match_on / trigger_match_value) for the click conversions — tap-to-call, WhatsApp CTA, PDF download, booking button. Get connection_id from seo_connections_list (platform google_analytics); get container_path from seo_gtm_status. CONTAINER PINNING: the first time a container is used successfully on a connection, that container is claimed from Google's own answer and stored on the connection. A later call naming a DIFFERENT container is refused with a 403 naming both — the connection's Google user can legitimately reach containers belonging to other tenants, so the pin is what stops one account editing another's container. Retrying the same call will not help; either use the pinned container, or clear the pin deliberately with seo_connection_update (gtm_container_path: null) and let the next successful call re-claim it.

tools.name: seo_gtm_tag_delete
tools.description: DESTRUCTIVE. Delete a GTM tag from the workspace. It stops working on the NEXT PUBLISH, not immediately, so the damage surfaces later than the action. A deleted conversion tag stops recording — the Google Ads or GA4 conversion it feeds flatlines with no error anywhere. Prefer paused: true on seo_gtm_tag_update, which is reversible. TWO-STEP CONFIRM: the first call does NOT delete — it returns a preview and touches nothing. Repeat with confirm: true (a strict boolean; the string 'true' only previews). Draft-only: the change lands in the workspace and serves nothing until seo_gtm_version_create then seo_gtm_publish. CONTAINER PINNING: the first time a container is used successfully on a connection, that container is claimed from Google's own answer and stored on the connection. A later call naming a DIFFERENT container is refused with a 403 naming both — the connection's Google user can legitimately reach containers belonging to other tenants, so the pin is what stops one account editing another's container. Retrying the same call will not help; either use the pinned container, or clear the pin deliberately with seo_connection_update (gtm_container_path: null) and let the next successful call re-claim it.

tools.name: seo_gtm_tag_get

tools.name: seo_internal_links
tools.description: Internal-link graph per page (orphans, inbound/outbound counts, click depth) for HIVEKU-HOSTED published projects only. Data source: computed every Sunday by the seo-analysis-sweep cron from a STATIC scan of the project's current code — not a live crawl; dynamic/CMS-driven links are invisible, and external/imported sites are never analyzed. Empty (with a note) for accounts without a published hosted project; never read empty as no-issues.

tools.name: seo_issues
tools.description: Detect SEO issues from the synced Search Console data (seo_search_metrics): position drops per query (last 30 days vs the previous 30), content decay (pages losing clicks), low-CTR opportunities (high impressions, low CTR) and declining impressions, sorted critical first. No arguments. Returns { issues: [{ id, type (rank_drop | content_decay | performance | index_issue | ...), severity (critical | warning | info), title, description, source, url, data }], total, critical, warnings }. Needs a GSC connection that has synced at least 60 days; with less data, or none, the list is empty, which is 'no data', not 'no issues' (check seo_connections_health). Each aggregation reads one dimension signature so clicks are not double counted. To act on one, file it with create_task or hand it to seo_task_implement.

tools.name: seo_keyword_cluster_create
tools.description: Persist a keyword cluster (seo_keyword_clusters) — the durable output of keyword-clustering work, so grouping research done in chat survives the session and shows on the dashboard. cluster_name is unique per account (409 on duplicate). List existing clusters with seo_keyword_clusters.

tools.name: seo_keyword_cluster_delete
tools.description: Delete a saved keyword cluster. Needs cluster_id from seo_keyword_clusters. Returns { data: { deleted: true } }; 404 when the id is not on this account. Hard delete, no undo: the member keywords and recommendations stored on the row go with it (the researched keywords on the SEO project are separate rows and stay). Confirm with the user before calling.

tools.name: seo_keyword_cluster_get
tools.description: Fetch one saved keyword cluster (seo_keyword_clusters: cluster_name, primary_keyword, search_intent, keywords[], keyword_count, total_volume, avg_difficulty, avg_cpc, target_url, content_status, content_recommendations). Needs cluster_id from seo_keyword_clusters (data[].id) or seo_keyword_cluster_create. Returns { data: <row> }; 404 when the id is not on this account. keywords[] is whatever shape the saver wrote (strings or objects with metrics); read it before assuming fields.

tools.name: seo_keyword_cluster_update
tools.description: Update a saved keyword cluster: cluster_name, primary_keyword, search_intent, keywords, keyword_count, total_volume, avg_difficulty, avg_cpc, target_url, content_status, content_recommendations. Needs cluster_id from seo_keyword_clusters; only the fields sent change. Returns { data: <the updated row> }; 404 when the id is not on this account. keywords and content_recommendations are full replacements, not merges, so send the complete list; keep keyword_count equal to keywords.length yourself, the route does not recompute it. Renaming to a cluster_name another cluster uses fails on the per-account unique key.

tools.name: seo_keyword_clusters
tools.description: List the keyword clusters saved on the account (seo_keyword_clusters: cluster_name, primary_keyword, search_intent, keywords[], keyword_count, total_volume, avg_difficulty, avg_cpc, target_url, content_status, content_recommendations), ordered by total_volume. Account-scoped, no project id: filter with search (cluster_name or primary_keyword contains), search_intent, content_status, page, limit (max 100). Returns { data, pagination }. Clusters exist only because someone saved them (seo_keyword_cluster_create or the dashboard); nothing clusters automatically. Use the returned id for seo_keyword_cluster_get / seo_keyword_cluster_update / seo_keyword_cluster_delete.

tools.name: seo_keywords_list
tools.description: Narrower-param alias of seo_list_keywords (same route; this one omits max_difficulty, sort_by and sort_order). Lists the researched keywords stored on an SEO tracking project (seo_keyword_analysis: volume, difficulty, cpc, intent) with search, search_intent, min_volume, page, limit filters. Needs project_id from seo_list_projects. Returns { data, pagination }. These are research rows, not the rank tracker: tracked keywords with positions are seo_rankings_list.

tools.name: seo_list_audits
tools.description: List the persisted site audits on the account (site_audit_tasks), newest first. Each row is one crawl: { id (the audit_id), task_id, target_url, status (queued / processing / completed / failed), pages_crawled, total_pages, crawl_progress, started_at, completed_at, error_message }; the crawl results themselves are read per audit with seo_audit_get. Audits are account-scoped: project_id (seo_list_projects) narrows to that project domain (404 when it is not this account's), domain narrows by target_url contains, status by state; page and limit (max 50) paginate. Returns { data: [...], pagination, hint }. Rows not yet completed or failed are only refreshed from DataForSEO when seo_audit_get is called on them, so a row can sit at processing here until someone polls it. An empty list means no crawl was ever started, never that the site is clean; start one with seo_run_audit. seo_audit_list is a narrower-param alias of this tool.

tools.name: seo_list_competitors
tools.description: List the competitor domains tracked on an SEO tracking project with the stored analysis columns (domain_rating, organic_keywords, organic_traffic, shared_keywords, keyword_gap, backlinks_count, referring_domains, competition_level, market_share, trend_direction, last_analyzed), ordered by organic_traffic. Needs project_id from seo_list_projects. Returns { data: [...], pagination: { page, limit, total, total_pages } } (limit max 50). The metrics are whatever was last written by seo_add_competitor or seo_competitor_update; nothing refreshes them on a schedule, so a live comparison is seo_research action competitors or domain-overview. seo_competitors_list is a narrower-param alias of this tool.

tools.name: seo_list_keywords
tools.description: List tracked SEO keywords for a project with volume, difficulty, and intent filters

tools.name: seo_list_projects
tools.description: List the SEO TRACKING projects on this account (one row per tracked domain) with their cached domain metrics (domain_rating, organic_keywords, organic_traffic, monthly_visits, cached_at) and counts of keywords, competitors, audits and content gaps. No ids needed; filter with is_active (the STRING "true"/"false"), search (name or domain contains), page, limit (max 100). Returns { data: [...], pagination: { page, limit, total, total_pages } }. The id here is the SEO tracking project id used by seo_list_keywords, seo_run_audit, seo_add_competitor and seo_content_gaps; it is NOT the website project id from sites_list that seo_project_get, pages_* and deploy_site take. seo_project_list_active is an alias of this tool.

tools.name: seo_list_rankings
tools.description: LIVE daily rank tracker for tracked keywords — reads what the daily ranking worker actually collects (the old data source was a stale table no job wrote to; this now reflects real checks). Covers Google and Bing SERP positions, local-pack positions (ranking_type=local + local_pack_position), and AI-engine citation tracking (search_engine: chatgpt | perplexity | ai_overview | claude | gemini). view=keywords (default): tracked keywords with current_rank / previous_rank / best_rank / worst_rank, local_pack_position, device_type, location_name, check_frequency, last_checked_at — filter by domain, keyword (contains), search_engine, ranking_type, device, min_position/max_position (on current_rank). view=history: per-check time series for ONE keyword (check_date, rank_position, local_pack_position, search_volume, serp_features) — pass ranking_id, or keyword + domain (+ optional search_engine/ranking_type/device disambiguators), with from_date/to_date.

tools.name: seo_listings_get
tools.description: The Listings page as data: one row per active Google Business Profile connection with the Listing Score (0 to 100 completeness) and its per-field breakdown, the NAP block (name, address, phone, website, hours, categories), verification and duplicate status, snapshot freshness, the directory-coverage block (the last Maps footprint scan, the directory checklist and its score, reputation sources) and the local-pack summary (tracked / in_pack / in_finder). No arguments. Returns { listings: [{ connection_id, display_name, state, score, nap, status, snapshot, error, error_code, directories, local_pack }], total_connections, shown, not_applicable_count, summary: { avg_score, insights_30d: { impressions, calls, directions, website_clicks } | null } }. Snapshot-first: rows come from the listing cache kept warm by the 6-hour cron; only a connected row with NO cached snapshot triggers a live Google fetch, and a GBP quota block shows as state 'error' with error_code rather than failing the call. A connection in needs_setup (no location picked) shows as incomplete, not as an error; not-applicable connections are excluded and counted. The Maps footprint scan is a separate paid call: seo_listings_scan.

tools.name: seo_listings_scan
tools.description: SPENDS MONEY. Run the on-demand Google Maps footprint scan for one GBP connection: finds unclaimed listings, duplicate entries and public-NAP drift for the business by searching DataForSEO Business Listings around the profile's name and address. Needs connection_id from seo_connections_list (platform google_business_profile, active). One DataForSEO business_listings call per scan, metered under the account's SEO research cap (429 research_cap when exhausted). 24-hour cooldown per connection: inside it the route answers 429 scan_cooldown with retry_at and the EXISTING scan, so do not retry; 409 scan_unavailable when the GBP listing has never synced (run seo_sync first). Returns { scan: { scanned_at, matches, duplicates, nap_drift, dfs_cost, ... } }, or { scan, persisted: false } when money was spent but the save failed (report the result anyway). Read seo_listings_get first; it already carries the last scan. Confirm with the user before calling.

tools.name: seo_llms_txt_generate
tools.description: Generate an llms.txt for a WEBSITE project from its real page map (site name, site URL, then up to 100 published pages as name, URL and meta description) and save it through the versioned file pipeline as public/llms.txt (llms.txt at the root for frameworks without a public/ directory). Needs project_id = the website project UUID from sites_list. Returns { ok, file_path, version_number, pages_indexed, content, note }. It is a file write like project_file_save: versioned and preview-synced, but NOT live until deploy_site, and it OVERWRITES an existing llms.txt without merging. Pages with no meta_description get a bare link, so run the AEO readiness check (seo_aeo_readiness) and fix descriptions first if the file is meant to be read by answer engines. Verify after deploy with fetch_url on https://<domain>/llms.txt.

tools.name: seo_local_compare_periods
tools.description: Current N days vs the previous N days — clicks, impressions, CTR, avg position.

tools.name: seo_local_rank_changes
tools.description: Keywords whose rank dropped by at least min_drop positions. Compares the most recent half of the window to the prior half.

tools.name: seo_local_rank_history
tools.description: Position-over-time series for one keyword (optionally scoped to a domain).

tools.name: seo_local_search_performance
tools.description: Aggregated clicks/impressions/CTR/avg-position over N days from synced GSC + Bing data.

tools.name: seo_local_top_pages
tools.description: Top landing pages by clicks from the synced seo_search_metrics table (Search Console and Bing Webmaster rows pulled by seo_sync / the 6-hour cron), summed over the last `days` days (required, 1 to 365). Optional source gsc | bing | all (default all; both sources are summed) and limit (default 20, max 200). Returns { data: { days, source, rows: [{ page, clicks, impressions, ctr, position }] } } with position impression-weighted. Reads the page dimension slice only; page + query together exist only in the archive (seo_query_page_metrics). GSC rows are Pacific-dated with about a 3-day lag, so the newest days under-count.
