Empty rows means nothing synced, not zero traffic.

tools.name: seo_local_top_queries
tools.description: Top search queries by clicks from the synced seo_search_metrics table (Search Console and Bing Webmaster rows pulled by seo_sync / the 6-hour cron), summed over the last `days` days (required, 1 to 365). Optional source gsc | bing | all (default all; the two sources are summed, which double counts a site connected to both) and limit (default 20, max 200). Returns { data: { days, source, rows: [{ query, clicks, impressions, ctr, position }] } } with position impression-weighted. Reads the query dimension slice only, so totals differ from seo_local_search_performance (date slice). GSC rows are dated in Pacific time and arrive about 3 days late: a window ending today under-counts the last 3 days. Empty rows means nothing synced, not zero traffic; check seo_connections_health.

tools.name: seo_new_lost_backlinks
tools.description: Read the MANUAL link-building tracker (seo_tracked_backlinks): links you built or are pursuing, entered by hand through seo_backlink_tracker_add or the dashboard, each with url, title, target_url, target_anchor, link_type, status (published | unpublished), date_published, page_authority, domain_authority, notes. Same route as seo_backlink_tracker_list. Optional project_id is a WEBSITE project id from sites_list (not the SEO tracking project); filter with since (ISO date: date_published on or after it, so undated rows drop out), status, link_type (contains), search (url / title / target_url / anchor contains), page, limit (max 100). Returns { data, pagination }. This is NOT DataForSEO new/lost backlink discovery: for links Google's index gained or dropped use backlinks_bulk_new_lost_backlinks, backlinks_timeseries_new_lost_summary or seo_research action backlinks-timeseries.

tools.name: seo_organic_leads
tools.description: Leads by acquisition channel for the 'SEO drove N leads' number: form submissions from the Hiveku tracking script joined to their session's channel (Organic Search, AI Assistants, Paid, Social, Direct, Referral, Email, in the analytics hub's vocabulary). Needs from and to as YYYY-MM-DD; optional project_id (WEBSITE project UUID from sites_list) scopes to one site. Returns { months: [{ month, channels: { <channel>: leads } }], channelTotals: { <channel>: { leads, people } }, organic: { leads, people }, aiAssistants: { leads, people }, attribution_note }. Session-level LAST-touch: a visitor who found the site through search and converted on a later direct visit counts as Direct, so treat organic as a floor and say so. Empty when the site does not run the tracking script or has no form submits in the window; cached 60 seconds per scope.

tools.name: seo_page_schema_delete
tools.description: Clear the JSON-LD structured data stored on one builder page (sets website_pages.structured_data to {}). Needs project_id = the WEBSITE project UUID from sites_list and page_id from pages_list. Returns { data: { deleted: true, page_id }, note }; 404 when the page is not in that project on this account. Clears the DB copy only: an ld+json block previously written into the page file by seo_page_schema_set { sync_to_file: true } stays in the file and keeps rendering until you re-save the file without it (project_file_save) and deploy. No undo; read seo_page_schema_get first if the schema might be wanted back. Confirm with the user before calling.

tools.name: seo_page_schema_generate
tools.description: Generate a JSON-LD structured-data PROPOSAL for one builder page - nothing is written anywhere. Builds the same base graph the deploy-time SEO injector emits (WebSite + Organization + WebPage, shared code so they cannot drift), upgraded to LocalBusiness with real NAP (name, address, phone, geo) when the account has a Google Business Profile connection with a cached listing snapshot (DB cache only, no Google call), plus a BreadcrumbList derived from the page slug and an Article node when page_type is blog_post. Needs project_id = the WEBSITE project UUID from sites_list and page_id from pages_list. Optional business overrides (business_name, business_type e.g. Plumber, phone, street_address, locality, region, postal_code, country, logo_url, image_url, same_as, author_name) beat GBP values. Returns { data: { page_id, page_slug, page_type, proposal: { schema, types, rationale }, validation, existing_schema_types, gbp_used, gbp_connection_id, site_url, note } } - rationale explains every choice, existing_schema_types shows what an apply would replace. Review the proposal, then store it with seo_page_schema_set (optionally sync_to_file: true) and deploy_site to make it render. No AI or metered calls.

tools.name: seo_page_schema_get
tools.description: Read the JSON-LD structured data stored on one builder page (website_pages.structured_data) with the schema types it declares, a validation result (@context must be schema.org; @type or @graph required; unique @id per @graph entity) and the page's meta for context. Needs project_id = the WEBSITE project UUID from sites_list and page_id from pages_list. Returns { data: { page_id, page_name, page_slug, page_type, is_homepage, schema, schema_types, validation: { valid, errors }, site_url, meta_title, meta_description, canonical_url } }; 404 when the page is not in that project on this account. This is the DB copy: schema hand-written into the page file is not read here (seo_research action instant-page on the live URL sees what actually renders). seo_schema_markup is a different, analysis-sweep table.

tools.name: seo_page_schema_set
tools.description: Store JSON-LD structured data on one builder page (website_pages.structured_data), replacing whatever was there, after validating it (@context https://schema.org, @type or @graph, no duplicate @id; 400 { error: 'Invalid schema', validation_errors[] } otherwise). Needs project_id = the WEBSITE project UUID from sites_list, page_id from pages_list, and schema (the full JSON-LD object; use @graph for several entities). sync_to_file: true also writes a <script type="application/ld+json"> block into the page's source file before </head> (or </body>) as a NEW file version through the versioned pipeline, replacing an existing ld+json block, which is what makes it render; the DB copy alone renders only where the site template reads structured_data. Returns { data: { page_id, schema, schema_types, synced_to_file, file_path, version_number, file_note } }. A synced file is NOT live until deploy_site. Validation is structural only: it does not check that the types or properties exist in schema.org, so verify with a Rich Results test after deploy.

tools.name: seo_page_seo_get
tools.description: Read one builder page's SEO meta as a unified view of what the database row (website_pages) and the page's CODE FILE say, with a validation score and per-field warnings (title length, description length, missing canonical, OG / Twitter tags). Needs project_id = the WEBSITE project UUID from sites_list and page_id from pages_list. Returns { data: { page: { id, name, slug, url }, project: { id, name, type }, meta: { title, description, keywords, canonicalUrl, og, twitter, robotsDirective, structuredData }, score: { overall, ... }, framework, file_path, source: 'filesystem' | 'database', sync_status: 'synced' | 'not-applicable', last_modified } }; 404 when the page is not in that project on this account. When source is filesystem the file values are what ships and the DB columns are informational; write file-backed meta with seo_page_seo_set, DB columns with pages_update.

tools.name: seo_page_seo_set
tools.description: Write SEO meta INTO a builder page's code file (the Next.js metadata export, or index.html for a SPA) as a versioned file write, the same lane as project_file_save. Needs project_id = the WEBSITE project UUID from sites_list and page_slug (the route, '' or '/' for the homepage, from pages_list); at least one of meta_title, meta_description, keywords, canonical_url, og, twitter (400 otherwise), and only the fields you send are written (an omitted description is left as it is in the file). Returns { data: { file_path, framework, diff: { before, after } (first 500 chars each), warnings[] }, note }; 400 with code unsupported_project_type (only builder Next.js projects have files to sync into; other types use pages_update) or page_file_not_found. NOT two-step and NOT live: the change is a new file version, preview-synced, and reaches the site only after deploy_site (ask-gated). It does not touch the website_pages DB columns (pages_update does). Read seo_page_seo_get first and keep titles under 60 and descriptions under 155 characters.

tools.name: seo_project_get
tools.description: Fetch a WEBSITE project's stored SEO settings: seo_settings (JSON), robots_txt_content, sitemap_settings, seo_monitoring. Needs project_id = the website project UUID from sites_list (NOT the SEO tracking project id from seo_list_projects). Returns { data: { id, name, slug, seo_settings, robots_txt_content, sitemap_settings, seo_monitoring } }. robots_txt_content is served as the site's /robots.txt from the NEXT deploy onward WHEN the project code ships no robots source of its own; any robots source in the code (public/robots.txt, robots.txt, app/robots.ts|tsx|js|jsx|txt) always wins over the stored value (read it with project_file_get), and a stored change is not live until deploy_site runs. Page-level SEO lives on website_pages: pages_get / pages_update, or seo_page_seo_get / seo_page_seo_set for the file-backed meta.

tools.name: seo_project_list_active
tools.description: Alias of seo_list_projects (identical route and params). Lists the SEO TRACKING projects (one per tracked domain) with cached domain metrics and counts; filter with is_active (STRING "true"/"false"), search, page, limit. Returns { data, pagination }. The id is the SEO tracking project id, not the website project id from sites_list.

tools.name: seo_project_update
tools.description: Update a WEBSITE project's stored SEO settings. Needs project_id = the website project UUID from sites_list (NOT the SEO tracking project id); pass any of seo_settings (object), robots_txt_content (string), sitemap_settings (object), seo_monitoring (object); at least one is required (400 otherwise). Returns { data: <the updated settings row> }. robots_txt_content is STORED on website_projects (and copied when the project is cloned) and is served as the site's /robots.txt from the NEXT deploy onward when the project code ships NO robots source of its own. Any robots source in the code (public/robots.txt, robots.txt, app/robots.ts|tsx|js|jsx|txt) always wins over the stored value, and a stored change is NOT live until deploy_site runs; after deploying, verify with fetch_url on https://<domain>/robots.txt.

tools.name: seo_query_page_metrics
tools.description: Read the permanent Search Console archive (seo_query_page_metrics): the ONLY place date, query AND page coexist per row (the live seo_search_metrics table holds each dimension separately and must never be summed across them), and unlike Google's rolling window it never expires. Needs site_url (the GSC property exactly as stored, 'sc-domain:example.com' or 'https://example.com/') OR connection_id (seo_connections_list, platform google_search_console; 400 when that connection has no site_url yet); from and to as YYYY-MM-DD, at most 16 months apart (400 range_too_long: split it); optional query_like and page_like (case-insensitive contains), group_by query_page (default) | query | page | date, sort clicks (default) | impressions | position, limit 1 to 5000 (default 200). Returns { site_url, range, group_by, sort, rows: [{ query?, page?, date?, clicks, impressions, ctr, position }], row_count, truncated, archive_coverage: { first_day, last_day, days_done, days_error, days_requested, complete, note }, data_quality_note }. ALWAYS read archive_coverage first: the archive backfills hourly, day by day, so a range that is not complete returns a FLOOR, not a decline. position is the plain average of daily positions in the group, not impression-weighted. Google anonymises rare queries at the query-and-page grain, so these clicks sum LOWER than the site total; quote whole-site totals from seo_gsc_search_analytics. GSC days are Pacific-dated and arrive about 3 days late.

tools.name: seo_ranking_predictions
tools.description: 30-day ranking forecasts per tracked keyword. Data source: computed every Sunday by the seo-analysis-sweep cron via linear TREND EXTRAPOLATION (not ML) over rank-check history (website_ranking_history) — organic keywords with 5+ checks spanning 21+ days in the last 120. confidence_score = trend-fit R-squared x 100; factors carries slope/data points; requirements and backlinks_needed are NOT computed. Empty (with a note) until rank tracking accumulates enough history.

tools.name: seo_rankings_list
tools.description: Alias of seo_list_rankings - identical route and params. LIVE daily rank tracker for tracked keywords — reads what the daily ranking worker actually collects (the old data source was a stale table no job wrote to; this now reflects real checks). Covers Google and Bing SERP positions, local-pack positions (ranking_type=local + local_pack_position), and AI-engine citation tracking (search_engine: chatgpt | perplexity | ai_overview | claude | gemini). view=keywords (default): tracked keywords with current_rank / previous_rank / best_rank / worst_rank, local_pack_position, device_type, location_name, check_frequency, last_checked_at — filter by domain, keyword (contains), search_engine, ranking_type, device, min_position/max_position (on current_rank). view=history: per-check time series for ONE keyword (check_date, rank_position, local_pack_position, search_volume, serp_features) — pass ranking_id, or keyword + domain (+ optional search_engine/ranking_type/device disambiguators), with from_date/to_date.

tools.name: seo_rankings_locations
tools.description: US location directory for rank tracking: resolves the exact location_code + location_name pair that seo_track_keyword and seo_rankings_platforms_set need (2840 = United States country-level; city and DMA codes make local/geo lanes precise). Live read of DataForSEO's serp locations directory - a free metadata endpoint, not a metered SERP call. US locations ONLY, matching the dashboard picker; for non-US country-level tracking pass the country's serp_locations code straight to seo_track_keyword. q is a substring match on location_name with best-match-first ordering (exact/prefix matches sort to the top); without q, cities sort before DMA regions, states and countries, so always pass q when hunting a specific city. Returns { locations: [{ location_code, location_name, location_type, country_iso_code }], total } - total is the returned count, capped by limit (default 50, max 500), NOT the directory size. 503 dataforseo_unconfigured when the server has no DataForSEO credentials; that is a server-config gap, never 'no locations'.

tools.name: seo_rankings_platforms_set
tools.description: DESTRUCTIVE ON REMOVAL. Set EXACTLY which lanes one tracked keyword is checked on. A tracked keyword is N website_rankings rows, one per (search_engine, device_type, ranking_type); this call computes the desired lane set from engines[] (google, bing, ai_overview, chatgpt, perplexity, claude, gemini) plus track_mobile (adds the Google mobile lane) and track_local (adds the Google local-pack lane; business_name for a new local lane, else inherited from a sibling), INSERTS the missing lanes and DELETES every existing lane not in the set, and a deleted lane takes its whole rank history with it by FK cascade. Needs keyword, location_name and target_domain spelled EXACTLY as seo_rankings_list shows them (that triple is the keyword's identity; 404 when it does not match). Returns { ok, added, removed, lanes }. 400 when engines is empty (to stop tracking, delete the keyword instead). Read seo_rankings_list with group_by_keyword first and list the lanes that will be removed before asking the user to confirm. New AI lanes cost about $0.10 per engine per check. Confirm with the user before calling.

tools.name: seo_report_add_section
tools.description: Append a markdown section to the Report Preview within a workspace deliverable.

tools.name: seo_report_clear
tools.description: Clear all Report Preview sections in a workspace deliverable (tabs are untouched).

tools.name: seo_report_update_section
tools.description: Update a Report Preview section (find by section_title; can also rename it).

tools.name: seo_research
tools.description: DataForSEO multi-tool. Pick `action` based on what you need. Defaults to 'domain-overview' when only `domain` is supplied. Most calls take 1–5s; bulk + reviews can take 30–120s. DOMAIN INTELLIGENCE (needs domain): domain-overview — traffic, top country, rank distribution domain-backlinks — backlink summary (root + subdomains) top-pages — highest-traffic pages on this domain competitors — competing domains in organic search ranked-keywords — every keyword this domain currently ranks for referring-domains — list of domains linking in subdomains — list discoverable subdomains whois-overview — WHOIS metadata (age, registrar, expiry) KEYWORD RESEARCH (needs keyword OR keywords[]): keyword-overview — volume, CPC, KD, intent (multi-keyword) keyword-ideas — expand to long-tail variants keyword-trends — search-volume trend bands related-keywords — semantic siblings historical-search-volume — multi-year volume trend keyword-difficulty / bulk-keyword-difficulty — KD scores bulk-traffic-estimation — estimated organic traffic for many URLs (needs targets[]) top-searches — what's hot in a location (needs location_name or location_code) serp — live Google SERP for a single keyword bing-serp — Bing SERP for a single keyword bing-keyword-volume / google-ads-search-volume — alternative volume sources google-trends-explore — Google Trends interest over time GAPS / COMPARISONS: keyword-gap — keywords competitors[] rank for that domain doesn't (needs domain + competitors[]) link-gap — backlinks competitors[] have that domain doesn't page-intersection — URL-level gap (needs targets[] of 2-20 URLs) LOCAL SEO / REVIEWS (Tranche A): gbp-info — Google Business Profile snapshot (needs domain or target) gbp-locations — find GBP locations by query (needs query) gbp-questions / gbp-reviews — Q&A and reviews on GBP yelp-reviews / trustpilot-reviews / tripadvisor-reviews maps-serp — Google Maps SERP (local pack tracking; needs keyword + location_code) local-finder-serp — local-finder variation SITE AUDIT DEEP DIVE (Tranche C) — most need `target` = a prior site-audit task_id from seo_audit_start: instant-page — fast single-page audit (needs url, no task_id) broken-links - the crawl's broken link edges (is_broken, or page_to_status_code >= 400), for broken-link building; same on_page/links source as internal-links, so it needs target = the task_id from seo_audit_start, NOT a url; returns link_from / link_to / text / page_to_status_code / type per edge. An empty result means none of the RESOLVED links were broken: a link whose target the crawl never fetched has page_to_status_code null and is counted neither way, so check total_items_count from internal-links before calling a site clean duplicate-content / duplicate-tags — content + meta dupes redirect-chains / non-indexable — crawl issues internal-links — link graph keyword-density — on-page term frequency BACKLINKS DEEP DIVE (Tranche D, needs target or domain): backlinks-timeseries — link velocity / growth & decay (use date_from + date_to) backlinks-anchors — anchor-text distribution backlinks-competitors — link-overlap-based competitor discovery backlinks-history — long-term link history bulk-page-summary — backlink summaries for many URLs at once (needs targets[]) REPUTATION / CONTENT ANALYSIS (Tranche F): sentiment-analysis — sentiment around a brand/term (needs keyword) content-mention-search — find web pages mentioning a term content-summary — aggregate sentiment + volume MERCHANT + APP DATA (Tranche G): amazon-products / google-shopping-products (needs query) amazon-reviews (needs target = ASIN) google-app-info / apple-app-info (needs app_id — package name for Play, numeric for Apple) AEO/GEO (answer-engine optimization): aeo-audit — multi-keyword feature-presence report (needs keywords[]; pass domain to check your own presence). PERSISTED to seo_serp_features + seo_featured_snippets so the dashboard + history queries work. For new code prefer the dedicated `seo_aeo_audit_run` tool (more knobs, clearer response shape). ai-keyword-volume — Google search volume for keywords (DataForSEO does NOT publish per-engine AI search volume; this is standard Google volume, useful as a proxy). LIGHTHOUSE: action='lighthouse' (needs url) — full Core Web Vitals + perf score.

tools.name: seo_run_audit
tools.description: Start a DataForSEO site crawl for an SEO tracking project and persist it as an audit row (site_audit_tasks). There is ONE crawl type: technical, content and mobile were never separate crawls, so there is no audit_type argument. Needs project_id from seo_list_projects (the SEO TRACKING project, not the website project); target_url defaults to https://<project domain>; max_crawl_pages defaults to 50 and clamps to 500. Returns 202 { data: { audit_id, task_id, target, status: 'queued', project_id, max_crawl_pages }, hint }; a `warning` with audit_id null means the crawl started but the row could not be saved (keep task_id). The crawl finishes asynchronously in 1 to 5 minutes: poll seo_audit_get with the audit_id (or task_id) until status is completed, then read `results` there. seo_audit_start is the same call. Metered per crawled page under the account's SEO research cap: 402 means the DataForSEO balance or cap is exhausted, 503 dataforseo_unconfigured means no credentials; neither means the site is clean.

tools.name: seo_schema_markup
tools.description: Read the stored structured-data analysis rows (seo_schema_markup: url, domain, has_schema, schema_types, is_valid, validation_errors, recommended_schema, status, analyzed_at), newest analysis first. Account-scoped, no project id: filter with domain (exact), has_schema and is_valid (STRING 'true' / 'false'), status, page, limit (max 100). Returns { data, pagination }. Rows are written by the analysis sweep for crawled pages; a page never analysed has no row, and nothing here generates schema. To read or write the JSON-LD a builder page actually carries use seo_page_schema_get / seo_page_schema_set.

tools.name: seo_serp_features
tools.description: Read the stored per-keyword SERP feature rows (seo_serp_features: which features appeared - featured snippet, people-also-ask, AI Overview, knowledge panel, local pack - and whether the account's domain holds the snippet), newest check first. Account-scoped, no project id: filter with keyword (contains), domain (contains), we_have_featured_snippet (STRING 'true' / 'false'), page, limit (max 100). Returns { data, pagination }. Rows are written by the AEO audit (seo_aeo_audit_run) and the analysis sweep, not by rank checks, so a keyword never audited has no row. Winnable snippets are seo_featured_snippets.

tools.name: seo_serp_get
tools.description: A DATABASE read of stored SERP analysis rows (seo_serp_analysis) for an SEO tracking project, newest first. Needs project_id from seo_list_projects; keyword narrows (contains), page and limit (max 100) paginate. Returns { data: [...], pagination }. No process on the platform writes this table today, so expect an empty list; it is not a live SERP and it does not call DataForSEO. For a LIVE SERP use seo_research action serp (keyword + location_code from serp_locations) or serp_organic_live_advanced; for Bing use seo_research action bing-serp.

tools.name: seo_sheet_add_rows
tools.description: Append rows to a tab of the account's ONE SEO workspace sheet (the same Sheet Canvas the dashboard SEO workspace shows; stored in account_ai_memory under _workspace:seo). Needs tab_name and rows (objects keyed by the tab's column names; a missing tab is created with those keys as columns). deliverable_slug is required by the schema for compatibility but no longer selects anything: there is one workspace per account and the value is only echoed back. Returns { data: { deliverable_id, deliverable_slug, tab_count, section_count, version } }. Appends only, never replaces; to reset a tab use seo_sheet_create_tab with the same name (idempotent replace).

tools.name: seo_sheet_create_tab
tools.description: Create a tab in a Sheet Canvas workspace. deliverable_slug is the workspace's slug (auto-created if missing). columns: [{id, name, type, width}] where type is one of text|number|metric|url|tag|status|date.

tools.name: seo_sync
tools.description: Run the data pull for the account's SEO connections NOW instead of waiting for the 6-hour cron: Search Console (daily totals, queries, pages), Bing Webmaster (stats, keywords) and Google Business Profile (reviews, insights). Optional connection_id (from seo_connections_list) limits it to one connection; full: true resets last_synced_at on the selected connections first, so GSC re-pulls its whole retention window (about 16 months) instead of the incremental window since the last sync. Returns { synced, total, full_resync, results: [{ id, platform, display_name, status: 'synced' | 'partial' | 'error' | 'skipped', actions_run }] }; 404 when no connection is active AND connection_status 'connected' (a 'pending' or 'error' row is skipped silently, so check seo_connections_health first). Takes up to two minutes. The rank tracker is NOT part of this: rankings are checked by the daily worker (seo_rankings_list shows last_checked_at).

tools.name: seo_task_changes
tools.description: Read what approving an SEO task's implementation would actually ship: the file list and per-file diff the coder turn wrote since it was dispatched, plus the Fly preview link where the change is already visible. Needs task_id (the seo_tasks id from seo_task_list / seo_task_get; the task must have gone through seo_task_implement). Returns { session_id, project_id, page_url, preview: { url, machine_status, last_activity_at } | null, publish_scope, state_fingerprint, since, files: [{ path, change: added | modified | deleted, version_id, version_number, created_at, commit_message, added_lines, removed_lines, old_lines, new_lines, rows (collapsed diff hunks), rows_truncated, diff_unavailable, detail }], truncation }; 404 when the task is not this account's or has no implementation session (run seo_task_implement first), 409 when the session has no dispatch timestamp (the window cannot be scoped). Read-only. Diff bodies are capped for very large turns while the line counts stay exact; publish_scope says when the deploy publishes from git and the DB diff is the wrong lane. Read this BEFORE agent_approval_approve; a one-line agent summary is not a review.

tools.name: seo_task_get
tools.description: Get one SEO/content pm_task with everything needed to decide on implementation: description, ai_instructions, the resolved page anchor (page_url), the linked website project, `implementable`, and the implement-rail state summary (session_id / dispatched_at / approved_at / deployment_id). For the live phase machine use seo_task_implement_status. Read-only.

tools.name: seo_task_implement
tools.description: Hand an SEO task to the coder agent for HEADLESS IMPLEMENTATION — the end state of this rail is CODE DEPLOYED TO THE CLIENT'S LIVE SITE. The agent edits the website project, typechecks, test-builds, then STAGES the production deploy behind the approval rail (it never ships on its own; approval happens via agent_approval_approve or the user's SEO workspace). TWO-STEP CONFIRM: the first call (without confirm) dispatches NOTHING — it returns { requires_confirm: true, preview } with the task title/description, target website project (name + domain), and resolved page anchor. Show it to the user, then repeat the IDENTICAL call with confirm: true (strict boolean) to dispatch the paid agent turn. Only open tasks (todo / queued / blocked / need_info) can be implemented; a running session 409s (never double-dispatches), an already-deployed task 409s. Billing gates match the interactive chat (402 when the AI budget or free daily limit is exhausted). After dispatch, poll seo_task_implement_status.

tools.name: seo_task_implement_status
tools.description: Consolidated status/result read for a task's implementation session. phase vocabulary: 'idle' (never dispatched) | 'running' | 'awaiting_approval' (a staged production deploy is waiting — the response carries its token/summary/expiry; approve via agent_approval_approve, reject via agent_approval_reject) | 'deploying' | 'completed' (deployed_at + deployment_url; the task auto-completes stamped with the DEPLOY time) | 'failed' (stage: agent | deploy, with the error). Performs the same status-sync writes as the dashboard (deployment linking, task auto-complete) — safe to poll.

tools.name: seo_task_list
tools.description: List the account's SEO/content pm_tasks — the implement-with-AI rail's task queue (audit findings, listings gaps, and digest items are filed here as tasks). Each row carries `implementable` (open status + linked website project) and an `implement` summary (dispatched_at / approved_at / deployment_id) when a coder session already ran. Filter by status (todo | queued | blocked | need_info | in_progress | done | cancelled), task_type ('seo' default | 'content' | 'all'), or website_project_id. Read-only.

tools.name: seo_topic_cluster_create
tools.description: Persist a hub-and-spoke topic cluster (seo_topic_clusters) — pillar page + supporting cluster pages/keywords for topical-authority planning. (domain, cluster_name) is unique per account (409 on duplicate). List existing clusters with seo_topic_clusters.

tools.name: seo_topic_cluster_delete
tools.description: Delete a saved topic cluster. Needs cluster_id from seo_topic_clusters. Returns { data: { deleted: true } }; 404 when the id is not on this account. Hard delete, no undo; the pillar page and cluster pages on the site are untouched. Confirm with the user before calling.

tools.name: seo_topic_cluster_get
tools.description: Fetch one saved topic cluster (seo_topic_clusters: domain, cluster_name, pillar_keyword, pillar_url, total_keywords, total_pages, total_traffic, avg_position, topical_authority_score, coverage_score, depth_score, cluster_keywords[], cluster_pages[], missing_subtopics[], competitor_authority, internal_link_score, linking_issues). Needs cluster_id from seo_topic_clusters (data[].id) or seo_topic_cluster_create. Returns { data: <row> }; 404 when the id is not on this account. Scores are stored values, not recomputed on read.

tools.name: seo_topic_cluster_update
tools.description: Update a saved topic cluster: cluster_name, pillar_keyword, pillar_url, total_keywords, total_pages, total_traffic, avg_position, topical_authority_score, coverage_score, depth_score, cluster_keywords, cluster_pages, missing_subtopics, competitor_authority, internal_link_score, linking_issues. Needs cluster_id from seo_topic_clusters; only the fields sent change. Returns { data: <the updated row> }; 404 when the id is not on this account. The array fields (cluster_keywords, cluster_pages, missing_subtopics, linking_issues) are full replacements; read the row first and send the whole list. The domain cannot be changed here.

tools.name: seo_topic_clusters
tools.description: List the hub-and-spoke topic clusters saved on the account (seo_topic_clusters: domain, cluster_name, pillar_keyword, pillar_url, total_keywords, total_pages, total_traffic, avg_position, topical_authority_score, coverage_score, depth_score, cluster_keywords[], cluster_pages[], missing_subtopics[], internal_link_score, linking_issues), ordered by topical_authority_score. Account-scoped: filter with domain (exact), search (cluster_name or pillar_keyword contains), page, limit (max 50). Returns { data, pagination }. Rows exist only because seo_topic_cluster_create (or the dashboard) saved them; the scores are whatever was stored, not recomputed. Use the returned id for seo_topic_cluster_get / seo_topic_cluster_update / seo_topic_cluster_delete.

tools.name: seo_track_keyword
tools.description: Start tracking a keyword's rank position over time for a target domain: creates the live-tracker row (website_rankings lane) the daily ranking worker checks AND queues the first check immediately, so rank data lands within minutes. Needs keyword and target_domain; location_code is a serp_locations code (2840 = United States, the default) and location_name is its human label. Returns 201 { data: <tracked_keywords row>, ranking: { id, already_tracked, current_rank, last_checked_at }, first_check: { queued, job_id } }; read history with seo_rankings_list view=history and the returned ranking.id. ranking_type='local' with business_name tracks the LOCAL PACK position; AI engines (chatgpt / perplexity / ai_overview / claude / gemini) track citation mentions and cost about $0.10 per keyword per engine per check. One call creates ONE lane (one engine, one device, one ranking_type); add or remove lanes for the same keyword with seo_rankings_platforms_set. The route derives a stable goal_id from (account, target_domain) when goal_id is omitted so keywords on the same domain group together; pass goal_id only to subdivide tracking within a domain. 409 when that keyword/domain/engine/location/device lane already exists.

tools.name: seo_tracked_keyword_delete
tools.description: Delete one tracked_keywords config row (the FK cascade takes its keyword_rank_history) and, when no other config row on the account still tracks the same keyword and domain, PAUSE every website_rankings lane for the pair (check_frequency 'paused'): the daily worker skips paused lanes, so checking and billing stop while the lanes and their website_ranking_history are PRESERVED. Sibling config rows leave the lanes running (lanes_paused: 0, explained in the note). Needs keyword_id from seo_tracked_keywords_list or seo_track_keyword (data.id). Returns { data: { deleted: true, lanes_paused }, note }; 404 when the id is not on this account. To start checking the keyword again later: re-track with seo_track_keyword (recreates the config row; the POST does not unpause existing lanes), then seo_tracked_keyword_update { tracking_frequency } to unpause every lane via the PATCH mirror - seo_rankings_platforms_set does NOT unpause existing lanes.

tools.name: seo_tracked_keyword_get
tools.description: Fetch one tracked_keywords CONFIG row (keyword, target_domain, target_url, search_engine, location_code, language_code, device_type, tracking_frequency, target_rank, tags, metadata, is_active) with its last 30 keyword_rank_history checks, PLUS the website_rankings lanes the daily worker actually checks for that keyword and domain: lanes: [{ id, search_engine, device_type, location_name, ranking_type, check_frequency, current_rank, previous_rank, last_checked_at }]. Needs keyword_id from seo_tracked_keywords_list or seo_track_keyword (data.id). Returns { data: <row + keyword_rank_history[]>, lanes: [...] }; 404 when the id is not on this account. lanes [] means nothing is being checked even though the config row exists (create lanes with seo_track_keyword or seo_rankings_platforms_set). Each lane id is the ranking_id seo_rankings_list view=history takes.

tools.name: seo_tracked_keyword_update
tools.description: Update one tracked keyword's config row AND mirror the check settings onto its website_rankings lanes: location_code (serp_locations code, 2840 = US), language_code, device_type (desktop | mobile), target_rank and tracking_frequency (daily, else weekly) are written to every lane for that keyword and domain, so the daily worker's next check uses them. is_active is the pause switch: false parks every lane at check_frequency 'paused' so the daily worker skips it and the spend stops, true resumes them at tracking_frequency, and both keep the config row and all rank history (prefer this to seo_tracked_keyword_delete, which destroys the row's keyword_rank_history). target_url and tags change the config row only (the worker never reads it), and search_engine changes the config row only because each lane IS an engine: add or remove engine lanes with seo_rankings_platforms_set. Needs keyword_id from seo_tracked_keywords_list plus at least one field (400 otherwise). Returns { data: <updated row>, lanes_updated: <number of lanes written>, lane_note? }; lanes_updated 0 with a lane_note means no lanes exist (nothing is being checked) or a device move collided with an existing lane for that device. 404 when the id is not on this account.

tools.name: seo_tracked_keywords_list
tools.description: List the tracked_keywords CONFIG rows for the account (keyword, target_domain, target_url, search_engine, location_code, language_code, device_type, tracking_frequency, target_rank, tags, is_active) with the last 7 keyword_rank_history checks attached to each. No ids needed; filter with domain (exact target_domain), search (keyword contains), is_active ("true"/"false"), tags (comma-separated, any match), page, limit (max 100). Returns { data: [...], pagination }. This is NOT the live rank tracker: positions the daily worker actually collects live in website_rankings and are read with seo_rankings_list; a keyword created through the dashboard can exist there with no row here. Use the returned id for seo_tracked_keyword_get / seo_tracked_keyword_update / seo_tracked_keyword_delete.

tools.name: seo_tracking_project_delete
tools.description: DESTRUCTIVE, CASCADES. Delete an SEO TRACKING project and, by FK cascade, every row that hangs off it: keyword_analysis (researched keywords), competitor_analysis, site_audits, serp_analysis, content_gaps, backlink_profiles and its backlinks, and domain_metrics. Needs project_id from seo_list_projects. Returns { success: true }; 404 when the id is not on this account. There is no undo and no soft delete. The live rank tracker (website_rankings lanes and their history) is NOT attached to this project and survives; the persisted site audits in site_audit_tasks also survive. To retire a project without losing its research, seo_tracking_project_update { is_active: false }. Confirm with the user before calling.

tools.name: seo_tracking_project_get
tools.description: Fetch one SEO TRACKING project (seo_projects) with its cached domain_metrics, the backlink_profiles summary (totals, dofollow/nofollow, new/lost 30d, toxic_score, link_velocity) and counts of keyword_analysis, competitor_analysis, site_audits, serp_analysis and content_gaps rows. Needs project_id from seo_list_projects. Returns { data: { id, name, domain, description, target_country, target_language, is_active, domain_metrics, backlink_profiles, counts } }; 404 when the id is not on this account. This is the SEO tracking project, not the website project: project settings for a built site are seo_project_get with the sites_list id.

tools.name: seo_tracking_project_update
tools.description: Update the config of an SEO TRACKING project: name, description, target_country, target_language, is_active. Needs project_id from seo_list_projects; only the fields sent change. Returns { data: <the updated seo_projects row> }; 404 when the id is not on this account. The domain cannot be changed (it is the project's identity; create a new project with seo_create_project). target_country / target_language are labels stored on the row ('United States', 'English'); they do not change the location_code of existing tracked keywords, which live on the keyword lanes.

tools.name: serp_locations
tools.description: Utility tool for serp_organic_live_advanced to get list of availible locations.

tools.name: serp_organic_live_advanced
tools.description: Get organic search results for a keyword in specified search engine

tools.name: serp_youtube_locations
tools.description: Utility tool to get list of available locations for: serp_youtube_organic_live_advanced, serp_youtube_video_info_live_advanced, serp_youtube_video_comments_live_advanced, serp_youtube_video_subtitles_live_advanced.

tools.name: serp_youtube_organic_live_advanced
tools.description: provides top 20 blocks of youtube search engine results for a keyword

tools.name: serp_youtube_video_comments_live_advanced
tools.description: provides data on the video comments you specify

tools.name: serp_youtube_video_info_live_advanced
tools.description: provides data on the video you specify

tools.name: serp_youtube_video_subtitles_live_advanced
tools.description: provides data on the video subtitles you specify

tools.name: shopify_admin
tools.description: Invoke a Shopify Admin API action via the builder's named-action proxy (the Admin token stays server-side). admin_action is the named handler (e.g. 'ping', 'get_shop', 'list_products', 'list_installed_apps', 'app_compat_check', 'create_product_draft', 'invalidate_cache'). params is the action-specific body.

tools.name: shopify_article_create
tools.description: Create a blog article. author_name is required because ArticleCreateInput.author is non-null. The schema declares NO default for isPublished, so published is sent explicitly and defaults to false here; published: true puts the article on the storefront at once.

tools.name: shopify_article_delete
tools.description: Permanently delete a blog article. Irreversible; returns the deleted article id. CONFIRM GATED: pass confirm: true or the call is refused, unrun, with the warning.

tools.name: shopify_article_get
tools.description: Fetch one blog article including its full HTML body. Returns null when the id does not exist on this shop.

tools.name: shopify_article_list
tools.description: List blog articles across all blogs, or one blog via blog_id. Uses the top-level articles connection because Blog.articles accepts neither query nor sortKey; blog_id becomes a blog_id: search term.

tools.name: shopify_article_update
tools.description: Update a blog article. Partial, but tags REPLACES the whole tag list. published: true makes it shopper-visible immediately; changing handle changes the live URL unless redirect_new_handle is set.

tools.name: shopify_blog_create
tools.description: Create a blog (a container for articles). A blog has no draft state; comment_policy defaults to the shop setting and MODERATED means shopper comments wait for comment_moderate.

tools.name: shopify_blog_delete
tools.description: Permanently delete a blog. Irreversible. The schema documents only that the blog is removed, not what becomes of the articles inside it, so move or export them first. Returns the deleted blog id. CONFIRM GATED: pass confirm: true or the call is refused, unrun, with the warning.

tools.name: shopify_blog_get
tools.description: Fetch one blog by id (title, handle, comment policy, template suffix, tags). Returns null when the id does not exist on this shop. Use article_list with a blog_id filter for its articles: Blog.articles accepts no query and no sortKey, so it cannot be filtered or sorted from here.

tools.name: shopify_blog_list
tools.description: List blogs (id, title, handle, commentPolicy). commentPolicy is MODERATED, CLOSED or AUTO_PUBLISHED and decides whether new shopper comments need comment_moderate.

tools.name: shopify_blog_update
tools.description: Update a blog. Partial. Changing handle moves every article URL under it, so pass redirect_new_handle and redirect_articles to have Shopify leave redirects behind.

tools.name: shopify_catalog_list
tools.description: List products from the connected store (handle, title, status, totalInventory aggregate, price, featured image). Use this to discover what to build a page around. For per-VARIANT stock counts use shopify_inventory_get. Convenience wrapper over shopify_admin(list_products).

tools.name: shopify_collection_create
tools.description: Creates a collection. Pass rule_set to make it SMART (appliedDisjunctively true = OR, false = AND) or product_ids to make it MANUAL. Two runtime traps the scope check cannot see: collectionCreate is PLAN-GATED and fails on Starter and Retail plans even with write_products granted, and the new collection is NOT visible on any sales channel because publishing needs write_publications, which Hiveku does not hold.

tools.name: shopify_collection_delete
tools.description: Deletes a collection. Irreversible: there is no undelete, the storefront URL 404s immediately, and any navigation menu or template pointing at it breaks. The products themselves are not deleted. Takes a wrapper input { id }, unlike the add/remove/reorder mutations which take bare arguments. CONFIRM GATED: pass confirm: true or the call is refused, unrun, with the warning.

tools.name: shopify_collection_get
tools.description: Reads one collection by id or by handle, with its first page of member products. ruleSet null means manual, non-null means smart, and the rule READ shape (conditionObject) cannot be fed back into collection_update, which takes conditionObjectId. Publication state is not returned; that needs read_product_listings, which Hiveku does not hold.

tools.name: shopify_collection_list
tools.description: Lists collections (Relay cursor paging, 250 max). ruleSet null means a manual collection, non-null means a smart one; there is no isSmartCollection boolean. sort_key is only ID, RELEVANCE, TITLE or UPDATED_AT (no CREATED_AT, no PRODUCTS_COUNT). Pass query: "collection_type:smart" or "collection_type:custom" to filter by kind. Publication state is not returned; that needs read_product_listings, which Hiveku does not hold.

tools.name: shopify_collection_products_add
tools.description: Adds products to a MANUAL collection via collectionAddProductsV2, never the V1 mutation, which aborts the whole batch on a single already-present product. Shoppers see the change as soon as the job runs; it is undone by collection_products_remove, which is why this is not confirm gated. Returns a Job: empty userErrors means Shopify ACCEPTED the work, not that it finished, so re-read the collection to confirm. Adding to a smart collection is refused by Shopify because its membership comes from its rules.

tools.name: shopify_collection_products_remove
tools.description: Removes products from a MANUAL collection. Shopify does NOT validate that the products are in the collection or that they exist at all, so empty userErrors proves nothing about what was removed; re-read the collection to confirm. Returns a Job: empty userErrors means ACCEPTED, not finished.

tools.name: shopify_collection_products_reorder
tools.description: Reorders products inside a collection. Only works when the collection sortOrder is MANUAL; on any other sort order Shopify rejects it. new_position is ZERO-BASED and is evaluated AFTER the earlier moves in the same call, so positions shift as the list is rebuilt. Sent as an UnsignedInt64 string. Returns a Job: empty userErrors means ACCEPTED, not finished.

tools.name: shopify_collection_update
tools.description: Updates a collection, including converting it to smart by sending rule_set (appliedDisjunctively true = OR, false = AND). rule_set REPLACES the whole rule list, so send the full desired set. product_ids is REFUSED here: Shopify accepts CollectionInput.products only on collectionCreate, so sending it would return success having changed no membership; use collection_products_add / collection_products_remove instead. Changing a smart collection rule_set re-evaluates membership ASYNCHRONOUSLY, so a read straight afterwards can still show the old members. Changing handle moves the live storefront URL; redirect_new_handle leaves a redirect behind. A rule_set read from collection_get cannot be resent unchanged, because the read exposes conditionObject and the input takes conditionObjectId.

tools.name: shopify_comment_list
tools.description: List shopper comments on blog articles with their moderation status (PENDING, UNAPPROVED, PUBLISHED, SPAM, REMOVED). Author email and commenter IP are protected customer data and are not returned.

tools.name: shopify_comment_moderate
tools.description: Moderate one article comment: approve PUBLISHES it publicly on the storefront under the article, spam hides it, not_spam un-marks spam and returns it to the pending queue without publishing. Not confirm gated because every decision is reversible by another decision: approve is undone by spam. There is no comment_delete here; deletion is the one irreversible move and it is deliberately not exposed.

tools.name: shopify_connect_start
tools.description: STEP 1 of connecting a store. Generate a Shopify authorize URL the USER opens in their own browser to approve the connection (you can't approve it for them — it's the merchant's Shopify consent screen). Prereq: the account needs a Shopify OAuth app (bring-your-own from the customer's Shopify Partners dashboard). Find one with oauth_app_list(provider='shopify'); register one with oauth_app_create(provider='shopify', products=['shopify_storefront'], client_id, client_secret) if none. Returns 412 code='no_oauth_app' if missing. intent_type: shopify_project_connect (bind to one project — pass project_id; this is the Ecommerce-tab case), shopify_account_connect (account default), or shopify_reconnect (re-auth an existing connection — pass connection_id). Returns data.setup_url (hand to user) + data.callback_url (must be in the Shopify app's Allowed redirection URLs). After the user approves, poll shopify_connection_status until the store appears.

tools.name: shopify_connection_status
tools.description: STEP 2 (poll). List the account's Shopify connections — the target after shopify_connect_start. Pass shop_domain to filter to one store; poll until a row appears with disconnected_at=null (that means the user finished approving). Returns sanitized rows only (shop_domain, shop_name, shop_id, scope, purpose, installed_at, disconnected_at, is_dev_store) — never tokens.

tools.name: shopify_customer_create
tools.description: Create a customer. Email marketing consent requires email and SMS consent requires phone in the same call. Addresses are not settable here, CustomerInput has no address field. Shopify sends the shopper nothing; no invite or activation email is triggered.

tools.name: shopify_customer_get
tools.description: One customer with addresses, amountSpent, tags, tax exemptions and email marketing consent. Name, email, phone and address need Shopify Level 2 protected customer data approval and are null without it. Returns null when the id does not exist.

tools.name: shopify_customer_list
tools.description: Page the customer list (Relay cursor, 250 max, no offset). Name, email, phone and address are protected customer data: without Shopify Level 2 approval they come back null with no error. Orders are not included, that needs read_orders.

tools.name: shopify_customer_marketing_consent_set
tools.description: Set a customer's email and/or SMS marketing consent through the dedicated mutations customerEmailMarketingConsentUpdate and customerSmsMarketingConsentUpdate. Split out of customer_update deliberately: this writes a CONSENT RECORD about a real person and can overwrite an opt-out, so it is confirm gated while ordinary profile edits are not. Only the settable states are accepted (NOT_SUBSCRIBED, PENDING, SUBSCRIBED, UNSUBSCRIBED); REDACTED and INVALID are states Shopify assigns itself. marketingState is NON-NULL on both consent inputs, so an opt-in level sent without a state is a validation error, not a partial update. Sends only the half you supply, and returns the resulting consent for each. It does NOT email anyone: nothing in this registry puts a message in a shopper inbox. CONFIRM GATED: pass confirm: true or the call is refused, unrun, with the warning.

tools.name: shopify_customer_update
tools.description: Update a customer. tags REPLACES the whole tag list, use tagsAdd/tagsRemove for an incremental change. Setting email or SMS marketing consent changes what a real shopper receives, and the matching email or phone must already be on the record.

tools.name: shopify_eject_manifest
tools.description: READ-ONLY. Returns a structured migration plan for moving this project off the Hiveku Shopify storefront to a stand-alone Hydrogen + Oxygen repo: what would be transformed, and where. It changes NOTHING -- the plan is computed on demand from the current code versions, nothing is written, and no eject is performed (the eject runner itself is not built). Use it to show a merchant what leaving would involve.

tools.name: shopify_file_list
tools.description: Lists Shopify Files (content library images, videos and generic files) with an optional Shopify search query. Fields differ by kind, so images, generic files and videos each carry their own extra keys. Relay pagination only, 250 max.

tools.name: shopify_inventory_get
tools.description: Per-VARIANT inventory for the connected store — what you need to build an inventory-aware page/funnel (list_products only gives the product-level totalInventory aggregate). Pass params.handle for one product, or params.first (1-50) for the latest N products. Returns each product's variants with inventoryQuantity, price, sku, title, options. Live read via the store's Admin API (token stays server-side). NOTE: the deployed page reads live quantityAvailable through the scaffolded Storefront client — this tool is for the agent to reason about stock while building.

tools.name: shopify_metafield_definition_create
tools.description: Create a metafield definition for one owner type. Needs write access to that owner (write_products, write_customers, write_content), so the union is declared and the per-owner scope is enforced in the call. `type` is fixed at creation and cannot be changed later, and every metafield stored under this namespace/key must match it.

tools.name: shopify_metafield_definition_delete
tools.description: Delete a metafield definition by id. With delete_all_associated_metafields true this also destroys EVERY metafield stored under that definition on every owner, permanently and with no undo, which is why it is confirm gated. The definition is read first so the owner type is known: it needs write access to that owner (write_products, write_customers, write_content), the union is declared and the exact scope is enforced before the delete runs. CONFIRM GATED: pass confirm: true or the call is refused, unrun, with the warning.

tools.name: shopify_metafield_definition_list
tools.description: Metafield definitions for ONE owner type, Relay paged. ownerType is required by Shopify and there is no all-owners listing, so call this once per owner type. The definition needs read access to its owner type, so the read union is declared and the exact scope is enforced per call.

tools.name: shopify_metafield_definition_update
tools.description: Update a metafield definition, identified by owner_type plus namespace and key rather than by id. `type` is NOT updatable and is not accepted here. Needs write access to the owner type (write_products, write_customers, write_content), declared as a union and enforced per owner in the call. Tightening validations returns a validationJob: existing metafields are re-checked asynchronously, so an empty userErrors means accepted, not finished.

tools.name: shopify_metafields_delete
tools.description: Permanently delete metafields by owner id, namespace and key. The values are gone: there is no undo and no version history, so this is confirm gated. Like metafieldsSet it carries no scope of its own and needs write access to the OWNER (write_products, write_customers, write_content), enforced per call. Returns one result PER REQUESTED metafield with deleted true or false, plus deleted_count and not_found_count: Shopify reports a metafield that did not exist as a null in position, NOT as an error, so a call that deleted nothing otherwise looks identical to one that deleted everything. ORDER, DRAFTORDER, DISCOUNT, LOCATION, MARKET and COMPANY owners are refused because Hiveku never requests those write scopes. CONFIRM GATED: pass confirm: true or the call is refused, unrun, with the warning.

tools.name: shopify_metafields_get
tools.description: Metafields on one owner (PRODUCT, COLLECTION, CUSTOMER, PAGE, ARTICLE, BLOG), Relay paged, 250 max per page. Metafields carry no scope of their own, so the owner type decides the scope (products/collections read_products, customers read_customers, pages/articles/blogs read_content). The exact one is enforced per call and named in the error, so nothing is declared statically. An EMPTY result can mean another app owns them: app-reserved namespaces are invisible to every other app regardless of scope.

tools.name: shopify_metafields_set
tools.description: Create or overwrite up to 25 metafields on owners of one type (metafieldsSet is hard capped at 25 per call). `type` is required and must match any existing definition exactly or Shopify refuses the write in userErrors. metafieldsSet has no scope of its own: it needs write access to the OWNER (write_products, write_customers, write_content), and the one that applies is enforced per call and named in the error; ORDER, DRAFTORDER, DISCOUNT, LOCATION, MARKET and COMPANY owners are refused because Hiveku never requests those write scopes. Omitting namespace stores the value in the app-reserved namespace, where no other app can see it.

tools.name: shopify_order_fulfillments
tools.description: Shipments for one order: status, tracking company/number/url, origin address and the fulfilled line items. Fulfillment and FulfillmentTrackingInfo are readable under read_orders; the FulfillmentOrder objects behind them are NOT - those need the fulfillment-order scopes Hiveku does not hold - so this shows what shipped, never what is assigned or holdable. read_orders reaches ONLY the last 60 days and an older order comes back null with no error; older orders need read_all_orders (Partner Dashboard approval, not held) and the truncation is SILENT. Customer name, email, phone and shipping/billing address are protected customer data needing Level 2 approval and can be null even with the scope granted. Fulfillment location and fulfillment service are omitted (read_locations / the fulfillments scope family). Accepts a numeric id or a full gid.

tools.name: shopify_order_get
tools.description: One order with line items, totals, shipping line and the customer block. read_orders reaches ONLY the last 60 days, so an order older than that returns null rather than an error: older orders need read_all_orders (Partner Dashboard approval, not held) and the truncation is SILENT. Customer name, email, phone and shipping/billing address are protected customer data needing Level 2 approval and can be null on a call that fully succeeded. Accepts a numeric id or a full gid. Line items are Relay-paginated at 250 max; lineItems.pageInfo.hasNextPage true means the order has more lines than were returned. Fulfillment orders, returns and inventory are NOT included - they need scopes Hiveku does not hold.

tools.name: shopify_order_list
tools.description: List orders with totals, status and customer block. read_orders reaches ONLY the last 60 days; older orders need read_all_orders (Shopify Partner Dashboard approval, not held) and the cut-off is SILENT, so a short list is not proof an order is missing. Customer name, email, phone and shipping/billing address are protected customer data needing Level 2 approval and can be null even though the scope is granted. The query argument takes Shopify order search syntax: financial_status:paid|pending|refunded|partially_refunded|authorized|voided, fulfillment_status:fulfilled|unfulfilled|partial|restocked, status:open|closed|cancelled, created_at:>2026-01-01, updated_at:<2026-02-01, tag:vip, plus name:, email:, sku:, AND/OR/NOT. Relay cursors only (max 250 per page, no offset): pass the returned endCursor as the after argument.

tools.name: shopify_order_transactions
tools.description: Payment transactions and refunds for one order, with the amounts captured, refunded and still outstanding. OrderTransaction and Refund are both covered by read_orders alone. read_orders reaches ONLY the last 60 days, so an older order returns null rather than an error - older orders need read_all_orders (Partner Dashboard approval, not held) and the cut-off is SILENT. Customer name, email, phone and shipping/billing address are protected customer data needing Level 2 approval and can be null even with the scope granted. Card and gateway payloads (paymentDetails, receiptJson) and the transaction location are NOT returned. Accepts a numeric id or a full gid.

tools.name: shopify_page_create
tools.description: Create an online store page. Created as a DRAFT unless you pass published: true. Shopify itself does the opposite: PageCreateInput.isPublished defaults to TRUE when no publish date is given, so a page created through the raw API is live the instant the call returns. This action always sends the field explicitly and defaults it to false, so an agent cannot publish to a client storefront by omission. Pass published: true to go live; page_update flips it back.

tools.name: shopify_page_delete
tools.description: Permanently delete an online store page. Irreversible; returns the deleted page id. CONFIRM GATED: pass confirm: true or the call is refused, unrun, with the warning.

tools.name: shopify_page_get
tools.description: Fetch one online store page including its full HTML body. Returns null when the id does not exist on this shop.

tools.name: shopify_page_list
tools.description: List online store pages (id, title, handle, isPublished, publishedAt). Relay cursor paging only, 250 max per page, no offset.

tools.name: shopify_page_update
tools.description: Update an online store page. Partial: only the fields you pass change. Changing handle changes the live URL, so pass redirect_new_handle: true to have Shopify leave a redirect from the old one.

tools.name: shopify_product_create
tools.description: Create a product. ProductCreateInput accepts no variants, images or ProductInput fields; Shopify ALWAYS auto-creates one standalone variant, so real variants need a following productVariantsBulkCreate with strategy REMOVE_STANDALONE_VARIANT or the product keeps a junk variant. The new product is on NO sales channel: publishing needs write_publications, which Hiveku does not hold.

tools.name: shopify_product_delete
tools.description: Delete a product permanently, with its variants and media. Irreversible; requires confirm: true. Runs synchronously so the deleted id comes back on this call. CONFIRM GATED: pass confirm: true or the call is refused, unrun, with the warning.

tools.name: shopify_product_duplicate
tools.description: Duplicate a product under a new title. The copy defaults to DRAFT unless new_status says otherwise, and is on NO sales channel: publishing needs write_publications, which Hiveku does not hold. Image copying returns a Job, so imageJob.done false means the images are still copying.

tools.name: shopify_product_get
tools.description: One product by id or by handle (exactly one), with options and the first page of variants. Publication state is NOT returned: resourcePublications needs read_product_listings, which Hiveku does not hold, and selecting it would fail the whole query.

tools.name: shopify_product_media_add
tools.description: Attach images, video or 3D models to a product from a PUBLIC https URL. Uses productUpdate(product:{id}, media:[...]) because productCreateMedia is deprecated in favour of productUpdate/productSet. Ingest is ASYNC: no error means accepted, not processed, so re-read Media.status until it is READY (FAILED carries mediaErrors). A file that is not publicly reachable cannot be uploaded here, because the stagedUploadsCreate flow needs a multipart byte POST this JSON proxy cannot make.

tools.name: shopify_product_media_delete
tools.description: Permanently delete media from a product. Reports failures on mediaUserErrors, not userErrors. Irreversible and shopper-visible, so it requires confirm: true. Non-image media ids must be passed as a full gid. CONFIRM GATED: pass confirm: true or the call is refused, unrun, with the warning.

tools.name: shopify_product_media_reorder
tools.description: Reorder a product's media. The mutation argument is id, not productId, and newPosition is UnsignedInt64 which must be sent as a JSON STRING. Returns a Job: empty mediaUserErrors means ACCEPTED, not finished, so poll job.done or re-read the media order. Position 0 is the featured image, so this is shopper-visible.

tools.name: shopify_product_media_update
tools.description: Update alt text or the preview image of existing product media. Reports failures on mediaUserErrors, not userErrors (the userErrors field on this payload is deprecated). A changed previewImageSource is re-ingested ASYNC, so re-read Media.status. Non-image media ids must be passed as a full gid, since a bare number is assumed to be a MediaImage.

tools.name: shopify_product_option_update
tools.description: Rename, reposition or edit the values of ONE option. The mutation is productOptionUpdate, singular, and takes exactly one option. variantStrategy MANAGE lets Shopify create and delete variants to match the new value set, so deleting a value with MANAGE DELETES ITS VARIANTS; LEAVE_AS_IS refuses the change instead. Confirm gated for that reason: its siblings product_options_delete and variants_bulk_delete are gated and this destroys variants just as permanently. CONFIRM GATED: pass confirm: true or the call is refused, unrun, with the warning.

tools.name: shopify_product_options_create
tools.description: Add one or more options (Size, Color) to a product. variantStrategy LEAVE_AS_IS keeps the existing variants and only defines the option; CREATE expands the catalog into every new combination, which can multiply the variant count and is shopper-visible at once.

tools.name: shopify_product_options_delete
tools.description: Delete options from a product. strategy DEFAULT destroys the variants that used the option, POSITION keeps the first value, NON_DESTRUCTIVE refuses rather than losing variants. Irreversible and shopper-visible, so it requires confirm: true. CONFIRM GATED: pass confirm: true or the call is refused, unrun, with the warning.

tools.name: shopify_product_options_reorder
tools.description: Reorder a product's options and, optionally, the values inside each one. Order is shopper-visible: option 1 is the first selector on the product page. Identify each option by id or by name, and pass the full ordered list.

tools.name: shopify_product_set
tools.description: Create or fully replace a product in one call. FULL REPLACE: anything omitted is deleted, so send the complete desired state. Target an existing product with product_id or handle; omit both to create. ProductSetInput carries NO id field, so identity comes from the identifier argument. Requires confirm: true. CONFIRM GATED: pass confirm: true or the call is refused, unrun, with the warning.

tools.name: shopify_product_update
tools.description: Update a product by id. ProductUpdateInput accepts no variants, images or options. tags REPLACES the entire tag list, so use tags_add / tags_remove for incremental tag changes.

tools.name: shopify_scaffold_compat
tools.description: Pre-flight a storefront scaffold BEFORE writing files: reports the project's router type, path aliases, Tailwind presence, and any route collisions for the given feature. Call this before shopify_storefront_scaffold to avoid clobbering existing routes.

tools.name: shopify_segment_create
tools.description: Create a customer segment from a ShopifyQL segment query, for example email_subscription_status = 'SUBSCRIBED'. segmentCreate takes bare name and query arguments, not an input wrapper. A bad query comes back as a userError, not a crash.

tools.name: shopify_segment_delete
tools.description: Delete a customer segment. Irreversible: the segment and its query are gone and every campaign or automation targeting it loses its audience. Customers themselves are not touched. Requires confirm: true. CONFIRM GATED: pass confirm: true or the call is refused, unrun, with the warning.

tools.name: shopify_segment_list
tools.description: Page customer segments (Relay cursor, 250 max, no offset). Each segment carries its ShopifyQL query string. Segments hold no customer data themselves, but the members behind them are protected customer data and need Level 2 approval to read.

tools.name: shopify_segment_members_list
tools.description: Page the customers currently in a segment, plus the segment total. A plain read: customerSegmentMembers accepts segmentId directly at 2025-10, so no customerSegmentMembersQueryCreate call is needed. Each node id is a CustomerSegmentMember gid, not a Customer gid. Name, email, phone and address are protected customer data and are null without Shopify Level 2 approval.

tools.name: shopify_segment_update
tools.description: Rename a segment or replace its ShopifyQL query. Both are optional; omitting one leaves it alone. Replacing the query silently changes who every campaign pointed at this segment will reach, since membership is evaluated at send time.

tools.name: shopify_status
tools.description: Get the project's effective Shopify connection (override or account default), with optional catalog sample.

tools.name: shopify_storefront_scaffold
tools.description: STEP 3 — write storefront feature files into the project (builder_code_versions) so the page can render live products + inventory. Idempotent (existing files skipped unless overwrite=true); pass dry_run=true first to preview the file plan + compat. Features: 'storefront-client' (the live Storefront API client exposing quantityAvailable — scaffold this first), 'product-detail-route' (full PDP flow: client + revalidate + reviews), 'cart', 'sitemap', 'revalidate-route' (cache-bust receiver for product/inventory webhooks), 'customer-account', 'reviews', 'subscriptions'. After scaffolding, the coder/deploy pipeline picks up the new files; use preview_sync / deploy to make them live.

tools.name: shopify_tags_add
tools.description: Add tags to a taggable Shopify object WITHOUT replacing the existing list (product_update and the other update actions REPLACE the whole tag list, which is why this exists). The scopes array is empty because the scope Shopify checks is the WRITE scope of whatever owner_id points at, which is not known until the call: it is enforced per call instead, and the error names the one missing scope. Products and collections need write_products, customers write_customers, pages/articles/blogs write_content. Orders, draft orders and companies are taggable in Shopify but unreachable here, because Hiveku never requests write_orders, write_draft_orders or write_companies; passing such a gid is refused with that named. Pass owner_id as a full gid, or as a numeric id plus owner_type.

tools.name: shopify_tags_remove
tools.description: Remove tags from a taggable Shopify object, leaving its other tags alone. Tag removal is CASE-INSENSITIVE but tags are stored with their original casing, so a read-back compared against the string you sent can differ. The scopes array is empty because the scope Shopify checks is the WRITE scope of whatever owner_id points at, enforced per call with the missing one named: products and collections write_products, customers write_customers, pages/articles/blogs write_content. Orders, draft orders and companies are taggable in Shopify but unreachable here and are refused by name. Pass owner_id as a full gid, or as a numeric id plus owner_type.

tools.name: shopify_theme_file_delete
tools.description: Permanently deletes one file from a theme (themeFilesDelete), one file per call. The theme ROLE IS READ BEFORE THE DELETE: if it is MAIN, the published theme, the call is REFUSED unless you pass allow_live_theme: true, because the deletion is live to every shopper at once and can break the storefront. Theme-code writes also need a Shopify- granted app exemption on top of write_themes and whether Hiveku holds it is UNVERIFIED, so this can 403 while a scope audit reads green. CONFIRM GATED: pass confirm: true or the call is refused, unrun, with the warning.

tools.name: shopify_theme_file_get
tools.description: Returns one theme file by exact filename, body included. The body union is normalised to { type, text, base64, url }: large or binary files come back as BASE64 or as a short-lived URL the caller must fetch itself, not as text.

tools.name: shopify_theme_file_list
tools.description: Lists the files of one theme (filename, content type, size, md5). Pass include_body to also return each file body, normalised from its three-member union into { type, text, base64, url }; it is off by default because a page of liquid bodies is megabytes. Relay pagination only, 250 max.

tools.name: shopify_theme_file_upsert
tools.description: Creates or OVERWRITES one file in a theme (themeFilesUpsert), one file per call. The theme ROLE IS READ BEFORE THE WRITE: if it is MAIN, the published theme, the call is REFUSED unless you pass allow_live_theme: true, because that edit is live to every shopper at once with no undo. Target an UNPUBLISHED or DEVELOPMENT theme; theme_list shows the roles. Needs a Shopify-granted app exemption on top of write_themes and whether Hiveku holds it is UNVERIFIED, so this can 403 while a scope audit reads green. Returns a Job: no userErrors means ACCEPTED, not finished. CONFIRM GATED: pass confirm: true or the call is refused, unrun, with the warning.

tools.name: shopify_theme_list
tools.description: Lists online store themes with role, processing state and timestamps. Exactly one theme has role MAIN and that is the published, shopper-visible one. Relay pagination only, 250 max.

tools.name: shopify_variant_search
tools.description: Find variants across the whole catalog by SKU, barcode, title or product. Relay pagination only, 250 max per page, no offset. inventoryQuantity is included; per- location inventory is not (read_inventory is not granted).

tools.name: shopify_variants_bulk_create
tools.description: Create variants on a product. productCreate always auto-creates one standalone variant, so pass strategy REMOVE_STANDALONE_VARIANT on the first real batch or the product keeps a junk variant. Per-location stock cannot be set here (write_inventory is not granted), and new variants are not visible on any sales channel until the product is published (write_publications is not granted).

tools.name: shopify_variants_bulk_delete
tools.description: Permanently delete variants from a product. The Shopify argument is spelled variantsIds, not variantIds. Irreversible and shopper-visible, so it requires confirm: true. CONFIRM GATED: pass confirm: true or the call is refused, unrun, with the warning.

tools.name: shopify_variants_bulk_update
tools.description: Update existing variants on a product. allowPartialUpdates defaults to FALSE, so one bad variant rolls the whole batch back; pass allow_partial_updates true to keep the good ones. Every variant entry must carry its id.

tools.name: shopify_variants_reorder
tools.description: Reorder the variants of one product. Positions are 1-based and shopper-visible immediately, since position drives which variant a product page selects first.

tools.name: shopify_webhook_create
tools.description: Create a shop-scoped webhook subscription delivering one topic to an https callback URL. Refuses, by name, any topic whose scope Hiveku does not request or this store did not grant, since Shopify permits a topic only when the app holds its scope. The created subscription is shop-scoped, so it is invisible to any app-scoped subscription declared in the app TOML and vice versa: an empty webhook_list does NOT mean no webhooks are running. Shopify also silently DELETES subscriptions whose scope is later revoked, so a scope downgrade kills this subscription with no error anywhere. CONFIRM GATED: pass confirm: true or the call is refused, unrun, with the warning.

tools.name: shopify_webhook_delete
tools.description: Delete one shop-scoped webhook subscription by id, after reporting the topic and endpoint it was serving. CONFIRM-gated: deleting one of Hiveku's own standard topics breaks order ingest and the review-request flow (orders/create, orders/updated), storefront cache invalidation (products/create, products/update, products/delete, collections/update) or uninstall detection (app/uninstalled), with no error anywhere. Only shop-scoped subscriptions are deletable here, so an app-scoped subscription declared in the app TOML survives this and keeps delivering; equally, Shopify silently DELETES subscriptions whose scope is later revoked, so a subscription can vanish without anyone calling this. CONFIRM GATED: pass confirm: true or the call is refused, unrun, with the warning.

tools.name: shopify_webhook_list
tools.description: List the shop-scoped webhook subscriptions on the connected store (topic, delivery endpoint, format, filter, API version), optionally filtered by topic. Returns ONLY shop-scoped subscriptions, never the app-scoped ones declared in the app TOML, so an empty result does NOT mean no webhooks are running. Shopify also silently DELETES subscriptions whose scope is later revoked, so a scope downgrade kills live webhooks with no error anywhere and they just vanish from this list.

tools.name: site_clone
tools.description: Duplicate a website project so you can experiment without affecting the original. Copies the current file tree (every is_current builder_code_versions row), project assets, settings, and navigation. The new project starts in draft status with a fresh subdomain — use preview_start on the returned project_id to spin up its Fly preview. What's NOT copied: the Supabase database, CloudFront / Cloudflare DNS / S3 hosting bucket / ACM cert, GitHub connection, custom domain. Each of those needs to be provisioned separately on the clone if the experiment needs them. copy_assets modes: • "reference" (default) — clone's asset rows point at the SAME S3 objects as the source. Cheap + instant. Best for short-lived experiments. Caveat: deleting an S3 object orphans the other side. • "duplicate" — re-uploads every asset under the clone's prefix. Slower + uses 2x storage, but the clone is fully independent. Use cases: try a risky refactor on the clone first, A/B variants, sandbox a destructive prompt, hand a clone to a different agent without touching production work.

tools.name: site_create
tools.description: Create a new website project. Three flavors: • BLANK: `{name, project_type?: "nextjs"|"vite"|"static-html", creation_mode: "blank"}` — bare Next.js+Tailwind scaffold (includes the premium section kit). • TEMPLATE: `{name, creation_mode: "template", template_id: "<id-from-templates_list>"}` — seeds the project with the template's sections, components, and example pages. • IMPORT: `{name, creation_mode: "import", project_type}` — for BRINGING AN EXISTING APP. The preview container seeds NOTHING (no starter kit, no section files that would break your build); push the code with project_import_presign → PUT tarball → project_import_finalize, then preview_start. Call templates_list first to see what template IDs are valid. Unknown template_id returns 400. The project's subdomain is auto-generated from the name + a random suffix; the live preview becomes available at hvk-<12-hex>.preview.hiveku.com (check sites_list for the canonical URL once created). Default project_type is "nextjs" when omitted.
