Any text is stored, and the CRM picker only has labels for connected, left_voicemail, no_answer, busy, wrong_number, callback_requested, not_interested, qualified and unqualified, so anything else renders as an unstyled chip with a BLANK label, which reads as a broken UI rather than as a bad value. This also does NOT touch voice_calls.disposition, the phone system's own answered/voicemail/missed/ai_handled/abandoned signal, so call lists, filters and voice_calls_export_csv never reflect what you set here. direction is optional and matters more than it looks on the create path: omit it on an outbound call and the activity is titled 'Inbound call' and the contact is resolved from the CALLER leg, which is your own DID, so the wrap-up links to the wrong contact or to none. The peer match is a last-7-digit contains ordered newest-first, so two calls with the same person inside that 4 minute window resolve to the newest one and you can tag the wrong leg. 422 nothing to save when neither a truthy disposition nor a non-blank notes is supplied (an empty string or whitespace-only notes counts as absent); 422 peer and startedAtIso required when peer holds fewer than 7 digits or startedAtIso is unparsable. Sending only notes leaves any existing disposition intact and vice versa, but a supplied notes REPLACES the old note wholesale, it does not append. Asymmetry worth knowing: on the CREATE path notes is written to BOTH metadata.user_notes and the activity's body column and the subject picks up the resolved contact name, while on the MERGE path only metadata changes and the existing subject and body are left alone. Because a service key has no builder profile the created activity has owner_id null, and rep-scoped CRM views (leaderboard, My Queue, contact filters) silently skip owner-null call activities. Unlike the dashboard PATCH /api/crm/activities/[id] this route writes no user_disposition_at, user_disposition_by or user_notes_updated_at, so the wrap-up shows up with no author and no timestamp, and it calls no audit helper, so nothing records that an agent set it. Safe against retries: the create is keyed on call_uuid and linked back onto the call, so a second identical request merges instead of duplicating, and the later recording worker deliberately copies user_disposition and user_notes forward, so what you write here survives post-processing. 402 voice_not_enabled when the paid Voice add-on is off.

tools.name: voice_call_get
tools.description: One call by voice_calls.id, for a deep link into a call older than the newest page voice_calls_list returns. Returns { call: { id, direction, from_number, to_number, peer_name, contact_id, started_at, answered_at, ended_at, duration_seconds, hangup_cause, recording_url, has_recording, recording_transcript, status } }. Three traps answer 200 having told you nothing true: recording_url is HARDCODED null on every response (has_recording is the real signal, and playable audio only comes from voice_recording_url_get), recording_transcript carries voice_calls.ai_summary, an AI-written prose summary, NOT the transcript (use voice_call_transcript_get for the actual words), and status is derived, so a call still ringing (no disposition, no ended_at) reads 'failed' while an ai_handled call reads 'completed'. from_number/to_number coerce a NULL number to the empty string, not to null, so an anonymous or missing caller ID reads as ''. This projection also drops most of the row: voice_calls_list returns raw DB rows with from_e164/to_e164 plus billable_seconds, ai_sentiment, spotted_keywords, attribution_json, utm_campaign, tracking_source, call_uuid, project_id, pool_session_id, queue_id, crm_activity_id and voicemail_read_at, none of which appear here. peer_name/contact_id come from a last-7-digit CRM match against non-deleted contacts, so two numbers sharing a tail attach the same contact and an archived contact reads as no match. The response carries PII: the far-party number, a named CRM contact, and an AI summary of a recorded conversation. 404 not_found is also the cross-tenant answer, since the lookup is scoped to the key's account. 402 voice_not_enabled when the paid Voice add-on is off, even though voice_calls_list answers fine on the same account because that route carries no plan gate.

tools.name: voice_call_originate
tools.description: RINGS A REAL PHONE. FreeSWITCH rings the chosen extension's physical device first; the moment a human answers it dials to_e164 - usually a customer's handset - and bridges the two legs. There is no draft, no confirmation step downstream of this call, and no recall once the extension is ringing. The bridged call BILLS PER MINUTE on the carrier and its outbound seconds COUNT TOWARD THE TENANT'S DAILY TOLL-FRAUD CAP, so a loop of originates can spend real money and then trip the cap for every other caller on the account. Place a call only when a human asked for that specific call. from_extension_id is REQUIRED: a service key has no extension of its own, so you must name which extension rings (get ids from voice_extensions_list), and it is resolved strictly on this account - a foreign or unknown id is 404 extension_not_found. Refusals, in the order enforced: 402 voice_not_enabled; 422 invalid_body; 403 blocked_number when to_e164 is on the account's outbound blocklist (matched with and without '+'; nothing is dialed); 404 extension_not_found; 409 browser_softphone_only for a softphone_desktop extension (browser softphones are refused on this path by design - the human is already at the keyboard, the WebRTC dock dials directly); 409 external_number_not_originatable for an external_number shell (no SIP registration, an originate would ring nothing and die at leg A); 403 not_your_number when an explicit caller_id_e164 is not an ACTIVE number owned by this account - checked here BEFORE the carrier, stricter than the dashboard path, and the value actually presented is the stored DID, never your raw string; 409 anonymous_not_supported_here when the extension is set to withhold its number and you sent no caller_id_e164; 409 no_caller_id when the tenant owns no usable DID at all. When caller_id_e164 is omitted the presented number is picked by chain: the extension's admin-assigned number, else a DID sharing the recipient's NANP area code (tracking/pool DIDs are never presented - that poisons attribution and callbacks die in an unrouted voicemail), else the 'main' DID, else any active DID. Returns { call_uuid, ringing_extension, caller_id }: call_uuid is the FreeSWITCH channel uuid of the RINGING leg (matches voice_calls.call_uuid) - a 200 means the PBX accepted the originate and the extension is now ringing, NOT that anyone answered or that the customer was reached; follow the outcome with voice_call_get. A 503 voice_server_error means the PBX did not confirm - do not blind-retry, the first attempt may still be ringing a phone. Because an Olympus key has no builder profile the audit write is SKIPPED (audit_logs.user_id is a NOT NULL FK), so this call leaves NO entry on the voice audit page.

tools.name: voice_call_tracking_diagnose
tools.description: The call-tracking doctor: one structured verdict on whether phone-call conversions are actually reaching Google Ads, and what to fix first. Returns seven checks, each with status ok|warn|fail|unknown, a plain-language explanation and one concrete next action, plus an overall verdict and an ORDERED fix_first list. Read fix_first rather than the check array: the checks are diagnostic, the order is the answer. Read-only, but not free: it makes outbound Google Ads READ calls and one HTTP GET of the tenant's deployed page. Pass skip_google and skip_site_fetch to stay entirely inside the database when either is slow or the connection is broken; both then report `unknown` rather than `ok`, and an `unknown` is NOT a pass. project_id is a selector inside the bound account, never a tenant argument: omit it and the doctor picks the most recently updated non-archived project, which on a multi-site account is very likely not the one you meant. days clamps to 1..365 (default 30). To prove number swapping actually works you need voice_call_tracking_live_probe, because that writes a row and cannot be reached from this read path.

tools.name: voice_call_tracking_live_probe
tools.description: Same verdict as voice_call_tracking_diagnose, but additionally asks the number pool for a DID exactly the way a visitor's browser does, which is the only way to PROVE number swapping works end to end. HAS A SIDE EFFECT, which is why it is a separate tool and not a flag on the read path: the probe writes a voice_pool_sessions row and HOLDS a tracking DID for the sticky window, so that number is unavailable to a real visitor until the window expires. On a pool with few active DIDs, repeated probing can starve live traffic. Run it to confirm a fix, not on a schedule. live_probe must be sent true to get the probe; without it this is just the read-only doctor with an extra round trip. Everything else behaves as in voice_call_tracking_diagnose.

tools.name: voice_call_tracking_outbox
tools.description: Row-level view of voice_conversion_uploads: which call conversions were queued, uploaded, failed or skipped, one row at a time, with the originating call joined on and each error_code translated into plain language. This is the companion to the doctor's aggregate verdict; use it once the doctor says uploads are failing and you need to know WHICH ones and why. Nothing in the product read this table before the route existed. The enqueue path wrote rows and the dispatch tick drained them, so a conversion that never reached Google left no visible trace. An empty result therefore means one of two very different things: nothing was ever enqueued (a tracking problem, ask the doctor) or everything uploaded cleanly. Filter status='failed' first. status and error_code accept a repeated param or a comma list; an unknown status is a 400 naming the valid set rather than a silent empty page. from/to filter created_at and a bad date is a 400. limit clamps to 1..200 (default 50), offset floors at 0, order is created_desc (default) | created_asc | oldest_queued. Account scope comes from the key binding, never from a parameter.

tools.name: voice_call_tracking_setup
tools.description: One idempotent operation that wires call-conversion tracking for a project end to end: number pool, tracking DIDs, per-project phone-tracking config, tenant conversion-upload policy, and the Google "Hiveku - Phone Call" conversion action. Returns per-step results plus an overall state, so success never has to be inferred from a bare 200. Safe to re-run: each step reports already_configured instead of duplicating work. SPENDS MONEY, but only one field does it. `did_count` is the ONLY thing here that can buy phone numbers. Omit it or send 0 and this provisions nothing on the carrier. When set, it buys only the shortfall between the pool's current active size and that target, at most 5 per run, and only after the E911 address checks out; a missing or unvalidated E911 address comes back as a `blocked` step naming the human action, so it never half-buys and never fails opaquely. Numbers, once bought, bill monthly until released. Use dry_run: true first on any account where you are not certain what already exists. The account comes from the key binding; a body-supplied account is neither read nor honoured.

tools.name: voice_call_transcript_get
tools.description: Full transcript for one call as { transcript: '<text>' }, read server-side out of the KMS recordings bucket rather than handed back as a URL. What comes back is the entire stored object body inline as one string, exactly as the post-process worker wrote it: no speaker array, no timestamps, no truncation and no pagination, so a long call returns a large payload in a single response. This is a verbatim record of a real conversation. Names, addresses, card and account numbers, health and financial detail all appear unredacted, and the handler applies NO redaction, NO consent check, NO retention check and no two-party-consent gate of any kind; the only thing it verifies is that the call belongs to the key's account. The id is voice_calls.id, the same id voice_recording_url_get takes. Silent failures: 404 no_transcript when transcript_s3_key is null, which is the normal state until the recording uploads and post-process runs, and a PERMANENT state when the extension has transcription switched off; 404 transcript_unavailable when the object cannot be read, which is byte-identical to what you get when HIVEKU_RECORDINGS_BUCKET is unset in that environment or the S3/KMS read is denied, because the reader swallows every non-NoSuchKey error to null, so a misconfigured deploy, an access-control failure and a swept object are indistinguishable (unlike voice_recording_url_get, this route never answers 503). The query selects ai_summary and then never returns it; read the summary from voice_call_get's recording_transcript field. 404 not_found for a call in another account; 402 voice_not_enabled when the Voice add-on is off.

tools.name: voice_calls_export_csv
tools.description: Exports this account's call detail records as CSV, one row per call, for diffing against a CallRail or ad-platform export. Columns: call_uuid, direction, from, to, disposition, started_at, answered_at, ended_at, duration_seconds, billable_seconds, tracking_source, ai_sentiment, ai_summary, utm_source, utm_medium, utm_campaign, keyword, ad_group, click_id_type, landing_url, repeat_caller, environment. THERE IS NO FILE AND NO DOWNLOAD LINK: the raw CSV body comes back inline as the tool result, so an unbounded call can drop up to 50,000 rows of caller numbers and full AI call summaries straight into the conversation. Always bound it with from and to. Read-only: no carrier call, no money, nothing sent to a person, but the payload is bulk PII, including AI summaries of recorded conversations and the landing pages callers came from. Traps. Truncation is SILENT: the cap is 50,000 rows and the file carries no marker, so if you count exactly 50,000 data rows assume it was cut and narrow the window. An unrecognised disposition or direction value is DROPPED rather than refused, so one typo silently exports every call in the period instead of the slice you asked for; the UI's Missed chip is three dispositions, which is what missed_any means (missed, abandoned, voicemail). sort outside the allowlist falls back to started_at and only the exact string 'asc' flips the order, so with the row cap desc keeps the newest calls and asc keeps the oldest. to is bumped to end of UTC day so the last day is included, while an unparsable from or to is silently ignored rather than refused. q searches ai_summary, plus a digits match on both numbers when it holds 3 or more digits, plus up to 50 non-deleted CRM contacts by first or last name matched against BOTH legs (the voicemail inbox matches the caller leg only, so the same q can return different sets there). Blank utm columns do NOT mean direct traffic: a call whose attribution sweep looked and found nothing is stored as an {unmatched:true} sentinel that is rendered exactly like never-processed. keyword prefers the Google Ads click_view enrichment and falls back to utm_term. click_id_type is the LABEL of whichever click id the session carried (gclid, gbraid, wbraid, fbclid, msclkid, ttclid), never the value. repeat_caller is 'true' or empty and never 'false'. Cells are formula-guarded, so a value starting with = + - @ tab or carriage return arrives with a leading apostrophe. COMPLIANCE NOTE: the dashboard version of this export writes a voice.cdr.exported audit row; this one calls the audit helper with a null actor, and that helper console-warns and returns without writing, so an export taken through this tool leaves NO entry on the voice audit page and will not appear in voice_audit_export_csv. 402 voice_not_enabled when the paid Voice add-on is off.

tools.name: voice_calls_list
tools.description: List call history. Filterable by direction, disposition, time window.

tools.name: voice_default_greetings_get
tools.description: Returns { account_name, defaults: { ivr, did, whisper, voicemail } }: the account's display name plus the four pre-canned greeting TEMPLATES filled in with it. These are suggestions, not configuration. Nothing here reads the IVR, DID, whisper or voicemail greetings the account actually has, so this can never tell you what callers hear today, it returns the identical four strings whether or not any greeting exists, and receiving a string changes nothing until you save it through the relevant IVR or voicemail route. The trap is that these strings are read ALOUD to callers once saved, and the name is seeded from accounts.name, the internal workspace label, NOT accounts.company_name (which exists and is not consulted). An account signed up as 'Psgi' produces 'Thanks for calling Psgi.' Check the name against the real trading name before writing it into a greeting. Second silent case: when accounts.name is empty or whitespace, account_name comes back as an empty string while the templates substitute the word 'us' ('Thanks for calling us.'). Read both fields, because that fallback is invisible if you only look at defaults. 402 is either voice_not_enabled (Voice add-on off) or account_past_due (billing): read the error key, not the status code.

tools.name: voice_diagnose_setup
tools.description: Snapshot of an account's voice provisioning state — tenant_provisioned, active DIDs, DIDs missing E911, extensions / ring_groups / IVRs / verified E911 addresses counts, plus a `blocking_issues` array of human-readable problems. First-resort tool when an admin asks 'is my phone system set up?' or 'why aren't my numbers working?'.

tools.name: voice_e911_address_create
tools.description: WRITES A CARRIER-SIDE RECORD WITH LIFE-SAFETY WEIGHT. Registers a street address with Telnyx (CASS validation — RAY BAUM's Act), and once a DID references it, this is the address emergency services are DISPATCHED TO on a 911 call from that number. A typo here misroutes an ambulance, not an email — only submit an address a human has confirmed. NO DEDUPE AT ANY LAYER: two identical calls create TWO carrier address records and two rows, and no route at any layer deletes or edits a voice_e911_addresses row, so a duplicate or mistyped address is permanent on this surface. Retry ONLY a call that did not answer 200. The carrier call runs BEFORE the local write, so a returned row always means Telnyx accepted the address: telnyx_address_id and verified_at come back already stamped, and the id is the e911_address_id every LOCAL number purchase requires (voice_number_purchase refuses local orders without one). RETURNS { address }: the full row — id, account_id, label, street, street2, city, state, postal_code, country, telnyx_address_id, verified_at, created_at, updated_at. Refusals: 422 invalid_body (label, street, city, 2-letter state and postal_code required; unknown keys are silently stripped, not refused); 422 e911_validation_failed when Telnyx/CASS rejects the address — the message field is the CARRIER'S OWN TEXT, so read it and resubmit a corrected address rather than retrying verbatim; 502 e911_validation_failed for any other carrier failure, which says nothing about the address itself (the carrier may merely be down — this is the one failure that is safe to retry); 402 voice_not_enabled without the paid Voice add-on. The audit row is skipped for Olympus keys (logVoiceAudit runs with a null user, its documented anonymous path), so nothing on the voice audit page records who registered the address.

tools.name: voice_e911_addresses_list
tools.description: List the account's E911 addresses (registered + pending verification).

tools.name: voice_extension_create
tools.description: Provisions a REAL SIP endpoint on the tenant's FusionPBX/FreeSWITCH box and THEN writes the row, returning { extension: { id, extension, display_name, endpoint_type, user_id, phone_model, mac_address, sip_username, presence_state, e911_address_id, created_at } }. This is a live phone-system change, not a draft: the number is dialable internally immediately, a handset or softphone can register to it, and any DID, IVR option or ring group later pointed at it will ring it. No carrier order, no number purchase, no money. The SIP password is returned by the phone system exactly once, encrypted before the insert, and appears NOWHERE in this response, so the device itself can only be set up from the dashboard. THE ORDER CAN ORPHAN. The PBX endpoint is created BEFORE the database insert, so a failed insert leaves a live SIP endpoint with no builder row and an unrecoverable password. The usual cause is a unique collision, and the 409 can name the wrong thing: the handler returns extension_taken for any P2002 whose reported target contains the substring 'extension', and this table carries two more unique constraints, per-account sip_username and one endpoint per (user, endpoint_type, device), whose Postgres constraint names both contain 'voice_extensions'. So a second softphone_mobile for the same person surfaces either as 'Extension 1005 is already in use on this account' or, if the target comes back as field names instead, as a bare 500 internal_error. Neither message is the truth, and both leave the PBX endpoint behind. Check voice_extensions_list before retrying. SILENT 200s to expect. (1) endpoint_type 'external_number' with no external_target_e164 is ACCEPTED here and creates a black hole: the call router finds no target and the caller hears nothing. The update twin refuses that combination (422 forward_target_required); this route does not, so always send both together. (2) external_target_e164 is discarded to null unless endpoint_type is exactly 'external_number'. (3) e911_address_id is stored with no check that the address belongs to this account or is verified, this route makes no carrier call, and nothing in the phone system reads an EXTENSION's e911_address_id at all: every emergency path keys on the DID (voice_numbers.e911_address_id), which is where the hard E911 gate lives. Treat this field as a label, never as an emergency registration. (4) the personal-ring-group reconcile, which is what makes the owner's other phones ring this new endpoint, is best-effort and this response has NO warning field, so a failed reconcile is invisible: confirm with voice_ring_groups_list. phone_model and mac_address are deliberately NOT exposed. The route would persist them and never push them to the phone system (syncExtensionDevice is called only by .../[id]/phone, which has no Olympus twin), so the database would badge a desk phone provisioned while the handset's boot request is served nothing. Device provisioning stays a dashboard action. Errors: 422 invalid_body with zod issues (extension must be 2-6 digits, display_name 1-120 chars); 409 not_provisioned when the tenant has no FusionPBX domain yet, which means voice was never enabled for this tenant and is not a server fault; 409 extension_taken; 403 not_a_member when user_id is not a member of THIS account (deliberately stricter than the dashboard route, which does not check); 403 account_suspended; 402 is either voice_not_enabled (Voice add-on off, or the account has no billing row at all) or account_past_due, so read the error key and not the status; 404 / 409 / 422 / 502 extension_provision_failed when the phone system refuses. This twin does NOT enforce the dashboard's per-user voice 'extensions' permission, so the API key is the only gate. The only undo is voice_extension_delete, which is irreversible and refuses while anything routes to the extension.

tools.name: voice_extension_delete
tools.description: Tears the SIP endpoint down on the phone system and deletes the row, returning { id, deleted: true, upstream_cleaned: boolean }. THIS TAKES A PHONE OFFLINE AND IS IRREVERSIBLE. The stored SIP password dies with the row, so the handset or softphone can never register again: recovery means creating a NEW extension and re-provisioning the device from the dashboard, which no Olympus tool can do. upstream_cleaned false means the row had never been provisioned to the PBX and only the local row was removed; true means the phone system confirmed the teardown. Confirm with a human before calling. It will not strand a live call path, but the guard is narrower than it looks. It refuses with 409 extension_in_use, naming them, while any number routes to this extension (inbound target type extension or voicemail) or any ring group lists it as a member. It does NOT check IVR menu options, ring-group no-answer fallbacks, or queues, so a phone-tree digit pointing here is silently orphaned: voice_ivr_walk will afterwards report that option as resolved.type 'unknown' while the menu still answers 200 and looks healthy. Walk the trees before deleting. The 409 you are most likely to hit is invisible in the dashboard: any user with two or more registering endpoints (desk phone or softphones) has an auto-managed PERSONAL ring group that the ring-group editor deliberately hides, and its member row blocks the delete. It appears in the message as '<Person> (personal) (8001)'. Re-point or thin the group first. PARTIAL TEARDOWN ON FAILURE: the AI receptionist's transfer config is pruned FIRST (this extension is removed from transfer_directory and from human_transfer_extension) and that prune is never rolled back. If the phone system then refuses (502 or 422 delete_failed) the extension still exists and still rings, but the AI can no longer transfer callers to it, and nothing in the response says so. Re-run the delete, or re-add the transfer target. Voicemail: the route does nothing to preserve the mailbox or the messages in it, and a number pointed straight at this extension's voicemail blocks the delete rather than being re-pointed, so re-point that DID yourself first. After the row is gone the owner's personal ring group is reconciled so their remaining phones re-bundle; that is best-effort and a failure only logs, with no warning in the response. This twin does NOT enforce the dashboard's per-user voice 'extensions' permission, so the API key is the only gate. 404 not_found for an unknown id or one owned by another tenant, which also means it was already deleted and is not retryable; 500 internal_error for anything that is not a phone-system refusal; 402 is voice_not_enabled or account_past_due.

tools.name: voice_extension_get
tools.description: Reads one extension by UUID and returns { extension: { id, extension, display_name, endpoint_type, user_id, phone_model, mac_address, sip_username, presence_state, e911_address_id, created_at } } and NOTHING ELSE. It is a narrow select, and the omissions are the trap: external_target_e164, ring_timeout_seconds, every voicemail_* field (enabled, PIN, greeting text, greeting source, transcribe, email-on-receipt), both outbound caller-ID columns and fusionpbx_extension_uuid are all absent, so this can never tell you where a PSTN-forward extension actually rings, whether voicemail is on, what greeting callers hear, or what number the seat presents on outbound calls. voice_extensions_list returns the whole row and is the read for those. presence_state is the stored column, not a live SIP registration probe, so 'offline' may just be stale. Because fusionpbx_extension_uuid is not selected, an extension that was never provisioned to the phone system, and therefore cannot register at all, looks identical here to a healthy one. 404 not_found covers both an unknown id and an id belonging to another tenant, so it is never a cross-tenant read. Gated on the Voice plan: 402 voice_not_enabled means this cannot even confirm an extension exists on an account with the add-on off, and 402 also carries account_past_due, so read the error key. voice_extension_status covers most of the same ground from the diagnostics route, has NO plan gate, accepts the dial number as well as the UUID, answers 200 { data: { found: false } } instead of 404, and DOES return external_target_e164; prefer it for lookups, and use this tool when you specifically need e911_address_id (which voice_extension_status omits) or a hard 404 to confirm an id.

tools.name: voice_extension_status
tools.description: Status of a specific extension — who owns it, endpoint type, registration state. `q` accepts either the dial number ('1003') or the extension UUID.

tools.name: voice_extension_update
tools.description: Edits one extension in place and returns { extension: { id, extension, display_name, endpoint_type, user_id, phone_model, mac_address, sip_username, presence_state, e911_address_id, outbound_caller_id_number_id, outbound_caller_id_anonymous, fusionpbx_extension_uuid }, warning?: string }. ALWAYS READ warning. The row is saved locally first and every push to the phone system afterwards is best-effort, so a 200 carrying a warning means the database and the PBX now disagree about the display name, ring timeout, voicemail toggle or PIN, caller ID, greeting audio, or which phones ring. Re-saving is the retry. IT SPENDS MONEY AND REACHES CALLERS. Once the row ends up with voicemail_greeting_source 'tts' plus greeting text plus a voice id (from this patch or already stored), the audio is rendered through Cartesia, billed per character, written to the voice_tts_renders ledger and rolled into the monthly period. Callers hear the new greeting as soon as it lands on FreeSWITCH. A re-save whose text hash is unchanged reuses the existing render and costs nothing. CALLER ID IS CARRIER-FACING: it changes the number the called party sees on EVERY future outbound call from this seat. outbound_caller_id_number_id must be a DID owned by this account and active, else 422 invalid_caller_id; a toll-free DID is refused with 422 toll_free_caller_id because a 911 call would then present a number with no dispatchable address. That toll-free test only recognizes NANP +1 8xx numbers (800/833/844/855/866/877/888), so a non-US toll-free is not caught. outbound_caller_id_anonymous true presents CLIR (the callee sees Blocked) and WINS over the number id, and it also skips the ownership branch entirely, so an outbound_caller_id_number_id sent alongside it is written with no account check at all: another tenant's DID id is stored on your row, and an id matching no row at all trips the database foreign key in an update that has no try/catch, so the request dies as an unhandled 500 with nothing saved. null on outbound_caller_id_number_id means fall back to the tenant default. SILENT NO-OPS, every one of them a clean 200. (1) The caller-ID push only happens when the row already has a FusionPBX uuid, and that path adds NO warning, so a caller-ID-only save on a never-provisioned extension returns clean and changes nothing on the phone system. (2) ring_timeout_seconds: null and voicemail_pin: null are written to the database but are excluded from the push by an explicit not-null guard, so FreeSWITCH keeps the previous timeout and the mailbox keeps its old PIN. (3) Clearing voicemail_greeting_source to null nulls the greeting pointers but deliberately does NOT delete the rendered greeting_1.wav from FreeSWITCH, so callers keep hearing the greeting the UI now reports as gone. (4) A 'tts' mode without BOTH text and voice, or 'upload' with no key ever uploaded, renders nothing and only returns a warning. (5) voicemail_transcribe, voicemail_email_on_receipt and voicemail_email_to are database-only here and are read later by the voicemail-uploaded ingest handler, never by the PBX. (6) e911_address_id is stored with no ownership or verification check and no carrier call, and no emergency path reads it off an extension. The response is a narrow select and never echoes external_target_e164, ring_timeout_seconds, any voicemail_* field or the greeting state, so you cannot confirm those from the reply: read them back with voice_extensions_list, which returns the whole row. Refusals: the body schema is strict, so any unknown key is 422 invalid_body; phone_model and mac_address get their own 422 use_phone_route because saving them here would change the database without changing the phone system, and their route has no Olympus twin. endpoint_type 'external_number' with no forward target, in this patch or already on the row, is 422 forward_target_required; sending external_target_e164 on any other endpoint type is 422 not_a_forwarding_extension; switching AWAY from external_number clears the stored target so a stale number cannot go live later. Changing endpoint_type or user_id rewrites the personal ring group in FusionPBX for the old AND the new owner, which is literally which phones ring, and a failure there is only a warning. user_id must be a member of this account (403 not_a_member); user_id null clears the owner and is always allowed. 404 not_found for an unknown or another tenant's id; 402 is voice_not_enabled or account_past_due. This twin does NOT enforce the dashboard's per-user voice 'extensions' permission, so the API key is the only gate.

tools.name: voice_extensions_list
tools.description: List the account's extensions (seat phones / softphones / external-number forwards).

tools.name: voice_ivr_create
tools.description: Creates AND provisions a working auto-attendant. Not a database write: it reserves a free extension from this account's 6000-6999 IVR pool, inserts the voice_ivrs row, then calls voice_server, which renders the greeting and every per-option announcement through CARTESIA (a paid TTS vendor, real money per render), writes the MP3s to S3 and to the PBX filesystem, and installs live FreeSWITCH dialplan rules on the shared EC2 box. From the moment it returns, any DID already pointed at this IVR plays it to real callers. RETURNS { ivr, tts_cost_cents, renders, warning? }: the saved row including the assigned extension and fusionpbx_ivr_uuid, the Cartesia spend in cents (cache hits on unchanged text plus voice cost nothing and are not ledgered) and the COUNT of renders billed into voice_tts_renders and voice_usage_periods.tts_cents. Refusals: 402 voice_not_enabled when the paid Voice add-on is off, which is a plan refusal and not an empty account; 409 not_provisioned when the account has no voice tenant yet (voice must be enabled on the PBX first); 409 no_extension_available when 6000-6999 is exhausted on this account; 409 extension_race when a concurrent create grabbed the same slot, which is retryable and re-scans for the next free number (pickIvrExtension is a best-effort scan, not a lock); 422 invalid_body. SILENT FAILURES, none of which error. greeting_tts_text with no greeting_voice_id renders NOTHING: the provisioner builds a greeting only when it has both text and a voice, so the menu answers callers with silence and the save still reports success. The same applies to every option's announcement_tts_text, which uses the IVR-level greeting_voice_id and never one of its own. An option whose target_id does not resolve in this account is NOT refused: it resolves to null and that digit is provisioned with no destination. The after-hours target is dropped the same way, leaving no after-hours route at all, and this route sends NO department with it, so an after-hours ai_agent always lands on the generic receptionist even when your menu options route to a specialist. business_hours is honoured open or closed PER DAY but the phone system supports only ONE shared open/close window, so when the submitted days disagree the response carries a `warning` naming the day whose window now applies to all of them. If FreeSWITCH provisioning fails you get 500 or 502 ivr_provision_failed WITH the saved row and a warning: the IVR exists, the extension stays reserved, nothing answers, and you fix it with voice_ivr_update rather than by creating a second one. Because an Olympus key has no builder profile the audit write is SKIPPED entirely (audit_logs.user_id is a NOT NULL FK), so this create leaves no entry on the voice audit page.

tools.name: voice_ivr_delete
tools.description: PERMANENTLY removes an auto-attendant and its call routing. IRREVERSIBLE and not database-only: voice_server drops the FreeSWITCH dialplan rules and DELETES the S3 audio objects (the greeting plus every option announcement), then the row is deleted and its 6xxx extension returns to the pool for reuse. There is no undo and the recorded prompts are gone; recreating the menu means paying Cartesia to render every prompt again. This route DOES refuse rather than orphan: 409 ivr_in_use while anything still routes here, and the message names each blocker - phone numbers whose inbound target is this IVR, ring groups falling back to it, queues overflowing to it, and OTHER IVRs whose menu digit or after-hours target points at it. Re-point those first. An option on THIS menu pointing at itself (press 9 to repeat) does not block its own deletion. WHAT THE GUARD DOES NOT COVER: it queries voice_numbers, voice_ring_groups, voice_queues and voice_ivrs only. A call-tracking DID pool whose voice_did_pools.inbound_target_id is this IVR, and a pending carrier order in voice_number_orders that will adopt into it, are both invisible to the check and are silently orphaned; every number that later joins that pool inherits a destination that no longer exists, and a DID left resolving a dead extension gives callers a fast busy while the dashboard still shows it as routed. RETURNS { id, deleted: true, warning? }. The warning is the partial-delete case: if voice_server does not confirm teardown the Hiveku row is STILL deleted, so the dialplan rule and the S3 audio can survive on the PBX for a menu Hiveku has forgotten (that orphan self-heals only if something re-provisions the same extension). A 200 with a warning is not a clean delete. An IVR that never reached the PBX (no voice tenant, or a null extension) is deleted with no teardown call and no warning at all. Also 404 not_found for an id on another account, and 402 voice_not_enabled when the paid Voice add-on is off. The audit write is skipped for Olympus keys, so nothing records who deleted it.

tools.name: voice_ivr_update
tools.description: Edits an existing auto-attendant and RE-PROVISIONS it end to end on every call, even a rename. voice_server re-renders any CHANGED greeting or option announcement through CARTESIA (paid TTS, real money per render), rewrites the MP3s in S3 and on the PBX filesystem, and re-installs the live FreeSWITCH dialplan rules, so callers hear the new menu immediately. RETURNS { ivr, tts_cost_cents, renders, warning? }: the persisted row, the Cartesia spend in cents and how many renders it paid for. Unchanged text plus voice is a hash cache hit and costs nothing. THE EXPENSIVE MISTAKE: the hash is over text PLUS voice, so changing greeting_voice_id alone invalidates the greeting AND every option announcement and a one-field save re-renders the entire menu at full price. PARTIAL BY DESIGN: a field you omit is not written. Omitting `options` keeps the stored menu and re-provisions from it; SENDING `options` REPLACES the whole menu, so a digit you leave out of the array is DELETED. Refusals: 404 not_found, which is also the answer for an IVR on another account; 402 voice_not_enabled when the paid Voice add-on is off; 409 not_provisioned when the account has no voice tenant; 422 invalid_body; and 409 menu_option_unresolvable, which happens only on a save that OMITS `options` while a stored option's target_type is not one of the seven canonical values. That refusal changes NOTHING at all and returns invalid_digits, so you repair those digits by sending a full `options` array once (the refusal is deliberate: guessing 'disconnect' for a broken option once made it permanently a hang-up as a side effect of renaming the IVR). SILENT FAILURES: greeting_tts_text or announcement_tts_text with no greeting_voice_id renders nothing and that prompt is simply silent; an option target_id that does not resolve in this account provisions that digit with no destination rather than erroring; an unresolvable after_hours_target_id is dropped, leaving no after-hours route; per-day business_hours windows collapse to ONE shared open/close window, reported as a `warning` naming the day that won. If voice_server fails you get 500 or 502 ivr_provision_failed with the ALREADY-UPDATED row plus a warning: Postgres moved, FreeSWITCH did not, and the two stay out of step until a later save succeeds. The audit write is skipped for Olympus keys, so this edit leaves no entry on the voice audit page.

tools.name: voice_ivr_walk
tools.description: Read one IVR phone tree with every menu target pre-resolved a single level deep, so you can narrate what a caller actually hears without a round-trip per option. Returns {ivr:{id,name,extension,greeting:{text,voice_id,rendered},options,invalid_input_max_attempts,business_hours,after_hours}}. options is keyed by digit, each {digit,target_type,target_id,label,announcement_tts_text,announcement_voice_id,resolved}; resolved is a union where extension carries extension+display_name, ring_group carries strategy plus its full member roster in priority (ring) order, ivr carries a sub-IVR stub of {id,name,extension} and DOES NOT recurse further, ai_agent carries only the account-wide ai_agent_enabled flag, and repeat/disconnect carry nothing. after_hours runs through the SAME resolver, so it degrades the same way. A deleted or missing target does NOT error: it becomes {type:'unknown',reason}, so a tree whose every option points at a deleted extension still answers 200 and looks healthy at a glance. Read every resolved.type before reporting that the menu works. A target_type outside extension/voicemail/ring_group/ivr/ai_agent/repeat/disconnect also comes back unknown with reason 'unsupported target_type: X', which means this route cannot name it, not that the menu is broken. A voicemail option with a null target_id is NOT a real mailbox lookup: it returns the synthesized literal display_name 'Default voicemail' with id and extension null. SILENT DROPS: only single-character keys matching [0-9*#] survive the loop, so menu_json's documented 'default' fallback key and any multi-character key are absent from options entirely and the fallback branch is invisible here. greeting.voice_id NEVER comes back null because it falls back to a hardcoded Cartesia default (a0e99841-438c-4a64-b679-ae501e7d6091), so a non-null voice is not evidence anyone chose one, while announcement_voice_id has no fallback and is just the IVR's own greeting_voice_id or null, so the two disagree on the same IVR; greeting.rendered false means the text was never synthesized to S3. invalid_input_max_attempts reports 3 when the column is null. NOTHING in this response reports fusionpbx_ivr_uuid, so a tree that reads perfectly here may never have been loaded onto the PBX and may route zero live calls: confirm provisioning with voice_diagnose_setup. BUSINESS HOURS ARE THE SOFTEST FIELD HERE: business_hours is non-null for ANY object in the column, but timezone and schedule are read only from the {timezone, schedule:{'0'..'6':[openMinute,closeMinute]}} shape (Sunday = 0), so a row stored in another shape reports timezone null and schedule {} and still looks configured; is_open_now is derived only from that embedded timezone (the separate business_hours_timezone column is never read) and is null both when the timezone is absent and when the date math throws, so null means unknown and never means closed. Even a well-formed schedule over-promises: the provisioner emits ONE FreeSWITCH time-of-day window shared across every open day and silently keeps the first open day's window when they differ, so differing per-day hours are narrated here and not enforced on the phone. Read-only itself; the write twins are voice_ivr_create / voice_ivr_update / voice_ivr_delete, each a live phone-system change that wants an explicit human confirmation. 402 voice_not_enabled when the Voice add-on is off for the account (or the account has no billing row); 404 not_found for an unknown id or one owned by another account.

tools.name: voice_ivrs_list
tools.description: List the account's IVR menus.

tools.name: voice_ivrs_reprovision
tools.description: REWRITES LIVE DIALPLANS: re-renders the targeted IVR menus from the rows already stored and re-installs their FreeSWITCH XML on the PBX, so callers dialing in are routed by the fresh rendering immediately. It changes NO stored menu configuration - idempotent, safe to re-run - and exists as the maintenance backfill for rendering-logic fixes (the shipped incident: a weekday-numbering bug that sent Monday callers to the after-hours branch on every IVR provisioned before the fix). USUALLY $0: unchanged greeting/announcement text hash-matches on voice_server and is not re-rendered; text that no longer matches is sent to Cartesia and billed, reported per-IVR as tts_cost_cents. Selection: omit the body (or send {}) for the default scope 'business_hours' (only menus carrying an hours schedule - the ones the weekday class of bug can affect); scope:'all' for every menu; ivr_ids for an explicit list, where a foreign or unknown id becomes a per-id failure ('This menu does not exist on this account.') and is never touched. 207 PARTIAL SEMANTICS: each IVR succeeds or fails alone, and the response is 207 the moment ANY one fails - ok:false with a per-IVR results[] entry (status, reason, warning, tts_cost_cents, renders). A 207 is not a retryable error: the 'reprovisioned' entries are already done; only the failed ones need attention, and re-running is safe. Built-in refusals: 409 not_provisioned when there is no PBX tenant; a menu option whose stored destination is unrecognised fails THAT IVR with no provision call and no write (the engine never invents a destination); malformed JSON is a hard 422, never treated as 'do the default scope'; the schema is strict, so a misspelled key ('ivr_id') is a 422 too. 402 voice_not_enabled. Audit write SKIPPED for keys (no builder profile) - the run leaves no voice-audit entry.

tools.name: voice_number_cnam_set
tools.description: WRITES THE CALLER-ID NAME TO THE CARRIER. The change goes to Telnyx, which pushes it into the national CNAM databases, so every person this tenant calls sees the new name on their handset once it propagates: typically 12 to 24 hours, up to 72. It is not instantly reversible, because clearing it is a second carrier write with the same delay. It places no calls and costs no per-use money, but it changes how this business is identified to the public. Worth doing: an unregistered number shows bare digits and carrier analytics at Verizon, T-Mobile and AT&T are far likelier to label it Potential Spam, so CNAM is one of the few reputation levers a tenant controls. Returns { number: { cnam_name, cnam_enabled, cnam_updated_at } } and NOTHING ELSE, not the rest of the number row. cnam_name is what the CARRIER returned, falling back to your name uppercased, so the stored value routinely differs in case from what you sent. THE SILENT FAILURE: cnam_updated_at is stamped when the carrier ACCEPTED the write, not when handsets show it. Never report the new name as live off that timestamp; it only means the request landed. Refusals, all before the carrier call so nothing is half-done: 422 invalid_body for a name over 15 characters or containing anything but letters, numbers and spaces (no ampersand, no punctuation, no accents), and for enabled true with a blank or whitespace-only name; 422 cnam_not_applicable_toll_free because CNAM is a geographic-number registry and toll-free NPAs 800, 833, 844, 855, 866, 877 and 888 are not in it; 422 not_provisioned when the row has no carrier id yet, which is the normal state for a half-provisioned or still-porting number; 404 not_found, which is also the cross-tenant answer. Any failure after that point is 502 cnam_failed: the usual case is a carrier rejection with nothing persisted, which is the safe direction, but the same 502 covers a carrier write that landed and whose response or local mirror write was lost, so verify with voice_number_get rather than assuming a 502 was a no-op. enabled false ignores cnam_name entirely and clears the local name to null. NO AUDIT ROW: the audit helper is called with a null user because a service key has no builder profile, which is its documented anonymous path, so it console-warns and writes nothing to audit_logs. This public-facing carrier change leaves no entry on the voice audit page. The per-user communications.numbers permission that guards the dashboard is not applied on this surface. 402 voice_not_enabled without the paid Voice add-on.

tools.name: voice_number_get
tools.description: One DID by voice_numbers.id, for the detail voice_numbers_list does not carry. Returns { number } as the ENTIRE unprojected row (findFirst with no select): e164, provider, provider_number_id (the Telnyx phone-number id), label, purpose, tracking_source, tracking_campaign_id, inbound_target_type, inbound_target_id, inbound_ai_department, geo_routing_json, e911_address_id, is_active, campaign_name, whisper_message, greeting_message, greeting_voice_id, greeting_audio_s3_key, greeting_text_hash, greeting_rendered_at, the four whisper_* equivalents, recording_enabled, forward_to_e164, telnyx_messaging_profile_id, messaging_profile_attached_at, tf_verification_status, cnam_name, cnam_enabled, cnam_updated_at, created_at and updated_at. Fields that answer with something other than what they look like: is_active true does NOT mean calls arrive, because routing lives in inbound_target_type plus inbound_target_id and the FusionPBX side of that pair is pushed best-effort by voice_number_update, so this row can describe a route FreeSWITCH never received. cnam_name and cnam_enabled are a LOCAL MIRROR written only after a successful carrier write, and cnam_updated_at is the carrier ACCEPT time, not the moment handsets show the name (12-24h typically, up to 72h), so a fresh timestamp is not evidence the name is live. tf_verification_status null means never submitted, not rejected. greeting_audio_s3_key and whisper_audio_s3_key are S3 object keys, not URLs, and nothing here plays them. recording_enabled null means inherit the tenant default, which is not the same as false. purpose 'pool' is the legacy spelling of 'did_pool' on old rows. geo_routing_json is raw JSON and null when no location rules were ever set. What is NOT here: pool membership. A pooled DID's routing, whisper and greeting are also configured on its pool and the router lets the per-number value win, so a value on this row can silently beat the pool page that claims to own it; check voice_pools_list. 404 not_found is also the cross-tenant answer, since the lookup is scoped to the key's account. 402 voice_not_enabled when the paid Voice add-on is off, even for a number that exists. Read-only: no carrier call, no cost, nothing reaches a person.

tools.name: voice_number_lookup
tools.description: Resolves a raw phone number to a CRM contact for an in-call contact card: { contact: { id, name } | null, last_call_at }. It is a phone-number-to-identity oracle scoped to the targeted account, so treat the result as PII. contact carries ONLY id and name (name falls back to the stored phone string, then to the literal 'Contact', when both name fields are empty), so no email, phone, company or owner comes back and anything richer needs a CRM tool. Matching is last-7-digits contains, deliberately looser than the screen-pop matcher: two different numbers sharing their final seven digits resolve to the same contact, duplicate CRM rows for one number resolve to whichever is seen first, and soft-deleted contacts never resolve at all, so an archived customer reads as no match. SILENT FAILURES: when number is omitted, empty, or has fewer than 7 digits once non-digits are stripped, the route answers 200 with { contact: null, last_call_at: null } without querying anything and never returns 400, so malformed input is indistinguishable from a genuine miss; and because the result map is keyed on the CONTACT's own last 7 digits while the read uses the query's last 7, a stored number whose tail differs (an extension suffix such as '555-1234 x99') matches the database filter and still resolves to contact: null. last_call_at is the started_at of the newest call on this account touching that same 7-digit tail, in either direction and at any disposition, so an unanswered outbound attempt sets it and it can even come from a different number sharing the tail; it is not evidence of a conversation. 402 voice_not_enabled when the Voice add-on is off.

tools.name: voice_number_orders_list
tools.description: Pending carrier number orders for the account — the 202-parked purchases from voice_number_purchase (and the dashboard's) that are committed at Telnyx but not active yet. Read-only: no spend, no carrier call. Returns { data: [ { id, telnyx_order_id, e164, purpose, label, e911_address_id, pool_id, sms_campaign_id, status, attempts, last_error, created_at, updated_at } ], pagination: { page, limit, total, total_pages } }, newest first. HOW TO READ status: 'pending' means the poll cron is still working the order — including the window where the number is already ACTIVE at the carrier and adoption is in flight, because 'complete' is stamped only AFTER the adoption write succeeds (claim-before-work), never before. 'failed' is terminal: the carrier reported failure, or the e164 collided with another workspace at adoption time — in the collision case the number was already RELEASED back to the carrier. 'expired' means THE CRON GAVE UP (still pending after 5 days or more than 2000 polls — src/app/api/cron/voice-number-order-poll/route.ts), NOT that the carrier order is gone: the DID may still be committed and platform-billed, so check the Telnyx portal by telnyx_order_id before ever re-buying. attempts and last_error are the cron's own bookkeeping; last_error non-null on a 'pending' row is a transient poll failure, not a verdict. pool_id can come back null on a deployment where the column is not yet pushed (the route degrades instead of 500ing) — and orders parked on such a deployment genuinely carry no pool, with an urgent inbox item telling ops to finish the join by hand. status is matched by raw equality with NO validation, so a typo like 'Complete' silently returns an empty list rather than erroring. page defaults 1; limit defaults 50, clamped 1 to 200, and must be numeric. Unlike the sibling resources on this multiplexer, this one answers 402 voice_not_enabled without the paid Voice add-on — a plan refusal, not an empty order book.

tools.name: voice_number_purchase
tools.description: SPENDS REAL MONEY AND KEEPS SPENDING IT MONTHLY. Buys a phone number (DID) at Telnyx that bills the account every month until someone releases it — $1.00/mo local, $5.00/mo toll-free plus a $0.03/min surcharge on every INBOUND toll-free minute from minute one (rates from the platform invoice compiler, src/lib/billing/voice-pricing.ts). The only undo is voice_number_release, which hands the number back to carrier inventory PERMANENTLY. Buy ONE number per call, and only a number a human approved by digits. required is [] because the real contract is conditional and enforced server-side: EXACTLY ONE of e164 or search must be present, a LOCAL purchase REQUIRES e911_address_id (from voice_e911_address_create — RAY BAUM's Act), and a TOLL-FREE purchase must OMIT e911_address_id entirely (TF is not E911-capable; sending one is an honest 422, never a silent ignore). Search first with voice_numbers_search and pass the winner as e164 — when you send search here instead, the route pins limit to 1 on the wire and BUYS THE FIRST MATCH sight unseen. 800 numbers are unpurchasable at every layer (premium carrier pricing, no billing pass-through): a +1800 e164 is refused and '800' is absent from the toll_free_prefix enum. THE 202 IS NOT AN ERROR AND NOT A NO-OP: error 'number_order_pending' (with order_id) means the carrier ACCEPTED the order — money is committed — but activation is still in flight (routine for non-quickship toll-free, up to 2 business days). The request is parked in voice_number_orders and a poll cron finishes adoption automatically; watch it with voice_number_orders_list and NEVER re-submit after a 202 — that buys a SECOND number. The proxy surfaces that 202 as a SUCCESS result carrying the error key, so check for 'number_order_pending' on every 'successful' call. Not idempotent, no dedupe: two identical calls are two purchases. Refusals, all BEFORE the carrier call: 422 invalid_body for every schema guardrail (missing e164/search; local without E911, message 'e911_address_id is required'; premium_800_not_purchasable; geo_filter_with_toll_free — TF searches take no area_code/locality/state; e911_not_applicable_toll_free; toll_free_not_10dlc — TF numbers use toll-free verification, never a 10DLC sms_campaign_id); 404 pool_not_found for a pool_id that is missing OR another tenant's (indistinguishable by design; a valid pool_id forces purpose 'did_pool' and the server owns the pool join, surviving a 202 park); 422 e911_address_invalid when the E911 address is not on this account or has no carrier registration; 422 target_not_found when inbound_target_id is missing, foreign, or unprovisioned; 501 voicemail_inbound_not_wired_yet; 409 number_unavailable when the e164 has history with ANOTHER workspace — answered before any money moves, and again after the buy if a search-flow collision is detected at adoption (that second path has already UNDONE the purchase at the carrier). After the carrier call: 404/422/502 number_provision_failed with the voice-server message, 500 internal_error. 402 voice_not_enabled without the paid Voice add-on. RETURNS 200 { number: { id, phone_number, provider_number_id, destination_uuid, e911_status ('validated' | 'not_applicable') }, sms_assignment? } — a 200 means the number is BOUGHT, adopted and billed from now on. The audit row is skipped for Olympus keys (logVoiceAudit('number.ordered') runs with a null user on both the 200 and 202 paths), so no purchase made here appears on the voice audit page.

tools.name: voice_number_release
tools.description: PERMANENTLY GIVES THE PHONE NUMBER BACK TO THE CARRIER. This is irreversible: no undo, no grace period, no confirmation argument. The DID returns to Telnyx inventory and CANNOT BE RE-BOUGHT: it can be sold to a stranger, inbound calls to it stop, and every place it is printed stops working, including vehicle wraps, business cards, signage, the Google Business listing, ad call extensions and email signatures. Only ever call this after a human has explicitly confirmed this exact number, by digits. Returns { id, e164, released, destination_removed, soft } on the carrier path, or { id, released: false, soft } when the row carried no provider_number_id, in which case NOTHING is sent to the carrier and the local row is simply removed. THE SILENT FAILURE: released is echoed straight from the voice server and the local row is deleted (or, with soft, cleared) REGARDLESS of its value, because the delete runs unconditionally once the release call resolves. A 200 carrying released:false means Hiveku has forgotten a number Telnyx may still own and still bill for, and there is no local row left to retry from. Check released on every response. PARTIAL TEARDOWN, none of it rolled back: BEFORE the carrier call the handler releases the FusionPBX inbound route (failure only console.warned), deletes this number's DNI pool membership, and clears the DID off every extension presenting it as caller ID on the PBX and here. If the carrier release then fails you get 502 release_failed with the local row intact, but the number is already out of its pool, off every extension's caller ID and NO LONGER TAKING INBOUND CALLS. Retrying is the only way forward and the number is unusable in between. There is no warning field on any response: a partial PBX teardown is invisible to the caller. NO DEPENDENCY GUARD ANYWHERE: this handler has no 409 at all. Nothing checks whether this is the account's only DID, its purpose 'main' business line, a tracking campaign's destination, a pool's last member or a number a workflow depends on. soft is NOT a safe mode and NOT a dry run: the carrier release happens either way, and soft only keeps the row for audit with is_active false and provider_number_id nulled instead of deleting it (a soft-released row still appears in voice_numbers_list unless you filter on is_active). soft must be the exact STRING '1', because the route compares searchParams.get('soft') === '1'; a boolean true serializes as 'true' and silently takes the HARD DELETE path. Per-extension caller-ID cleanup is best-effort and never throws, so a phone whose cleanup failed keeps presenting a number the account no longer owns, which fails STIR/SHAKEN attestation and becomes spoofing if the carrier re-sells the DID. This route writes NO audit row at all, so a permanent release leaves no entry on the voice audit page, and the per-user communications.numbers permission that guards the dashboard is not applied on this surface. 404 not_found is the missing-row and cross-tenant answer; a carrier-side 404 also comes back as HTTP 404 but with error release_failed, and any other carrier failure is 502 release_failed. An unexpected exception is 500 internal_error. 402 voice_not_enabled without the paid Voice add-on. To take a number out of service reversibly, use voice_number_update with is_active false instead; that keeps the DID.

tools.name: voice_number_update
tools.description: CHANGES A LIVE PHONE LINE. Editing inbound_target_type, inbound_target_id, inbound_ai_department or forward_to_e164 rewrites the FusionPBX inbound route, so the very next inbound call rings somewhere else. Editing e911_address_id calls Telnyx and changes the street address emergency services are dispatched to on a 911 call from this number. Editing greeting_message or whisper_message with a matching voice id renders new audio through Cartesia, which COSTS MONEY per render (hash-compared, so an unrelated field edit does not re-render). Returns { number }: the row as written by the single update, captured BEFORE the audio render and BEFORE the PBX push, so greeting_audio_s3_key, greeting_text_hash, greeting_rendered_at and the whisper equivalents in the response are the PRE-render values and are stale on any call that rendered audio. Re-read with voice_number_get. THE SILENT FAILURE: the FusionPBX push is best-effort. A failure is console.errored and this route still answers 200 with the new row, leaving Hiveku showing one route while FreeSWITCH still rings the old target until a human repairs it. The same 200 comes back when the account has no voice tenant row, because the sync returns early with no fusionpbx_domain and pushes nothing. A TTS failure is swallowed the same way: 200, and callers hear the robotic say:flite fallback instead of the greeting you just set. SECOND SILENT FAILURE: the parse coerces a null e911_address_id to undefined, which Prisma reads as no change, so an attempt to CLEAR E911 answers 200 having ignored that key entirely (and on a toll-free DID that same null is read as 'no E911 sent', so it does NOT trip the toll-free refusal either). Half-applied patch: if the carrier rejects an e911_address_id change you get 502 e911_carrier_sync_failed and ONLY that one column is rolled back, while every other field in the same call is already committed and neither the PBX sync nor the TTS render ever ran. Refusals this route DOES enforce, all before any write: 422 e911_not_applicable_toll_free when a NON-NULL e911_address_id is sent on a toll-free DID; 422 e911_required when activating a non-toll-free DID that has no E911 address, and 422 e911_address_invalid when that address is not on this account or carries no carrier registration (RAY BAUM's Act); 422 inbound_target_unroutable when a routing change names a target that is missing, on another account, or has no dial extension, because the sync would otherwise RELEASE the inbound route and leave the row claiming a number is routed while it is dead; 422 geo_rule_target_invalid for the same problem inside a location rule; 409 managed_by_pool listing the fields, when this number sits in a pool that ACTUALLY manages them (a pool owns routing only once it has a destination, whisper only when whisper is enabled with a template, greeting only when it has greeting text), though clearing a managed field to null and re-sending an unchanged value are both deliberately allowed; 422 number_in_pool when setting purpose 'main' on a number that still rotates between website visitors. is_active false is a partial release: it clears this DID off every extension presenting it as caller ID, on the PBX as well as here, best-effort per extension, so a failed clear is only logged and that phone keeps presenting a number this account no longer presents. The body is strict, so an unknown key is a 422 that writes nothing: cnam_name and cnam_enabled are NOT settable here (use voice_number_cnam_set), nor are tf_verification_status or the audio-cache columns. This route calls NO audit helper at all, so a routing change made here leaves no entry on the voice audit page, and the per-user communications.numbers permission that guards the dashboard is not applied on this surface. 404 not_found is also the cross-tenant answer. 402 voice_not_enabled without the paid Voice add-on.

tools.name: voice_numbers_list
tools.description: List the account's DIDs (E.164 phone numbers). Filter by is_active.

tools.name: voice_numbers_search
tools.description: Searches Telnyx carrier inventory for buyable phone numbers. SEARCH ONLY: it places no order, RESERVES NOTHING and spends no money, so a number listed here is still on the open market and another buyer can take it between this call and any purchase. Returns { results: [ { e164, locality, state, monthly_cost_cents, setup_cost_cents, features, number_type } ] }; locality, state and both cost fields can each be null. features is a string array such as voice and sms, and a result without sms cannot text. monthly_cost_cents is a RECURRING carrier charge and setup_cost_cents a one-time one, nonzero on premium prefixes, so a shortlist handed to a human carries real cost. The purchase lane is voice_number_purchase: shortlist here, get a human's yes on the exact e164 and its costs, then buy that ONE number by e164 - never tell anyone a number has been ordered or reserved until the purchase tool returns. Refusals: 422 missing_filter when a LOCAL search names none of area_code, locality or state, because an unbounded 'every DID in North America' request just burns a Telnyx call; 422 invalid_body when number_type toll_free is combined with any geographic filter, since toll-free inventory is non-geographic and Telnyx would return zero rows, and equally when toll_free_prefix is sent under local mode. 800 is deliberately missing from toll_free_prefix and cannot be searched at all: premium carrier pricing with no billing pass-through makes it unpurchasable at every layer. THE TRAP THAT IS NOT A CLIENT ERROR: 503 voice_server_update_pending on a toll-free search whose results are not all toll-free. That is a deploy-window guard, not a bug: a voice server predating toll-free support ignores the field, runs a LOCAL search and hands back geographic numbers, and buying one of those as toll-free would land a local DID with NO E911. The builder auto-deploys in about 35 minutes while the voice server is a manual deploy, so this window is real. Retry later, do not fall back to a local search and call it toll-free. Other traps: an empty results array on a 200 means no matching inventory, not a failure; there is NO cursor and NO pagination, so limit (1 to 50, default 20) is the entire result set you can ever get; area_code must be exactly three digits with no +1 and state must be a two-letter code, which the route uppercases for you; any voice-server 5xx surfaces as 503 voice_server_error while a non-carrier exception is rethrown as a 500. Each call is one outbound Telnyx API request billed to this account's carrier relationship, so do not loop it to page through inventory. 402 voice_not_enabled without the paid Voice add-on.

tools.name: voice_phone_tracking_config_delete
tools.description: Deletes a project's phone-tracking config for ONE environment - turning tracking off for that tier. The row is gone (there is no disable-but-keep; to pause while keeping settings, use voice_phone_tracking_config_set with enabled false - but remember that is a FULL REPLACE, resend everything). The deployed site still carries the injected tracking script until that environment is REDEPLOYED; the script's config lookups just stop answering, so calls stop attributing immediately but the tag lingers in the HTML. Attribution history and the pool itself are untouched. 400 invalid_env without ?env=; 404 not_found when no config row exists for this project+env on this account (also the cross-tenant answer); 402 voice_not_enabled. RETURNS { ok: true }. The audit write is skipped for Olympus keys, so this disable leaves no entry on the voice audit page.

tools.name: voice_phone_tracking_config_get
tools.description: Read a website project's phone-tracking (number-swap) config for ONE environment (development|staging|production - preview is excluded by design, its container is ephemeral). Returns { config, siblings }: config is the env's row or null, siblings:[{environment, enabled, pool_id}] says where tracking IS configured, so config:null with a production sibling means 'off here, live there' - not 'never set up'. The config carries pool_id, enabled, swap_selector, swap_text_regex, swap_source_numbers (E.164 list the snippet swaps even without tel: links), widget_enabled/widget_position/widget_fallback_e164, and consent_mode. DEPLOY-WINDOW FICTION: if the consent_mode column is not pushed on this deployment, every row silently reports consent_mode 'analytics' as a synthesized default and nothing in the payload says so. Remember the config row is only half the story: the tracking script itself is injected into the site at DEPLOY time, so an enabled config on a never-redeployed site swaps nothing - voice_swap_test is the end-to-end truth. 400 invalid_env without ?env=; 404 project_not_found is also the cross-tenant answer; 402 voice_not_enabled. Read-only.

tools.name: voice_phone_tracking_config_set
tools.description: Upserts a project's phone-tracking config for one environment - and it is a FULL REPLACE, not a merge: every omitted field is RESET to its default on the stored row. Concretely, omitting these CLEARS them: swap_selector -> null, swap_text_regex -> null, swap_source_numbers -> [] (the whole list), widget_fallback_e164 -> null, widget_enabled -> false, widget_position -> 'bottom_right', enabled -> true. THE ONE EXCEPTION is consent_mode: omitted means UNCHANGED on an existing row ('immediate' only on first create) - a partial save must not reset a tenant's privacy posture. So: read voice_phone_tracking_config_get first and resend every field you want to keep. environment travels in the BODY on this tool (the proxy cannot send query params on PUT); it defaults to nothing - omitting it is 400 invalid_env. CONSENT IS BAKED INTO THE DEPLOYED SITE: the consent gate is written into the site's HTML at deploy time, so changing consent_mode (or enabling tracking at all) does NOTHING on the live site until that environment is REDEPLOYED - say so every time you change it. swap_source_numbers IS THE CALLRAIL-CUTOVER LEVER: list the old CallRail (or any legacy) numbers as they appear in the page text and the snippet swaps them even with no tel: link - the whole write is refused with 422 invalid_swap_source_numbers naming the exact unparseable entry (entries are normalized to E.164 and deduped; max 5). Refusals: 404 project_not_found and 404 pool_not_found are each also the cross-tenant answer (project and pool are checked separately); 422 invalid_body; 402 voice_not_enabled. Deploy-window tolerance: a missing consent_mode column saves everything else and drops only that field (console warn, not surfaced). RETURNS { config }. The audit write is skipped for Olympus keys, so this change leaves no entry on the voice audit page.

tools.name: voice_pool_create
tools.description: Creates a tracking-DID (dynamic number insertion) pool. Writes ONE database row - no carrier call, no PBX call, no spend, and the pool is born EMPTY: numbers join via voice_pool_numbers_add, and a project opts in via voice_phone_tracking_config_set, so nothing swaps anywhere until both happen. Defaults chosen from a production starvation incident: conversion_sticky_days defaults to 2 (NOT 30) because a converted hold removes the DID from rotation for the whole window; sticky_minutes defaults to 30; exhaustion_policy defaults to swap_fallback (visitors see the main DID when every pool number is held; 'reject' keeps the number the page already rendered). An optional destination declares pool-level routing inherited by every number that later joins; its target is validated against THIS account (422 invalid_destination) or one tenant could ring another's extension. Prompt fields (whisper_template/greeting_text/voice ids) kick off Cartesia audio rendering fire-and-forget - the create returns immediately and ring time falls back to robo-TTS until the audio lands. DEPLOY-WINDOW TRAP: if the newer call-handling columns are not pushed on this deployment, the create still succeeds but SILENTLY DROPS the destination and every call-handling field (a console warn, nothing in the response), so re-read with voice_pool_get before trusting them. 422 invalid_body for a malformed payload; 402 voice_not_enabled when the paid Voice add-on is off. RETURNS { pool }. The audit write is skipped for Olympus keys, so this create leaves no entry on the voice audit page.

tools.name: voice_pool_delete
tools.description: PERMANENTLY deletes a tracking-DID pool - and it deletes WITHOUT dependency checks. The voice_did_pools row goes and its attribution sessions and membership rows CASCADE with it, so every in-flight visitor session is ORPHANED: a visitor still looking at a swapped number on the site calls a DID whose pool no longer exists, and the call's source attribution is gone even though the call still connects (the DIDs keep whatever per-number routing they had). Any project phone-tracking config still pointing at this pool is silently stranded too. IT RELEASES NOTHING: the member DIDs stay owned, active, billed and keep purpose 'did_pool' - they do NOT flip back to 'tracking' the way voice_pool_numbers_remove flips them, so after a delete the number list shows pool-purposed DIDs that are in no pool. To retire a pool cleanly: voice_phone_tracking_config_delete (or repoint) the projects using it, voice_pool_numbers_remove each member, THEN delete. Uses a bounded RETURNING so it works in schema deploy windows. RETURNS { ok: true } with no warning key. 404 not_found is also the cross-tenant answer; 402 voice_not_enabled. The audit write is skipped for Olympus keys, so nothing records who deleted it.

tools.name: voice_pool_e911_apply
tools.description: Applies ONE validated E911 (emergency dispatch) address to every LOCAL number in a pool - the office-move tool, because pool DIDs are interchangeable and a pool where three numbers still point at the old suite is a 911 dispatch to the wrong address. This makes a REAL CARRIER CALL PER LOCAL NUMBER, and per number the CARRIER is updated FIRST and the local row only afterwards, so a number can never read 'validated' against an address Telnyx does not hold - a failed number's row is untouched. Toll-free members are SKIPPED, NOT FAILED (toll-free is not E911-capable at the carrier; a mixed pool applies to its local half). THE BATCH NEVER ABORTS: one refusal does not lose the others' work; every failure is collected into failed:[{e164,error}] with the carrier's own message (a number with no carrier id fails with 'number has no carrier id — re-provision it first'). A number already on the target address is silently left alone (neither updated nor failed). RETURNS { updated, skipped_toll_free, failed } - a 200 with a non-empty failed array is a PARTIAL success; retry is safe because already-updated numbers are skipped on the next pass. Refusals: 422 e911_address_invalid when the address is another account's OR has never been carrier-validated (no telnyx_address_id) - register and validate it on the E911 page (voice_e911_address_create) first; 404 not_found for a foreign pool; 402 voice_not_enabled. The audit write is skipped for Olympus keys, so this bulk change leaves no entry on the voice audit page.

tools.name: voice_pool_get
tools.description: One tracking-DID pool by id, with its member DIDs hydrated - the single-pool read voice_pools_list does not offer. Returns { pool } with the full knob set (sticky windows, exhaustion_policy, call handling, tracking sources, the raw un-resolved destination trio) plus member_count and members:[{member_id, weight, voice_number_id, number:{id,e164,label,is_active}|null, created_at}] - note this shape DOES carry weight and is_active, which the fleet list drops. member_count counts raw membership rows while a member whose DID was deleted or belongs to another account hydrates number:null, so count > non-null members means a stale membership, not truncation. THE CALL-HANDLING BLOCK CAN BE FICTION: whisper/greeting/caller_id/attribution/tracking_source fields ride a second read that swallows P2022, so on a deployment where those columns are not pushed the pool silently reports hardcoded defaults (whisper_enabled false, caller_id_mode 'caller', attribution_model 'first_touch', tracking_source_mode 'all', rest null) with nothing in the payload saying the read failed. inbound_target_type/inbound_target_id come back as a bare type and UUID with no name resolution. PII: members carry live E.164 tracking numbers. Read-only: no spend, nothing leaves the database. 404 not_found is also the cross-tenant answer; 402 voice_not_enabled when the paid Voice add-on is off.

tools.name: voice_pool_numbers_add
tools.description: Adds an EXISTING owned DID to a tracking pool - this does NOT buy a number (voice_number_purchase does that). Three writes ride one call: the membership row; the DID's purpose flips to 'did_pool' so the whole product treats it as a tracking number from now on; and the pool's destination (if set) is inherited BEST-EFFORT - the DID's routing is rewritten and its FusionPBX route synced, but a route hiccup does NOT fail the add, so a 200 can hide a member that still routes nowhere: verify with voice_pool_numbers_list/voice_pools_list routing if the pool has a destination. Refusals: 404 number_not_found for a DID that is another account's OR inactive (the two are indistinguishable by design - the anti pool-stuffing check); 409 already_in_pool because a DID can live in exactly ONE pool (the message says whether it is this pool or another - remove it there first); 404 not_found for a foreign pool id; 422 invalid_body; 402 voice_not_enabled. weight (1-100, default 1) biases rotation toward this DID. RETURNS { member } (its id is the member_id used to remove). The audit write is skipped for Olympus keys, so this add leaves no entry on the voice audit page.

tools.name: voice_pool_numbers_list
tools.description: List the DIDs in one tracking pool.
