Returns { members:[{member_id, weight, voice_number_id, number:{id,e164,label,is_active}|null, created_at}] }, oldest membership first. member_id (NOT voice_number_id) is what voice_pool_numbers_remove takes. weight (1-100) biases rotation - this and voice_pool_get are the only reads that show it. number:null means the membership row points at a DID that was deleted or is not this account's (the hydration is account-scoped on purpose); such a stale row still occupies the DID's one-pool-per-number slot until removed. is_active false means the DID is in the pool but the assigner will not hand it out, so it quietly shrinks capacity. PII: live E.164 tracking numbers. Read-only: no spend, nothing leaves the database. 404 not_found is also the cross-tenant answer for the pool id; 402 voice_not_enabled.

tools.name: voice_pool_numbers_remove
tools.description: Removes one DID from a tracking pool by MEMBER id (member_id from voice_pool_numbers_list, NOT the voice_number_id and not an E.164). The membership row is deleted and the DID's purpose flips back to 'tracking' - it stays owned, active, billed and keeps its current routing; nothing is released to the carrier (retiring a DID entirely is voice_number_release, a different, gated act). What it does NOT do: existing sticky sessions on this DID are not ended, so a visitor already assigned this number keeps seeing it and calls keep arriving and attributing until the session expires - removal only stops NEW assignments. Removing a pool's last active number leaves new visitors on the exhaustion_policy fallback. 400 missing_member_id without the param; 404 not_found for a member id that is not in THIS pool (or a foreign pool id); 402 voice_not_enabled. RETURNS { ok: true }. The audit write is skipped for Olympus keys, so this removal leaves no entry on the voice audit page.

tools.name: voice_pool_update
tools.description: Edits a tracking-DID pool - THE call-handling lever after voice_call_tracking_setup. PARTIAL: only the fields you send change; nullable fields clear on explicit null (tracking_source_rules null is written as SQL NULL properly). THE DESTINATION IS THE BIG SIDE EFFECT: sending destination BULK-APPLIES it to every current member DID - each member's voice_numbers routing is rewritten AND its FusionPBX route is re-synced, one by one; per-member failures never fail the save, they come back as destination_apply_failures (a count) and those members keep their OLD routing until re-saved - a response carrying that key is a PARTIAL success, act on it. destination null clears the pool default only: members keep their current routing, future joiners inherit nothing. The target is validated against THIS account (422 invalid_destination). Prompt changes (whisper_enabled/whisper_template/greeting_text/either voice id) re-render audio fire-and-forget; ring time falls back to robo-TTS until it lands, and a voice change without re-render would keep playing the old voice forever - which is why the render fires on voice changes too. tracking_source_mode/rules gate NEW mints only; visitors inside a sticky window keep serving. DEPLOY WINDOW: a PATCH touching call-handling or destination fields while the columns are not pushed is an honest 503 not_ready - retry later, nothing was dropped; a rename alone survives the window. is_active false stops NEW assignments; existing sessions run out on their own. 404 not_found for another account's pool; 422 invalid_body; 402 voice_not_enabled. RETURNS { pool, destination_apply_failures? }. The audit write is skipped for Olympus keys, so this edit leaves no entry on the voice audit page.

tools.name: voice_pools_list
tools.description: List every tracking-DID (dynamic number insertion) pool on the account with its call handling, its member DIDs, and where each member DID actually sends an inbound call. Returns {pools:[{id,account_id,name,description,sticky_minutes,conversion_sticky_days,exhaustion_policy,is_active,inbound_target_type,inbound_target_id,forward_to_e164,created_at,updated_at,whisper_enabled,whisper_template,greeting_text,caller_id_mode,attribution_model,whisper_voice_id,greeting_voice_id,tracking_source_mode,tracking_source_rules,member_count,members:[{voice_number_id,e164,label,purpose,routing:{type,target_name,forward_to_e164}}]}]}. THE CALL-HANDLING BLOCK CAN BE FICTION: whisper_enabled, whisper_template, greeting_text, caller_id_mode, attribution_model, whisper_voice_id, greeting_voice_id, tracking_source_mode and tracking_source_rules come from a SECOND read wrapped in a try/catch that swallows P2022, so if those columns are not pushed on this deployment every pool silently reports the same hardcoded defaults (whisper_enabled false, caller_id_mode 'caller', attribution_model 'first_touch', tracking_source_mode 'all', the rest null) and NOTHING in the payload says the read failed. Never report those as a tenant's configured settings without corroborating in the dashboard. The POOL-LEVEL destination is returned raw and un-resolved: inbound_target_type and inbound_target_id come back as a bare type string and a bare UUID with no name, and only the per-member routing block is name-resolved. member_count counts raw membership rows while members[] skips any row whose DID is missing from the account-scoped number lookup, so member_count greater than members.length means the DID was deleted or belongs to another account, not that the page was truncated. Member rows also DROP voice_pool_members.weight, which is what biases rotation, so you cannot see why one DID is served more often than another from this response. In routing, a non-null type with target_name null means the target was deleted or belongs to another account; type null returns the LITERAL synthesized string 'Account default routing' as target_name, which is a label this route invents and not a real target; routing.forward_to_e164 is populated only for external_number extensions, so a null there is not proof the call stays on the platform. PII: this response carries live E.164 tracking numbers, and when a seat-assigned extension has a blank display_name the label falls back to the linked user's first/last name and then to their raw EMAIL ADDRESS, so a staff member's email can appear in routing.target_name. No pagination and no filters: inactive pools come back too, so filter on is_active yourself. tracking_source_mode and tracking_source_rules gate NEW session mints only, so tightening the rules does nothing to a visitor already inside a sticky window (sticky_minutes, extended by conversion_sticky_days once they call), and a pool whose DIDs are all held by sticky sessions falls back per exhaustion_policy ('swap_fallback' shows the tenant's main DID and flags the call, 'reject' keeps the number the page already rendered). Read-only itself; the write lane is voice_pool_create / voice_pool_get / voice_pool_update / voice_pool_delete plus the membership and config tools. 402 voice_not_enabled when the Voice add-on is off for the account (or the account has no billing row).

tools.name: voice_port_order_action
tools.description: Run one carrier action on a filed port order: confirm | cancel | activate. CONFIRM IS THE LEGAL ACT: it sends the request to the LOSING carrier under the signed LOA - from that moment the losing carrier is processing a release of the customer's numbers. Check voice_port_order_requirements FIRST; confirming with unmet requirements bounces back as an exception days later. CANCEL asks the carrier to withdraw (cancel-pending collapses to local 'cancelled'). ACTIVATE is a REQUEST, not completion: it moves action_status to 'activating' only; the local status flips to 'ported' when the carrier actually finishes (webhook/poll), which is also what triggers adoption. Local status is RANKED and never regresses: after confirm the row deliberately reads 'pending_carrier' while the carrier still echoes 'in-process' - that is the vocabulary running one step ahead, not a bug. Returns {port_order, raw} - the row masked (PIN/account write-only), raw whitelisted (the carrier's end_user block never passes through). Refusals: 422 invalid_action for anything else; 404 not_found (foreign ids look identical); 409 not_submitted on a draft with no carrier order (submit via voice_port_order_create's recovery path first). Olympus writes leave no audit row (service keys have no user; the audit path is skipped). 402 voice_not_enabled when the Voice add-on is off for the account (or the account has no billing row).

tools.name: voice_port_order_comment_add
tools.description: Append a comment to the carrier-ops thread on one port order. THIS IS VISIBLE TO THE CARRIER'S PORTING OPERATIONS TEAM (it shows in Telnyx's portal too) and cannot be edited or deleted from this platform once posted: NEVER paste a PIN, an account number, or anything this API masks everywhere else - the masking exists precisely so those values do not end up in places like this thread. Use it to answer carrier questions ('bill uploaded, please re-review') and keep an excepted port moving. Body 1..4000 chars. Returns {comment} as the carrier recorded it. Refusals: 409 not_submitted on a draft (there is no carrier thread to write to); 404 not_found for an unknown or foreign order id; 422 invalid_body outside 1..4000. Olympus writes leave no audit row (service keys have no user; the audit path is skipped). 402 voice_not_enabled when the Voice add-on is off for the account (or the account has no billing row).

tools.name: voice_port_order_comments_list
tools.description: Read the carrier-ops thread on one port order - the dialogue with the carrier's porting operations team, where they ask for corrections or documents and a timely reply keeps the port on schedule. Returns {comments:[{id, body, user_type, created_at}]} - sanitized to those four fields; user_type says who wrote it (the carrier's side vs ours). A DRAFT (never filed) returns 200 {comments:[]} WITHOUT calling the carrier, which is indistinguishable from a filed order that simply has no comments - check telnyx_order_id via voice_port_order_get before reading an empty thread as silence from carrier ops. This is a live network call: {error:'carrier_error',message} at the carrier's status (5xx collapses to 502). Read-only. 404 not_found for an unknown or foreign order id; 402 voice_not_enabled when the Voice add-on is off for the account (or the account has no billing row).

tools.name: voice_port_order_create
tools.description: CREATE AND FILE a number-port order with the carrier - a LEGAL filing on the customer's behalf. It writes a local draft row, then files a real carrier order; 'submitted' in the response means filed with OUR carrier and being validated - NOTHING moves at the losing carrier until voice_port_order_action confirm, which is the legal act under the signed LOA. Tell the customer to KEEP SERVICE ACTIVE at the losing carrier until the port completes: cancelling early kills the numbers. Returns {port_order, sibling_orders:[], warning?}: the carrier auto-splits a create by country/type/losing-carrier, so one call can yield several rows - siblings share batch_key (= the primary's PORT-XXXXXX support_key); treat the batch as ONE filing. losing_pin and losing_account_number are WRITE-ONLY: encrypted at rest and masked in every response (PIN as bullets, account number bullets + last 4), so do not expect to read them back. A 502 submit_failed IS NOT A NO-OP: the draft row exists (its id is in port_order_id) and on the patch_details_failed path a CARRIER DRAFT exists too (action_status 'draft_only'); fix via voice_port_order_update + confirm on that SAME id - re-calling this tool files a DUPLICATE carrier order. warning 'persist_partial' means the carrier orders exist but some local rows failed; do NOT re-create - the split ids are recoverable by ops. Prefer voice_portability_check first, and use voice_port_order_share_link_create for the LOA e-sign + bill upload (the client fills their own PIN/account there). Olympus writes leave no audit row (service keys have no user; the audit path is skipped). 422 invalid_body; 402 voice_not_enabled when the Voice add-on is off for the account (or the account has no billing row).

tools.name: voice_port_order_get
tools.description: Read one number-port order by id. Returns {port_order:{...}} in the same masked shape as voice_port_orders_list, resolved with an account-scoped findFirst, so an id belonging to another tenant is a 404 and never a cross-tenant read of someone else's porting paperwork. This is the only way to reach an order older than the 100-row window voice_port_orders_list caps at, and you need the id from elsewhere: support_key is a field on the row, not a lookup key here. SAME PII WARNING: only losing_pin and losing_account_number are masked, and the account number still shows its real last four digits; the billing street address, the billing telephone number, the authorized signer, the full E.164 list, the LOA and bill S3 keys, and the unmasked authorization_json / end_user_location_json blobs all come back verbatim. THIS IS THE LOCAL MIRROR, NOT THE CARRIER. status, status_raw, foc_date and exception_details_json are whatever the last carrier webhook or the porting-status poll cron wrote; this route performs no refresh, so a freshly changed order can read stale, and an unknown carrier token updates status_raw ONLY and leaves status frozen. The local vocabulary also runs one step ahead of the carrier by design, so 'submitted' can sit on an order the carrier still holds as an unconfirmed draft: read action_status (draft_only|details_set|submitted|activating|cancelled) for what the carrier actions actually did. last_notified_status and last_notified_comment_at are notification watermarks advanced by the sweep cron, not port state, and reading last_notified_status as the status will report the wrong thing. SUCCESS THAT IS NOT SUCCESS: adoption_state_json is the per-e164 adoption ledger {adopted_at, provider_number_id, route_created, messaging_attached} and adopted_at is set only once EVERY number on the order is adopted, so status 'ported' with adopted_at null means the transfer completed at the carrier while the DIDs are not yet usable on the platform. 'exception' means the losing carrier flagged a fixable problem, with its codes verbatim in exception_details_json (ACCOUNT_NUMBER_MISMATCH, LOA_ILLEGIBLE and similar); pair it with voice_port_order_requirements. Read-only itself; carrier-facing corrections go through voice_port_order_update (the local-only notes PATCH stays untwinned). 404 not_found for an unknown or foreign id; 402 voice_not_enabled when the Voice add-on is off for the account (or the account has no billing row).

tools.name: voice_port_order_refresh_status
tools.description: Pull the LIVE status from the carrier for one port order and mirror it onto the local row - the manual fallback when a webhook was missed. Nothing changes AT the carrier. The mirror is RANK-GUARDED: local status only moves FORWARD to a known canonical token and never leaves ported/rejected/cancelled, so a 200 whose port_order.status did not change is normal and correct in two cases - the carrier echoed an UNKNOWN token (only status_raw updates; the order may have advanced under a name this platform does not know - status_raw is the honest answer) or the carrier's echo lags the deliberately-ahead local vocabulary. Never read an unchanged status as 'the refresh failed'. Notifications are NOT sent from here; the poll cron's watermark sweep picks up any transition this write causes, so refreshing does not double-notify. Returns {port_order, raw} - the row masked (PIN/account write-only), raw whitelisted (no end_user block). Refusals: 404 not_found (foreign ids look identical); 409 not_submitted on a draft with no carrier order. Olympus writes leave no audit row (service keys have no user; the audit path is skipped). 402 voice_not_enabled when the Voice add-on is off for the account (or the account has no billing row).

tools.name: voice_port_order_requirements
tools.description: Ask the carrier what this port order still needs (an LOA, a recent bill, a verification code) before it can be confirmed, so a confirm is not filed with unmet requirements that bounce back as an exception days later. Returns {requirements:[{field_type,name,description,acceptance_criteria,met}]}; the raw carrier payload is deliberately NOT returned, because it carries the end-user admin block holding the account number and PIN that are masked everywhere else. THE EMPTY LIST IS THE TRAP AND IT IS THE WHOLE POINT OF READING THIS CAREFULLY: an order that has never reached the carrier (telnyx_order_id null, which every draft is) short-circuits to 200 with requirements: [] without calling out at all, and a carrier payload whose requirements key is not an array produces the identical empty result. An empty array therefore means 'nothing was ever asked' exactly as often as it means 'nothing is outstanding'. Confirm the order actually has a telnyx_order_id via voice_port_order_get before reading an empty list as all-clear, and note that having a telnyx_order_id still does not mean the order was confirmed (check action_status). met is Boolean(field_value): it says a value was SUBMITTED, not that the carrier ACCEPTED it, so an illegible LOA or a mismatched account number reads met true here and only surfaces as an exception on the order days later. LITERAL FALLBACKS MASQUERADING AS DATA: name falls back to record_type and then to the literal string 'Requirement', field_type falls back to the literal string 'document', and description and acceptance_criteria come straight from the carrier and are frequently null, so a vague-looking entry may be a payload this route could not name rather than a vague requirement. This is a LIVE NETWORK CALL out through the voice server to the carrier, not a local read: expect real latency and a real failure mode. The order is resolved account-scoped BEFORE its telnyx_order_id is handed to the carrier lookup, precisely because that carrier call would otherwise be a cross-tenant read of another account's port paperwork. Errors: {error:'carrier_error',message} at the carrier's own status code, collapsed to 502 when the carrier returned 5xx, and {error:'internal_error'} at 500 otherwise. Read-only: uploading the LOA or the bill, and confirming or cancelling the order, are legal acts under a signed authorization; voice_port_order_action is the ask-gated lane for confirm/cancel/activate and its own description says to read THIS tool first. 404 not_found for an unknown or foreign order id; 402 voice_not_enabled when the Voice add-on is off for the account (or the account has no billing row).

tools.name: voice_port_order_share_link_create
tools.description: Mint a login-free handoff link for one port order - the CLIENT (the losing-carrier account holder) opens /port-setup/{token} to fill in the account number, PIN and service address, upload a recent bill, and E-SIGN THE LOA. THE URL IS A CREDENTIAL: whoever holds it can write losing-carrier secrets onto this order and sign the authorization, logged out - and it is shown ONCE (only a hash is stored; there is no way to read it again, only revoke and re-mint). Never paste it into a ticket, a doc, or chat with anyone but the client. With recipient_email set it also SENDS A REAL EMAIL to that address with the link; email_sent:false in the response means the link was minted but the email did not go out - deliver the URL yourself. ttl_days 1..90, default 30. Returns {url, expires_at, token_id, email_sent}; keep token_id if you may need a targeted revoke. This is the intended path for LOA + bill: prefer it over collecting PINs into voice_port_order_update yourself. Olympus writes leave no audit row (service keys have no user; the audit path is skipped). 404 not_found for an unknown or foreign order id; 422 invalid_body; 402 voice_not_enabled when the Voice add-on is off for the account (or the account has no billing row).

tools.name: voice_port_order_share_link_revoke
tools.description: Revoke this port order's handoff link(s) - the kill switch for a leaked or stale credential URL. With token_id (from voice_port_order_share_links_list) it revokes exactly that link; WITHOUT token_id it revokes EVERY live link on the order, so omit it only when that is what you mean. Returns {revoked: n}. revoked: 0 with a token_id means that token was not a live link on THIS order (already revoked, expired, or someone else's) - nothing foreign can be revoked from here. Revocation is immediate and permanent for the token (the client's form stops opening); mint a fresh link to re-enable the handoff. A revoked link does not undo anything the client already submitted through it. Olympus writes leave no audit row (service keys have no user; the audit path is skipped). 404 not_found for an unknown or foreign order id; 402 voice_not_enabled when the Voice add-on is off for the account (or the account has no billing row).

tools.name: voice_port_order_share_links_list
tools.description: List this port order's ACTIVE handoff links - unrevoked and unexpired only, newest first. Returns {links:[{id, created_at, expires_at, use_count, last_used_at}]}. THE URL IS NEVER HERE: only token hashes are stored, so the link itself was shown exactly once at mint time - this tool answers 'does a live link exist, has the client opened it' (use_count / last_used_at), not 'what is the link'. If the client lost the URL, revoke and mint a fresh one. An empty list means no LIVE links; revoked or expired ones are filtered out, not flagged. The id column here is the token_id that voice_port_order_share_link_revoke takes. Read-only. 404 not_found for an unknown or foreign order id; 402 voice_not_enabled when the Voice add-on is off for the account (or the account has no billing row).

tools.name: voice_port_order_update
tools.description: Carrier-facing corrections on a FILED port order - the fix-and-resubmit path after an exception (read the codes in exception_details_json via voice_port_order_get) and pre-confirm adjustments (FOC datetime, SMS toggle). The carrier PATCH runs FIRST; the local row updates only after the carrier accepted, so a 502 carrier_error means NOTHING changed anywhere - fix and retry is safe. After correcting an exception, re-run voice_port_order_action confirm; an update alone resumes nothing. Exactly these 8 fields, strictly - any other key is 422 invalid_body, and the local-only notes edit is not exposed here. losing_account_number / losing_pin are WRITE-ONLY: sent plaintext to the carrier, stored encrypted, masked in the response - you can set them, never read them. Returns {port_order} masked. Refusals: 409 not_submitted on a draft (no carrier order to PATCH); 409 order_terminal once ported/cancelled/rejected; 422 empty_update on an empty body; 404 not_found (foreign ids look identical). Olympus writes leave no audit row (service keys have no user; the audit path is skipped). 402 voice_not_enabled when the Voice add-on is off for the account (or the account has no billing row).

tools.name: voice_port_order_verification_codes_send
tools.description: Trigger the carrier to send verification codes for a port order - A CUSTOMER-FACING SIDE EFFECT: the customer's ACTUAL PHONES ring (verification_method 'call') or receive an SMS ('sms', the default), right now, once per listed number, on the numbers still served by their CURRENT carrier. Warn the customer before firing, never fire speculatively or in a loop, and never re-send while codes are still outstanding - each send is another round of their phones going off. The customer reads the codes to you; submit them with voice_port_order_verification_codes_verify. phone_numbers is 1..100 and SHOULD be numbers on this order - the route checks only the count, so an off-order number reaches the carrier and fails there. Returns {result} as the carrier reports the dispatch. Refusals: 409 not_submitted on a draft with no carrier order; 404 not_found for an unknown or foreign order id; 422 invalid_body. Olympus writes leave no audit row (service keys have no user; the audit path is skipped). 402 voice_not_enabled when the Voice add-on is off for the account (or the account has no billing row).

tools.name: voice_port_order_verification_codes_verify
tools.description: Submit the verification codes the customer collected (after voice_port_order_verification_codes_send made their phones ring or buzz) to the carrier for one port order. verification_codes is 1..100 of {phone_number, code} - the phone_number must match the number the code was sent to. A wrong or expired code is the CARRIER's error to report (it comes back as {error:'carrier_error',message} at the carrier's status, 5xx collapsed to 502), not a local refusal - on a code failure re-collect from the customer, and only re-SEND (their phones go off again) if the codes expired. Returns {result} verbatim from the carrier; read it for per-number acceptance rather than assuming a 200 verified everything. Refusals: 409 not_submitted on a draft with no carrier order; 404 not_found for an unknown or foreign order id; 422 invalid_body. Olympus writes leave no audit row (service keys have no user; the audit path is skipped). 402 voice_not_enabled when the Voice add-on is off for the account (or the account has no billing row).

tools.name: voice_port_orders_list
tools.description: List the account's number-port orders (moving a phone number in from a losing carrier), newest first. Returns {port_orders:[...]} of voice_port_orders rows: status, status_raw, action_status, support_key (PORT-XXXXXX), batch_key, losing_carrier_name, billing_name, billing_phone_number, billing_address_json, authorized_signer, phone_numbers, requested/actual/foc dates, telnyx_order_id, exception_details_json, adoption_state_json, adopted_at, rejection_reason, notes. THIS RESPONSE IS CUSTOMER PII AND LEGAL PORTING PAPERWORK. EXACTLY TWO FIELDS ARE MASKED AND NOTHING ELSE IS REDACTED: losing_pin returns as bullets, and losing_account_number returns as bullets plus the REAL LAST FOUR DIGITS, which the route decrypts on purpose to produce, so this call does disclose the tail of the losing carrier's account number (if decryption throws, the tail is silently empty and looks identical to a short number). The billing street address, the billing telephone number (the BTN), the authorized signer's name, the full E.164 list and the S3 keys of the signed LOA and the carrier bill all come back verbatim. authorization_json and end_user_location_json are ALSO returned untouched and are documented in the schema as {authorized_person, billing_phone_number, account_number, pin_passcode} and the end user's street address, so the masking is not a defence for them; nothing in this platform writes authorization_json today, which is why it reads null, but the sanitizer would not cover it if anything ever did. Do not paste this response into a channel, a ticket or a document. HARD CAP: take 100, with no pagination, no cursor and no filter, so an account with more than 100 orders can never reach the oldest ones through this tool and the cut is silent; use voice_port_order_get with a known id to reach past it. STATUS TRAPS: the LOCAL vocabulary deliberately runs one step AHEAD of the carrier, so 'submitted' means filed with OUR side and being validated while the carrier order may still be raw draft and unconfirmed, and 'pending_carrier' means it sits with the LOSING carrier; the carrier's own raw token 'submitted' maps to pending_carrier, so the two vocabularies collide on the same word and status_raw is what answers what the carrier thinks. action_status (draft_only|details_set|submitted|activating|cancelled) is the sub-state of the carrier action calls and is the honest answer to 'was this actually confirmed'. An unrecognised carrier token normalizes to NULL and the local status DELIBERATELY DOES NOT MOVE (only status_raw is updated), so an order that looks stuck may have advanced at the carrier under a token this platform does not know. 'cancel-pending' collapses into 'cancelled', so an in-flight cancellation reads as finished unless you check status_raw. One submission can appear as several rows because the carrier auto-splits a create by country/type/SPID; siblings share batch_key. Read-only itself; the write lane exists now - voice_portability_check (free), voice_port_order_create (files a real carrier order), voice_port_order_action (confirm is THE legal act under the signed LOA), voice_port_order_update and the share-link/comments/verification tools - each wanting an explicit human decision. 402 voice_not_enabled when the Voice add-on is off for the account (or the account has no billing row).

tools.name: voice_portability_check
tools.description: Pre-flight for a number port: can these numbers move to Hiveku at all, and do they FastPort / support SMS? FREE at the carrier and read-only on the carrier side - no order is created, nothing is filed, nothing changes at the losing carrier - so run it BEFORE collecting the LOA paperwork. Takes 1..100 numbers; '+' is prepended when missing. Returns {results:[{phone_number,portable,fast_portable,messaging_capable,not_portable_reason}]}. THE LIST CAN BE LONGER-LOOKING THAN THE TRUTH: any number the carrier did not echo back comes back as a SYNTHESIZED entry (portable false, reason 'No verdict returned for this number...') - that is 'the carrier said nothing', typically a typo'd number, not a carrier denial; do not report it as 'cannot be ported'. portable false WITH a real reason is the carrier's actual verdict. messaging_capable false on a number you plan to text is a real problem to raise before filing. This is a live network call: errors are {error:'carrier_error',message} at the carrier's status (5xx collapses to 502) or {error:'internal_error'} at 500. No write happens anywhere, so there is no audit row to expect. 422 invalid_body outside 1..100 numbers; 402 voice_not_enabled when the Voice add-on is off for the account (or the account has no billing row).

tools.name: voice_presence_get
tools.description: Live BLF lamp state for the account's extensions: { extensions: [{ extension, registered, state, direction, other_party }], channels_ok }, where state is offline | idle | ringing | in_call | hold and other_party is the far-party number of the call in progress. Treat the payload as PII: it says who is on the phone right now and with which number. It is a point-in-time snapshot proxied from voice_server, not a subscription, so two consecutive calls legitimately disagree. THE SILENT FAILURE: the body { extensions: [], channels_ok: false } is returned both when the tenant has no fusionpbx_domain provisioned (voice never set up) and when the voice_server call threw and was swallowed into a console.error, and it is also what a genuinely idle or empty account returns whenever channel state is down. The route emits no 5xx, so an empty list must never be read as 'nobody is on a call'. When channels_ok is false but the list is non-empty, FreeSWITCH channel state was unavailable and every lamp degrades to registered/offline: ringing, in_call and hold can never appear no matter what is really happening. Second trap: this Olympus twin is deliberately stricter than the dashboard. An Olympus key carries no system_role, so the handler takes the restrictive branch UNCONDITIONALLY and extensions owned by a saas_owner or saas_user are always filtered out, meaning an extension voice_extensions_list shows can be legitimately absent here. FusionPBX-side registrations with no matching voice_extensions row for the account are dropped silently too. 402 voice_not_enabled when the Voice add-on is off. Takes no parameters.

tools.name: voice_queue_create
tools.description: Creates an ACD call queue and provisions it on the PBX. READ THIS FIRST: QUEUES ARE NOT PRODUCTION-READY ON THIS PLATFORM. mod_callcenter silently moves an agent to On Break after missed calls and NOTHING in this product ever resets that state, so a staffed queue quietly stops ringing its agents with no error anywhere; and a queue whose fusionpbx_queue_uuid is null was never loaded into FreeSWITCH and answers nothing. For real call distribution PREFER A RING GROUP (voice_ring_group_create) until queues graduate. What actually happens: voice_server /internal/provision/queue is called BEFORE the row write and creates the mod_callcenter queue, its agent tiers and its dialplan rule on the shared EC2 PBX box, so unlike voice_queue_update a provisioning failure ABORTS the create - 4xx/5xx queue_provision_failed at the carrier's own status and NO row exists; a 200 from this tool therefore always carries a real fusionpbx_queue_uuid. The 5xxx dial extension is auto-allocated (409 no_extension_available when the account's 5000-5999 pool is exhausted). Refusals, verbatim: 409 not_provisioned when the tenant has no PBX domain yet (enable voice first); 422 invalid_member when ANY members[].extension_id is not this account's (the anti cross-tenant-staffing check); 422 greeting_voice_required for greeting_tts_text with no greeting_voice_id; 402 voice_not_enabled when the paid Voice add-on is off. MEDIA HONESTY: moh_s3_key is forwarded to the PBX only when it is an account-scoped allowlisted S3 key (ivr-audio/<this account uuid>/...); anything else - an https URL included - is STORED but never sent, and moh_local_path in the response is written ONLY from what voice_server reported placing, so null there means callers hear the default hold music no matter what the row says. greeting_tts_text is stored copy only - no create path renders queue greeting audio yet. RETURNS { queue, warning? }; a warning on a 200 is a partial success (the queue is live, the clip is not) - relay it. sla_answer_seconds, callback_enabled and member skills are persisted and never reach the phone system. No carrier spend. The audit write is skipped for Olympus keys, so this create leaves no entry on the voice audit page.

tools.name: voice_queue_delete
tools.description: PERMANENTLY deletes an ACD call queue. IRREVERSIBLE: the mod_callcenter queue, its agent tiers and its dialplan rule are torn down on the PBX, then the voice_queues row is deleted and its agent rows cascade. The 5xxx extension returns to the pool and can be claimed by something else, so recreating the queue may not get the same number back. RETURNS { id, deleted: true, warning? }. THE WARNING IS A PARTIAL DELETE, NOT A NOTE: teardown runs first but a failure is only reported, never aborted, so the row is deleted regardless and a live queue and dialplan rule can survive on the phone system for a queue Hiveku has forgotten. The warning says to run a tenant repair if calls still reach it, and that is literal - callers can still land in an unmanaged queue. Compare with voice_ring_group_delete, which aborts and deletes nothing when teardown fails. It DOES refuse with 409 queue_in_use while any phone number still routes here, naming how many, because that DID would otherwise start silently failing live calls. That number count is the ONLY dependency it queries. It is also the only pointer the routing schema models for a queue (an IVR menu digit and a ring-group fallback cannot target a queue), with two exceptions nothing checks: a call-tracking DID pool whose voice_did_pools.inbound_target_id is this queue, and a pending carrier order in voice_number_orders that will adopt into it, are both silently orphaned along with every number that later joins that pool. Also 404 not_found for a queue on another account, and 402 voice_not_enabled when the paid Voice add-on is off. The audit write is skipped for Olympus keys, so nothing records who deleted it.

tools.name: voice_queue_get
tools.description: One ACD queue with its member rows, by id. Returns { queue: { ...full voice_queues row, members: [{ id, queue_id, extension_id, skills, tier, position, timeout_seconds, created_at }] } } - the same shape voice_queues_list returns per entry, without pulling the whole fleet. Read-only: no spend, nothing leaves the database, nothing changes on the PBX. READ THE TWO NULLS BEFORE CALLING A QUEUE LIVE, and neither is reported as an error: fusionpbx_queue_uuid null means the queue exists in Postgres but was never loaded into FreeSWITCH, so it answers nothing (the dashboard renders a 'not provisioned' banner for exactly this state); extension null means no 5xxx dial number was ever allocated, and every routing path resolves its target down to a numeric extension string, so the queue is unreachable even when provisioned. Member rows carry extension_id UUIDs with NO dial number and NO display name - join against voice_extensions_list to say who staffs it. moh_local_path null means the system default hold music plays regardless of moh_s3_key, so a set key is not proof branded audio plays. position only affects ring order under the top_down strategy. 404 not_found is also the cross-tenant answer, indistinguishable from a deleted queue. 402 voice_not_enabled when the paid Voice add-on is off (or the account has no billing row), which is a plan refusal and not a missing queue.

tools.name: voice_queue_update
tools.description: Edits a live ACD call queue and re-provisions it. voice_server is called BEFORE the database write and REPLACES the mod_callcenter queue row, its agent tiers and its dialplan rule WHOLESALE on every save, including a pure rename, and re-places the hold-music audio; callers already waiting in the queue and callers arriving next are routed by the new config immediately. No TTS and no carrier spend. RETURNS { queue, warning? }, the queue re-read after the write with its members[] included. A 200 DOES NOT MEAN THE PHONE SYSTEM AGREED: a provisioning failure is caught, the edit still saves, and the only signal is `warning` saying the phone system did not pick up the change; a queue with no voice tenant or no extension saves with a different warning and pushes nothing at all. PARTIAL, with two different null rules. abandon_target_type, abandon_target_id, moh_s3_key, greeting_tts_text and greeting_voice_id are read by KEY PRESENCE, so sending null CLEARS them and omitting keeps the stored value; every other scalar falls back to the stored value. `members` REPLACES the roster wholesale and every extension_id must belong to this account (422 invalid_member); omit the key to leave agents alone, or send an empty array to leave the queue with no agents. THE ABANDON TARGET IS NOT HARD-VALIDATED, unlike a ring-group fallback. An abandon_target_id that is not in this account, or a ring group or IVR whose extension is NULL, resolves to nothing and the queue is provisioned with NO timeout action while the row happily stores the target: the dashboard shows an overflow destination and callers who exhaust max_wait_sec are dropped instead. Verify the target resolves before relying on it. Only voicemail, extension, ring_group and ivr are accepted (voicemail and extension take a voice_extensions uuid); ai_agent and external_number are 422 invalid_body even though the column allows them, and the abandon_target_external_e164 column cannot be set through this tool at all. MEDIA TRAPS. moh_s3_key is forwarded to the PBX only when it is an S3 key whose first segment is ivr-audio, did-audio or voicemail-greeting AND whose second segment is exactly this account's uuid, at most 512 chars, with no '..', no leading slash, no empty segment and none of the characters FreeSWITCH or the XML renderer would reinterpret; anything else, an https URL included, is STORED but never sent and the response tells you callers hear the default hold music. greeting_tts_text is stored copy only: the provisioning call is never handed the text or the voice, only a greeting_s3_key that NO path in this product ever writes, so the 'entry greeting did not land ... Re-save to retry' warning can never clear no matter how many times you retry. Sending greeting text with no voice (neither sent nor already stored) is 422 greeting_voice_required. skills on a member is persisted and never sent to mod_callcenter; callback_enabled and sla_answer_seconds are persisted and never sent either, so no callback is offered to anyone and no SLA is enforced. Also 404 not_found for another account's queue, 402 voice_not_enabled when the paid Voice add-on is off, and 422 invalid_body from a STRICT schema that rejects unknown keys. The audit write is skipped for Olympus keys, so this edit leaves no entry on the voice audit page.

tools.name: voice_queues_list
tools.description: List the account's ACD call queues (mod_callcenter), newest first, with no pagination, no filter and no cap: every queue with every member row comes back in one response. Returns {queues:[<full voice_queues row> + members:[...]]}: name, strategy (longest_idle|round_robin|top_down|agent_with_least_talk_time|random), extension, music-on-hold keys, greeting text/voice, announce_position, announce_frequency_sec, max_wait_sec, sla_answer_seconds, callback_enabled, the abandon target (abandon_target_type / abandon_target_id / abandon_target_external_e164, the last being a PSTN number an abandoning caller is pushed to), fusionpbx_queue_uuid, and each member's {id,queue_id,extension_id,skills,tier,position,timeout_seconds,created_at}. TWO NULLS MEAN THE QUEUE DOES NOT WORK AND NEITHER IS REPORTED AS AN ERROR: fusionpbx_queue_uuid null means the queue exists in Postgres but was never loaded into FreeSWITCH, so it answers nothing (the dashboard renders a 'not provisioned' banner for exactly this state; an API caller sees only a null); extension null means no 5xxx dial number was ever allocated, and every routing path in this system (a DID, an IVR option, a ring-group timeout) resolves its target down to a numeric extension string, so a queue with a null extension is unreachable even when it is provisioned. Check both before telling anyone their queue is live. Member rows carry extension_id UUIDs and NO dial number and NO display name, so you cannot say who staffs a queue from this response alone: join against voice_extensions_list. moh_local_path null means the queue falls back to the system default hold music no matter what moh_s3_key says, so a set moh_s3_key is not proof branded hold music plays. position is mod_callcenter's tier_position and only affects ring order under top_down (longest_idle and random ignore it), so reordering members changes nothing under those strategies. voice_queue_members has no account_id column of its own and is reached only through the account-scoped queue relation. Read-only itself; voice_queue_create exists now (it provisions mod_callcenter on a SHARED PBX box - read its NOT-production-ready warning first) and voice_queue_get reads one queue. 402 voice_not_enabled when the Voice add-on is off for the account (or the account has no billing row).

tools.name: voice_recent_calls
tools.description: Recent calls + dispositions for diagnosing call-flow issues. Used to investigate "calls aren't coming through" or "goes to voicemail too fast".

tools.name: voice_recording_url_get
tools.description: Issues a presigned S3 GET for a call's recorded audio: { url, expires_in_seconds: 300 }. DANGER, read before calling: the returned URL is an unauthenticated, shareable download of a real conversation. The AWS signature rides in the query string, so ANYONE who receives the link can stream or save the audio with no Hiveku login, no account and no further check for the next 5 minutes (RECORDING_URL_TTL_SECONDS = 300, not adjustable per call and NOT revocable once issued). Pasting it into a ticket, a chat message, a log line or an agent transcript republishes the recording to everyone who can read that surface, and it keeps working there until it expires. The route enforces no consent, retention or redaction check, so two-party-consent obligations rest entirely with the caller, and the presign is signed by pinned HIVEKU_ADMIN credentials rather than by the tenant. Prefer voice_call_transcript_get when you only need what was said. Silent failures: despite the /recordings/ path the id is voice_calls.id, NOT call_uuid and not an id from any recordings table, so the FreeSWITCH uuid 404s forever; 404 no_recording when recording_s3_key is null, which is the normal answer for the minutes after hangup while the EC2 uploader lands the file, and permanent for calls that were never recorded; 503 misconfigured when HIVEKU_RECORDINGS_BUCKET is unset; a 200 does NOT prove the object exists, because the presign is a local signature with no S3 round trip, so a swept or missing object still returns a happy URL that 404s at S3 when opened; 404 not_found for a call in another account; 402 voice_not_enabled when the Voice add-on is off. The us-east-2 KMS bucket has no CORS, so the URL plays in an audio element or a direct download but a browser fetch or XHR against it is blocked.

tools.name: voice_ring_group_create
tools.description: Creates a ring group and makes it live. It provisions the PBX FIRST (the FusionPBX ring-group row, one destination per member and the dialplan rule on the shared EC2 box) and only then writes the Hiveku rows in one transaction, so on success dialling the group's extension immediately rings real desk phones and softphones, and any DID later pointed at it sends live callers there. No TTS and no carrier spend on this call itself. RETURNS { ring_group } carrying the saved row plus fusionpbx_ring_group_uuid, member_count and member_destination_uuids. THE EXTENSION IS YOURS TO PICK AND NOTHING CROSS-CHECKS IT. `extension` is a 2-6 digit number you supply (7xxx is the convention); it is not allocated and it is not compared against the IVR 6000-6999 pool, the queue 5000-5999 pool, user extensions from 1001 up, or the 8001-8999 personal ring-group pool. Two dialplan rules matching the same digits are resolved by order, silently, which is how a live misroute happens. The only real guard is the unique index on (account_id, extension), and it fires AFTER the PBX provision: a duplicate is not caught as a 409, it falls through to the generic handler and comes back as 500 internal_error with the FusionPBX group ALREADY CREATED and no Hiveku row to manage it. Pick a free number with voice_extensions_list and voice_ring_groups_list first. Refusals: 402 voice_not_enabled when the paid Voice add-on is off; 409 not_provisioned when the account has no voice tenant; 422 members_not_found listing extension ids that are not on this account; 422 timeout_target_id_required, timeout_target_not_found (also the answer for a non-UUID id, and for a target row that exists but has a NULL extension) and timeout_target_external_e164_required; 422 invalid_body, and the schema is STRICT so an unknown or renamed key is rejected rather than dropped. The fallback is hard-validated on purpose: a group saved with a fallback type and no resolvable target renders as configured while FreeSWITCH has no post-bridge action at all, so unanswered callers hear silence and then get hung up on. A voice_server failure maps to 404, 422, 409 or 502 ring_group_provision_failed and writes no Hiveku row. MONEY: timeout_target_type 'external_number' forwards every unanswered call out to the PSTN through Telnyx, which bills carrier minutes on each one and is subject to the toll-fraud cap and caller-id rules; only the E.164 shape is checked here, tenant ownership and fraud rules are enforced by voice_server at apply time.

tools.name: voice_ring_group_delete
tools.description: PERMANENTLY deletes a ring group and the routing that depends on it. IRREVERSIBLE: the FusionPBX group, its member destinations and its dialplan rule are torn down and the Hiveku row is deleted, with member rows cascading. There is no undo; recreating it means re-entering every member and fallback, and the freed extension can be claimed by something else in the meantime. This is the SAFEST-ORDERED of the three routing deletes: teardown runs FIRST and a failure returns 502 ring_group_teardown_failed having deleted NOTHING, so a failed call here is safe to retry (the IVR and queue deletes behave differently and delete the row anyway). It also REFUSES rather than orphaning: 409 ring_group_in_use while a phone number routes to it, another group falls back to it, an IVR menu digit or after-hours target points at it, or a queue overflows to it, and the message names each blocker so you can re-point them first. That guard exists because an IVR menu digit renders as a plain transfer in FreeSWITCH, so a deleted group turns that keypress into dead air with no error recorded anywhere. WHAT IT DOES NOT CHECK: only voice_numbers, voice_ring_groups, voice_ivrs and voice_queues are queried. A call-tracking DID pool whose voice_did_pools.inbound_target_id is this group, and a pending carrier order in voice_number_orders that will adopt into it, both pass the guard and are silently orphaned, including every number that joins that pool later. RETURNS { id, deleted: true } with no warning key, because the only failure mode is the 502 that changes nothing. A group that never reached the PBX is simply deleted. Also 404 not_found for an id on another account, and 402 voice_not_enabled when the paid Voice add-on is off.

tools.name: voice_ring_group_get
tools.description: One ring group with its member rows, which voice_ring_groups_list does not return. RETURNS { ring_group: { ...row, members[] } } ordered by priority ascending. The row carries name, strategy, ring_seconds, extension, the three timeout_target fields, fusionpbx_group_uuid, rr_cursor (the persistent round-robin pointer the voice server increments per call, never written by the builder) and is_personal / personal_user_id, so the auto-created personal groups from the 8001-8999 pool show up here alongside real teams. Members carry extension_id, priority, weight, delay_seconds and timeout_seconds. READ THE TWO NULLS. fusionpbx_group_uuid null means the group exists only in Postgres and has never reached FreeSWITCH, so it cannot ring anyone no matter how correct the row looks, and an edit to it will report a clean 200 while changing nothing on the phone system. A null extension means nothing can dial or transfer to it, and it also disqualifies the group from being another group's fallback. members[].extension_id is a voice_extensions UUID, not a dial number; resolve the actual phones with voice_extensions_list. members[].timeout_seconds is stored per leg but any edit through voice_ring_group_update re-pushes every leg at the group-level ring_seconds, so a per-member value here is not necessarily what FreeSWITCH is using. Read-only, no spend, nothing changes. 404 not_found is also the answer for a group on another account, so it does not distinguish deleted from foreign. 402 voice_not_enabled when the paid Voice add-on is off, which is a plan refusal rather than a missing group.

tools.name: voice_ring_group_update
tools.description: Edits a live ring group: who rings, in what order, for how long, and where an unanswered call falls through to. It COMMITS the Hiveku rows first and then pushes to voice_server, which rewrites the FusionPBX group and its timeout action and replaces the member destinations, so the set of phones that ring for real inbound calls changes immediately. No TTS and no carrier spend on the call itself. RETURNS { ring_group, warning? } where ring_group is the DATABASE row, not the phone system's state. TWO WAYS THIS ANSWERS 200 HAVING NOT CHANGED THE PHONES. First, when the group has no fusionpbx_group_uuid (never provisioned) the route updates Postgres, SKIPS FreeSWITCH entirely and returns a clean 200 with NO warning at all; check that field with voice_ring_group_get before trusting a save. Second, a voice_server failure is a SOFT warning on a 200: the DB committed, the dialplan is one edit behind, and the response says so in `warning` rather than failing. PARTIAL, with two wholesale exceptions. Omitted fields are left alone, but member_extension_ids REPLACES the entire membership, and an empty array is accepted and drops every member, leaving a group that rings nobody. Sending ring_seconds alone also OVERWRITES timeout_seconds on every member row and re-pushes the members, because the live bridge dialstring is built from those rows. A THIRD THING NOTHING TELLS YOU: whenever members are pushed, every leg is sent with the group-level ring_seconds as its timeout, so per-member timeout_seconds is persisted and displayed but never reaches FreeSWITCH from this tool; only delay_seconds survives per member. The fallback is resolved from EFFECTIVE values (the field you sent, else the stored one) whenever ANY of the three timeout fields is present, so a partial body like timeout_target_id on its own is fully validated; a name-only save deliberately does not re-validate stored timeout state, so a legacy broken target cannot block a rename. Sending timeout_target_type null clears the fallback and nulls the id and E.164 with it. Refusals: 422 timeout_target_not_found (also when the target row has a NULL extension, which would otherwise make voice_server CLEAR the FreeSWITCH fallback while this row claims one is set), 422 timeout_target_self because a group falling back to itself ring-loops until the caller or the carrier gives up, 422 timeout_target_id_required, 422 timeout_target_external_e164_required, 422 members_not_found listing ids not on this account, 422 invalid_body (the schema is STRICT, so a renamed key fails loudly instead of being dropped), 404 not_found which is also the answer for another account's group, and 402 voice_not_enabled when the paid Voice add-on is off. MONEY: switching the fallback to external_number bills carrier minutes on every unanswered call from then on.

tools.name: voice_ring_groups_list
tools.description: List the account's ring groups (parallel-ringing strategies).

tools.name: voice_settings_get
tools.description: Read the account's single voice_tenant_config row, the phone system's guardrails and post-call policy, and the mandatory read before voice_settings_update. Returns { settings } carrying fusionpbx_domain, carrier_mode, concurrent_call_cap, daily_outbound_cap_cents, recording_enabled, recording_retention_days, hipaa_mode, ai_agent_enabled, missed_call_autoresponder_enabled, missed_call_autoresponder_body, conversion_upload_enabled, conversion_upload_disposition, conversion_upload_min_duration_sec, conversion_upload_value, conversion_upload_currency, ga4_upload_enabled, keyword_spotting_enabled, keyword_spotting_terms and provisioned_at. SILENT FAILURE: settings is NULL on a 200 when the account pays for the Voice add-on but the PBX tenant was never provisioned. Null is not an error and it is not a row of defaults, it means there is no row at all, and voice_settings_update against that account comes back as a bare 500 while voice_tenant_healthcheck returns the single failed check tenant_config_present. TRAPS. conversion_upload_value is a Prisma Decimal(12,2) and Prisma's Decimal serializes through toString, so it arrives as a QUOTED STRING like '12.50' rather than a JSON number; null there means upload with no value, so the Google conversion action's own defaultValue applies. keyword_spotting_terms is a bare nullable Json column, so null (never configured) is a distinct state from an empty array. recording_enabled is only the TENANT default: voice_numbers.recording_enabled is a per-DID override that beats it and this response cannot see those, so recording_enabled false is not proof that any given number is unrecorded. daily_outbound_cap_cents here is the cap the toll-fraud guard actually enforces, and it is a DIFFERENT column from account_credits.voice_daily_outbound_cap_cents reported by voice_usage_get, so the two can disagree and only this one stops calls; voice_toll_fraud_state reads this same column and adds today's spend against it. hipaa_mode is readable here but cannot be changed by any API key. ai_agent_enabled and provisioned_at are readable here and appear in NO write path on this route. Read-only, no cost, nothing reaches a person, no carrier is touched. 402 voice_not_enabled (carrying subscription_plan) without the paid Voice add-on; the key needs olympus:voice:read.

tools.name: voice_settings_update
tools.description: RECONFIGURES A LIVE PHONE SYSTEM'S GUARDRAILS. Writes only the keys you send onto the one voice_tenant_config row for this account. No carrier API is called and no PBX write happens here, but every value is read by a service that spends money, deletes recordings or texts a customer. Returns { settings } with the updated row. RESPONSE GAP: the PATCH select omits ga4_upload_enabled, ai_agent_enabled and provisioned_at even though ga4_upload_enabled IS written here, so a successful ga4_upload_enabled change is simply absent from the reply. Do not read that as a dropped write; confirm with voice_settings_get. CONSEQUENCES, each verified in the handler and its consumers. daily_outbound_cap_cents is the toll-fraud ceiling: voice_server's toll_fraud_guard polls every 30 minutes, sums today's outbound voice_calls.billable_seconds at a deliberately conservative flat 1 cent per minute, and over cap it flags the tenant and uuid_kills NEW outbound channels. Raising it raises the real Telnyx spend absorbed before a compromised extension is stopped, which is a money decision for a human, not a fix for 'outbound calls are being rejected'. Cap state lives in voice_server memory and is re-evaluated on the next poll, so a change takes up to 30 minutes to land and lowering it never drops calls already in progress. The range is 100 to 100000 cents; the guard treats 0 as never auto-cap but this route's floor of 100 makes disabling it impossible here. recording_retention_days causes IRREVERSIBLE DELETION: the daily 08:40 UTC pruner deletes the S3 recording AND transcript objects of calls older than the window, nulls both pointers and clears the CRM timeline's play button, 200 calls per tick oldest first, and nothing restores them; ai_summary and the CRM activity text survive. Cutting 365 to 30 destroys eleven months of call audio on the next tick. 0 means keep forever and those tenants are never scanned. recording_enabled is only the tenant default and a per-DID voice_numbers.recording_enabled override beats it, so setting false does not stop recording on a DID carrying its own override; it also silences the two-party-consent announcement, which is usually the opposite of what a compliance request wants. missed_call_autoresponder_enabled makes future missed inbound calls TEXT THE CALLER a real SMS that costs money per segment; the send goes through dispatchAccountSms, which does screen the do-not-text list and run the reputation governor. SILENT NO-OP: both senders require enabled AND a non-empty missed_call_autoresponder_body, so enabling with the body still null texts nobody, forever, with no error anywhere. conversion_upload_enabled starts pushing attributed calls into the connected Google Ads account as offline conversions every 5 minutes, which changes reported performance and can move automated bidding; ga4_upload_enabled does the same over the GA4 Measurement Protocol. TRAP: the dashboard disables those two controls until an ads connection exists, but THIS ROUTE CHECKS FOR NO CONNECTION AT ALL, so enabling them with nothing connected is accepted, answers 200, and uploads nothing. keyword_spotting_terms REPLACES the stored array wholesale, so sending one term deletes the other ninety-nine and [] clears them; every term is trimmed, lowercased and deduped by the schema, so the stored value will not match your casing. NOT EXPOSED ON PURPOSE: hipaa_mode is accepted by the zod schema and then silently dropped for every API-key caller (a key has no builder profile so it is never staff) while the route answers 200 echoing the OLD value, so this tool deliberately cannot send it; flipping HIPAA mode is a staff action in the dashboard. ai_agent_enabled is not in the write schema either, so this cannot turn the AI receptionist on or off. REFUSALS: 422 invalid_body with a zod issues array, which writes nothing; 402 voice_not_enabled without the paid add-on; 403 without olympus:voice:write; 401 on a bad key. SILENT FAILURES: an account with no voice_tenant_config row hits an unhandled Prisma P2025 and returns a bare 500 rather than a clean 404, so call voice_settings_get first and never PATCH when settings is null; an empty body parses fine, writes only updated_at and answers 200 unchanged. NO AUDIT ROW IS WRITTEN: the route logs the before/after diff through logVoiceAudit with a null user id, which is that helper's documented anonymous path, so it console-warns and persists NOTHING because audit_logs.user_id is a non-nullable FK. A cap raise or a retention cut made here leaves no entry on the communications audit page and no attributable actor. Tell a human exactly what you changed.

tools.name: voice_sms_brand_feedback_get
tools.description: The stored carrier feedback explaining why the account's 10DLC brand was rejected. Returns `feedback`, the brand_feedback_json snapshot already on the row, whose categories (TAX_ID, ADDRESS, and so on) name the EXACT brand fields the carriers refused, so a correction can be targeted instead of guessed. Read-only: it returns what the status cron captured when the brand went FAILED, and does NOT fetch anything fresh from the registry. `feedback: null` therefore means no failure snapshot is stored, NOT that the brand is healthy; read the brand's status for that. An account with no brand at all is a 404 `no_brand`. Fixing the named fields and calling voice_sms_brand_submit again is a fresh, fee-bearing carrier filing, not an edit.

tools.name: voice_sms_brand_submit
tools.description: Create or update the account's single 10DLC brand and FILE IT WITH THE CARRIERS. Not a draft. IRREVERSIBLE AND FEE-BEARING. It submits the legal entity (legal company name, EIN, entity type, registered address, contact email and phone) to Telnyx, which forwards it to The Campaign Registry and the US carriers for vetting. Vetting is a paid third-party review. Once submitted it CANNOT be withdrawn or un-filed from here: the identity data now sits with the registry and the carriers, a brand-vetting fee may already be incurred, and a later correction is a RE-VET (another review, another fee), never a deletion. A wrong EIN or legal name typically returns as a FAILED brand with TCR feedback and has to be re-filed. Get the EIN and legal name right the first time; this is a filing about a real company, and it wants a human decision rather than an agent's inference. One brand per account: calling again updates the existing row and re-submits, and an existing telnyx_brand_id routes to update-and-revet rather than creating a duplicate. Returns `brand` plus `submission_error`: a Telnyx failure does NOT block the local save, so `submission_error` non-null means the row persisted but the carriers never saw it, and READING ONLY THE 200 WOULD TELL YOU IT WORKED. Retry after fixing the cause. Read voice_sms_brand_feedback_get first when re-filing a rejected brand: it names the exact fields the carriers refused.

tools.name: voice_sms_bulk_send
tools.description: SENDS UP TO 200 REAL TEXT MESSAGES in one call — one per CRM contact, dispatched SERIALLY to real handsets, billed per segment, with no draft state, no idempotency key and NO RECALL. Recipients come from crm_contacts.phone ONLY, never from your input, and foreign or soft-deleted contact ids silently DROP OUT of the batch, so compare the response's total against the count you sent. Refusals BEFORE any row is written: 402 voice_not_enabled; 409 sms_not_enabled — this route DOES enforce 10DLC readiness (a VERIFIED brand with an ACTIVE campaign, or a verified toll-free sender), deliberately stricter than voice_sms_send_to_contact which checks nothing; 403 not_your_number when from_e164 is not an is_active DID on this account (toll-free verification is NOT checked on an explicit DID — an unverified TF sender clears the 403 and then fails every row inside sendSms); 409 no_sending_number when the auto-pick fails closed — under a key the pick is the ACCOUNT-level main-then-any choice admitting local plus VERIFIED toll-free, because a service key has no personal caller-ID assignment; 404 template_not_found, account-scoped; 422 invalid_body (1-200 contact UUIDs, body 1..1600 chars, no media on this route). Inside the loop each contact is handled independently: no parseable phone counts skipped_no_phone, an opted-out peer counts skipped_opt_out and is never dialed, everyone else gets a thread upsert then a live send. A MID-BATCH FAILURE IS A PARTIAL SUCCESS, not an error status: a carrier or governor refusal on row N lands that contact in failed[] with its message row persisted as delivery_status 'failed', and the loop KEEPS GOING — and because the shared governor's daily and per-minute caps still apply to every row here, a cap or kill-switch hit partway through typically fails ALL remaining rows with the same reason. NEVER blindly re-run the same contact list after a partial batch: everyone in accepted already received the text and would receive it AGAIN; retry only the contact_ids in failed[], and when the error text names the governor (paused, cap, velocity) an immediate retry cannot help. Merge vars render per-contact ONLY when body.trim() exactly equals the stored template body; any edited body is sent VERBATIM to all 200, literal braces included. {sender_first_name}/{sender_last_name} render EMPTY under a key (no profile behind it); {business_name} still resolves. scheduled_for is an ABSOLUTE UTC instant with NO quiet-hours rule and no contact-timezone check (it can land at 3am local); it defers only when more than 30 seconds ahead, writing delivery_status 'scheduled' rows for /api/cron/sms-scheduled-tick — list those with voice_sms_scheduled_list and cancel individually with voice_sms_scheduled_cancel; anything nearer or in the past SENDS NOW. Template usage is bumped once per batch, not per recipient. Each ACCEPTED immediate send is mirrored to the contact's CRM timeline and fires the sms.delivered webhook (an event that fires at carrier ACCEPT, never at delivery); scheduled rows are not mirrored. Response { accepted, scheduled, skipped_opt_out, skipped_no_phone, failed: [{contact_id, error}], total }, where 'accepted' means Telnyx took the message, not that it arrived. The audit row is SKIPPED for keys (logVoiceAudit userId null is its anonymous path: console-warn only, because audit_logs.user_id is a NOT NULL FK), so a 200-message blast leaves no entry on the voice audit page.

tools.name: voice_sms_campaign_appeal
tools.description: Appeal a REJECTED or SUSPENDED 10DLC campaign - Telnyx re-queues the existing registration for manual review with your appeal_reason attached. ADDS A NOTE ONLY. The campaign's content is UNCHANGED: the reviewers re-read the same use case, description, message flow and samples with your reason alongside. An appeal is only useful when the rejection was WRONG; if the content was the problem, fix it and go through voice_sms_campaign_delete + a fresh voice_sms_campaign_submit instead (there is no content-edit-and-re-review lane yet). Only campaigns Telnyx knows about (telnyx_campaign_id set) in canonical FAILED or SUSPENDED accept an appeal: 422 not_registered means the row never reached Telnyx (that is voice_sms_campaign_resubmit territory), 422 not_appealable means the current status does not allow it. A carrier-side failure is 502 appeal_failed with NOTHING written locally - the row still reads FAILED/SUSPENDED and the appeal can simply be retried. On success the row flips to canonical PENDING (raw APPEAL_PENDING, our synthetic marker - Telnyx reports nothing until the review lands) and the status cron resumes watching it; expect days, not minutes. appeal_reason goes to the TCR reviewers VERBATIM (20-2000 chars - contentless appeals are auto-rejected). Called with an API key the dashboard audit row is skipped (logged server-side only). 402 voice_not_enabled without the paid Voice add-on.

tools.name: voice_sms_campaign_carriers_get
tools.description: Live per-carrier (MNO) verdict for ONE 10DLC campaign, read straight from Telnyx on every call (no cache). Returns {registered, campaignStatus, tcrStatus, carriers} where each carrier is {mno, networkId, status:'approved'|'review_pending'|'not_qualified'|'unsupported', supported, qualified, reviewPending, tpm, mmsTpm, brandTier, dailyCap}, sorted AT&T, T-Mobile, Verizon Wireless, US Cellular, then alphabetical. This is what answers 'T-Mobile is filtering us but AT&T is fine' and 'what throughput did each carrier grant'. campaign_id is the HIVEKU voice_sms_campaign UUID (brand.campaigns[].id from voice_sms_registration_get), NOT telnyx_campaign_id: the lookup is findFirst by primary id scoped to the account, so passing the Telnyx id (the id printed all over the carrier report) returns 404 campaign_not_found rather than anything more helpful. TRAPS, all of which look alike: a campaign that never reached Telnyx answers 200 with registered:false and carriers:[], meaning 'not submitted', not 'every carrier refused'; carriers:[] on a 200 with registered:true means Telnyx has published no mnoMetadata yet, again not a refusal; and a Telnyx failure answers HTTP 502 with registered:true, error 'carrier_status_unavailable', the raw upstream message and empty carriers. That 502 is deliberate fail-soft, so report 'carrier breakdown unavailable' and keep the canonical verdict from voice_sms_registration_get rather than telling anyone their campaign broke. campaignStatus and tcrStatus here are Telnyx/TCR RAW strings (ACTIVE, TCR_ACCEPTED, MNO_PENDING) taken live from the vendor, never the canonical vocabulary; the campaign's stored canonical status is read by this handler and deliberately not returned, so never test these fields the way can_send tests for ACTIVE. Reads TELNYX_API_KEY on the builder web service, which must stay in sync with the voice_server key: a rotated or unset key 502s every call with 'TELNYX_API_KEY is not configured' while the campaign itself is perfectly healthy. Read-only, no cost, nothing is sent to a person and nothing changes carrier-side. 402 voice_not_enabled without the paid Voice add-on.

tools.name: voice_sms_campaign_delete
tools.description: Remove an INERT 10DLC campaign row - the trash/cleanup action for the FAILED, EXPIRED, or never-submitted rows that pile up after repeated rejections. HARD DELETE of the local row; the history survives only in the voice audit log. Deliberately refuses (422 not_deletable) any campaign that is ACTIVE, PENDING, VERIFIED, or SUSPENDED - a working or in-flight registration can never be removed this way. Deletable iff the row never reached Telnyx (telnyx_campaign_id null) OR its status is terminally FAILED / EXPIRED. A SUSPENDED campaign goes through voice_sms_campaign_appeal, not deletion. The Telnyx-side record of a deleted FAILED/EXPIRED campaign is deliberately left orphaned - it carries no numbers and does not bill, and deleting locally does NOT refund the vetting fee already spent. There is no content-edit route: fixing a rejected campaign's copy is delete + a fresh voice_sms_campaign_submit (a NEW ~$15 vetting fee) or, for a row that never reached Telnyx, voice_sms_campaign_resubmit for free. campaign_id is the LOCAL row UUID; foreign/missing ids 404. Called with an API key the dashboard audit row is skipped (logged server-side only). 402 voice_not_enabled without the paid Voice add-on.

tools.name: voice_sms_campaign_draft
tools.description: Draft a carrier-compliant 10DLC campaign from the account's own business context and brand guide, streamed back field by field: campaign name, use case, description, message flow, sample messages and keyword sets. Optional `prompt` steers it. DRAFTS TEXT ONLY. No campaign row is created, nothing reaches Telnyx, The Campaign Registry or the carriers, and there is nothing to withdraw. The irreversible, fee-bearing step is filing the draft with voice_sms_campaign_submit afterwards (~$15 vetting per fresh submission). Requires the account's brand to be VERIFIED first, the same precondition the create route enforces; on an unverified brand this refuses rather than drafting something that could not be filed. Pass the result through voice_sms_cta_preflight before submitting it: the drafter writes a plausible message flow, but only preflight checks that the opt-in page it names actually contains the required disclosures.

tools.name: voice_sms_campaign_get
tools.description: One 10DLC campaign row in full: status (canonical and raw), telnyx_campaign_id, description, message_flow, sample_messages, keyword sets, appeal fields. The single-row read behind the resubmit/appeal/delete decision, without pulling the whole brand the way voice_sms_registration_get does. campaign_id is the LOCAL row UUID (brand.campaigns[].id from voice_sms_registration_get), NOT telnyx_campaign_id - the Telnyx id 404s. A missing and a foreign id both answer 404 not_found. TRAP: telnyx_campaign_status here is the CANONICAL vocabulary (TCR_ACCEPTED normalizes to PENDING - a campaign that reached Telnyx is NOT approved; only ACTIVE is). PRIVACY: the row is unmasked - do not paste it into customer-facing copy. Read-only, no cost. 402 voice_not_enabled without the paid Voice add-on.

tools.name: voice_sms_campaign_resubmit
tools.description: Retry lane for a 10DLC campaign row that never reached Telnyx. voice_sms_campaign_submit persists locally even when the carrier submit fails, leaving telnyx_campaign_id null; this re-files that row without spending a second vetting fee on a duplicate. THIS FILES THE CAMPAIGN and is fee-bearing at the registry. It sends the use case, description, message flow, sample messages and opt-in/opt-out keywords to Telnyx, then The Campaign Registry and the carriers. Not reversible from here. The body is OPTIONAL. Send nothing to re-file the row exactly as stored. Send a body and it must be the COMPLETE campaign payload, the same schema as create, not a patch: the row's editable fields are overwritten from it before re-submitting, so omitting a field you previously set CLEARS it. The usual flow is to fix the description a reviewer flagged and retry. Run voice_sms_cta_preflight on the message_flow before retrying. Resubmitting the same flow that was rejected buys another rejection.

tools.name: voice_sms_campaign_submit
tools.description: Create a 10DLC campaign under the account's VERIFIED brand and FILE IT WITH THE CARRIERS. Not a draft (that is voice_sms_campaign_draft, which writes no row). IRREVERSIBLE AND FEE-BEARING. Each FRESH submission that reaches the registry spends roughly $15 of carrier vetting, and once filed it CANNOT be withdrawn from here: a telnyx_campaign_id is stamped on the row, monthly campaign and carrier pass-through charges begin, and a rejected campaign is contested through voice_sms_campaign_appeal, never by filing again. Returns { campaign, submission_error }. submission_error NON-NULL means the row SAVED LOCALLY but the carriers never saw it (and no vetting fee was spent) - READING ONLY THE 200 WOULD TELL YOU IT WORKED. Fix the cause and retry with voice_sms_campaign_resubmit on THAT row (campaign.id); calling this tool again creates a duplicate filing. Refusals, all 422 BEFORE any spend: no_brand / brand_not_verified (the brand must be canonical VERIFIED - read voice_sms_registration_get); use_case_needs_subtypes (MIXED takes 2-5 sub_usecases, LOW_VOLUME 1-5, every other use case takes none); cta_not_verifiable - the CTA preflight is ENFORCED SERVER-SIDE on this route: the opt-in URLs named in message_flow are fetched with NO JavaScript, the way the reviewer's crawler works, so the opt-in page must be SERVER-RENDERED and carry all 8 required CTA elements, including the no-sharing disclosure sentence ('we will not share your mobile information with third parties for marketing'). Run voice_sms_cta_preflight first; acknowledge_cta_warnings is the informed override for warning-level findings only. The description and use case must MATCH what the brand's website visibly does - reviewers cross-check, and a mismatch is a rejection. APPROVAL IS NOT THE END. TCR_ACCEPTED (and TELNYX_ACCEPTED) are NOT sendable states - they normalize to canonical PENDING on purpose, because campaigns have gone TCR_ACCEPTED then TELNYX_FAILED. Only canonical ACTIVE counts, then allow 24-72h of carrier propagation before full deliverability, and on a multi-campaign account the sending number must still be ASSIGNED to the campaign with voice_sms_number_assign_campaign after it goes ACTIVE. Called with an API key there is no builder profile, so the dashboard audit row is skipped (logged server-side only) - tell the account owner what was filed.

tools.name: voice_sms_cta_preflight
tools.description: Check a 10DLC campaign's message flow the way a carrier will, BEFORE you pay to file it. Fetches each opt-in URL the flow names with NO JavaScript, exactly as the reviewer's crawler does, and reports which required CTA elements are actually present in the returned HTML. Returns a `report` of found/missing elements. Run this first, always. It files nothing, writes no row, contacts no registry, and leaves nothing to withdraw, so a missing disclosure costs a re-check here instead of a rejection fee and roughly a week of carrier review. A CTA rendered only by client-side JavaScript will pass in a browser and FAIL here, which is the single most common reason a campaign is rejected. Caller-supplied URLs go through an SSRF guard. message_flow is capped at 4096 characters and a missing or empty one is a 422 naming the field.

tools.name: voice_sms_messaging_profile_attach
tools.description: Bulk-attaches ALL of the tenant's active DIDs to their approved 10DLC messaging profile — voice_server walks voice_numbers and PATCHes each one on Telnyx, mutating live carrier config per DID, then stamps messaging_profile_attached_at back. Use it as the backfill after the first campaign verifies, or as the recovery path when a campaign was re-issued with a fresh messaging_profile_id. THIS IS NOT CAMPAIGN ASSIGNMENT: attaching a DID to the profile lets it ride that profile, but an account running MORE THAN ONE 10DLC campaign still needs voice_sms_number_assign_campaign per number, or its sends die at the carrier with Telnyx error 40010 even though this call returned the number in attached[]. Omit telnyx_messaging_profile_id and voice_server picks the latest VERIFIED campaign's profile; pass an explicit id ONLY for a re-issued campaign — a wrong id detaches working numbers from the profile they were sending under, and the explicit id also BYPASSES the sanity check below, so double-check it against voice_sms_campaign_get first. Refusals: 402 voice_not_enabled; 409 no_campaign when the id is omitted and no campaign row on this account carries a messaging profile (register the 10DLC brand + campaign first); 422 invalid_body. A voice_server/carrier failure surfaces at ITS status as attach_failed (a 5xx upstream becomes 502; a 4xx passes through at its own code), with nothing partial recorded here. SUCCESS IS A PARTITION, NOT A VERDICT: 200 returns { profile_id, attached[], skipped_already[], failed[] } and a 200 with entries in failed[] is a PARTIAL success — read failed[] before declaring the account fixed. Re-running is safe in the narrow sense that already-attached DIDs land in skipped_already rather than erroring. The audit row is skipped for keys (logVoiceAudit userId null: console-warn only), so this carrier-config change leaves no entry on the voice audit page.

tools.name: voice_sms_number_assign_campaign
