Use this when a user gives you the short id from the dashboard but you need the full UUID for the rest of the workflow API.

tools.name: workflow_resume
tools.description: Clear an auto-pause on a workflow and reset its failure counter so it accepts triggers again. Hiveku auto-pauses a workflow when its circuit breaker trips (repeated failures) or it detects a cascade loop. While paused the webhook KEEPS ACCEPTING deliveries — they are stored and never processed — so resuming is only half the job: call workflow_stranded_list afterwards to see what piled up, then workflow_stranded_replay to actually run it. Fix the cause first. Resuming a workflow that is still broken just trips the breaker again.

tools.name: workflow_run
tools.description: Trigger a workflow run — works for BOTH test runs during development AND production invocation. ★ test_mode:true runs on a DISABLED workflow (the safe dry-run no longer requires arming the real webhook first). test_mode DOES interpolate {{…}} expressions: each skipped node's `would_have` shows the RESOLVED values the real run would have sent (with the raw templates under `would_have._template` when they differ) — an empty resolved field next to a {{ref}} is a blank-merge bug made visible. Sets triggered_by="manual" on the run row, which the executor handles identically to a real trigger firing. Accepts `id` or `workflow_id`. Two modes: (1) SYNC (default) — waits for completion, returns final status (completed | error), output, and error. Use for short workflows (under ~25s) and for test runs where you want immediate feedback. (2) FIRE-AND-FORGET — set fire_and_forget=true to return 202 with a run_id; use for long workflows. After any run, call workflow_run_get with the returned run_id to inspect per-node step_states (input/output/error per node) — that's your primary debug surface. **`test_mode: true` is the safe dry-run flag.** When set, the engine: (a) skips the run-quota burn + cascade detection + run-row creation (transient, doesn't pollute history); (b) short-circuits every SIDE-EFFECTING node before it fires (no real emails, Slack posts, CRM writes, HTTP requests, helpdesk tickets, DB writes, deploys, etc.). Each skipped node returns a mock NodeExecutionResult with `__dry_run: true`, `action: '<nodeType>'`, and `would_have: { ...the args it would have sent }`. Pure handlers (data transforms, array ops, flow control) STILL run for fidelity. Downstream nodes that reference `{{nodeId.output.X}}` see either the would_have payload or a synthetic field (e.g. messageId for sendEmail) — so the workflow's structural correctness is testable even though no real side effect fires.

tools.name: workflow_run_cancel
tools.description: Stop a run that is still going (status running, pending or waiting). Terminal runs are refused with 409 naming the status they are already in, so this cannot 'cancel' something that already finished, and it never rewrites history. Cancelling does NOT undo side effects that already fired: steps completed before the cancel stay done, which is why a cancel is a way to stop the bleeding, not a rollback. Returns { data: { run_id, status: 'cancelled', cancelled_by } }; the actor recorded is the API key, not a caller-supplied name.

tools.name: workflow_run_get
tools.description: Get one workflow run with the full per-node execution detail. Returns: status (pending|running|completed|failed), input_data, output_data, error_message, and step_states — a map of { nodeId: { status, input?, output?, error? } } showing exactly what each node received, produced, or failed on. This is the agent's primary debug tool: after workflow_run, fetch this to see which node tripped and why, then call workflow_node_update to fix and re-run. (Alias of workflow_run_status — same payload, clearer name.)

tools.name: workflow_run_logs
tools.description: Return the per-node lifecycle log lines captured during a workflow run — the engine's structured trace (config / starting / handler invoked / retry / timeout / completion / soft-fail) per node, NOT raw stdout. Complements workflow_run_get (which shows step_states.X.error/output) by showing the timeline of WHAT happened during execution, not just the final state. Response: `{ logs: [{node_id, node_status, ts, level, msg}], summary: {total, by_level: {info,warn,error}, by_node: {<id>: count}} }` sorted by timestamp. Capped at 50 lines per node (longer-running handlers truncate the tail). Filter via `node_id` (one node only) or `level` (info|warn|error). Use to: - Verify a node was reached + how long it took - See retry attempts before a final failure - Confirm soft-fail (on_error=continue) fired as expected - Audit dry-run / test_mode short-circuits

tools.name: workflow_run_replay
tools.description: RE-RUNS A PAST RUN'S INPUT FOR REAL, as a NEW run - confirm with the human first. Requires confirm:true and refuses with 400 without it. This is not workflow_stranded_replay: that one replays submissions banked while a workflow was PAUSED, in bounded confirmed batches; this one re-fires a single specific run you name. Because it creates a new run, per-run send-once idempotency does not protect it, so every send in the graph happens again. Returns 202 { data: { source_run_id, run_id, status: 'started' } } (run_id may be null if the row was not visible within the poll window - read workflow_runs_list to find it). Refused 409 while the workflow is paused (resume it first, and check workflow_stranded_list before replaying anything), and 422 when the run's stored input was truncated and cannot be faithfully replayed.

tools.name: workflow_run_retry
tools.description: RE-EXECUTES A FAILED RUN FOR REAL - confirm with the human first. Requires confirm:true and refuses with 400 without it. Every side-effecting step runs again: emails and SMS send, CRM rows are written, external calls fire. The engine's send-once guard is keyed PER RUN, so it does NOT dedupe a retry against the original attempt - if the original sent an email before failing on a later step, the retry sends it again. Runs inline to completion (up to 300s) and returns { data: { new_run_id, retry_count } }. Refused when the run is not in a retryable status or its retry budget is spent. For a run so old its stored input was truncated, prefer fixing the workflow and triggering fresh.

tools.name: workflow_run_status
tools.description: Get the status and full execution detail of a workflow run. Returns: status (pending|running|completed|failed), input_data, output_data, error_message, triggered_by, started_at, completed_at, AND step_states — a per-node map of { nodeId: { status, input?, output?, error? } } showing exactly what each node received, what it produced, and which one (if any) failed. This is the agent's primary debugging surface: after workflow_run, fetch step_states to see which node tripped, then workflow_node_update to fix and re-run. workflow_run_get is an alias for this tool.

tools.name: workflow_run_summary
tools.description: Aggregate run summary for a workflow over a configurable window. Returns: total counts by status (succeeded/failed/running/pending), success_rate (0..1), latency_ms percentiles (p50/p95/p99/mean), up-to-5 most-recent failures with error_message, and pointers to the most recent success + failure (`last_succeeded_at`, `last_failed_at`, `last_failed_run_id` — drill into the latter with workflow_run_get when something looks off). Caps at 1000 runs in the window; narrow the `since` to look at a tighter slice.

tools.name: workflow_runs_list
tools.description: List recent runs of a workflow (paginated). Same route as workflow_run_status/workflow_run_get for a single run.

tools.name: workflow_runs_recent
tools.description: Account-wide recent-runs feed across ALL workflows. Highest-value when debugging a form that's not landing: filter status=failed + since=last 10 min and you see exactly which workflow tripped, no need to iterate every workflow_id. Each entry includes workflow_name, status, triggered_by, error_message, started_at, completed_at, and duration_ms. Default window: last 1 hour. Use this BEFORE workflow_runs_list when you don't yet know which workflow is broken.

tools.name: workflow_set_recipient
tools.description: Rewrite the `to` field on every (or a subset of) sendEmail node in a workflow. Common per-site operation during migrations — replaces a full workflow_update payload with a one-line call. Defaults `mode` to 'expression' (the sendEmail field mode that supports templating); pass 'literal' for a hardcoded address. Snapshots a workflow_versions row before writing so the change is reversible via workflow_version_restore.

tools.name: workflow_set_schedule
tools.description: Set or update the cron schedule for a workflow (upsert). Patches the workflow's scheduledTrigger node in place — does not touch other nodes/edges. cron_expression is a 5-field cron string (e.g. "0 9 * * 1-5" = weekdays at 9am). Supports *, */N, ranges (1-5), comma lists (1,3,5). Set enabled=false to pause the schedule without disabling the whole workflow.

tools.name: workflow_stranded_list
tools.description: Submissions a workflow RECEIVED while it was paused and never processed. Read-only — always call this before replaying. This is the failure mode that looks like nothing happened: a paused workflow still accepts its webhook, so payloads are stored in trigger_runs but produce no CRM record and no notification. The leads are not lost, they are invisible. Returns the pause window, the count, and one row per submission carrying trigger_run_id, received_at, form_name, and payload_KEYS — the field names only, never the values. A stranded payload can hold personal data, so the contents are deliberately withheld: you can tell the operator HOW MANY leads are waiting, when they arrived and which form they came from, but you cannot read them their names or email addresses from here, and you should not promise to. Rows are capped at 200, so a large count may be partial. Already-replayed rows are filtered out, so this shows exactly what a replay would run.

tools.name: workflow_stranded_replay
tools.description: SENDS REAL NOTIFICATIONS. Re-runs stored submissions through the workflow's CURRENT definition. Requires confirm:true. Call workflow_stranded_list first and show the user what would run — these submissions can be days old, so replaying emails someone about a form they filled in last week. Capped at 25 per call; pass trigger_run_ids to replay a specific subset instead of everything. Resume the workflow first (workflow_resume) or the replay just strands them again.

tools.name: workflow_templates_list
tools.description: List the canonical agent-instantiable workflow templates. Returns slug, label, description, the variables each template needs (with type/required flags), and the raw definition (with `{{var.NAME}}` placeholders). Pair with workflow_create_from_template to instantiate. The catalog is the form/newsletter migration defaults plus the standing SEO/PPC/reputation delivery playbooks (search-terms-to-negatives for Google AND Bing, disapproval triage, impression-share and budget reviews, lost-backlink alert, tech-audit regression, rank-drop response, content-decay refresh, monthly AEO visibility, GBP review SLA + weekly post draft, CWV watch, ...). Read the returned `count` — the catalog grows between releases. Every PPC write in them stages to approval, never auto-applies. ★ Every template carries its full node graph. Pass _fields:["slug","label","description"] unless you actually need to read the graph.

tools.name: workflow_templating_syntax
tools.description: Returns the workflow templating language reference: which `{{...}}` expressions the executor resolves at run-time, what the `trigger.output.payload`/`headers`/`query` scopes contain, how to reference upstream node outputs, the `{mode, value}` field modes used by sendEmail, and worked examples. Read this BEFORE you write any node `data` that interpolates a value — the alternative is guessing from another workflow's JSON.

tools.name: workflow_test
tools.description: Run a workflow as a SAFE DRY-RUN. Functionally identical to `workflow_run` with `test_mode: true`, but the named tool makes it discoverable — agents shouldn't have to remember the flag. What it skips (no real side effects fire): - Outbound emails / SMS / Slack / Discord notifications - CRM writes (contact / deal / activity / company create+update+delete + tag changes) - HTTP apiCall to external URLs (the engine returns a mocked response shape) - Helpdesk ticket creates + replies - PM task writes - Database writes (dbInsert / dbUpdate / dbDelete) - Deployments + GitHub pushes - File saves to project (builder_code_versions writes) What still runs (for fidelity): - Pure data transforms (transformData, forEach, switch, conditional) - Array ops (sort, filter, map, reduce) - Template resolution + flow control - Trigger nodes (deterministic payloads from input_data) Returns the same shape as workflow_run — step_states.X.output carries `__dry_run: true` and `would_have: {...args}` on every short-circuited node. Run-quota is NOT debited, no run row is persisted, cascade detection is bypassed.

tools.name: workflow_trigger_create
tools.description: Create a workflow_triggers row that wires an external event into one specific node in the workflow's definition. The trigger row carries the webhook URL / cron / DB-watch metadata; the workflow's definition still needs a corresponding *Trigger node (e.g. webhookTrigger) — use workflow_node_add for that. Call workflow_trigger_types_list first to see config keys per trigger_type. Returns the trigger plus, for webhook triggers with authentication='bearer', a one-time bearer_token (NOT shown again — record it).

tools.name: workflow_trigger_delete
tools.description: Remove a workflow trigger.

tools.name: workflow_trigger_get
tools.description: Full detail for ONE trigger — its type, config and current state. workflow_triggers_list gives the summary; use this when you need the exact configuration of a single trigger.

tools.name: workflow_trigger_types_list
tools.description: Discover every trigger_type the workflow_triggers table accepts plus the config keys each type reads. Returns: webhook (with http_method/authentication/response_mode), scheduled_trigger (with cron_expression/timezone), database_trigger (with table_name/operations/column_filters). Call before workflow_trigger_create so you pass the right config shape — config is otherwise untyped and unknown keys are silently ignored. For INTERNAL event-driven triggers (CRM contact created, PM task moved, helpdesk ticket assigned, billing invoice paid, Shopify order, form submitted, etc.) call `workflow_event_trigger_types_list` instead — those are workflow-graph trigger nodes, not workflow_triggers table rows.

tools.name: workflow_trigger_update
tools.description: Update a workflow trigger: enable/disable it, rename it, change the accepted HTTP method, or replace its filter_config (which is where webhook AUTH lives). WEBHOOK AUTH — filter_config.authentication is what actually gates a form's webhook, NOT the workflow-level authRequired flag. Values: 'none' = PUBLIC (the correct setting for a website lead-capture form — the browser posts with no token); 'bearer' | 'basicAuth' | 'headerAuth' | 'jwtAuth' = protected (a credential is required). Writing filter_config also rewrites require_auth_token to match, so the boolean and the config can never disagree. TROUBLESHOOTING: if a form submission returns 401 "Unauthorized: Missing Bearer token" (or the visitor sees a fake success but no email/CRM fires), the trigger requires auth it should not — call this with filter_config:{authentication:'none'} to make it public. Do NOT diagnose form-webhook 401s as a platform/Clerk issue; check workflow_triggers_list for require_auth_token=true first. filter_config is REPLACED, not merged: send the whole object, or you will drop the keys you left out. Read the current one with workflow_trigger_get first.

tools.name: workflow_triggers_list
tools.description: List triggers configured on a workflow.

tools.name: workflow_update
tools.description: Update top-level workflow fields (name, description, is_enabled) OR replace the entire `definition` graph in one call. For granular changes prefer workflow_node_add / workflow_node_update / workflow_node_delete / workflow_edge_add / workflow_edge_delete — those snapshot every change individually with a `change_summary`, while this tool's full-definition write produces a single coarse snapshot. Definition shape: { nodes: [{id, type, data, position}], edges: [{id, source, target, sourceHandle?, targetHandle?}] }. Toggle `is_enabled` here or use the dedicated workflow_enable / workflow_disable tools.

tools.name: workflow_validate
tools.description: Server-side validation of the workflow's current definition. Catches structural problems BEFORE workflow_run / workflow_enable so you don't get a run-time 'Unsupported node type' surprise. Reports errors (unknown node types, missing required fields, dangling edges to non-existent nodes, duplicate ids, no trigger) and warnings (orphan nodes — unreachable from any trigger, multiple triggers — only the first fires, self-loops, invalid source handles). Returns { ok, issues[], summary: { nodes, edges, triggers, errors, warnings } }. Call after every batch of edits.

tools.name: workflow_version_get
tools.description: Fetch a specific version snapshot with its full definition. `version` is the monotonic integer (e.g. 7), NOT the row uuid. Use to diff a previous state against the current workflow or to preview what workflow_version_restore will do.

tools.name: workflow_version_restore
tools.description: Roll back a workflow's definition to a previous version. The CURRENT definition is snapshotted first (so the restore is itself reversible), then the workflow row is overwritten with the prior version's graph. Use when an agent's edits break something and you want to bail cleanly. Returns { restored_from_version, new_snapshot_version }.

tools.name: workflow_versions_list
tools.description: List version snapshots of a workflow's definition (most recent first). Every definition write (PATCH or granular node/edge op) creates a snapshot, so this is the audit log of who changed what when. Each entry has `version` (monotonic int), `change_summary` (e.g. 'add node webhookTrigger_abc12345'), and `created_at`. The full definition is omitted to keep payloads small — use workflow_version_get for that.

tools.name: workflow_webhook_auth_set
tools.description: Put header authentication on a workflow's webhook WITHOUT ever seeing the secret. The server generates a 128-bit value, stores it on the trigger, stamps it into the workflow definition for the owner's editor panel, and returns only `secret_last4` so you can confirm which credential is live. You cannot read the value back: workflow_get, workflow_version_get and the trigger tools all redact it. Give the last4 to the human and have them copy the full value from the workflow editor. Use this instead of leaving a webhook public when you have no shared secret to configure. Requires an existing webhook trigger on the workflow (create one with workflow_trigger_create or by adding a webhookTrigger node). Only mode 'headerAuth' is supported here; bearer auth is set from the editor panel. Returns { ok, mode, header_name, secret_last4, webhook_path }.
